script.speaker: A
script.line: Good morning Pavel, it's Ingrid from planning. Thanks for taking my call. The Danish customer needs all eighty pallets by the 15th, and I'd like to discuss that.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Morning, Ingrid. Right, I looked at it yesterday. Honestly, we can't send everything by the 15th, but about sixty percent, so forty-eight pallets, can leave on time.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Forty-eight is a start, but the customer won't be happy. Could the remaining thirty-two follow in a second truck a few days later?

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's what I'd suggest. The first truck would collect at ten fifteen on Thursday, and the second one the following Wednesday.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Understood. Could we speed things up by sending the second part by air, so it still arrives close to the 15th? I can ask finance to cover the extra cost.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I appreciate the offer, but I'd rather not. The second lot only comes off the line on Thursday afternoon, and it still has to pass the full quality check.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I see. So even a faster carrier wouldn't help, because the goods wouldn't be ready to ship.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Exactly. And I don't want to promise a date and then miss it. You know how that goes.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Fair enough. Then I'll tell the customer to expect forty-eight pallets by the 15th and the rest the week after.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good. Please also confirm the dock slot at your end for ten fifteen, otherwise the driver will wait outside.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I'll call the warehouse right after this and send you a written confirmation before the end of today.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Perfect. Then I'll let the line manager know, and I'll email you the lot numbers tomorrow.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of Ingrid's call?
options: To ask Pavel for a lower price after a customer complaint
To agree how to deliver an order that cannot all arrive on time
To cancel the order because the customer changed its plans
To report a quality problem with a lot already delivered
questions.explanation: Ingrid says the customer needs all eighty pallets by the 15th, and Pavel explains only sixty percent can leave on time.

questions.q: When will the first truck collect the goods?
options: Thursday afternoon
The following Wednesday
On the 15th at ten
Thursday at ten fifteen
questions.explanation: Pavel says the first truck would collect at ten fifteen on Thursday; Thursday afternoon is when the second lot is finished.

questions.q: What will Ingrid do right after the call?
options: Phone the warehouse about the dock slot
Ask finance to book an air shipment
Send Pavel the lot numbers
Tell the line manager about the delay
questions.explanation: Ingrid says she will call the warehouse right after this and send a written confirmation.

questions.q: Why does Pavel say the second lot only comes off the line on Thursday afternoon?
options: To apologise for a mistake in the order
To ask Ingrid for more time on the price
To explain why he turns down the air freight idea
To suggest a cheaper carrier for the second part
questions.explanation: He says it right after Ingrid offers air freight, so the point is that faster transport would not help because the goods are not ready.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Kenji, thanks for making the time. I'd like to start with your notice about the gasket component, because the standard lead time moves from eight weeks to ten.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, and I apologise for the short warning. Our upstream supplier has a long queue, so ten weeks is the realistic number from the next order.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Two extra weeks hurts. To keep the same service level, I need to know what it does to our safety stock. My rough guess is a quarter more.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That sounds about right to me. I'd double check it against your own demand variability, though, since you know your forecast errors better than I do.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I will. Before that, could you keep the eight weeks for the two orders we've already planned? That would give us a bridge.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I wish I could. If it were up to us, I'd say yes. But the delay starts further up the chain, and I'd be promising something someone else controls.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Understood, so you can't guarantee it even for those two orders. Then we'll plan with ten weeks across the board.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I think that's the safer approach. What I can do is send you a weekly update on the queue, so you see any improvement early.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That would help a lot. Could you start next week?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Of course. Shall we meet again to go through it? Maybe a short session at two o'clock next Tuesday.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Two o'clock works for me. I'll bring the new safety stock numbers so we can compare them with your figures.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Great. I'll update the lead time in our system today, and I'll copy you on the confirmation.

questions.q: What is the main topic of the meeting?
options: A price increase on the gasket component from the next order
A quality complaint about the most recent delivery of gaskets
A longer lead time and what it means for stock levels
A new delivery address for all of the open gasket orders
questions.explanation: Ana mentions the lead time moving from eight weeks to ten and asks about safety stock.

questions.q: Why does Kenji refuse to keep the eight-week lead time for the two planned orders?
options: The delay is caused by something further up the supply chain
His company wants to raise its prices before the next order
The two planned orders are too small to be prioritised
Ana's forecasts are not reliable enough to promise anything
questions.explanation: Kenji says the delay starts further up the chain and he would be promising something someone else controls.

questions.q: What will Ana bring to the meeting at two o'clock next Tuesday?
options: Kenji's weekly queue report
A signed contract for ten weeks
The upstream supplier's price list
Her new safety stock numbers
questions.explanation: Ana says she will bring the new safety stock numbers to compare with Kenji's figures.

title: A batch on hold, a deal

script.speaker: A
script.line: Tomas, I'm glad we're on voice now. The batch we flagged this morning is on hold while we investigate a deviation on the filling line.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Right, I saw your note. Can you give me the headline? How much stock is affected, and how long before somebody makes a call?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Two lots are caught up, roughly nine thousand units. The lab needs about ten days for a full root cause review, so the decision lands around the 5th of February.

script.speaker: B
script.line: The 5th is a problem. We have a customer commitment that week. Is there any chance of releasing the lot that's already packed?

script.speaker: A
script.line: I can't do that, I'm afraid. Until we know whether both lots were touched, releasing anything would be a gamble, and I won't put my signature behind that.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Fair point, I walked into that one. What if I asked you to bring the review forward instead? Even a few days would take the pressure off.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That I can work with. With a priority slot, the lab can report on Wednesday, a week earlier. But it costs another team its slot, so I'll need your support.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Done, I'll vouch for it with their manager. And in return I'll stop pushing for a partial release and pull stock from the second warehouse to cover the customer.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That works for me. Just make sure whoever books the transfer references the hold, so nobody ships from the wrong location by accident.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good call. I'll add a note in the system today and ask the warehouse to block those two lots physically too.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Thanks. I'll message you the minute the lab has anything, even if it's only preliminary, so you're not left guessing.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That would be great. Let's keep this thread open and talk again on Wednesday morning.

questions.q: What is the main outcome of the call?
options: The hold is cancelled after Tomas objects strongly to the delay
They agree on a faster lab review in exchange for no early release
Tomas agrees to cancel the customer commitment for that week
Mei hands the investigation over to another quality team
questions.explanation: Mei moves the sample to the priority queue and Tomas stops pushing for a partial release.

questions.q: Why does Mei refuse to release the packed lot straight away?
options: The packed lot has the wrong labels on the boxes
Nobody knows yet whether the problem affected both lots
The customer has not yet confirmed the order for it
The warehouse has no space left to store the lot
questions.explanation: Mei says that until they know whether the deviation touched both lots, releasing anything would be a gamble.

questions.q: What will Tomas do to cover the customer?
options: Ship the packed lot to the customer on Wednesday
Move the lab sample into the priority queue
Ask the customer to wait until the 5th of February
Take replacement stock from the second warehouse
questions.explanation: Tomas says he will pull stock from the second warehouse to cover the customer.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Mateo, have you read the announcement? Thirty percent of the roles in planning and distribution are changing, and nothing says who will own the monthly review.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I did, twice. Honestly, I'm more worried about my team. We schedule around twelve hundred batches a year, and nobody has told us whether that work moves to your group.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's my fear too. I'd like to email the director today and ask directly, since waiting only makes the rumours worse.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I'd hold back on that. Going over your manager's head right now could look aggressive, and she may not have the answers either. Could we ask her first?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Fine, I can live with that, as long as we don't wait for weeks. What if we send her one short list of questions this afternoon?

script.speaker: B
script.line: I'll keep it to four questions, and you add the reporting lines ones. She's on a call with the director at two o'clock, so she may have news later.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good timing. I'll write the draft now and send it to you in about an hour, so you can trim it before it goes out.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Perfect. If she hasn't replied by tomorrow, we can both agree to escalate. Talk soon.

questions.q: What is Mateo's team mainly worried about?
options: Whether their batch scheduling work will move to Dana's group
Losing thirty percent of their budget and their headcount
Being moved to report directly to the director of operations
Missing the two o'clock call between Dana and the manager
questions.explanation: Mateo says nobody has told them whether the work of scheduling twelve hundred batches moves to Dana's group.

questions.q: What will Dana do first?
options: Email the director today to ask about the new structure
Join the manager's call with the director at two o'clock
Write a draft list of questions and send it to Mateo
Cut the list down to four questions before it goes out
questions.explanation: Dana says she will write the draft now and send it to Mateo in about an hour.

questions.q: Why does Mateo say that going over the manager's head could look aggressive?
options: To criticise Dana's manager in front of the team
To suggest Dana should look for a different job
To persuade Dana not to contact the director yet
To explain who will own the monthly review now
questions.explanation: He says it just after Dana wants to email the director, and then suggests asking the manager first.

questions.q: What do the two colleagues agree to do?
options: Ask the manager first and escalate only if she does not reply
Wait quietly until the manager has spoken to the whole department
Both write to the director today and copy the manager in
Ask for a meeting with the director and the whole department
questions.explanation: Mateo says they will escalate only if the manager has not replied by tomorrow.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good morning, Pedro. About yesterday's problem with the inventory dashboard, I can confirm the numbers were about eight percent too high for most of Wednesday.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Thank you for the update. So the warehouse team miscounted the physical stock? I need to know whether we should plan a recount.

script.speaker: A
script.line: No, not at all, and I understand why you'd think that. The physical stock was correct. The mistake happened in the data load, where in-transit transfers were counted twice.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I see, so it was a reporting issue, not a stock issue. Why did the duplication happen only on Wednesday?

script.speaker: A
script.line: A new transfer file repeated the old lines, and our duplicate check missed it because the file name had changed. I've now added a rule based on content.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's reassuring. And what about the history? Several people exported the wrong figures, so I'd like to know whether those days have been corrected as well.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Yes, I've reloaded Wednesday's data and checked it against the warehouse system. Anyone who exported before noon yesterday should download the report again.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Understood, I'll let the planning team know today. Thank you for the quick fix and the clear explanation.

questions.q: What caused the wrong numbers on the dashboard?
options: The warehouse team made a mistake counting physical stock
A user deleted some stock records from the system by mistake
The dashboard was switched off for maintenance overnight
In-transit transfers were counted twice during the data load
questions.explanation: Yuki says the mistake happened in the data load, where in-transit transfers were counted twice.

questions.q: Why did Pedro first ask about a recount?
options: He had found some extra boxes in the warehouse
He thought the stock itself might have been wrong
Yuki had asked him to plan a recount for Wednesday
The dashboard had stopped working completely
questions.explanation: Pedro asks if the warehouse miscounted, and Yuki replies that the physical stock was correct.

questions.q: What can we infer about people who exported figures before noon yesterday?
options: They have to recount the stock in the whole warehouse
Their files have wrong numbers and need to be replaced
They will lose access to the dashboard for a few days
Their exports were corrected automatically overnight
questions.explanation: Yuki tells them to download the report again, which means the old exports are wrong.

title: Too much work at quarter close

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hi Camila, can you hear me okay? The connection seems shaky on my side. I wanted to talk about my workload during quarter close, if you have a minute.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I can hear you, just with some echo. Go ahead. Honestly, I've noticed you've been online late, so I'm glad you're bringing it up.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Thanks. The thing is, I'm working about eighteen percent more hours than normal, and I still can't finish the accruals review properly. Sorry, did that cut out?

script.speaker: B
script.line: You said eighteen percent more hours, and the accruals review. Yes, that's too much. Walk me through your main tasks and we'll see what can go.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Well, there's the weekly stock report, the reconciliation with the warehouse, and the supplier statements. The statements take the longest, and they're not urgent until after the close.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Then let's park the statements until the 22nd of November. And Nuno could take the weekly stock report, since he's done it before.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That would free up a lot of time. I'd keep the reconciliation, because I know the history behind the differences.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Agreed. Let's check in on how it's going. Are you free on Friday at ten, in the small meeting room?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Friday morning is difficult, I'm covering the front desk for the audit team until noon. Could we do it in the afternoon?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Sure, let's say three o'clock. Hmm, no, I'm with the auditors at three. How about four, in my office, away from this bad connection?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Four in your office is perfect. I'll prepare a short list of what I've handed over and what's still open.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Great. And thanks for speaking up early, Ibrahim. It's much easier to fix this now than in the middle of the close.

questions.q: Why does Ibrahim talk to Camila?
options: He wants to move to another department soon
He needs a new video tool for his meetings
He wants to report a problem with the auditors
He wants to reduce his workload during the close
questions.explanation: Ibrahim says he wants to talk about his workload during quarter close.

questions.q: Which task will Ibrahim keep?
options: The reconciliation with the warehouse
The weekly stock report
The supplier statements
The front desk cover
questions.explanation: He says he would keep the reconciliation because he knows the history behind the differences.

questions.q: When and where will they meet on Friday?
options: At ten in the small meeting room
At three o'clock with the auditors
At four o'clock in Camila's office
At noon at the front desk
questions.explanation: Camila suggests four in her office and Ibrahim says that is perfect.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Omar, thanks for coming down to the site. I have bad news. The container from the Vietnamese plant is held at customs because a certificate of origin is missing.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's unfortunate. How many orders does it affect? I need to know what to tell the customer team.

script.speaker: A
script.line: About one hundred and fifty orders are waiting for that stock. The good news is we hold twelve weeks of cover on the main items, so nothing is critical yet.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Okay, so we're not in a panic. What do you need from me? I could ask the supplier to send the document today.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Please do. I'll call our customs broker this afternoon to find out how long the release takes once the certificate arrives. They usually say three working days.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Understood. Actually, I just remembered something. The supplier's export manager is on leave until next week, so getting the stamp could be a problem.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Then that's a second issue. Let's find someone else at their end who can sign, and meet again tomorrow morning at nine to compare what we have.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good plan. I'll write to their sales contact now, and I'll bring whatever they answer to our meeting tomorrow.

questions.q: What is the main problem Emma describes?
options: A supplier has cancelled a hundred and fifty orders this week
The container was damaged during the journey to the site
A shipment is held at customs because a document is missing
The customs broker has raised its fees for this month
questions.explanation: Emma says the container is held at customs because a certificate of origin is missing.

questions.q: When will Emma and Omar meet again?
options: Tomorrow at nine in the morning
This afternoon
Next week
In three working days
questions.explanation: Emma suggests meeting again tomorrow morning at nine; the other times are the broker call, the manager's return and the release time.

questions.q: What will Omar do next?
options: Call the customs broker to ask about the release time
Tell the customers that their orders are cancelled
Sign the missing certificate himself to save time
Write to the supplier's sales contact about the stamp
questions.explanation: Omar says he will write to their sales contact now.

questions.q: Why does Omar mention that the export manager is on leave?
options: To explain why the container left the plant late
To point out a new difficulty with getting the document
To ask if he could take some time off himself
To suggest changing the supplier for future orders
questions.explanation: He says the manager is on leave until next week, so getting the stamp could be a problem.

title: A blocker in the supply plan

script.speaker: A
script.line: Do you have two minutes while we walk, Marta? I'm blocked on the weekly supply plan, and I'd rather tell you before the stand-up.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Sure, go ahead. What exactly is stuck?

script.speaker: A
script.line: The master-data update for the new pack sizes. Until the lead times are loaded, the plan can't calculate orders for about forty percent of the items on my list.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Forty percent is a lot. When was the update requested? I thought data services promised it for the 10th.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's what I said in my email, but I checked the ticket again, and it's actually the 11th of September. Sorry for the confusion.

script.speaker: B
script.line: No problem, so it's due today, not yesterday. Late, but not hugely. Can I do anything to unblock you?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Not really. I can't change the master data myself, because the agency doesn't give us write access, and that's the real reason I'm stuck.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Right. Here's a workaround. Run the plan using the old lead times for those items and add a manual buffer of one week. We can correct it after the update.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That could work, as long as the planners know the output is provisional. I'll mark the file clearly.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good idea. I'm going to chase data services myself this morning, and I'll message you as soon as the lead times are in.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Thanks, that helps. In the meantime I'll start with the items that aren't affected, so we don't lose the whole morning.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Perfect. And please mention it at stand-up, so nobody is surprised if the plan arrives a few hours late.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Will do. I'll keep it short and say you're working on the data update.

questions.q: Which date was the master-data update actually due?
options: The 10th of September
The 11th of September
The end of the month
Last Friday
questions.explanation: Tomas corrects himself and says the ticket shows the 11th of September.

questions.q: Why can't Tomas change the master data himself?
options: He does not know how to change that data
Marta has forbidden him from changing it
Data services is on holiday this week
His agency does not have write access
questions.explanation: Tomas says the agency doesn't give them write access, and that is the real reason he is stuck.

questions.q: What will Marta do this morning?
options: Follow up with data services about the lead times
Run the plan using the old lead times for now
Mark the file as provisional for the planners
Start with the items that are not affected
questions.explanation: Marta says she will chase data services herself this morning.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Henrik, thanks for seeing me. I need your approval for an urgent order of sixty pallets of cartons, and the supplier needs an answer by half past four today.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Okay. First, which cost centre is this going against, and what's the justification? Urgent orders always make me nervous.

script.speaker: A
script.line: It goes against the packaging line, in the operations budget. The justification is that we're running low, and the regular order won't arrive until next month.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Hmm, I'm not convinced it's that urgent. The supplier charges an eight percent premium for rush orders, and last quarter we ended up with too many cartons.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I understand the concern, but this time it's different. Last quarter's forecast was too high. This month, packing orders have been above plan every week.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Can you show me that? I'd like to see numbers, not just a feeling.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Of course. Here, on my laptop. Current stock is eleven days of cover, and weekly usage has gone up from forty to fifty-five pallets since the start of the month.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Hold on. So at this rate you'd run out in about a week and a half, before the regular order arrives. That changes things.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Exactly. The extra eight percent is cheaper than stopping the line for even one shift.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Fair enough, the data supports you. I'll approve it now, but please add the usage chart to the request, so finance has the evidence.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I'll attach it right away and email the supplier as soon as the system shows your approval.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good. And next time, send me the numbers first, so we don't need a debate in the meeting room.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of the meeting?
options: To complain about the supplier's high prices
To plan the forecast for next quarter
To get approval for a rush purchase of cartons
To move a cost centre to another budget
questions.explanation: Sara asks for approval of an urgent purchase order of printed cartons.

questions.q: What convinces Henrik to approve the order?
options: A bigger discount offered by the supplier for rush orders
The large number of cartons left over from last quarter
Rising weekly usage compared with the stock that is left
A phone call from the production manager that morning
questions.explanation: Sara shows stock of eleven days of cover and usage rising from forty to fifty-five pallets, so Henrik says the data supports her.

questions.q: What will Sara do after the meeting?
options: Attach the usage chart and then contact the supplier
Wait until the regular order arrives next month
Ask finance for a different cost centre code
Rewrite the forecast for the next quarter
questions.explanation: Sara says she will attach the chart right away and email the supplier once the approval shows.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Victor, thanks for joining. My macro for the weekly allocation file stopped working after the update, and I have to send the report by half past four today.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Okay, let's see. When you say the update, do you mean the Windows update from last night? Some people have had problems with that.

script.speaker: A
script.line: No, no, not that one. I mean the update to the planning tool on Monday. Since then, the export has a different column order.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Ah, I misunderstood, sorry. So the macro itself hasn't changed, but the file it reads has a new layout. That makes more sense.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Exactly. And it isn't failing completely. It breaks on about fifteen percent of the rows, which is almost worse, because the errors are hard to spot.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, partial failures are tricky. For now, here's a temporary workaround: export the data in the old format from the tool's settings, and the macro should run as before.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Okay, but I don't want to depend on that for long. Can your team actually fix the macro for the new layout?

script.speaker: B
script.line: That needs the development team, so I'm escalating it to them now as a priority ticket. I'd say they will look at it tomorrow morning.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Tomorrow is fine, as long as today's report goes out. Could you stay with me while I try the old export?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Of course. Share your screen and I'll watch each step. If the numbers look odd, we'll stop and check straight away.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Thanks, that's reassuring. Right, I'm sharing now. Can you see the settings menu?

questions.q: What problem does Olivia report?
options: Her computer will not install the latest Windows update
A report went to the wrong people by mistake yesterday
The planning tool has become far too slow to use
A macro fails because the exported file has changed layout
questions.explanation: Olivia explains the planning tool update on Monday changed the column order in the export.

questions.q: By what time must Olivia send her report today?
options: Tomorrow morning
Half past four
On Monday
Last night
questions.explanation: She says she has to send the report by half past four today; the other times are the developers' review, the tool update and the Windows update.

questions.q: Why does Victor apologise?
options: He forgot to open a ticket for her problem
He wrongly thought she meant a Windows update
He broke the macro himself with a change
He was late to the call because of a meeting
questions.explanation: Victor first asks about the Windows update, then says he misunderstood when Olivia means the planning tool update.

questions.q: What will Victor do now?
options: Fix the macro himself before the end of today
Install the latest Windows update on her laptop
Send her an old version of the exported file
Watch her screen as she tries the old export
questions.explanation: Victor agrees to watch each step while she shares her screen.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Lukas, thanks for jumping on voice. About the Friday call: half past four your time is ten thirty for me, but I know it's late for your team.

script.speaker: B
script.line: It is a bit late, especially on a Friday, when half the team wants to leave early. But we've never found a better slot.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I checked both calendars. A call at eight in the morning for me would be two in the afternoon for you, and nobody has a conflict then.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's early for you, though. What if we rotate? One week at half past four, the next week at the early slot, so we share the inconvenience.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I like that. Every second Friday I get up early, and every other Friday you finish late. It's fair, and easy to remember.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Before we lock it in, I have good news. Our new planner in Singapore starts Monday, and my manager wants her on this call regularly.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's great. Does she mind the late slot?

script.speaker: B
script.line: She told me she prefers it, because she has a long commute and likes starting late. So she could take the late call on her own.

script.speaker: A
script.line: In that case, we may not need to rotate every week. You and I take the early slot, and she covers the late one when needed.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, let's try that for a month and review it. I'll send a new series of invitations today.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Perfect. Please put the agenda link in the invite, so she can prepare.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Will do. I'll also introduce her to you by chat on Monday morning.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Lovely. Welcome her from me, and tell her not to worry about the first call.

questions.q: What are Chloe and Lukas trying to do?
options: Find a meeting time that is fair for both regions
Cancel the Friday call and use email instead
Write a new agenda for the regional team
Hire another planner for the Singapore office
questions.explanation: Chloe wants to change the Friday call because the current time is late for Lukas's team.

questions.q: At what time does the current Friday call take place for Lukas?
options: Eight in the morning
Two in the afternoon
Half past four
Ten thirty
questions.explanation: Chloe says half past four your time; eight and two are the proposed early slot, and ten thirty is her own time.

questions.q: What can we infer about the new planner?
options: She already joined the team last week
She will replace Chloe on the call
She is willing to attend the late calls
She prefers the early slot
questions.explanation: Lukas says she prefers the late slot because of her commute, so she could take that call.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hannah, the stock count from Monday the 22nd of April shows one item off by two hundred units. The system says six hundred, the counters found four hundred.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's a big gap. My first thought is a transfer from the second warehouse that nobody booked. I saw a truck unload for that item last week.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Possible, but I checked, and the transfer was booked on the 18th. So the second idea is a wrong location. The pallet could be sitting in the overflow area.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's more likely. The overflow rack isn't on the counters' list, so they would have missed it. Should I ask someone to look there?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Yes, please, and then we recount the whole aisle on Thursday morning, not just that location, so we can be sure.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Fine. One more small thing, though. The scanner in aisle four keeps freezing, so the recount may take longer than usual.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good to know. I'll ask maintenance to replace it before Thursday, and I'll tell you by tomorrow whether that's possible.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Thanks. Meanwhile I'll walk to the overflow rack this afternoon and send you photos of whatever I find.

questions.q: What are Pedro and Hannah trying to find out?
options: Why the physical stock does not match the system
Why a transfer was cancelled at the second site
Which scanner in the warehouse needs replacing now
When the truck from the second site arrived
questions.explanation: Pedro says the system shows six hundred but the counters found four hundred, and they look for causes.

questions.q: When will the aisle be recounted?
options: Monday the 22nd
The 18th
This afternoon
Thursday morning
questions.explanation: Pedro says they recount the whole aisle on Thursday morning; the other times are the first count, the transfer date and Hannah's walk.

questions.q: Why would the counters have missed the pallet?
options: The scanner froze during the count
The overflow rack was not on their list
The transfer was never booked
They counted the wrong item
questions.explanation: Hannah says the overflow rack isn't on the counters' list, so they would have missed it.

questions.q: What will Pedro do about the scanner?
options: Walk to the overflow rack this afternoon
Ask maintenance to replace it before Thursday
Send Hannah photos of the missing pallets
Recount the whole aisle by himself on Thursday
questions.explanation: Pedro says he will ask maintenance to replace it before Thursday and tell Hannah by tomorrow.

title: A truck with a warm reading

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hello Hugo. I have a problem with the shipment from the warehouse in Spain. The truck had a temperature excursion on the way.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Oh no. How serious is it? Please tell me exactly what you know.

script.speaker: A
script.line: The driver called me this morning. He said the cooling unit stopped for a while. I have not seen the report yet.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I need the data logger report first. Without it, I cannot say if the goods are safe. How many batches are in this truck?

script.speaker: A
script.line: There are one hundred and twenty batches. I am sorry, Hugo. I know this is a bad situation.

script.speaker: B
script.line: It is not your fault, but I am a little worried. Please ask the carrier for the report as soon as you can.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I already asked. The carrier's quality manager has the file, but she is on a flight until eleven o'clock.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Then I cannot make a decision now. I need to see her file first. Please keep the truck closed and do not unload anything.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Okay. One thing from the driver: he said twenty-five percent of the loggers show a high number, but he is not sure.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That could mean a lot or a little. I do not want to guess. Please do not tell the warehouse team to use the goods.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Understood. I will call the carrier again after eleven o'clock and send you the report immediately.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Thank you. After I read it, I will tell you if we can use the goods or if we need extra tests.

questions.q: What is the main problem in this conversation?
options: The truck arrived late and missed its delivery slot
Some batches were missing when the truck was checked
The warehouse in Spain has no space for the goods
A truck's cooling stopped, so the goods may not be safe
questions.explanation: Lucia says the truck had a temperature excursion because the cooling unit stopped.

questions.q: Why can Hugo not decide now?
options: He has not seen the data logger report
The warehouse team is on holiday this week
The driver is not at work until tomorrow
Lucia has not yet called the carrier at all
questions.explanation: Hugo says he needs the data logger report first, and the carrier's manager is on a flight.

questions.q: How does Hugo feel about the situation?
options: Angry, because Lucia ignored a warning
Relaxed, because the problem is small
Concerned, but he does not blame Lucia
Bored, because it happens every week
questions.explanation: Hugo says 'It is not your fault, but I am a little worried.'

questions.q: What will probably happen to the goods before the report arrives?
options: They will be used by the team straight away
They will be sent back to the warehouse in Spain
They will stay in the closed truck, unused
They will be moved into a cold room at once
questions.explanation: Hugo asks Lucia to keep the truck closed and not to unload anything.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Daniel, I got your message, and I understand why you're upset. You've asked for updates on the delayed orders, and I've sent them late for four weeks now.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Exactly. I have customers calling me every day. Thirty percent of my key accounts have asked where their stock is, and I don't have an answer.

script.speaker: A
script.line: You're right, and I'm sorry. The data arrives on Friday evening, so I could only write the update on Monday afternoon. That's no excuse, but it's the cause.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Fine, but I need something I can rely on. What's going to change?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Starting on the 12th of January, no, sorry, the 19th, I'll send a short update every Monday before ten, with each order, its status and its new date.

script.speaker: B
script.line: The 19th is two weeks away. Can't you start sooner? A call tomorrow, maybe, to cover the worst cases?

script.speaker: A
script.line: I can do that. I'll call you tomorrow morning about the late orders, and the written routine starts on the 19th. After four weeks we can review it.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Okay, that sounds fair. Thanks for staying calm about this. I'll tell my team to expect your call.

questions.q: Why is Daniel unhappy?
options: Updates on delayed orders keep arriving late
Customers have cancelled many of their orders
Priya refused to take his calls this week
His team has been reduced to just two people
questions.explanation: Priya admits she has sent the updates late for four weeks.

questions.q: When will the new weekly updates begin?
options: The 12th of January
Tomorrow morning
After four weeks
The 19th of January
questions.explanation: Priya corrects herself from the 12th to the 19th.

questions.q: What will Priya do tomorrow morning?
options: Send the first weekly list of orders
Phone Daniel about the late orders
Review the new routine with Daniel
Visit his key accounts in person
questions.explanation: Priya says she will call Daniel tomorrow morning about the late orders.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Andrew, let's look at our on-time and in-full numbers. This month we are at ninety-one percent, and our target is ninety-five. I need to understand what happened.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, I saw it. The main reason is two late shipments to the same customer. Those two orders were about twenty-five percent of that customer's monthly volume.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Why were they late? Was it the carrier or something on our side?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Both, to be honest. The first one waited three days for a missing document, and the second one missed its truck because the packing finished late.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Okay. So what do we do about it? I don't want to see this again next month.

script.speaker: B
script.line: First, I will make a checklist for documents, so nothing is missing before the truck arrives. I can finish it by next Wednesday.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good. And for the packing delays?

script.speaker: B
script.line: That is the warehouse manager's job. I will ask him to pack urgent orders earlier. The carrier contract changes in six weeks, so we can ask for a backup truck.

script.speaker: A
script.line: You do the checklist by Wednesday and talk to the warehouse manager this week. I will speak to the carrier about a backup truck before the month ends.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Agreed. I will send you a short summary of these actions this afternoon, so we both have it in writing.

questions.q: How much of the customer's monthly volume did the two late orders represent?
options: Ninety-one percent
Twenty-five percent
Ninety-five percent
Six percent
questions.explanation: Andrew says those two orders were about twenty-five percent of that customer's monthly volume.

questions.q: Why was the second shipment late?
options: A document was missing for three days
The carrier cancelled its truck that day
The customer changed the order quantity
Packing finished too late for the truck
questions.explanation: Andrew says the second one missed its truck because the packing finished late.

questions.q: Who will talk to the carrier about a backup truck?
options: Camila, before the end of the month
Andrew, by next Wednesday at the latest
The warehouse manager, later this week
The customer's buyer, this afternoon
questions.explanation: Camila says she will speak to the carrier before the end of the month.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Welcome, Mateo. Let me explain which systems you need. There are three: the planning tool, the shared drive and the ticketing system. Which one worries you most?

script.speaker: B
script.line: The planning tool, I think. I used a different one before, and my manager wants me to check an order of six hundred cartons this week.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Don't worry. First, request access to the planning tool in the ticketing system. The licence can take up to four weeks, so ask today.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Four weeks? That's a long time. How can I check the order without it?

script.speaker: A
script.line: You can ask me for a screen export for now. Or use the training version, which has the same screens but old data. I'll send you the link.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Okay, thank you. I'm a bit nervous, but that helps. Oh, and I can't see the planning folder on the shared drive. It says I have no permission.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hmm, that's strange. It should have been set up on your first day. I'll message the helpdesk now, and let's check the folder again tomorrow morning.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Great. If it still doesn't work, I'll add it to the same ticket so nothing gets lost.

questions.q: What is the conversation mainly about?
options: How to count cartons in the warehouse correctly
A complaint about the speed of the helpdesk
Which systems Mateo needs and what to request first
How to prepare for an English placement test
questions.explanation: Dana lists three systems and tells Mateo to request planning tool access first.

questions.q: How long can the planning tool access take?
options: Until tomorrow morning
About one day
Up to four weeks
A few hours
questions.explanation: Dana says the licence can take up to four weeks.

questions.q: How does Mateo feel at the start of the conversation?
options: Worried about the planning tool
Confident about all three systems
Angry with his manager
Bored by the explanation
questions.explanation: He says the planning tool worries him most, and later he says he is a bit nervous.

questions.q: What can we infer about the shared drive problem?
options: The folder was deleted by mistake last week
Mateo has to pay extra to get that access
Dana does not have access to it either
Mateo's access was not set up as expected
questions.explanation: Dana says it should have been set up on his first day.

title: Chairing a call for the first time

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hello, Yuki. This is Lukas. It is my first time chairing this call, so please help me if I forget something.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good morning, Lukas. Of course. I am happy to help. We have everyone from supply and sales on the line.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Thank you. I plan to start with the stock report, then the delayed order, and then the open actions. Is that order okay for you?

script.speaker: B
script.line: I think the delayed order should come first. It is the most urgent one, and the sales team has to leave early.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good point. We will do the delayed order first. It is about one hundred and twenty cartons that are still in the warehouse.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, and the customer is asking for them every day. We should finish that topic quickly.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I also have to say that I have a hard stop. I need to leave at eleven o'clock for another meeting, so please keep your answers short.

script.speaker: B
script.line: No problem. If we run out of time, we can continue in a short follow-up meeting. Shall we do it on Monday?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Monday is difficult, because I will be at the plant all day. Could we try Tuesday?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Tuesday is not good for me. I have a training course. What about the 29th of October?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Yes, the 29th works. Wait, I think the meeting room is already booked, so let's do it by phone again.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That is fine with me. A phone call is easier for the people who work from home.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good. I will send the invitation today. Let's begin.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, I think everyone is here. Please go ahead, Lukas. You are doing well.

questions.q: What is Lukas doing at the start of the call?
options: Cancelling the meeting for lack of time
Opening the call and setting the agenda order
Reporting a serious stock problem to sales
Giving a training course to the sales team
questions.explanation: Lukas explains his plan for the agenda and Yuki suggests a change.

questions.q: Which topic will be discussed first?
options: The report on current stock
The delayed order of cartons
The list of open actions
The training course plan
questions.explanation: Lukas agrees that the delayed order will come first because it is the most urgent.

questions.q: Why does Lukas ask people to keep their answers short?
options: The sales team arrives late to the call
The meeting room is already booked
Yuki has a training course on Tuesday
He must leave for another meeting at eleven
questions.explanation: Lukas says he has a hard stop at eleven o'clock for another meeting.

questions.q: How will the follow-up meeting probably be held?
options: By phone, on the 29th of October
In the meeting room on Monday
At the plant on Tuesday morning
In the training room after lunch
questions.explanation: They agree on the 29th and, because the room is booked, to do it by phone.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hi Jon. I have some news about the forecast, and it is not good. I wanted to tell you before the meeting tomorrow.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Okay, tell me. What exactly happened there?

script.speaker: A
script.line: A competitor started selling a similar product in our main market. So we expect demand to be about fifteen percent lower for the next quarter.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Fifteen percent! That is a lot. And we already placed orders with the supplier for the full amount.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I know. That is why I am calling. What can we do about the orders that are already placed?

script.speaker: B
script.line: I'm not sure. Most are confirmed, and the supplier needs three weeks to change a quantity. I have four hundred and fifty order lines open. I'm a bit overwhelmed.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hey, take a breath. It is not a disaster. We have time, and we can fix this step by step.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Thanks, but I have to update the plan, call the supplier and tell the warehouse. It is too much before nine o'clock tomorrow.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Then let me take one thing. I will check with the customers which orders are really firm, and I will send you the list this afternoon.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That would help a lot. Then I can see which of the four hundred and fifty lines we can reduce.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Exactly. You focus on the supplier and the plan. We will talk again at nine tomorrow, before the big meeting.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Okay. I feel better now. I will call the supplier this afternoon and ask what is possible.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good. And remember, nobody expects a perfect solution on the first day.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Thank you, Katarina. See you tomorrow at nine.

questions.q: Why will demand be lower?
options: The company raised its prices this quarter
A big customer cancelled its yearly contract
A competitor began selling a similar product there
The supplier delivered several weeks late
questions.explanation: Katarina says a competitor started selling a similar product in their main market.

questions.q: Why does Katarina offer to check with the customers?
options: Because the supplier asked her to
Because she wants to cancel all orders
To help Jon, who has too much to do
Because customers called her yesterday
questions.explanation: Jon says it is too much work, and Katarina answers 'Then let me take one thing.'

questions.q: What is the most likely goal of the list Katarina will send?
options: To show which order lines can be reduced
To find new customers for the product
To thank the supplier for the delay
To raise the forecast for next quarter
questions.explanation: Jon says the list will help him see which of the four hundred and fifty lines he can reduce.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Pedro, thanks for walking with me. Before I leave for two weeks, let's go through what's open. The most urgent one is the supplier forecast, due on Thursday morning.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Okay. So I send it on Thursday, and you're back on the 14th?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Not exactly, no. I leave on the 14th of January, that's Thursday evening, so I'll be away for two weeks. I'm back at the end of the month.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Ah, sorry, I mixed that up. So the forecast is due before you go?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Yes, that's what I meant. I'll finish most of it today, but I need you to check the final numbers and send it, because I'll be getting ready to travel.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Fine. Where are the files? I don't want to search the shared drive while you're gone.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Everything is in the folder called holiday handover, with a note for each item. The ones that can wait are marked in grey, so you can ignore them for now.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good. And if something goes wrong with the supplier, who should I call?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Call Hannah in logistics first. She knows the contract, and she can decide small things without me. Only message me if it's really serious.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Understood. I'll look at the folder this afternoon, and then I'll send you a short email tomorrow so you know I've got everything.

questions.q: What must be done on Thursday morning?
options: Search the shared drive for files
Call Hannah in logistics
Come back from holiday
Send the supplier forecast
questions.explanation: Yuki says the supplier forecast is due on Thursday morning.

questions.q: Why does Pedro say 'Sorry, I mixed that up'?
options: He thought Yuki was returning on the 14th, not leaving
He forgot where the handover folder was saved
He thought the forecast was due a week earlier
He had mixed up Hannah with someone else
questions.explanation: Pedro asks if she is back on the 14th, and Yuki says she leaves on the 14th of January.

questions.q: What will Pedro do tomorrow?
options: Call Hannah about the supplier contract
Finish the forecast himself tomorrow morning
Send Yuki an email to confirm he has everything
Message Yuki if something serious happens
questions.explanation: Pedro says he will send a short email tomorrow so Yuki knows he has everything.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Samuel, do you have a minute? I wanted to explain how we handle allocation this month, before you see the numbers in the system.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Sure. I saw the email. We asked for four thousand units for the market, and my sales team is already worried.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Yes, and I'm sorry. Supply is limited this month, so we can only give you twelve percent less than you requested. Other markets have urgent orders too.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Okay, I understand the logic. Can we look at it again when more stock arrives? Let's meet on the 29th of October at two o'clock.

script.speaker: A
script.line: The 29th is good, but two o'clock isn't. I have a supplier review. Could we do ten in the morning?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Ten is too early, I'm travelling. How about half past eleven? That's the best I can do.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Half past eleven is fine. I'll book a room. Please bring the figures for your open orders.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Will do. Thanks for explaining it before I saw the system.

questions.q: What is the conversation mainly about?
options: Cancelling a large order for the whole market
Training the sales team to use the new system
Explaining a smaller allocation and setting a meeting
Choosing a new supplier for the second half of the year
questions.explanation: Claire explains the twelve percent cut in allocation and they set a meeting.

questions.q: What time will they meet on the 29th of October?
options: Half past eleven
Two o'clock
Ten in the morning
Half past one
questions.explanation: After two other times are refused, they agree on half past eleven.

questions.q: What will Samuel bring to the meeting?
options: A list of the other markets
A new stock count
The supplier review
The figures for his open orders
questions.explanation: Claire asks him to bring the figures for his open orders.

questions.q: Why does Claire say 'Other markets have urgent orders too'?
options: To ask Samuel for help with the other markets
To justify why Samuel's market gets less stock
To say that the supplier delivered stock late
To suggest moving stock from one market to another
questions.explanation: She says it right after announcing the twelve percent reduction, as the reason for it.

title: A firm date for an urgent order

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hi Emma. I need a firm delivery date for the urgent order from our biggest customer. They keep asking me every hour.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Okay. Let's check the three parts: production, transport and customs. Production first. The goods are ready today.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Great. So can I tell the customer Thursday?

script.speaker: B
script.line: I'd rather not say Thursday. Last time the same route had a delay at the border, and I don't want to promise something we can't keep.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I see. So transport is the risk. What can we do?

script.speaker: B
script.line: There is an express truck. It costs about eight percent more, but it goes directly. With it, we can deliver by Friday morning.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Friday is fine for the customer. Is that really a firm date?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, if the customs papers are ready by tomorrow. I'll send them to the broker this afternoon.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Perfect. Then I'll confirm Friday to the customer and add a note to the order.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good. Please send me the customer's address again, in case the driver needs a phone number.

questions.q: When can the goods arrive if the express truck is used?
options: Thursday
Friday morning
This afternoon
Tomorrow evening
questions.explanation: Emma says that with the express truck, they can deliver by Friday morning.

questions.q: What will Emma do this afternoon?
options: Phone the customer to confirm the date
Add a note about Friday to the order
Book a driver for the express truck
Send the customs papers to the broker
questions.explanation: Emma says she will send the papers to the broker this afternoon.

questions.q: Why does Emma say she would rather not say Thursday?
options: She worries a border delay could break the promise
Production will not be ready until Friday
The customer does not want delivery on Thursday
She wants to use a cheaper truck than usual
questions.explanation: She says the same route had a delay at the border last time and she doesn't want to promise something they can't keep.

questions.q: What do they decide?
options: To wait for the customs office to call back
To ship on Thursday using the normal route
To offer the customer Friday using an express truck
To cancel the urgent order and start again
questions.explanation: They agree on Friday delivery with the express truck, and Mark will confirm it.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hello Mei, this is Kenji, the safety officer. Thanks for taking my call. I'd like to explain the rules for your visit on Monday, the 22nd of March.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Hi Kenji, thanks for calling. Yes, please. I've never been to a production site, so I want to do everything right.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good. First, collect a visitor badge at reception and wear it all the time. Please bring a photo identity card too.

script.speaker: B
script.line: No problem. What about clothes? Do I need anything special?

script.speaker: A
script.line: In the production area you need a helmet, safety glasses and safety shoes. We lend the helmet and glasses, but the shoes must be your own or borrowed here.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I don't have safety shoes, and my size is small, so maybe you don't have any. Could I just wear normal shoes?

script.speaker: A
script.line: I'm sorry, that's not possible in the production hall. But if we can't find your size, you can watch the line from the viewing gallery in normal shoes.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Okay, that's fair. I'd prefer to walk through, but I accept it. Also, I planned to arrive at eleven. Is that fine?

script.speaker: A
script.line: The tour starts at eleven, but the safety induction takes thirty minutes. Could you arrive at half past ten?

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's early because of my flight, but all right, if the tour starts exactly at eleven, with no waiting.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Agreed. One more thing: please stay on the green walking lines, and never cross the yellow ones without a guide.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Understood. And what happens if the alarm sounds while I'm there?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Stay calm, follow your guide to the assembly point in the car park, and wait until we count everybody.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Got it. Thanks, Kenji, I feel better now. See you Monday.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of the call?
options: To cancel Mei's visit for safety reasons
To book a flight and hotel for Mei
To explain safety rules before a site visit
To report an accident at the plant last week
questions.explanation: Kenji says he wants to explain the rules for her visit.

questions.q: What time will the tour start?
options: At eleven o'clock
At half past ten
Thirty minutes after eleven
At ten
questions.explanation: Kenji says the tour starts at eleven and he agrees to start exactly then; half past ten is the induction.

questions.q: What will probably happen if Mei finds no safety shoes in her size?
options: She will walk through the hall in normal shoes
The visit will be cancelled for safety reasons
She will go in wearing only a helmet and glasses
She will watch the line from the gallery
questions.explanation: Kenji says that if they can't find her size, she can watch from the viewing gallery.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hello Sofia, it's Victor from the audio-visual team. I'm in the meeting room now, testing the screen and microphone. Can you hear me clearly?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Hi Victor. I can hear you, but your voice is very quiet. And there's a little echo.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Okay, that's helpful. The microphone is only at thirty percent, so I'll raise it. Is that better?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Much better, thank you. The echo is gone. Can you move the camera? I can only see the ceiling and half of the table.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Sure. I'm tilting it down now. Do you see the whole table?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, perfect. But the screen share is blurry. I can't read the numbers on the slide.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That could be the resolution. I'll change it, and I'll write the settings in the room log, so the next team can repeat them.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good idea. I'm a bit worried about the real meeting, because the directors' team joins us at a quarter to four. We can't have problems then.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I understand. I'll fix the resolution and send you a test link by noon. You test it on your laptop and tell me by two o'clock.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Agreed. And I'll ask the organiser to open the room at half past three, so you can do a last check before the meeting.

questions.q: When does the real meeting start?
options: At half past three
At a quarter to four
At two o'clock
At noon
questions.explanation: Sofia says the directors' team joins at a quarter to four; the other times are the room opening, her test deadline and the link.

questions.q: How does Sofia feel about the real meeting?
options: Completely relaxed about the whole thing
A little worried about the technology
Angry with the organiser of the meeting
Excited about meeting the directors
questions.explanation: She says she is a bit worried and that they can't have problems then.

questions.q: What will Victor do by noon?
options: Test the link from his own laptop at home
Open the meeting room for the directors' team
Raise the microphone volume to full
Fix the resolution and send a test link
questions.explanation: Victor says he will fix the resolution and send a test link by noon.

title: A forecast jump and a tender

script.speaker: A
script.line: Chloe, quick question about the forecast. For one product, month three jumps by thirty percent compared to month two. I need to understand it before I order materials.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, I expected your call. That jump comes from a tender. If we win, the customer will buy for twelve weeks starting in month three.

script.speaker: A
script.line: And have we won it? Because I can't build twelve weeks of extra stock based on a maybe.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Not yet. The decision comes on Wednesday, and I'd say our chances are good, but it's not confirmed.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Could you tell me who the customer is, or how the volumes were calculated? Then I could judge the risk myself.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I'd like to help, Mateo, but I can't go into that. Let's just say the people involved asked us to keep the details inside a very small group.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Understood, that makes sense. Then what do you suggest? Should I wait, or place a partial order for long-lead materials?

script.speaker: B
script.line: I'd wait for Wednesday. I'll call you right after the committee meets, probably around a quarter to four, and then you'll know.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Fine. I'll prepare both scenarios, so I can react the same afternoon.

questions.q: What is the jump in month three based on?
options: A tender that has not been decided yet
A price cut for existing customers
A new factory opening in month three
A correction of the old sales figures
questions.explanation: Chloe says the jump comes from a tender and the decision is not confirmed.

questions.q: Why won't Chloe tell Mateo who the customer is?
options: She does not actually know who the customer is
She thinks the forecast is probably wrong
The details must stay within a small group
She is too busy to explain it before Wednesday
questions.explanation: Chloe says the people involved asked them to keep the details inside a very small group.

questions.q: What will Mateo do before Wednesday?
options: Order materials for twelve weeks at once
Call the customer to ask about the tender
Prepare plans for both possible outcomes
Place a partial order for long-lead items
questions.explanation: Mateo says he will prepare both scenarios so he can react the same afternoon.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Arjun, thanks for taking the time before you leave. I'm worried about taking over the weekly report, so could we go through the whole process step by step?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Of course. It's simpler than it looks. Every Thursday evening, the planning leads upload their files to the shared folder, and on Friday you merge them into the master workbook.

script.speaker: A
script.line: And what's the deadline for sending it out?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Friday at a quarter past ten. Leadership reads it before their weekly call, so even five minutes late gets noticed.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Got it. Are there common errors I should watch for?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Two come to mind. Some leads forget to update the currency column, and one file always arrives with hidden rows. If the totals look too round, check those first.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Useful. Now, my real request: could you stay on for the first two reports? Your contract ends this week, but the 19th of November would be safer for me.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I'd love to, but my next project starts on Monday and I've already signed. I can record a video and join a thirty minute call on your first Friday.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's a good alternative, thank you. Could we do the call at nine, before the deadline pressure starts?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Nine works. And if something goes wrong later, ask Li in finance. She built half of the workbook and she answers quickly.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Perfect. I'll write the steps down as I watch the video and share the notes with you for a check.

questions.q: What does Sofia ask Arjun to do?
options: Help her learn the process and stay longer
Write the next weekly report for her instead
Introduce her to the leadership team
Fix the errors in the master workbook for her
questions.explanation: Sofia asks for a full walkthrough and also asks if he could stay on for the first two reports.

questions.q: By what time must the report be sent on Friday?
options: Nine in the morning
Thursday evening
Monday morning
A quarter past ten
questions.explanation: Arjun says the deadline is Friday at a quarter past ten; nine is the call time and Thursday evening is when files arrive.

questions.q: Why can Arjun not stay until the 19th of November?
options: Leadership refused to extend his contract
He has already signed for another project
He is going on a long holiday next week
Sofia does not really need his help
questions.explanation: He says his next project starts on Monday and he has already signed.

questions.q: What will Arjun do for Sofia?
options: Extend his contract until the 19th of November
Record a video and join one call on Friday
Fix the workbook before leaving the company
Ask Li to write the first report for her
questions.explanation: Arjun offers a screen video and a thirty minute call on her first Friday.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Rachel, thanks for coming. You seemed quiet in yesterday's meeting, and I wanted to check in. Is everything all right?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Thank you for asking, Omar. To be honest, I get nervous speaking English in big meetings. I understand everything, but when I have to answer quickly, my mind goes blank.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's very common, and your English is good. It's the speed and the audience that make it hard. Would some practical tips help?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, please. Anything would be welcome.

script.speaker: A
script.line: First, send your notes to the chair before the meeting. Then people already know what you'll say, and there's less pressure.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I can do that. It's like having a safety net.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Second, try to ask one question in every meeting. It can be a simple one, just to warm up your voice.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Hmm, one question every time sounds difficult. Could I start with every second meeting? I'd feel more comfortable.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Fine, a compromise. Every second meeting, but in return, present the update on the three hundred delayed cartons on the 22nd of September. Just that part.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's a deal. I'll write the script and practise it with you beforehand, if you have time.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Of course. Let's rehearse on Friday afternoon, and I can also arrange a short English course for you if you'd like.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That would be great. Thank you for being so supportive.

questions.q: What is the main topic of the conversation?
options: How to reduce the delays on the carton orders
Why Rachel was late to the previous meeting
How to write clearer reports for the director
How Rachel can speak English more confidently
questions.explanation: Rachel admits she is nervous speaking English and Omar gives tips.

questions.q: What will Rachel present at the meeting on the 22nd of September?
options: The update on the delayed cartons
The results of her English course
The whole quarterly report
A question about meeting rules
questions.explanation: Omar asks her to present the update on the three hundred delayed cartons, just that part.

questions.q: What will Omar and Rachel do on Friday afternoon?
options: Start the new English course
Send her notes to the chair
Rehearse her presentation together
Hold the meeting with the director
questions.explanation: Omar says 'Let's rehearse on Friday afternoon.'

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hello Marco, this is Leila from the travel desk. I got your chat message about the train booking. How can I help?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Hi Leila. The supplier meeting on the 11th of March has moved to the afternoon, so I need a later train. It's about the one hundred and fifty units.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Okay. So you want to change the outward journey, the one that arrives before nine?

script.speaker: B
script.line: No, no, the outward train is fine. I meant the return. The current one leaves at half past two, which is too early now.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Ah, I see. I misunderstood, sorry. The return train, then. There's a change fee of twelve euros, since your ticket is the flexible type, not the cheapest one.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Twelve euros is fine. What other times are there?

script.speaker: A
script.line: There's one at twenty past four, but it's tight if the meeting goes on until four. The next one leaves at five past six, and it has plenty of seats.

script.speaker: B
script.line: How long is the meeting? I think it ends around four, but with suppliers it often runs over. Better take the later one.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That sounds wise. I'll change it to five past six and send you the new ticket in a few minutes.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Great. Will I be charged once, or per ticket?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Only once, because it's a single booking. You'll see the change on your next expense report.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Perfect, thanks. Have a nice day.

questions.q: What does Marco want?
options: To cancel the supplier meeting on the 11th
To book a cheaper train for the outward trip
To change his return train to a later one
To change the room for the supplier meeting
questions.explanation: Marco says the meeting moved to the afternoon, so he needs a later train, and he means the return.

questions.q: Which train does Leila book?
options: The one at five past six
The one at half past two
The one at twenty past four
The one before nine
questions.explanation: Leila agrees to change it to five past six.

questions.q: What can we infer about Marco's choice of the later train?
options: He wants to avoid paying a higher fee
He plans to visit another supplier later
He doesn't like travelling on early trains
He thinks the meeting may run over
questions.explanation: Marco says suppliers' meetings often run over, so it's better to take the later one.

title: A ticket open for a week

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hi Aisha, I got your message. You wanted an update on the ticket about the report that won't load, right? It's been open a week now.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Exactly, and it's becoming a problem. The report fails every time it reaches two hundred and forty order lines, so I can't see the whole picture.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Yes, I looked at it this morning. The status is waiting for the database team. It's priority medium, which is why it has taken longer.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Medium? It blocks my weekly planning. Could you raise it to high and fix it today?

script.speaker: A
script.line: I can raise it to high, but I can't promise today. The database team has a freeze until Monday, so nobody can change the system before then.

script.speaker: B
script.line: So the earliest fix is Monday?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Right. In the meantime, I can set up a lighter version of the report that splits the lines into two parts. It's not perfect, but you'll see everything.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Okay, I'll take that, even if it's not what I asked for. Please send me the instructions today.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Will do. I'll email them within the hour and call you Monday afternoon to confirm the real fix.

questions.q: What are Aisha and Chris discussing?
options: A request for a new laptop for Aisha
A delay in fixing a report problem
A complaint about a late supplier delivery
A training course for the planners
questions.explanation: Aisha asks for an update on a ticket open for a week about a report that won't load.

questions.q: Why can the problem not be fixed today?
options: Chris is away on holiday until next Monday
The database team has a freeze until Monday
The report was deleted from the system by mistake
The ticket priority is too low to be handled yet
questions.explanation: Chris says the database team has a freeze until Monday.

questions.q: What will Chris do after the conversation?
options: Fix the database himself over the weekend
Close the ticket and open a new one
Order new software for the planning team
Email instructions for a lighter report version
questions.explanation: Chris says he will email the instructions within the hour.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Dana, glad I caught you. Something is odd in the plan: your forecast for the autumn is forty containers, but our production schedule covers only about a twelfth of that.

script.speaker: B
script.line: A twelfth? That's a strange ratio. Hold on, is that a rounding issue, or are we talking about different things altogether?

script.speaker: A
script.line: My guess is the latter. Your forecast is in packs, whereas our plan counts single units, and there are twelve units to a pack.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Of course, that would explain it. Someone must have pasted the pack numbers straight into your template without converting them. The unit column header isn't very clear either.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Quite. I don't think anyone is to blame. I'd just like a conversion check built in, so the numbers are tested before they reach the plan.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Agreed. Why don't I look at the template in my office on Wednesday morning, and you join me to go through it?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Wednesday works, but I'll be at the plant in the morning. Could we do it at the café on the ground floor after lunch instead?

script.speaker: B
script.line: The café is noisy and I'll want my screen. How about a call, say at half past eight on Wednesday, before you leave for the plant?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Better still. Half past eight by video, then. I'll send a few examples tonight, so we can see exactly where the units go astray.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good. I'll also ask our data team to add a warning if the unit label is missing.

questions.q: What problem do Raj and Dana discover?
options: The forecast and the supplier plan use different units
The forecast was sent to the wrong supplier by email
The containers were damaged on the way to the plant
The production plan was never approved by Dana's team
questions.explanation: Raj explains the forecast is in packs while the supplier plan counts single units.

questions.q: What conversion is behind the mismatch?
options: One container equals forty packs
One pack equals forty units
One unit equals a twelfth of a container
One pack equals twelve single units
questions.explanation: Raj says there are twelve units to a pack.

questions.q: How and when will they meet on Wednesday?
options: In Dana's office in the morning
By video call at half past eight
At the café on the ground floor
At the plant on Wednesday morning
questions.explanation: After rejecting the office and the café, they agree to a video call at half past eight.

title: Two options for a supply gap

script.speaker: A
script.line: Ingrid, can you hear me? The audio is poor on my end, so tell me if I break up. Shall we go through the gap before tomorrow's planning meeting?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes please. I can hear you fine, just a bit slowly. What are we looking at?

script.speaker: A
script.line: For the blister family, your demand is two thousand five hundred cartons higher than my supply plan in week three. That's the shortfall.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Right, that matches what I have. Sales are adamant about those volumes, because of the retailer promotion.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Understood. I see two options. Option one is overtime on the packing line, which closes most of the gap but costs extra.
