script.speaker: B
script.line: And what is the second option?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Option two is moving stock from the other site. It's cheaper, but it only covers about half, and it arrives a week late. Sorry, did you get that?

script.speaker: B
script.line: I caught most of it. Overtime is faster and bigger, the transfer is cheaper and slower. Which do you recommend?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Honestly, overtime. But I need a decision from you today so I can book the crews.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I'd rather not choose today, Hugo. Overtime means extra cost, and I've been told the budget for this quarter is already tight. I'd feel uneasy deciding that alone.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's fair. So you'd want someone with budget authority to look at it first.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Exactly. Let's put both options on the slide for tomorrow at nine and let the group decide. I'll add the promotion details.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good. I'll prepare the costs for each option tonight, so the numbers are ready before the meeting.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Perfect. Send them to me by six, and I'll check that the volumes match.

questions.q: What is the disadvantage of option two, moving stock from the other site?
options: It costs more than the overtime option does
It covers only half the gap and arrives late
It needs the retailer promotion to be cancelled
It requires a decision from the whole sales team
questions.explanation: Hugo says option two is cheaper but covers only about half and arrives a week late.

questions.q: Why does Ingrid not want to decide today?
options: She did not hear the two options clearly
Sales asked her to wait for the promotion
She thinks the transfer option is much better
She does not want to approve the cost alone
questions.explanation: She says overtime means extra cost, the budget is tight, and she'd feel uneasy deciding alone.

questions.q: What will Hugo do tonight?
options: Prepare the costs for both options
Book the packing crews for overtime
Cancel the retailer promotion
Move stock from the other site tonight
questions.explanation: Hugo says he will prepare the costs for each option tonight.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Camila, thanks for calling. Shall we run through your update for Monday's meeting? Give me the two-minute version, as if I were the director.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Here goes. Our stock of slow movers is down thirty percent, and we expect another ten percent by year end. The main driver is... sorry, I lost my place.

script.speaker: A
script.line: No problem, take a breath. The key message is simple: you reduced the stock, and the plan is on track.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's the thing, I'm very nervous. The director interrupts a lot, and I'm afraid I'll freeze when she asks about the numbers.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I understand, but you know these numbers better than anyone. And remember, you have two minutes, not twenty. Let's practise the likely questions.

script.speaker: B
script.line: She'll probably ask why the expiry write-offs are still high. I haven't got a clean answer yet.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I'll take that one. I'll pull the write-off figures for the last six months and send you a one-page summary by Friday.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That would be a relief. Thank you, Ibrahim. Then I can focus on the main story.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Exactly. Another likely question: what happens if sales drop? Keep your answer short: you have a safety buffer.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Right, a buffer of three weeks. I'll mention the buffer first and then the numbers.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good. We can rehearse once more on Monday at half past eight, before the meeting at ten.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Great, I feel much calmer now. See you Monday.

questions.q: What are Ibrahim and Camila doing?
options: Planning a new layout for the warehouse
Writing a long report on expiry dates
Rehearsing a short update for senior managers
Training a new colleague on the system
questions.explanation: Ibrahim asks Camila to give her two-minute update as if he were the director.

questions.q: What time is the meeting on Monday?
options: At half past eight
On Friday
At ten
By the end of the year
questions.explanation: Ibrahim says the meeting is at ten; half past eight is the extra rehearsal.

questions.q: What will Ibrahim do by Friday?
options: Send a one-page summary of write-off figures
Rehearse with the director before Monday
Write the slide about the safety buffer
Call the director's assistant on Monday
questions.explanation: He says he will pull the write-off figures and send a one-page summary by Friday.

questions.q: Why does Ibrahim say 'you have two minutes, not twenty'?
options: To criticise her for talking for too long
To tell her the meeting has been shortened
To ask her to add some more slides
To calm her by saying the update is short
questions.explanation: He says it right after she says she is nervous, to reassure her that the task is small.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hello, Chris. Thank you for the time. I need to finalise the plan for the software training, and honestly I'm a bit stressed about it.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Don't worry, we'll sort it out together. Let's start with the audience. Who needs to be there?

script.speaker: A
script.line: The planners and the customer service team, about twenty people. Some are new, so they've never used the system.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Then we need a basic session, not an advanced one. How long should it be? I suggest two hours, with a break.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Two hours sounds right. I was thinking of the 24th of July, because it's a Monday and most people are in the office.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good choice. Mondays are quiet, so people will have time. Now, who prepares the materials?

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's what worries me. I have to write the slides, the exercises and the test data, and I also have my normal work. I'm afraid I can't finish everything.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Okay. Let me take the slides. I've done similar presentations before, and it'll take me only an afternoon. You prepare the exercises and the test data.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That would help a lot. Thank you. I'll send you the screenshots I already have, so you don't start from zero.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Perfect. And please don't feel you must do everything alone. If the exercises get too much, tell me early.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I will. I feel much better now. I'll book the training room and send the invitation today.

questions.q: How long will the training session last?
options: A whole afternoon
About two hours
Twenty minutes
A full day
questions.explanation: Chris suggests two hours with a break and Amara agrees.

questions.q: Why is Amara stressed?
options: She has never used the new software herself
She has too many tasks besides her normal work
The training room is not available that day
Chris has cancelled the training session
questions.explanation: She says she has to write slides, exercises and test data and also has her normal work.

questions.q: What can we infer about the audience?
options: They are all very advanced users already
They are mostly from the finance team
They work in several different countries
Some of them have never used the system before
questions.explanation: Amara says some people are new and have never used the system, so the session must be basic.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Andrew, thanks for joining from there. Let's do the launch readiness check for the new pack size. Launch is on the 11th of October, correct?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Correct. Morning, Camila. I'm happy to start with logistics if you like, or do you prefer to go in order?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Let's go in order, then. Artwork first. Where do we stand?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Artwork is green. The printer has the final files and the proofs were signed off yesterday, so nothing to worry about there.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Excellent. The first batch is next. I know yield was a concern in the trial.

script.speaker: B
script.line: It's amber. The trial yield was about five percent below target, which the team thinks is a settings issue. They'll run another test this week.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Fine, amber but manageable. And logistics?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Logistics is red, I'm afraid. The new carton is slightly taller, so the existing pallet pattern doesn't fit under the carrier's height limit.

script.speaker: A
script.line: How long does it take to fix? Please tell me it's not a long process.

script.speaker: B
script.line: The carrier needs two weeks to approve a new pallet pattern. So unless they speed it up, we may well miss the 11th.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Understood. Let me escalate that with their account manager. Let's reconvene tomorrow at three in the afternoon to see what they say.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Tomorrow at three is difficult, I have a customs audit. Could we do Thursday at ten instead?

script.speaker: A
script.line: On Thursday at ten I'll be on a train with poor signal. Could we say Thursday at four?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Four works for me. I'll send the invite and include the pallet drawing, so the carrier sees it too.

questions.q: What is the status of the first batch?
options: Amber, with yield five percent below target
Green, with all the proofs signed off already
Red, because of the carrier's pallet pattern
Amber, because the artwork is not yet ready
questions.explanation: Andrew says it's amber and the trial yield was about five percent below target.

questions.q: Why is logistics red?
options: The carrier refused to work with them again
The launch date was moved a week earlier
The new carton is too tall for the pallet limit
The printer lost the final artwork files
questions.explanation: Andrew says the new carton is taller so the existing pallet pattern doesn't fit under the height limit.

questions.q: When will Camila and Andrew talk again?
options: Tomorrow at three
Thursday at ten
Thursday at four
On the 11th of October
questions.explanation: After two proposed times fail, they agree on Thursday at four.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hello Aisha, it's Kenji from planning. Is this a good moment? I'm calling about a goodbye lunch for Diana, who leaves us at the end of June.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Oh, I'm sorry to hear she's leaving. Yes, I have a few minutes. When are you thinking of having it?

script.speaker: A
script.line: We thought of Tuesday, the 29th of June, at half past twelve. Most of the team can come on that day.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Tuesday works for me. Where will it be? Somewhere close to the office?

script.speaker: A
script.line: There's an Italian place around the corner. They have a table for ten people, and they give us twelve percent off for groups.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That sounds lovely. Is there anything I can do to help with the preparations?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Yes, actually. We want to buy a small gift, five euros from each person. Could you collect the money in your department?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Well, to be honest, the month-end reports keep me at my desk all week, and I hardly see anyone from my team.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Oh, I understand. No problem at all, I'll ask someone on the finance floor instead.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Thanks, and sorry about that. Do you already have an idea for the gift?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Maybe a big book about gardens. She loves them, and she's about to move into a new flat.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Maybe something small instead, like a nice scarf. She's flying to her new city next month, so she can't carry much.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good thinking, a scarf is light. I'll send everyone the invitation today. See you on Tuesday!

questions.q: Why does Kenji call Aisha?
options: To ask her to help with month-end reports
To tell her about a new restaurant
To invite her to a goodbye party for herself
To plan a farewell lunch for a colleague
questions.explanation: Kenji says he is calling about a goodbye lunch for Diana, who is leaving.

questions.q: How many people is the restaurant table for?
options: Five
Twelve
Ten
Twenty-nine
questions.explanation: Kenji says the Italian place has a table for ten people.

questions.q: What does Aisha mean when she talks about the month-end reports?
options: She is too busy to collect the gift money
She cannot come to the lunch on Tuesday
She does not want to give money for a gift
She thinks the lunch should wait until next month
questions.explanation: She says the reports keep her at her desk all week, so she hardly sees her team and cannot collect money.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Right, before we get to the room, let's pin down the criteria for the two demand sensing vendors. I'd put forecast accuracy uplift first.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Agreed, but I'd weight integration effort just as heavily. Vendor one claims an eight percent error reduction, yet it needs a full rebuild of our data feeds.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's the catch. Eight percent is pilot data, so treat it as a ceiling, not a promise. Vendor two is slower to show results, but it plugs into our systems.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Fair point. So price comes third, then the support model, since our planners in Monterrey work odd hours.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Sounds right. I'll turn that into a scoring sheet this afternoon, so we can both score before the demos.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good. I'll ask both vendors for references from a pharma customer, and I want them back by Friday, otherwise the demos slip.

script.speaker: A
script.line: And I'll chase their security questionnaires. Those are always slower than anyone admits, so I'll need until the 5th of March to get both completed.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Fine, that still leaves us a week before the steering meeting. So you own the scoring sheet and the questionnaires, and I own the references.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Exactly. Sheet this afternoon, references by Friday, questionnaires by the fifth. Let's repeat that in the meeting so nobody forgets.

questions.q: What does Rachel think about the eight percent figure?
options: It comes from a pilot, so it may be too optimistic
It is the price cut that vendor two has promised us
It has already been confirmed by two customers
It shows vendor one is easy to connect to
questions.explanation: Rachel says it comes from their pilot data only, so it is a ceiling, not a promise.

questions.q: Why does Rachel need until the fifth of March for the questionnaires?
options: She has to wait for both vendors to finish their demos
Security questionnaires usually take longer than expected
Victor has to approve the questions before she can start
The steering meeting was moved to a later date
questions.explanation: She says those questionnaires are always slower than anyone admits.

questions.q: What will Victor do before Friday?
options: Write the scoring sheet for the vendor criteria
Chase the security questionnaires from both vendors
Ask both vendors for references from pharma customers
Book the steering meeting for the following week
questions.explanation: Victor says he will ask both vendors for pharma references and wants them back by Friday.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hi Tomas, I got your message about the forecast files. What exactly is confusing you?

script.speaker: B
script.line: I have two versions. One is called final, dated the 19th of July, and another is called final two. And the regional team wrote that they updated everything this morning.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Let me look. The one called final two is the newer one. I saved it at ten o'clock, after the regional call.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Okay. But the regional team wrote that they added sixty orders in the north, and I can't see that in either file.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hold on, I need to correct something. I saved final two at eleven, not ten, so it's after their message at ten thirty. Their sixty extra orders are already inside.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Ah, that explains it. The north column just looks bigger because of the new orders. But why does the first file still exist?

script.speaker: A
script.line: It's a backup from the 19th of July, from before the update. I should have deleted it, sorry. Please use only final two.

script.speaker: B
script.line: No problem. I'll move the old file to the archive folder, so nobody opens it by mistake.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Perfect. And from now on I'll put the date and the time in the file name, so it's always clear.

questions.q: What is Tomas's main problem?
options: He does not know which forecast file is the latest
He cannot open the message from the regional team
He wants to change the orders for the north region
He lost the final forecast file from last week
questions.explanation: Tomas says he has two versions and asks which one is right.

questions.q: At what time did Lucia save the file called final two?
options: At ten o'clock
At ten thirty
At nineteen hundred
At eleven o'clock
questions.explanation: Lucia first says ten, then corrects it: she saved final two at eleven, not ten.

questions.q: Why does the north column look bigger in the new file?
options: It still contains old numbers from the backup file
It includes sixty extra orders from the regional team
Lucia typed some wrong figures into the new file
The regional team removed some orders from the sheet
questions.explanation: Lucia says their sixty extra orders are already inside the new file.

questions.q: What will Tomas do with the old file?
options: Delete it today
Send it to the regional team
Move it to the archive folder
Rename it with the time
questions.explanation: Tomas says he will move the old file to the archive folder.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Thanks for making time, Elena. I wanted to go through the accuracy review for the Chilean market, because the pattern is hard to ignore.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Of course. I saw the chart you sent. Is it as bad as it looks?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Well, for six months we've forecast higher than actual sales, every single month. The average gap is about twelve hundred kilograms, which ties up cash in stock.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I'm not surprised. To be honest, our sales team likes to add a cushion, because they're afraid of running out and being blamed.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's understandable, but it's systematic. I'd like to apply an automatic reduction to the statistical forecast, starting from the next cycle.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I can see the logic, but I'd be uncomfortable doing it for the whole market. The new tender starts on the 11th of October, and those volumes are genuinely uncertain.

script.speaker: A
script.line: So you'd rather not touch the numbers before then?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Not entirely. What I can offer is a correction only on the established products, and we review the tender items separately once we see the first orders.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's a fair compromise, although I would have preferred a full correction. Can you make sales explain any manual increase?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, I'll ask the team to add a short comment whenever they override your number. That should reduce the cushion habit.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good. I'll draft the rule and send it to you for approval this week, and we'll look at the results together next month.

questions.q: What is the conversation mainly about?
options: How to plan the launch of a new tender product
How to train the sales team on forecasting tools
How to negotiate a lower price with suppliers
How to reduce a regular pattern of over-forecasting
questions.explanation: Arjun raises that forecasts were higher than sales every month and proposes a correction.

questions.q: What is the average monthly gap between forecast and sales?
options: About six hundred kilograms
About twelve hundred kilograms
About two thousand kilograms
About one hundred kilograms
questions.explanation: Arjun says the average gap is about twelve hundred kilograms.

questions.q: How does Arjun feel about Elena's final offer?
options: He accepts it, but he wanted more
He is angry and rejects it
He is delighted with every detail
He does not care either way
questions.explanation: He calls it a fair compromise but says he would have preferred a full correction.

questions.q: What can we infer about the reason Elena refuses a full correction?
options: She believes Arjun's chart contains some mistakes
She cannot speak to the sales team about changes
She fears that cutting tender volumes could leave them short
She thinks the tender will be cancelled before October
questions.explanation: She says the tender volumes are genuinely uncertain, so reducing them automatically is risky.

title: Catching up after a late start

script.speaker: A
script.line: Sorry, Marco, my train was stuck outside Hamburg and I've only just dialled in. What have I missed so far?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Not much, don't worry. We agreed the buffer for the new product should cover four weeks of demand, and everyone sends comments by Monday.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Four weeks sounds like a lot to me. Last time we only needed about two, I'm quite sure of it.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I thought so too, but Priya pulled the numbers. When the last product launched, sales ran twenty percent above plan for the first month.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hmm, I remember it differently, but I haven't seen those figures. Can you share the sheet?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Sure, I'm sending the link now. Look at column F. Actual sales were twenty percent higher, and it took us three weeks to catch up.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Okay, I see it. I was wrong. With that gap, two weeks of buffer wouldn't have been enough, so four it is. What happens next?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Everyone sends their comments by Monday, and then Priya updates the plan. You didn't miss much, so you're fine.

questions.q: By how much did sales exceed the plan after the last launch?
options: Four percent
Twenty percent
Forty percent
Two percent
questions.explanation: Marco says sales ran twenty percent above plan for the first month.

questions.q: Why does Ingrid change her mind about the buffer?
options: She sees data showing sales beat the plan
Marco says the decision was already approved
She suddenly remembers the earlier launch clearly
Priya refuses to discuss it any longer
questions.explanation: After seeing column F she says she was wrong, because actual sales were twenty percent higher.

questions.q: What can we infer about Ingrid's opinion before she saw the sheet?
options: She wanted a buffer of six weeks
She believed a two-week buffer had been enough
She thought the meeting should be cancelled
She had already read Priya's numbers
questions.explanation: She says last time they only needed about two weeks and she is sure of it.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Samuel, can you hear me? The audio keeps cutting out on my side.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, now I can, Sara. It's a bit crackly, but I can follow. How can I help?

script.speaker: A
script.line: It's about my holiday. I still have about sixty hours unused, and I'm worried I'll lose them at the end of the year.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Right, let me explain the rule. You can carry over up to forty hours into the next year, but they have to be used by the end of March.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Forty? So I'd lose twenty hours. That seems a shame, especially since I cancelled my summer trip for the audit.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I understand. In a case like yours, a manager can request an exception, and your director has to sign the form.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good, I'll ask my director then. Is there a deadline for the form?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, it has to reach us by the 29th of February. After that date, the normal rule applies and the extra hours are gone.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Okay. And is this only for this year?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Just this year. Oh, one thing, though. The form is on the employee portal, and I think the portal has been offline since Friday.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Offline? That's a nuisance. Couldn't you just send me a copy by email?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Let me check. I'd rather not send an old version, because the layout changed this month. I'll ask the portal team today.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Okay, so you'll find out and tell me?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, I'll write to you tomorrow morning, and if the portal is still down, I'll send the new form as an attachment.

questions.q: Why is Sara calling Samuel?
options: To report a problem with the audio system on her laptop
To request a new job in another team
To book a holiday for next summer
To ask what happens to her unused holiday hours
questions.explanation: Sara says it is about her holiday and that she is worried about losing unused hours.

questions.q: How many hours can normally be carried over?
options: Sixty
Twenty
Forty
Thirty
questions.explanation: Samuel says you can carry over up to forty hours.

questions.q: Why can Sara ask for an exception?
options: She has been at the company for many years
Her director is away until the end of March
The company asked her to cancel her summer trip
She missed the deadline because of the portal
questions.explanation: Sara says she cancelled her trip when the company asked her to help with the audit, and Samuel says an exception is possible in such a case.

questions.q: What does Samuel suggest about sending an old copy of the form?
options: It would be faster than using the portal
It might be out of date and not accepted
It is the only version her director signs
It would be accepted after the 29th of February
questions.explanation: He says the layout changed this month, so he would rather not send the old version.

title: Peaks in months four and five

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good morning, Samuel, it's Sara from the packaging plant. Thanks for sending the new twelve-month rolling forecast.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good morning, Sara. I hope it's useful. Does anything stand out?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Honestly, months four and five. The peaks are about twelve percent higher than this year, and our line struggles to cover that without extra shifts.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I know, those are the campaign months. The numbers might still move a little, though, so I can't call them fixed.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's exactly my problem. I'd need a firm commitment of at least one hundred and fifty orders a month to justify bringing in temporary staff.

script.speaker: B
script.line: A hundred and fifty firm is more than I can promise today. What if I commit to one hundred firm, and the rest stays a flexible range you review monthly?

script.speaker: A
script.line: One hundred is thin, but I could live with it if you give me an early view of the final volumes, say six weeks ahead instead of four.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Six weeks is hard for me, but I can give you a preliminary number at that point and the confirmed one at four weeks.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That works. I'll accept a hundred firm orders, and I'll prepare the staffing plan on that basis.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Great. I'll put it in writing and send you the updated agreement by Friday.

questions.q: What is the call mainly about?
options: Whether the plant should move to a new site
How to lower the price of the packaging material
How to cover the demand peaks in months four and five
Why the plant needs to change its packaging materials
questions.explanation: Sara explains that the peaks in months four and five are hard to cover and asks for a commitment.

questions.q: How many firm orders a month does Samuel finally commit to?
options: One hundred
One hundred and fifty
Fifty
Twelve
questions.explanation: Sara asks for one hundred and fifty, Samuel offers one hundred, and she accepts a hundred firm orders.

questions.q: What will Samuel do by Friday?
options: Send the updated agreement in writing
Hire temporary staff for the plant
Prepare the staffing plan
Give Sara the confirmed volumes
questions.explanation: He says he will put it in writing and send the updated agreement by Friday.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good morning, Nora. I'm here because the last delivery arrived with damaged cartons, and I'm not happy about it.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good morning, Mr Ibrahim. I'm very sorry to hear that. Please sit down and tell me what happened.

script.speaker: A
script.line: The delivery arrived on the 23rd of November, and six cartons at the bottom of one pallet were crushed.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Let me write that down. The 23rd, six cartons. Did anyone take photos?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Yes, my warehouse team took many. Sorry, I made a mistake with the date. It was the 24th, not the 23rd. The truck was unloaded at eleven in the morning.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Thank you for correcting that. Please send me the photos today, and I will register a claim with the carrier.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I will. But my customers are waiting, and I can't sell damaged boxes. What will you do about a replacement?

script.speaker: B
script.line: We'll send six new cartons, and I'll ask the warehouse to pack them on a separate pallet. They should leave on Monday.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good. I hope this doesn't happen again, because it's the second time this year.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I understand why you're frustrated. I'll also ask the carrier to explain what went wrong, and I'll call you with their answer.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Thank you, Nora. I appreciate that you are taking it seriously.

questions.q: Why does Ibrahim visit Nora?
options: To change the date of the next delivery to his site
To ask for photos of a pallet from the warehouse
To complain about a truck that arrived very late
To complain about damaged cartons and ask for new ones
questions.explanation: He says the last delivery arrived with damaged cartons and asks about a replacement.

questions.q: When was the delivery unloaded, after the correction?
options: On the 23rd of November, at eleven in the morning
On the 24th of November, in the evening
On the 24th of November, at eleven in the morning
On Monday morning, at eleven
questions.explanation: Ibrahim first says the 23rd, then corrects it to the 24th and says the truck was unloaded at eleven.

questions.q: How does Ibrahim feel at the end of the meeting?
options: Still angry with the warehouse team and the carrier
Embarrassed about his mistake with the date
Worried that the carrier will be changed again
Satisfied that his complaint is being taken seriously
questions.explanation: He thanks Nora and says he appreciates that she is taking it seriously.

questions.q: What can we infer about this problem?
options: It is the first time cartons were damaged
The carrier already apologised for it
Ibrahim's team crushed the cartons
It has happened with this supplier before
questions.explanation: He says it is the second time this year.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Jon, thanks for jumping on the call after our chat. I want to be clear about the penalty clause, because forty order lines arrived late last month.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I understand, Nora, but with respect, about half of those lines were late because your team changed the specification eight weeks into the contract.

script.speaker: A
script.line: The change request came when you were already behind on the first batch, though. The clause still applies to everything delivered after the agreed date.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Would you consider applying it only to the lines we delayed ourselves? I'd rather not fight over the rest.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I can't waive it entirely, but I could halve the penalty on the lines affected by the change, provided you give me a proper recovery plan.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's fair. I'll send a recovery plan with new dates for every late line, and I'll have it ready by Tuesday.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good. And please confirm in writing that future specification changes will be logged with a date, so we avoid this argument.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Agreed. In exchange, could we have a freeze on changes in the last two weeks before delivery?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Yes, let's add that to the contract amendment. I'll ask legal to draft it tomorrow.

questions.q: What does Nora offer on the lines affected by the change?
options: To cut the penalty by half
To remove the penalty completely
To double the penalty
To leave the penalty unchanged
questions.explanation: She says she cannot waive it entirely but could halve the penalty on those lines.

questions.q: What will Jon prepare by Tuesday?
options: A draft of the contract amendment for the lawyers
A list of the future specification changes
A new price for all of the delayed lines
A recovery plan with new dates for the late lines
questions.explanation: He says he will have the recovery plan with new dates ready by Tuesday.

questions.q: Why does Jon say "with respect" before talking about the specification?
options: To disagree politely and blame the buyer's change
To thank Nora for taking the time to talk
To apologise for the late lines in advance
To ask for a longer contract with the buyer
questions.explanation: The phrase softens his disagreement as he blames the late specification change on Nora's team.

questions.q: What is the conversation mainly about?
options: How to write a new supplier contract from scratch
How to speed up the next delivery to the site
How to change the product specification again
How to settle a dispute over a late-delivery penalty
questions.explanation: They argue about the penalty clause and agree a compromise.

title: Short of cartons before the meeting

script.speaker: A
script.line: Morning, Hugo. You look rested. Did you go anywhere nice over the weekend?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Morning, Marta. Yes, we drove up to the lake with the kids. It rained on Saturday, but Sunday was lovely. And you?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Just a quiet weekend at home, I'm afraid. I did hear that you have a problem with the packaging order, though.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Right. We're short of about twenty-five hundred cartons for next week's run, and the supplier says the new stock won't arrive for two weeks.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's a real problem. We could borrow from the Leeds site, but they'd need a few days to ship.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Actually, the supplier's rep just texted me. Another customer cancelled an order, which freed up stock, so our cartons can arrive on Thursday.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's excellent news. Then there's no need to borrow from Leeds, and the production run can stay on schedule.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Exactly. I'll tell the line supervisor before the meeting starts, so she doesn't re-plan the whole week.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good idea. I'll let the others know when we begin, and we can move on to the next item, since people are arriving now.

questions.q: What is Hugo's problem?
options: There are not enough cartons for next week's production
His weekend trip was cancelled because of the rain
The Leeds site refused to share its stock of cartons
The line supervisor is away for the whole week
questions.explanation: He says they are short of about twenty-five hundred cartons for next week's run.

questions.q: How long did the supplier first say the new stock would take?
options: A few days
Until Thursday
Two weeks
Until the weekend
questions.explanation: Hugo says the supplier first said the stock would not arrive for two weeks.

questions.q: Why can the cartons now arrive earlier?
options: The Leeds site sent them by truck
The supplier opened a new factory
Another customer cancelled an order
Hugo bought them from a different supplier
questions.explanation: The rep texted that another customer cancelled an order, which freed up stock.

questions.q: What will Hugo do before the meeting starts?
options: Tell the line supervisor about the change
Call the Leeds site about borrowing cartons
Order more cartons from another supplier
Cancel next week's production run
questions.explanation: He says he will tell the line supervisor before the meeting starts.

title: A simpler way to run meetings

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hi Rachel, do you have a few minutes? I'd like to talk about our Wednesday meeting, if that's okay.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Sure, Ethan. Is something wrong? Did I forget to send the notes again?

script.speaker: A
script.line: No, nothing like that. The meeting starts at two o'clock, but it often runs until half past three, and I think we could use the time better.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Oh, I see. You want to move it to another day? I know Wednesday is hard for the Madrid team.

script.speaker: A
script.line: No, no, the day is fine. I mean the way we use the time. Some updates are very long, and we don't have an agenda.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Ah, sorry, I misunderstood. So you think my updates are too long?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Not only yours, everybody's, including mine. I just think a simple structure would help.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Okay, I like that idea. What do you have in mind?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Maybe each person gets three minutes, and we write the topics in a shared document the day before.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's reasonable. I tend to explain every detail, so a time limit will be good for me.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Great. Could we try it for four weeks and then check if it works?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, let's do that. I'll prepare the agenda document today and share it with everyone.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Perfect, thanks. To be honest, I was a bit nervous about raising this, so I'm glad you took it so well.

questions.q: What does Ethan want to improve?
options: The quality of Rachel's weekly reports
The day the meeting takes place
The number of people who attend the meeting
The way the weekly meeting is organised
questions.explanation: He talks about long updates and having no agenda.

questions.q: How long will each person speak in the new structure?
options: Two minutes
Three minutes
Ten minutes
Half an hour
questions.explanation: Ethan suggests that each person gets three minutes.

questions.q: How did Ethan feel before the call?
options: Very angry
A little nervous
Completely relaxed
Bored
questions.explanation: At the end he says he was a bit nervous about raising the subject.

questions.q: What did Rachel first think Ethan wanted?
options: To change the day of the meeting
To cancel the meeting completely
To remove Madrid from the meeting
To make her stop sending notes
questions.explanation: She asks if he wants to move it to another day, and he says no.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good afternoon, Chloe, this is Raj from the airline's rebooking desk. You asked me about your connection in Amsterdam.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Thanks for calling back. We landed late, and I have just thirty-five minutes to reach the gate.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I understand. To be straight with you, the system gives you only about a fifteen percent chance of making it. The Lisbon flight departs at ten past six.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Fifteen percent isn't much. What are my other options?

script.speaker: A
script.line: There's a later flight at nine forty tonight, or one first thing tomorrow, on the 24th of June. Both have seats.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Tonight is better, but I have a meeting in Lisbon at nine tomorrow, and my host needs to know whether I'll make it.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Here's the difficulty. Whether the six ten flight waits for you is the duty manager's call, and he hasn't answered yet. Until then, I can't rebook you.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's frustrating. So I don't know whether to run or to stay put?

script.speaker: A
script.line: I'd say walk briskly towards the gate while I wait. If he says no, I'll move you to the nine forty at once.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Fine. Message me the moment you know, please. I'd like to tell my host whether to expect me tonight.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Of course. I'll text you within ten minutes, as soon as the duty manager replies.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Great. Meanwhile I'll warn my host I might arrive late tonight, but I won't cancel anything.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Sensible. I'm sorry for the inconvenience. I know it's not what you wanted after a long day.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Thanks, Raj. It's not your fault. Talk to you in ten minutes.

questions.q: At what time does the first flight to Lisbon depart?
options: At nine forty tonight
At ten past six
At nine tomorrow morning
At thirty-five past six
questions.explanation: Raj says the Lisbon flight departs at ten past six; nine forty is the later flight and nine tomorrow is her meeting.

questions.q: How does Chloe feel about the situation?
options: Angry about how Raj spoke to her
Frustrated by the uncertainty
Calm and not at all worried
Confident she will make her connection
questions.explanation: She says it is frustrating not to know whether to run or stay, and later tells Raj it is not his fault.

questions.q: What will Raj do within ten minutes?
options: Book a hotel room for her tonight
Move her straight to the nine forty flight
Call her host in Lisbon to explain
Text her once the duty manager answers
questions.explanation: He says he will text her within ten minutes, as soon as the duty manager replies.

title: Locked out of the contracts folder

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hi, I can't open the shared folder with the supplier contracts. It says access denied, and I need it for a meeting.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Let me check your account. You're in the planning group, but that folder belongs to the procurement group, so you aren't a member right now.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's odd. I had access last year. Has something changed?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, permissions are reviewed every twelve weeks, and yours expired. To get back in, the folder owner, Ms Okafor, must approve a request, and I can raise it now.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Please do. Could you come to my desk on Monday morning to test it?

script.speaker: B
script.line: I'm actually in the Zurich office on Monday. How about Tuesday at nine, here in your department?

script.speaker: A
script.line: On Tuesday morning I have a workshop in room four until noon. Let's say Tuesday afternoon, in the meeting room next to the kitchen?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Perfect. Tuesday at two in the meeting room next to the kitchen. I'll send the invitation as soon as Ms Okafor approves.

questions.q: What is Mark's problem?
options: He forgot his password for the planning group
He cannot find the room for his meeting
He wants to delete an old folder of contracts
He cannot open a folder and needs access approved
questions.explanation: He says the folder says access denied, and Katarina explains a request must be approved.

questions.q: Why did his access stop working?
options: His permission ended in a regular review
Ms Okafor deleted his account last week
He moved to the procurement group
The folder was moved to a different office
questions.explanation: Katarina says permissions are reviewed every twelve weeks and his expired.

questions.q: Where and when will they meet?
options: Tuesday at two, in the meeting room next to the kitchen
Monday morning, at his desk in the planning area
Tuesday at nine, in his own department's office
Tuesday at noon, in room four after the workshop
questions.explanation: The final plan is Tuesday at two in the meeting room next to the kitchen.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That went well, Mei. Honestly, I think the room was with you from the first slide.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Really? I was so nervous that I rushed through the second half.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Nobody noticed. What worked was your opening, where you started with the customer story instead of the chart. They'll remember that.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Thanks. I wasn't sure about the story, but someone told me to try it.

script.speaker: A
script.line: One thing to improve, though. You had twelve slides of tables, and the directors wanted the decision, not the workings. Next time, lead with two slides.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Fair enough. I got carried away because I was afraid of questions I couldn't answer.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Understandable. And good news: the finance director liked it, and she wants you, not me, to present to the board on Thursday the 3rd of October, at nine thirty.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Wow, I didn't expect that! Then I'll shorten the deck this week, and I'll send it to you for a quick look before that.

questions.q: What is the conversation mainly about?
options: Preparing slides for a visit from a customer
A complaint about the finance director's decision
Moving a board meeting to another room
Feedback on a presentation and a new opportunity
questions.explanation: Marco gives feedback on the presentation and then shares news about the board meeting.

questions.q: What part of the presentation did the audience remember?
options: The tables of figures
The appendix slides
The fast second half
The opening customer story
questions.explanation: Marco says the opening with the customer story worked and that they will remember it.

questions.q: How does Mei react to the news at the end?
options: She is worried and refuses
She is surprised and pleased
She feels bored and tired
She is angry with Marco
questions.explanation: She says "Wow, I didn't expect that!" and starts planning to shorten the deck.

questions.q: What can we infer about Marco's earlier plan?
options: Mei was always meant to present to the board
The board meeting had been cancelled
The finance director was absent that day
He was going to present to the board himself
questions.explanation: He says the director wants Mei, not him, to present, so he had planned to do it.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Luis, before the two o'clock review, can I show you where I'm coming from on the upside scenario? I'm pushing for eighteen percent above baseline.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Eighteen? That's aggressive. Finance only budgeted a few percent above baseline, and I don't want us carrying stock we can't sell.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Sorry, I wasn't clear. Eighteen percent applies only to the product family in the tender, and only if we win it. Everything else stays at baseline.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Ah, that changes things. I thought you meant the whole portfolio. In that case, what's the probability of winning?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Sales say around fifty-fifty. So my suggestion is that we keep baseline as the consensus, and write the tender upside as a flagged assumption.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I can live with that, provided the assumption is explicit. If we win, we trigger a capacity review within a week.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Agreed. I'll put the assumption and the trigger on the first slide, so nobody can miss it.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good. Then at two o'clock you present it and I'll back you up. I was worried this would turn into a long argument.

questions.q: What do Amara and Luis agree on?
options: Use an eighteen percent increase for every product
Keep baseline, and flag the tender upside as an assumption
Cancel the tender upside and ignore the sales view
Move the two o'clock review to a different day
questions.explanation: Amara suggests baseline as consensus with a flagged assumption, and Luis says he can live with that.

questions.q: Where does the eighteen percent apply?
options: To the whole product portfolio of the company
To last quarter's actual sales figures
Only to the product family in the tender
To the finance budget for next year
questions.explanation: Amara clarifies it applies only to the tender product family, if they win.

questions.q: How does Luis feel when he first hears eighteen percent?
options: Delighted by the size of the upside
Confused about the time of the meeting
Sceptical and worried about extra stock
Annoyed with the sales team's forecasts
questions.explanation: He calls it aggressive and says he does not want to carry stock they cannot sell.

questions.q: Why does Amara want to flag the tender upside as an assumption?
options: Finance asked her to remove it
The tender is not certain to be won
The baseline is already too high
Luis will present it alone
questions.explanation: She says sales see about a fifty-fifty chance, so it cannot be treated as baseline.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Victor, can you hear me? Sorry, your video is freezing a little on my side.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I hear you fine, Rachel. Let's carry on, and if it gets worse I'll switch to audio only. So, what would you like to get from our meetings?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Mainly two things. I want to understand how the monthly supply and demand review reaches its decisions, and I want to get better at presenting numbers to non-planners.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good goals. For presenting, you can shadow me at the review on the 5th of May. For decision-making, we'll talk after each one.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That would be fantastic. How often would you like to meet? I was thinking every week.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Weekly is too much, honestly. My calendar is full because of a backlog of about six hundred containers at the port. Every two weeks is realistic.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Of course, every two weeks is fine. Would it be possible to have a short check-in message in between?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Messaging is not my strength. My inbox is a graveyard, as my team will happily tell you.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Understood. Then I'll save my questions for our meetings and bring a short list each time.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Perfect. Send me your first list by Friday, and we'll set the first session for the week after the review.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Will do. I'll send the list on Friday and book a time in your calendar. Thanks, Victor.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of this conversation?
options: To set goals and a routine for mentoring
To solve a problem with containers at the port
To plan a presentation for a customer
To review Rachel's performance this year
questions.explanation: They talk about Rachel's goals, how often to meet and what she wants to learn.

questions.q: When will Rachel shadow Victor?
options: By Friday, with her first list
Every two weeks, after each meeting
The week after the review
At the review on the 5th of May
questions.explanation: Victor says she can shadow him at the review on the 5th of May.

questions.q: Why does Victor refuse weekly meetings?
options: He is going on holiday soon after the review
His video connection is too weak for weekly calls
He prefers to meet only after each review
His calendar is full because of a container backlog
questions.explanation: He says weekly is too much because of the backlog of containers at the port.

questions.q: What will Rachel do by Friday?
options: Book the container shipment for the port
Attend the review with the director
Send Victor her first list of questions
Send Victor a short message every day
questions.explanation: Victor asks for her first list by Friday and she agrees to send it.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Amara, I'm finally back. The conference in Lisbon was worth it, mostly. Two talks really stuck with me.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Tell me. I've been curious since you posted that photo of the huge stage.

script.speaker: A
script.line: The first was about digital twins for distribution networks. The second, on planning under uncertainty, was even better. The speaker was brilliant on using scenario ranges instead of single numbers.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's close to what we're trying with our forecast ranges. Did you meet anyone useful?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Yes, a logistics director from a cold-chain firm. She offered us a control tower visit on the 15th of March. Sorry, I mean the 17th.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good thing you said so. And anything disappointing? You did say mostly.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Yes, the exhibition hall. Every vendor promised artificial intelligence planning, and only one could show a real customer result. A bit of a letdown.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Ha, typical. Let's go through your notes at the planning meeting on Tuesday, and I'll ask the director's office to confirm the visit.

questions.q: On which date will the visit to the control tower take place?
options: The 17th of March
The 15th of March
Tuesday
The 7th of March
questions.explanation: Pedro first says the 15th, then corrects it to the 17th.

questions.q: What will Amara do after the call?
options: Book a flight to Lisbon for the visit
Write a report about the conference talks
Ask the director's office to confirm the visit
Call the vendor she met at the exhibition
questions.explanation: She says she will ask the director's office to confirm the visit.

questions.q: Why does Amara say "You did say mostly"?
options: To disagree with his opinion of the talks
To ask him what was disappointing
To end the conversation quickly
To complain about the conference photo
questions.explanation: She is reminding him of the word "mostly" to get him to explain the negative part.

questions.q: What is the conversation mainly about?
options: A problem with a cold-chain shipment to Lisbon
Plans for a new stand at the exhibition
Highlights and a disappointment from a conference
A change to the Tuesday planning meeting
questions.explanation: Pedro describes two talks, a useful contact and a letdown at the exhibition.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good morning, Andrew, it's Claire from the planning department. Thank you for taking my call.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good morning, Claire. How can I help?

script.speaker: A
script.line: We need an extra production slot next month. A customer ordered more than we expected, so we need another batch.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Let me check the schedule. Hmm, next month is nearly full. The earliest free day is the 29th of April.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's too late for us. We hoped for the second week. Can you move another order?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Not without asking the other customer. But I can offer the 29th, with one condition. You must send the raw materials ten days before.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Ten days is difficult, because our supplier needs time. Could we send them one week before?

script.speaker: B
script.line: A week is too short for our quality check. How about eight days, and your team confirms the order by two o'clock today?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Eight days is possible. I'll check with the supplier and confirm by two this afternoon.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good. In return, we'll keep the slot reserved until then and not offer it to anyone else.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Thank you. I'll send you the purchase order as soon as it's confirmed.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Perfect. Please put the reference on the order so we find it quickly. Talk to you this afternoon.

questions.q: Why does Claire call Andrew?
options: To cancel a batch that was already planned
To change the raw materials for next month
To ask about the results of a quality check
To ask for an extra production slot
questions.explanation: She says they need an extra production slot next month.

questions.q: Which date does Andrew offer for the extra slot?
options: The second week of April
The 29th of April
Two o'clock today
Eight days from today
questions.explanation: He says the earliest free day is the 29th of April.

questions.q: Why does Andrew refuse to accept the materials only one week before?
options: His line is closed that week
The supplier asked for ten days
Another customer needs the slot
His quality check needs more time
questions.explanation: He says a week is too short for their quality check.

questions.q: What can we infer if Claire does not confirm by two o'clock?
options: Andrew might give the slot to someone else
Claire will lose her purchase order
Andrew will move the slot to an earlier day
The eight days will become ten days
questions.explanation: He promises to keep the slot reserved until then, which suggests it may be released afterwards.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Aisha, do you mind if I pick your brain over coffee? Everyone keeps throwing around terms I only half understand.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Not at all. Fire away, and stop me whenever it gets too jargon-heavy.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Let's start with lead time. Is it the time from order to arrival, or from planning to shipping?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Order to arrival. Roughly speaking, the clock starts when we place the purchase order and stops when the goods are physically in the warehouse.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Got it. And safety stock? I gather it's a buffer, but who decides how big it is?

script.speaker: B
script.line: It's a buffer against surprises. Planners propose it, but finance lives with the cash it ties up. Right now we hold forty percent more than target on some items.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That seems like a lot. And what about on-time in-full? People say it like a mantra.

script.speaker: B
script.line: It's the share of deliveries that arrive on the agreed day with the full quantity. Miss either one and the order doesn't count.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Makes sense. Last one: batch release. I assume quality signs off?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, a batch can't be sold until quality has reviewed the paperwork and released it. That's separate from it being physically made.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Would you walk me through the release paperwork now? There's a meeting at nine tomorrow, and I'd like to follow along.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I'd love to, but I'd rather not teach you a half-correct version. The last time I explained it to a visitor, an auditor had to correct me.

questions.q: What does lead time measure, according to Aisha?
options: From the planning meeting until the goods are shipped
From the start of making a batch until it is finished
From placing the purchase order until goods reach the warehouse
From the end of production until quality signs off
questions.explanation: She says the clock starts at the purchase order and stops when goods are in the warehouse.

questions.q: Why does finance care about the size of safety stock?
options: Extra stock ties up cash
Finance chooses which suppliers to use
Safety stock is always forty percent of sales
Planners cannot calculate it
questions.explanation: Aisha says finance has to live with the cash that safety stock ties up.

questions.q: Why does Aisha decline to explain the release paperwork?
options: She is not sure she would explain it correctly
She has a meeting at nine tomorrow
She thinks Kenji already understands it
She is not allowed to discuss quality matters
questions.explanation: She says she would rather not teach a half-correct version and mentions an auditor had to correct her.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hello Ben, it's Leila from the travel agency. Can you hear me? The line is weak.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, I hear you, but there's an echo. Thanks for calling about the conference flight.

script.speaker: A
script.line: No problem. I found two options for Barcelona. The first leaves at ten to seven, costs four hundred and ten euros, and arrives at ten fifteen.

script.speaker: B
script.line: And what about the second one?

script.speaker: A
script.line: It leaves at eleven twenty and costs three hundred and sixty euros, but it arrives at one forty-five in the afternoon.

script.speaker: B
script.line: The conference starts at twelve, so the cheaper one is too late. But I remember our policy says anything above four hundred euros needs my manager's approval.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Exactly. The first flight is ten euros over, so you need approval. Do you want me to hold the seat while you ask?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, please. I'll ask my manager this afternoon. Also, I must be back before the 11th of January, because we have a stock count with three hundred order lines.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Then the return on the tenth works. I'll hold both seats and call you at four to hear what your manager says.

script.speaker: B
script.line: At four I'm in a workshop. Could you call after five instead?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Unfortunately we close at five. How about I send an email, and you call me when you can?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Actually, email isn't good either, because the approval may come late. I'll call you myself tomorrow at nine.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Tomorrow at nine works. I can hold the seats until then, but not later than ten o'clock.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Understood. Thank you, Leila, and sorry for the trouble.

questions.q: What is the conversation mainly about?
options: Changing a hotel booking for the conference
Cancelling a conference trip because of the policy
Choosing a conference flight and getting approval
Paying for a stock count with the manager
questions.explanation: They compare two flights and discuss the manager's approval.

questions.q: At what time does the cheaper flight arrive?
options: At one forty-five
At ten fifteen
At ten to seven
At eleven twenty
questions.explanation: Leila says the second flight arrives at one forty-five in the afternoon.

questions.q: What can we infer about the more expensive flight?
options: It is cheaper than the other flight
It arrives too late for the conference start
It has no seats left for tomorrow
It costs more than the policy limit
questions.explanation: Ben says anything above four hundred euros needs approval, and Leila says it is ten euros over.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Mateo, about the urgent order for the hospital distributor. Should we pay for air freight or wait for the sea shipment?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Air gets there in three days, but it costs roughly four times more. Sea is cheaper, but the container is still two weeks away.

script.speaker: A
script.line: And the customer needs the goods by the 5th of March, otherwise they have to cancel a campaign.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Sea would arrive on the 3rd, only two days before that. That's risky if there's any port delay.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Exactly, and port congestion has been bad lately. I'd lean towards air for at least half the order.

script.speaker: B
script.line: A split shipment could work, but we should check the budget first. I'm worried about the extra cost.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Wait, good news. The shipping agent just wrote that the vessel left early and now arrives a week sooner.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Then I think we don't need air at all. Sea gives us a comfortable margin for the 5th of March.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Agreed. I'll cancel the air quote and ask the agent to confirm the new arrival in writing today.

questions.q: What are Aisha and Mateo trying to decide?
options: Which customer to serve first
Whether to cancel the campaign
How to ship an urgent order
How to reduce port congestion
questions.explanation: They compare air freight and sea freight for an urgent order.

questions.q: How much more does air freight cost than sea?
options: About four times more
About two times more
About three times more
About half as much more
questions.explanation: Mateo says air costs roughly four times more.

questions.q: What will Aisha do next?
options: Book a split shipment with the shipping agent
Cancel the air quote and get written confirmation
Call the hospital distributor about the delay
Ask Mateo to check the budget for air freight
questions.explanation: She says she will cancel the air quote and ask the agent to confirm in writing today.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Right, let's go through what's still open for the close. First, late goods receipts: about thirty percent of last week's inbound isn't booked yet.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's worse than I expected. Is it mostly the northern warehouse?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Mostly, yes. They're short-staffed, and the paperwork is piling up. I'll chase them, but I'd appreciate a nudge from you too, since you know the manager.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Sure, I'll call him today. What about the unconfirmed purchase orders?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Twenty-two are still open, mainly with two suppliers who haven't answered since the start of the month. I'm getting rather worried about those.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I'll take the suppliers. If they don't reply by eleven tomorrow, I'll escalate to their account managers.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Perfect. Then let's reconvene to check progress. Thursday at eleven, here in this room?

script.speaker: B
script.line: On Thursday I'm at the finance workshop until noon. Could we do Wednesday at four in my office instead?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Wednesday at four is fine, but your office is a long way from my desk. Shall we meet in the cafeteria, halfway?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Fine, as long as we sit in the quiet corner by the windows. I'll bring my laptop.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good. And please keep me posted about the northern warehouse before then, even if it's only a short message.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Of course. If they promise a booking date, I'll send it to you straight away.

script.speaker: A
script.line: What bothers me is the thirty percent. If that figure doesn't drop, the close report will have visible gaps.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I know, and I don't love it either. Let's hope the call to the warehouse shifts something.

questions.q: When and where will they meet again?
options: Thursday at eleven, in the meeting room
Wednesday at four, in Kenji's office
Tomorrow at eleven, in the cafeteria
Wednesday at four, in the cafeteria
questions.explanation: After two changes they agree on Wednesday at four in the cafeteria.

questions.q: How does Yuki feel about the unconfirmed purchase orders?
options: Fairly worried
Completely unconcerned
Angry with Kenji
Amused by the delay
questions.explanation: She says she is getting rather worried about those.

questions.q: What will Kenji do today?
options: Contact the suppliers' account managers
Call the manager of the northern warehouse
Book the cafeteria for Wednesday
Finish the close report
questions.explanation: He says "I'll call him today", meaning the northern warehouse manager.

title: Pulling a delivery forward a week

script.speaker: A
script.line: Dana, got a minute? I'm hoping you can pull forward our delivery by a week. The clinic launch has moved up.

script.speaker: B
script.line: A full week? That's tough. Which order are we talking about?

script.speaker: A
script.line: The one planned for Thursday next week. I need it this Thursday, so the team can prepare the launch.

script.speaker: B
script.line: The difficulty is that the factory line is booked, and moving your order means bumping another one. Plus, the carrier only has a slot at nine thirty on Thursday.

script.speaker: A
script.line: And which order would be the one that gets bumped?

script.speaker: B
script.line: A regional order for the northern distributor. It's smaller, about twelve percent of your volume, so it's the obvious candidate.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Would the distributor mind? I don't want to cause problems for a colleague.

script.speaker: B
script.line: They'd rather have a partial delivery on time than a late one, but I'd need to call them first.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I'd be grateful. And what if I accept half of my order now, and the rest next week as planned? That might make it easier.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That works better. Then the northern order only slips by two days instead of a week.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's more than fair, and I'm sorry for the late request.

script.speaker: B
script.line: It's alright. Let me confirm with the factory and the carrier. Can you wait until noon?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Of course. Please text me as soon as you know, and I'll come and find you if I don't hear anything.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Will do. If the carrier can't do nine thirty, I'll look at Friday morning and tell you what changes.

questions.q: How big is the northern order compared with Pavel's volume?
options: About half
About twelve percent
About a third
About two days
questions.explanation: Dana says it is about twelve percent of Pavel's volume.

questions.q: What will Dana do before noon?
options: Deliver half of the order by herself
Cancel the northern order for good
Book a new line at the factory
Check with the factory and the carrier
questions.explanation: She says she will confirm with the factory and the carrier and asks Pavel to wait until noon.

questions.q: Why does Dana say "A full week? That's tough"?
options: To show the request will be hard to meet
To refuse the request at once without a reason
To ask Pavel to wait for a week
To agree to the request without conditions
questions.explanation: It signals difficulty while still inviting more detail.

questions.q: What is the conversation mainly about?
options: Choosing a new carrier for the clinic launch
Finding a compromise to bring a delivery forward
Reducing the size of the regional order
Planning an event for the clinic launch next week
questions.explanation: They trade off orders and agree a split delivery.

title: No free racks in the warehouse

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good morning, Fatima, it's Adam from the central warehouse. I'm calling because we're nearly full. We have about six hundred batches in stock and no free racks.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good morning, Adam. That's not good. How many deliveries are due this week?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Four trucks. If they all arrive, we have nowhere to put the pallets.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Let me think. The two deliveries of packaging material aren't urgent, so I can delay those by a few days. The other two are needed for production.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That helps. And could some of the finished goods be moved to the second site?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Possibly. Let's walk the aisles together. Can you meet me tomorrow at nine at your warehouse?

script.speaker: A
script.line: At nine I have the fire inspection on site. Would you prefer to meet in my office at eleven?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Eleven is possible, but the visit would be more useful at the racks. Let's meet at the loading dock gate at eleven and walk from there.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good. Eleven at the loading dock gate. I'll bring the stock list, and I'll reduce the number of pallets before then if I can.

questions.q: How many trucks are due this week?
options: Four
Two
Six
Nine
questions.explanation: Adam says four trucks are due.

questions.q: Why can't Adam meet at nine?
options: He is visiting the second site
He has a call with production
He is away from the warehouse
He has a fire inspection
questions.explanation: He says he has the fire inspection on site at nine.

questions.q: What does Fatima imply when she says the visit would be more useful at the racks?
options: She dislikes meeting in offices in general
She thinks the racks are broken or unsafe
She wants to see the storage space in person
She wants to cancel all the deliveries
questions.explanation: She prefers the loading dock gate and a walk through the aisles to talking in an office.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Help desk, Ingrid speaking. How can I help?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Hello, this is Marco from supply planning. I'm walking between meetings, so sorry for the noise. My account is locked, and I have a presentation at two.

script.speaker: A
script.line: No problem. First I have to verify who you are. Could you tell me your employee number and your manager's name?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Of course. It's seven four one two, and my manager is Helen Brooks.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Thank you, that matches. I can see the account locked after too many failed attempts. Did you change your password recently?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, but that was two weeks ago, and I've used the new one every day without any problem. So I don't understand why it's locked.

script.speaker: A
script.line: If I may, the log tells a different story. About twenty failed sign-ins since eight this morning, all from a mobile device, all using the old password.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Twenty? That can't be me. I haven't typed anything wrong. Hold on. My phone's email app! It must be trying the old password in the background.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's what the data suggests. The app keeps retrying, and the account locks itself every time.

script.speaker: B
script.line: You're right, I should have thought of that. So what do I do now?

script.speaker: A
script.line: I'll unlock the account now. Then please open the mail app on your phone, remove the account, and add it again with the new password.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Understood, I'll do that right away, before my meeting.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good. If it locks again within the next hour, call us back and we'll check the log together.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Thanks a lot, Ingrid. You've saved my presentation.

questions.q: What caused the account to lock?
options: Mobile email app retrying the old password
Someone guessing his password
A problem with his employee number
A failed update of the presentation software
questions.explanation: Ingrid shows failed sign-ins from a mobile device using the old password.

questions.q: What will Marco do on his phone?
options: Remove the mail account and add it with the new password
Delete the mail app and install it again later
Change his password again before the meeting
Restart the phone and wait for ten minutes
questions.explanation: Ingrid asks him to remove the account and add it again with the new password.

questions.q: Why does Ingrid say "If I may, the log tells a different story"?
options: To ask for his employee number
To end the call quickly
To blame his manager
To disagree politely using the system data
questions.explanation: She softens the disagreement and then supports it with the log.

questions.q: What is the call mainly about?
options: Marco asks to change his manager
Marco gets help with a locked account
Ingrid reports a problem on her phone
Marco and Ingrid plan a presentation
questions.explanation: Ingrid verifies him, finds the cause and unlocks the account.

title: Why safety stock is too high

script.speaker: A
script.line: Chris, thanks for joining the call. I saw in the chat that safety stock on the blue sachets is forty percent above target. Why is that?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, I've seen it. It goes back to March, when the forecast jumped because of a big tender. We bought extra stock, but the tender turned out smaller.

script.speaker: A
script.line: So we're holding stock we don't need. I'd like to burn it all down by the end of the month. Can you do that?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Not all of it, honestly. The shelf life is long, so there's no urgency, and a sudden discount would hurt our margin.

script.speaker: A
script.line: And what can you realistically do instead, then?

script.speaker: B
script.line: I can stop new orders right away and let normal demand take it down. That would bring us to target in about three months.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Three months is slower than I wanted. Is there anything faster?

script.speaker: B
script.line: I could offer some of the stock to the southern region, which is short. That would save about a month.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good. Do both. Please send me a short plan before our review on Tuesday at nine.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Will do. I'll send it on Monday afternoon, so you can read it before the meeting.

questions.q: Why is Dana calling Chris?
options: To cancel a tender that was too small
To order more blue sachets for the south
To ask why safety stock is above target
To announce a new discount for customers
questions.explanation: She opens by asking why safety stock is forty percent above target.

questions.q: When is the review meeting?
options: On Monday afternoon
At the end of the month
In three months
On Tuesday at nine
questions.explanation: Dana asks for the plan before the review on Tuesday at nine.

questions.q: Why was there too much stock?
options: A supplier delivered twice by mistake in March
A tender was smaller than the forecast expected
Sales dropped after a discount
The southern region cancelled its order
questions.explanation: Chris says the forecast jumped because of a tender that turned out smaller.

questions.q: What will Chris send Dana before the review?
options: A list of southern customers
A new sales forecast
A short plan to reduce the stock
A discount offer for the sachets
questions.explanation: Dana asks for a short plan and Chris says he will send it on Monday.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hello, Lucia? Sorry, you're breaking up. I only caught a few words. Can you repeat the main points?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Sure, I'll go slowly. Is this better? The customer wants to move the delivery by two weeks.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Better, yes. Did you say two weeks earlier, or later?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Later. They changed their launch date, so the shipment would leave in two weeks instead of this Monday.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Understood. And the price? I thought I heard you mention twenty-five percent.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes. Your quote said rates go up by twenty-five percent after the end of the month, and a two-week delay would push us past that date.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Right, that's true. But if you confirm the original slot, I can keep the old rate.

script.speaker: B
script.line: The problem is I can't confirm yet. The customer's logistics head hasn't approved the new date, and he's travelling until Monday.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Ah, so the decision depends on him.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Exactly. Until he answers, I can't say whether we keep the slot or move it.

script.speaker: A
