script.line: Could you hold the old slot until Monday? It's only a few days.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, but I'll need it in writing. Could you send an email with all the numbers after this call?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Of course. I'll write it right after we hang up, and I'll update you on Monday once he replies.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Then I'll hold the slot until Monday evening. Thanks, Lucia.

questions.q: What is the conversation mainly about?
options: A change in the customer's price list for March
A problem with Lucia's phone line and the signal
A possible shipment delay and its effect on price
A new carrier for the customer's next shipment
questions.explanation: They discuss moving the shipment by two weeks and the higher rate that would follow.

questions.q: Until when will Lukas hold the original slot?
options: For two weeks
Until Monday evening
Until the end of the month
Until Lucia sends the email
questions.explanation: He finally says he will hold the slot until Monday evening.

questions.q: Why can't Lucia decide yet?
options: Lukas has not confirmed the new rate to her
The customer cancelled the whole shipment
The customer's logistics head has not approved yet
She cannot hear Lukas on the phone line
questions.explanation: She says the logistics head hasn't approved and is travelling until Monday.

questions.q: What will Lucia do after the call?
options: Send an email with all the numbers
Call the logistics head
Confirm the new date to the customer
Change the rate with the carrier
questions.explanation: Lukas asks for an email with the numbers, and she says she will write it right after the call.

title: Telling the committee about the slip

script.speaker: A
script.line: Arjun, thanks for calling. I understand there's an issue with the rollout schedule.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes. The data migration is behind, and I think we'll slip by two weeks. The go-live was the 8th of January, so now it would be the 29th.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hmm, two weeks from the 8th is the 22nd. Is it the 22nd, or a longer slip?

script.speaker: B
script.line: You're right, my mistake. It's the 22nd, a Monday. I counted from the wrong week.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Okay. So what exactly caused the delay? I need to explain it to the steering committee.

script.speaker: B
script.line: The test environment was unavailable for six days, so the migration tests started late.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's a clear reason. I'd keep the message simple: one cause, a two-week slip, and a recovery plan. Committees don't like surprises.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Agreed. Should we mention the risk that it might slip further?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Yes, briefly. Say we'll know for sure after the first full test run. When is that?

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's planned for next Wednesday, if the test environment stays available.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good. I'll brief the committee on Thursday, so please send me a one-page summary by tomorrow evening.

questions.q: What is the call mainly about?
options: How to restart the data migration quickly
How to report a delay to the committee
How to choose a new test environment
How to change the go-live team members
questions.explanation: Olivia and Arjun agree what to tell the steering committee about the slip.

questions.q: What is the new go-live date?
options: The 29th of January
The 8th of January
The 15th of January
The 22nd of January
questions.explanation: Arjun first says the 29th, then corrects it to the 22nd.

questions.q: What will Arjun send Olivia?
options: A new test schedule for Wednesday
A slide for Monday morning
A one-page summary by tomorrow evening
A list of committee members
questions.explanation: Olivia asks for a one-page summary by tomorrow evening.

title: Checking batch records before the audit

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hi Marta, it's Ben. I'm calling about next month's internal audit. Do you have a moment?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Hi Ben, yes. Is it the documentation check?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Exactly. I need someone to check that our batch records are up to date. We have about one hundred and twenty batches from the last quarter.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's quite a lot. What do you need exactly?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Just a quick sample, forty percent of them, so about fifty records, to see if signatures and dates are complete.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I'd love to help, but I'm still buried in the supplier files, and my manager keeps adding new tasks.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I understand. Is there anyone in your team who could do it?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Juan has done it before, and he's quicker than me. I'll ask him today and let you know tomorrow.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Perfect. And who should answer questions about training records? Is that you or Juan?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Me. I know that area well, so I'll take training and storage, and Juan can handle the batch records if he agrees.

questions.q: Why does Ben call Marta?
options: To ask for help checking records before an audit
To report a problem with the training records
To ask about the supplier files and their status
To cancel the audit planned for next month
questions.explanation: He says he needs someone to check that the batch records are up to date.

questions.q: About how many records should be checked?
options: About one hundred and twenty
About forty
About fifty
About twelve
questions.explanation: Ben wants a sample of forty percent, so about fifty records.

questions.q: Why does Marta not take the task herself?
options: She does not know the batch system
She is on holiday next month
She prefers to answer training questions only
She is too busy with other work
questions.explanation: She says she is buried in the supplier files and her manager keeps adding tasks.

questions.q: What will Marta do today?
options: Check fifty records herself
Update the training records
Ask Juan if he can do the check
Call the auditors
questions.explanation: She says she will ask Juan today and let Ben know tomorrow.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Henrik, I'm calling about the excipient shipment. It's now five days late, and my production plan for next week depends on it.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I know, Camila, and I apologise. We had a problem on our blending line, and the batch failed an internal check.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's the third delay in three weeks. I need to understand what's different this time.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Fair question. The cause was a faulty sensor, which has been replaced. I'm confident it won't repeat.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I hope so. What can you deliver, and when?

script.speaker: B
script.line: I can't send everything at once. What I can do is a split: sixty percent on Thursday, and the rest on the 10th of May.

script.speaker: A
script.line: The 10th is too late for the second part. My line stops before then. Could the remainder arrive by the 3rd of May?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Only if you accept smaller drums for the first part, because we can fill smaller drums faster.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Smaller drums are fine, although they cost us more to handle. I'll accept if you cover the extra freight.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Agreed, I'll cover the freight. I'll send you the new delivery schedule in writing today.

questions.q: What caused the delay?
options: A strike at the port that blocked trucks
A shortage of raw materials at the plant
A faulty sensor on the blending line
A mistake in the order from the customer
questions.explanation: Henrik says the cause was a faulty sensor, which has been replaced.

questions.q: What will Henrik send today?
options: Smaller drums for the first part
The new delivery schedule in writing
A refund for the freight
A new quality report
questions.explanation: He says he will send the new delivery schedule in writing today.

questions.q: Why does Camila say "That's the third delay in three weeks"?
options: To show the problem keeps happening and she is annoyed
To thank Henrik for being so honest with her
To ask for a larger delivery this time
To suggest changing the delivery date again
questions.explanation: She is pointing to a repeated problem to challenge his confidence.

questions.q: What do they agree in the end?
options: One full delivery on the 10th of May with a discount
A discount on all of Camila's future orders
Cancelling the second part of the delivery
A split delivery, smaller drums and freight paid by Henrik
questions.explanation: They agree on a split, smaller drums for the first part, and Henrik covering the freight.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Camila, thanks for your time. I'd like to propose automating the weekly stock report. Right now I spend half a day on it.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Interesting. How much effort would it take? I assume you'd need the tech team.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Not much. I think I can build it myself in about eight weeks, working a few hours a week.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Eight weeks? That seems long for a simple report. Or do you mean eight weeks of full-time work?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Sorry, I wasn't clear. Eight weeks on the calendar, but only a couple of hours each week. In total, it's maybe two days.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Got it, that's much better. What about the risks? If the automation breaks, nobody sees the numbers.

script.speaker: A
script.line: True. I'd keep the manual version as a backup for the first month, and add a check that flags empty data.

script.speaker: B
script.line: And who maintains it when you're on holiday? That's what worries me.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good question. I'd document it and train one more planner, so there are always two people who understand it.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Okay, then I support it. Can you share a short plan before our two o'clock meeting tomorrow? I'll ask the tech team to review it.

questions.q: How much time per week will Omar spend building the report?
options: Half a day
Two days
A couple of hours
Full-time
questions.explanation: He clarifies it is eight weeks on the calendar but only a couple of hours each week.

questions.q: Why will Omar keep the manual version at first?
options: Because the tech team asked him to
Because the new report is too slow
To train a new planner in the process
As a backup in case the automation breaks
questions.explanation: He says he will keep the manual version as a backup for the first month.

questions.q: What will Omar share before the meeting?
options: A working prototype
The IT review
A short plan
A training document
questions.explanation: Camila asks him for a short plan before the two o'clock meeting tomorrow.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Mark, have you got a minute? I want to update you on the deviation we found during packaging yesterday.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Of course, go ahead. What happened exactly?

script.speaker: A
script.line: The label printer drifted, and some labels were stuck about three millimetres too low. We caught it at the visual check.

script.speaker: B
script.line: And how many cartons are affected, roughly?

script.speaker: A
script.line: About fifteen percent of the run of two thousand cartons.

script.speaker: B
script.line: And is the product itself affected, or only the label?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Only the label. The product inside is untouched, and the seals are intact. Still, we've put the cartons on hold until quality decides.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Sensible. What is the corrective action?

script.speaker: A
script.line: We recalibrated the printer, and from now on the operator checks the first carton every hour instead of every four hours.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good. When will we know what happens to those cartons? Our shipment leaves on Friday, and I'd hate to delay it.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Normally the decision would come on Thursday. But there's good news: the quality manager checked samples this morning and says we can relabel them by hand, with no investigation.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's a relief. Then the Thursday decision isn't needed, and the shipment can go as planned.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Exactly. A team of four will relabel the cartons tomorrow, and I'll send you a short report when they finish.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Great. Thanks, Priya. I'll tell customer service there's no change.

questions.q: What is the conversation mainly about?
options: A damaged shipment of cartons at the port
A labelling problem and what to do about it
A new label printer for the whole plant
A change in the shipping date for the customer
questions.explanation: Priya describes misplaced labels, the product status and the corrective action.

questions.q: When will the cartons be relabelled?
options: On Thursday
Tomorrow
On Friday
This morning
questions.explanation: Priya says a team will relabel them tomorrow.

questions.q: What will Priya do after the team finishes?
options: Tell customer service about the change
Recalibrate the printer
Send Mark a short report
Delay the shipment
questions.explanation: She says she will send Mark a short report when they finish.

questions.q: Why does Mark say "That's a relief"?
options: He is happy that the printer was replaced already
He is pleased that there was no deviation at all
He is relieved that the cartons will be destroyed
He is glad the shipment does not need to be delayed
questions.explanation: He says it right before noting the shipment can go as planned.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Henrik, let's go through the key suppliers before I hand over. I only have about thirty minutes, so I'll stick to the essentials.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Perfect. Which ones keep you up at night?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Two of them. The film supplier is reliable but proud, so never assume flexibility. The solvent supplier promises the world and delivers late about twelve percent of the time.

script.speaker: B
script.line: So I should double-check the solvent supplier's confirmations?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Always, and phone rather than email. They answer calls straight away, but emails can take days.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Noted. And the recurring problem you mentioned in your notes, the price renewal?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Right. The renewal is due on the 24th of November, and they want an increase. I haven't decided how to respond, because finance hasn't sent me the budget limit yet.

script.speaker: B
script.line: So that's something I'd inherit unresolved?

script.speaker: A
script.line: I'm afraid so. Once the finance partner gives you the number, you can negotiate. Until then, don't promise them anything.

questions.q: How often is the solvent supplier late?
options: About six percent of the time
Almost every time
About twelve percent of the time
Only in November
questions.explanation: Camila says they deliver late about twelve percent of the time.

questions.q: Why should Henrik phone the solvent supplier instead of emailing?
options: The supplier only accepts calls from senior managers
Phone calls get answered quickly, but emails take days
Emails are not allowed for price matters
Calls are cheaper than emails for the company
questions.explanation: Camila says they answer calls straight away, but emails can take days.

questions.q: What can we infer about the price renewal when Henrik takes over?
options: It will still be open, waiting for finance
It will already be signed before he starts
Camila will negotiate it herself after leaving
The supplier will drop the increase for now
questions.explanation: Camila has not decided, because finance has not sent the budget limit, so Henrik inherits it unresolved.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Claire, we need to plan the cold-chain shipment for the 11th of November. It's four hundred and fifty pallets, and the customer is strict about temperature.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Understood. What are we considering for packaging? Insulated boxes with gel packs, or active containers?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Active containers for the long leg, since they hold temperature for up to five days. Passive boxes are cheaper, but they only last two days.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Transit by road is three days, so passive boxes are out. What about delays at the border?

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's exactly why we need a backup carrier. The usual one has had two late loads this year.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I'd suggest the second carrier on standby, with a vehicle ready one day before departure.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Agreed. Who tracks the shipment in transit?

script.speaker: B
script.line: I can do it myself, using the temperature loggers. Alerts go to my phone if the temperature rises above eight degrees.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good. Let's confirm everything with the carriers and the customer. Can we meet to finalise on Monday at nine thirty, in the small meeting room?

script.speaker: B
script.line: On Monday I'm at the port with the customs agent. What about Tuesday at nine thirty, in my office?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Tuesday works, but my office has the bigger screen. Can we use that one?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Sure. Tuesday at nine thirty in your office.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Great. Please bring the carrier quotes, so we can decide on the backup straight away.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Will do. I'll also bring the logger specifications, so we can check the temperature range.

questions.q: For how long can active containers hold the temperature?
options: Up to two days
Up to five days
Up to three days
Up to one day
questions.explanation: Victor says they hold temperature for up to five days.

questions.q: Where and when will Victor and Claire meet?
options: Tuesday at nine thirty, in Victor's office
Monday at nine thirty, in the small meeting room
Tuesday at nine thirty, in Claire's office
Monday at the port with the customs agent
questions.explanation: After two changes, Claire agrees to Tuesday at nine thirty in Victor's office.

questions.q: Why does Claire ask about delays at the border?
options: To argue for using passive boxes instead
To change the date of the shipment
To ask for a different border crossing
To raise a risk a backup carrier would cover
questions.explanation: Victor replies that this is why they need a backup carrier.

questions.q: What is the conversation mainly about?
options: Choosing a new customs agent for the port
Planning a temperature-controlled shipment
Replacing a late carrier with a new one
Buying new loggers for the whole office
questions.explanation: They discuss packaging, transit time, a backup carrier and tracking.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Nora, do you have a minute? I read your request for the forecasting course, and before I approve anything I'd like to understand why it matters now.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Sure. It's a four-day workshop on probabilistic forecasting, and it targets exactly the slow-moving products where our current method keeps missing by a wide margin.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's relevant, I agree. What does it cost, and how long would you be away from the desk?

script.speaker: B
script.line: About eighteen hundred euros, and the sessions run from Tuesday to Friday. I'd ask a teammate to cover the weekly planning run while I'm out.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Eighteen hundred is more than the training budget allows this quarter, to be honest. Could the provider give a discount if we book early?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Possibly. Their website mentions a reduced rate for registrations before the end of the month, so I can ask them today.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good. Then here's what we do. You email the provider and send me the final price by Thursday, and I'll take the request to finance at nine o'clock that morning.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Perfect. I'll also write a one-page summary of how I'd use the course, so finance sees the benefit. It will be ready by Wednesday evening.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Even better. If the numbers work, you're booked, and the cover plan is the last thing we confirm.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Understood. I'll put the cover plan in the same email, so nothing is missing.

questions.q: By when does Nora need to send Omar the final price?
options: By Wednesday evening
By the end of the month
By Tuesday morning
By Thursday
questions.explanation: Omar says 'send me the final price by Thursday', while Wednesday evening is only for the summary.

questions.q: What will Omar do once he has the price?
options: Book the course himself
Take the request to finance
Ask the provider for a discount
Cover the weekly planning run
questions.explanation: Omar says he will 'take the request to finance' on Thursday morning.

questions.q: Why does Omar mention the training budget?
options: To show that the cost could be a problem
To tell Nora that her request is refused for now
To suggest a cheaper provider
To ask who will cover Nora's work
questions.explanation: He says eighteen hundred is more than the budget allows, so the price is a concern, not a refusal.

questions.q: What is the conversation mainly about?
options: Finding someone to replace Nora while she travels
Comparing two training providers
Getting a course approved and agreeing next steps
Planning next quarter's budget review
questions.explanation: Nora asks for approval of a course, and they end with clear steps and owners.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good morning, Sofia. You mentioned on the phone that there was a problem with one of the pallets?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, thank you for seeing me so quickly. Packaging noticed that the labels on one pallet show an expiry date a full month later than the real one.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That is serious, but I'm glad it was caught before dispatch. First, I'd like to place the whole pallet on quality hold so nobody moves it by mistake.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Understood. It already has a red tag. Can the team simply relabel it, or do we need a formal deviation first?

script.speaker: A
script.line: We do need the deviation, I'm afraid, but the rework itself is easy. If the line has a gap, relabelling could happen on Friday at half past one.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Friday works, the line is free after lunch. One small problem, though: the printer is nearly out of ink, and the new cartridge arrives only on Thursday.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Then let's not leave it to chance. Please test the printer on Thursday afternoon, and call me straight away if the cartridge is late.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Of course. And the shipment was due out on the eighth of September. Should I warn the customer team?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Not yet. I expect the rework will fit inside that date, so I'll update you after Friday's slot.

questions.q: Why did Sofia come to see Adam?
options: To ask for a longer shelf life on a product
To report mislabelled stock and agree how to fix it
To request money for a new label printer
To cancel a shipment to a customer
questions.explanation: Sofia says the labels on one pallet show the wrong expiry date, and they plan the rework.

questions.q: When is the relabelling planned?
options: Thursday afternoon
The eighth of September
Friday at half past one
Friday morning, before the lunch break
questions.explanation: Adam says relabelling could happen 'on Friday at half past one'.

questions.q: Why does Adam ask Sofia to test the printer on Thursday?
options: Because the deviation needs a signed test page
Because the customer wants to see a sample
Because the pallet must leave on Thursday
Because ink could run out before the rework
questions.explanation: Sofia says the printer is nearly out of ink and the cartridge comes Thursday, so Adam wants it checked beforehand.

questions.q: What does Adam think about the shipment date?
options: He expects it can still be kept
He thinks it will slip by a month
He wants the customer told today
He believes the deviation will be refused
questions.explanation: Adam says the rework 'will fit inside that date' and tells Sofia not to warn the customer yet.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hi Dana, I'm calling about my new laptop. I saw in the chat that it's ready, but I'm not sure what happens to my files.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Hi Mateo, yes, it's ready for pickup. Everything on your old laptop is copied over automatically, apart from the personal apps, and then we wipe the old machine.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Wait, you wipe the local folder? I keep about forty batch reports there, and they aren't saved anywhere else.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Oh, sorry, I wasn't clear. The wipe only happens on the old laptop, after the transfer. Your new one receives the local folder too, including the forty reports.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Ah, I see. So nothing is lost, it just gets cleaned from the old machine at the end.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Exactly. The copy takes about two hours, so start it when you arrive. The new laptop is also about twenty-five percent faster, so expect smoother spreadsheets.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's good news, my planning files are really heavy. When do I have to hand back the old one?

script.speaker: B
script.line: By Thursday afternoon. After that the system flags it as missing and your manager gets an automatic email, which nobody wants.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Ha, no thanks. Can I still use the old one until then, if I need something?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, but only to look things up, because anything you save there after the transfer won't be copied.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Understood. I'll come down this afternoon, start the copy, and leave the old laptop with you on Thursday.

questions.q: By when must Mateo return the old laptop?
options: After the two-hour copy
Thursday afternoon
Tomorrow morning
As soon as he arrives
questions.explanation: Dana says to hand it back 'by Thursday afternoon'.

questions.q: Why is Mateo worried about the local folder?
options: Forty reports are saved only there
It is too big to copy in two hours
It contains his personal apps
His manager wants to read it
questions.explanation: Mateo says he keeps forty batch reports there 'that aren't saved anywhere else'.

questions.q: What will Mateo do next?
options: Keep saving files on the old laptop until Thursday
Email his manager about the deadline
Wipe the old laptop himself
Go to IT this afternoon and start the transfer
questions.explanation: At the end he says he will come down this afternoon and start the copy.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hi Samuel, it's Camila from supply planning. Thanks for taking the call. I know it's late where you are.

script.speaker: B
script.line: No problem, Camila. Your message said something about a risk, so I'm all ears.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Yes. Based on the current forecast and the supplier's lead time, we'll run out of the main product in about six weeks, unless we decide something this week.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Six weeks is not a lot. How sure are you about that number?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Quite sure. The supplier needs two weeks just to confirm a new order, and the northern region is ordering faster than we forecast.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I see. So what are you asking me to do?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Two things. First, could you move the spring promotion in the north to a later date, so demand stays lower for now?

script.speaker: B
script.line: I'm afraid I can't do that. I'd love to help, but let's just say that move would land badly with a few people who are watching that account closely.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Understood. Then the second option is to raise an urgent order with the supplier, but that needs your sign-off on the extra cost.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That I can work with. Can you send me the numbers? I'll review them with my director at two o'clock tomorrow.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I'll send a one-page summary within the hour, with the extra cost clearly shown.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good. And if my director agrees, I'll confirm to you straight after the meeting.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Perfect. Thanks, Samuel, and sorry again for calling so late.

questions.q: When will Samuel discuss the numbers with his director?
options: Within the hour
In two weeks, after the supplier answers
Tomorrow at two o'clock
In six weeks
questions.explanation: Samuel says he will review them with his director 'at two o'clock tomorrow'.

questions.q: Why is there a risk of running out of the product?
options: The supplier's factory closes for two weeks
The warehouse has no free space
Samuel cancelled a large order
Northern orders are growing faster than forecast
questions.explanation: Camila says 'the northern region is ordering faster than we forecast'.

questions.q: Why does Samuel refuse to move the promotion?
options: He thinks the forecast is too high for the northern region
The promotion was paid for in advance
It would upset people tied to an important customer
It has already ended
questions.explanation: He says the move 'would land badly' with people watching that account closely, which hints the customer is important.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good morning, Mei, and thanks for joining. I hear line two will be down for maintenance for three days.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good morning, Chris. Yes, from Monday. It's a bearing replacement that really couldn't wait any longer.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Understood. Could you tell me how much output we lose, so I know which orders have to move?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Our estimate is about thirty-five percent of the line's weekly output.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Forgive me, but that seems low. Three days out of five is sixty percent, so I would have expected a much bigger loss.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I see why you'd think so, but those three days are the quiet ones. Only one shift runs from Monday to Wednesday, while Thursday and Friday run two.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Ah, that's a fair point. Could you send me the schedule? I'd like to check it against our order book.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Of course. It's in your inbox. Take a look at the second tab.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Right, I have it open. You're correct, the lost hours add up to roughly a third of the week. That's better news than I feared.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good. And how many orders does that affect on your side?

script.speaker: A
script.line: About two hundred and forty order lines are due in that window. Most can wait until the following week, but I'd like to protect the urgent ones.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Then I'd suggest you flag the urgent ones today, and I'll try to fit them into the Thursday shift, so they ship before the twenty-seventh of July.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That works. I'll send you the list this afternoon, and thank you for being so open with the data.

questions.q: What is the call mostly about?
options: Deciding which orders to protect while a line is stopped
Asking for extra shifts on every line on a permanent basis
Complaining that maintenance was announced late
Reporting a quality problem on line two
questions.explanation: They discuss lost output and agree to protect the urgent orders during the stop.

questions.q: How many order lines are due in the affected window?
options: About thirty-five
About two hundred and forty
About three hundred and sixty
About one hundred and twenty
questions.explanation: Chris says 'about two hundred and forty order lines are due in that window'.

questions.q: Why is the loss smaller than Chris first thought?
options: The maintenance was shortened from three days to just two days last week
Other lines will take over the work
The line usually runs at half speed
Only one shift normally runs on the days of the stop
questions.explanation: Mei says only one shift runs from Monday to Wednesday, so fewer hours are lost.

questions.q: How does Chris feel after seeing the schedule?
options: Still doubtful about the thirty-five percent
Annoyed that Mei did not warn him sooner
Relieved that the impact is smaller
Worried that more orders must move
questions.explanation: Chris says 'That's better news than I feared', so he feels relieved.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hello Lukas, this is Yuki from the packing partner. I'm calling about last week's batch. Could you tell me the release date?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Hi Yuki. I can't give you a date yet, I'm afraid. The lab is still testing a five percent sample, and we expect the results on Thursday.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's a pity. About a hundred and twenty orders depend on this batch, so my customer is asking me every day.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I understand. There's also a documentation gap. The cleaning record is missing a signature from your side, and I can't release anything without it.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Oh, I didn't know. I'll ask my supervisor to sign it today and send you a scan.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good. The eight-week stability data is complete, so that part is fine. After the signed record and the lab results, I need one more day to review.

script.speaker: A
script.line: So could you at least promise a date for the end of the week?

script.speaker: B
script.line: I can't promise it, but I can send you an estimate tomorrow at noon, after I see the signed record.

script.speaker: A
script.line: OK, that helps. I'll send the scan this afternoon and wait for your message.

questions.q: What is the main situation in this call?
options: Yuki wants to change the number of orders
Lukas wants to return a batch to the packing partner for repacking
The lab has lost a sample
A batch is not released yet and Yuki wants a date
questions.explanation: Yuki asks for the release date, and Lukas explains why he cannot give one yet.

questions.q: When will Lukas send his estimate?
options: Tomorrow at noon
On Thursday
At the end of the week
This afternoon
questions.explanation: Lukas says 'I can send you an estimate tomorrow at noon'.

questions.q: Why can't Lukas release the batch now?
options: The eight-week stability data is incomplete
Testing is not finished and one record is unsigned
The customer cancelled the orders
The lab sample was too small to give a reliable result
questions.explanation: He mentions the lab is still testing and the cleaning record lacks a signature.

questions.q: What will Yuki do this afternoon?
options: Call the customer to explain the delay in detail
Send a scan of the signed cleaning record
Collect a new sample for the lab
Phone the lab for the results
questions.explanation: Yuki says 'I'll send the scan this afternoon'.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Lucia, sorry to interrupt, but I need your help with the packaging film. I'd like you to escalate it to the supplier's director.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Sure, sit down. Give me the facts first. What exactly is stuck?

script.speaker: A
script.line: The film was promised for the start of February. Nothing has arrived, and their account manager has been telling us 'next week' for three weeks now.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Three weeks of excuses. That's not good.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Sorry, let me correct that. It's four weeks. I counted from the first email, not the second.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Four weeks, then. And what's the impact if the film doesn't arrive?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Production of the main pack would stop on the fourteenth of March, and that pack is about twenty percent of our monthly volume.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Hmm, that's significant. I'm a little surprised nobody raised it earlier, but I'm glad you brought it to me now. I'll write to their director today.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Thank you. Should I send you the order history?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, and add the date of every promise they broke. Directors respond better to a clear timeline than to a complaint.

questions.q: What does Hugo want Lucia to do?
options: Look for a new film supplier in another country
Approve overtime on the line
Move the production date
Contact the supplier's director about the delay
questions.explanation: Hugo says 'I'd like you to escalate it to the supplier's director'.

questions.q: For how long has the supplier been saying 'next week'?
options: Three weeks
Two weeks
Four weeks
Twenty weeks
questions.explanation: Hugo corrects himself and says 'It's four weeks'.

questions.q: How does Lucia feel about the situation?
options: Slightly surprised, but willing to help
Angry with Hugo for waiting so long to tell her
Not worried about the delay
Amused by the supplier's excuses
questions.explanation: She says she is 'a little surprised' it was not raised earlier, yet she will write to the director.

questions.q: What does Lucia think is the best way to approach the director?
options: Phone him in person with a complaint
Offer him a longer contract
Threaten to stop all orders
Show a clear timeline of broken promises
questions.explanation: She says directors 'respond better to a clear timeline than to a complaint'.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hi Raj, it's Lucia. I just got back from the Lisbon trip, and I'm not sure how to file my expenses.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Hello Lucia. Easy enough. Upload every receipt over twenty-five euros to the portal, with a photo of the paper copy. Smaller ones fall under the daily allowance.

script.speaker: A
script.line: And the per diem? Do I claim it day by day?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, one line per day. The rate depends on the city, and any meal paid by the hotel gets deducted.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Got it. One thing worries me. I paid a hundred and twenty euros for taxis, and the driver only gave me a handwritten note.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That one will probably be rejected, I'm afraid. Handwritten notes aren't accepted. You'd need an official invoice.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I'll try asking the hotel, since they booked the cab. And what's the deadline for all this?

script.speaker: B
script.line: It was the twenty-ninth of January. But good news: finance has just moved it to the fifth of February because of a system update.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That changes my plan, then. I was going to stay late tonight to finish, but I'll do it on Monday instead.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Sensible. Just don't leave it to the last day, since the portal gets slow near the deadline.

questions.q: What is the call mainly about?
options: How to submit travel expenses correctly
Booking a hotel for the next trip
Changing the daily allowance rate
Fixing a problem with the portal
questions.explanation: Lucia asks how to file expenses and Raj explains receipts, allowances and the deadline.

questions.q: What is the final deadline for the expenses?
options: The twenty-ninth of January
The first of February
The fifth of February
Next Monday
questions.explanation: Raj says finance 'moved it to the fifth of February'.

questions.q: Why will the taxi expense probably be rejected?
options: It is more than the daily allowance for Lisbon
The only proof is a handwritten note
It was paid by the hotel
It was booked after the trip
questions.explanation: Raj says 'Handwritten notes aren't accepted'.

questions.q: What will Lucia probably do tonight?
options: Stay late to upload the receipts
Go home without finishing the expenses
Visit the finance office
Book another trip
questions.explanation: She says she will do the expenses on Monday instead of staying late tonight.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Adam, my VPN is driving me crazy. It keeps dropping whenever I'm in a video call from home.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Sorry to hear that. Does it happen on every call, or only on some?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Mostly the long ones. Yesterday I was kicked out of three meetings in a row, and I was presenting in one of them.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Ouch. Are you on wifi or on a cable?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Wifi. The router is in the living room and my desk is upstairs, so the signal isn't great.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That could be part of it. Let me check the logs. Yes, I can see your connection dropped about thirty percent of the time over the last week. That's high.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Then maybe my laptop is the problem. Could I get a new one?

script.speaker: B
script.line: I can't approve that, I'm afraid. The logs point to the wifi, not the laptop. I can switch your VPN server and order a network cable.

script.speaker: A
script.line: A cable would be fine. How long would it take to arrive?

script.speaker: B
script.line: It should reach you by Friday. I'll also log a ticket, so the network team can check the server on the third of March, when their maintenance window opens.

script.speaker: A
script.line: The third of March is a while away. Is there anything I can do before then?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Try the new server today, and call me on Monday if it still drops.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Will do. Thanks, Adam, that's a clear plan.

questions.q: What problem does Katarina report?
options: Her laptop will not start in the morning
She cannot log in to the office network
Her connection drops during video calls at home
Her router keeps changing its password
questions.explanation: She says the VPN keeps dropping when she is in a video call from home.

questions.q: How often did the connection drop last week, according to the logs?
options: About one time in three
Only during presentations
Once in each of three meetings
Every day at the same hour
questions.explanation: Adam says it dropped 'about thirty percent of the time'.

questions.q: What will Adam do for Katarina?
options: Approve a new laptop
Replace her home router
Ask her to work in the office on Friday
Change her server and order a cable
questions.explanation: He says he will move her to a different server and order a network cable.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Welcome back, Camila! Walk with me, and I'll catch you up on the way to the meeting. How was your leave?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Thanks, Ethan. Wonderful, but exhausting. So what did I miss? I heard there were changes in the organisation.

script.speaker: A
script.line: A few. Supply and demand planning now report to the same director, and the regional planners sit in one team.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Interesting. And the tools? I saw an email about a new planning platform.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Yes, it goes live in the spring. It will replace about forty percent of our spreadsheets, and training starts next month.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Forty percent is already a lot. I assume my first week will be mostly reading emails.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Not quite. I wanted you to present at tomorrow's priority review, but good news: the director postponed it to next week.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's a relief. What should I focus on, then?

script.speaker: A
script.line: The demand review for the new product launch. Read the summary I forwarded, and we'll go through it together on Friday morning.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Great, I'll read it tonight, and we can go through my questions then.

questions.q: What does Ethan say about the new platform?
options: It has been running in every region since last spring
It will replace around forty percent of the spreadsheets
It will replace every spreadsheet
It was cancelled by the director
questions.explanation: Ethan says it 'will replace about forty percent of our spreadsheets'.

questions.q: What will Camila do tonight?
options: Present at the priority review
Attend the platform training
Meet the new director
Read the summary Ethan forwarded
questions.explanation: She says she will read it tonight.

questions.q: Why does Ethan say 'good news' in the middle?
options: To announce that she has been chosen for a new role
To say the platform launch is cancelled
To tell her she has more time before presenting
To praise her for taking leave
questions.explanation: The good news is that the priority review was postponed to next week.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of the conversation?
options: Updating Camila on changes after her leave
Planning the dates of Camila's next period of leave
Training Camila on a new tool
Reviewing Camila's performance
questions.explanation: Ethan tells her about the organisation, tools and priorities she missed.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hi Camila, Ethan here from the supplier. I wanted to call you myself rather than send an email, because the news isn't great.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That already sounds ominous. Go ahead.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Starting next week, the minimum order quantity for the blue cartons goes up from six hundred to a thousand units. Our raw material supplier changed its batch size.

script.speaker: B
script.line: A thousand? That's a big jump for us. Which orders does it apply to?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Any order we receive after Tuesday falls under the new rule.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Then I'd like to place one more order under the old quantity. A thousand would leave us with far too much stock.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I understand. Let me check with my manager. Okay, good news: we can accept one last order at six hundred units, if it reaches us before Tuesday.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's great. In that case I'll bring my order forward and send it tomorrow instead of next week.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Perfect. Delivery would take around eight weeks, as always.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Fine. I'll also ask my team whether a thousand is manageable for the later orders.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Of course. And if your volumes stay low, we can talk about a shared storage option. Thanks for understanding, Camila.

questions.q: Until when can Camila order the old quantity?
options: Until the end of the quarter
Only until tomorrow
Until eight weeks from now
Until Tuesday of next week
questions.explanation: Ethan says the last order at six hundred must reach him 'before Tuesday'.

questions.q: Why is the minimum order quantity going up?
options: The raw material supplier changed its batch size
Demand for the blue cartons has fallen sharply this year
Ethan's company wants to cut costs
Camila's orders were too small last year
questions.explanation: Ethan says 'Our raw material supplier changed its batch size'.

questions.q: What will Camila do after the call?
options: Wait until after Tuesday
Send her order tomorrow
Ask for a thousand units
Cancel all future orders
questions.explanation: She says she will 'send it tomorrow instead of next week'.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Before we close, let me quickly recap the actions, if the audio holds. It keeps cutting out on my side.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I can hear you, Kenji, though you break up now and then. Please go ahead, and I'll shout if I miss something.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Thanks. First, the supplier review is on Thursday, and I'll send the invitation today. Second, Ana, you update the safety stock for the main products.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Sorry, one correction. The supplier review is on Wednesday, not Thursday, because their director travels then. You missed an action: someone should ask logistics about the ten-week lead time.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Right, thank you. Wednesday it is. I'll take the logistics question myself, since I know the contact. Now, the last point is the twenty percent price increase from the supplier.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, can we decide today whether to accept it?

script.speaker: A
script.line: I don't think so. We need the finance director's view on the margin, and she hasn't replied to my email yet.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Understood. Then let's park the decision, and I'll chase her office tomorrow so we can decide in the next meeting.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good plan. Thanks everyone, and sorry again about the poor connection.

questions.q: When will the supplier review take place?
options: On Thursday
On Friday
On Wednesday
Next month
questions.explanation: Ana corrects Kenji: 'The supplier review is on Wednesday, not Thursday'.

questions.q: Who will ask logistics about the lead time?
options: Ana
The finance director
The supplier's director
Kenji
questions.explanation: Kenji says 'I'll take the logistics question myself'.

questions.q: Why does Ana say 'Sorry, one correction'?
options: To tell Kenji she cannot hear him
To fix the day of the supplier review
To refuse the safety stock task
To add the price increase to the agenda
questions.explanation: Right after that phrase she changes Thursday to Wednesday.

questions.q: What happens with the price increase?
options: The team accepts it today with a small discount
The team rejects it today
The decision waits for the finance director's view
The supplier withdraws it
questions.explanation: Kenji says they need the finance director's opinion first, so they 'park the decision'.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Rachel, I see a full truck in bay three that nobody is unloading. What's going on?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good morning, Ibrahim. The goods arrived today, but we can't release them yet. The certificate of analysis in the paperwork doesn't look right.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Are you sure? I thought the supplier emailed all the documents last week.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I assumed that too, but let me check the log. Here: the certificate in the email is dated the eighth of June, and it belongs to the previous lot.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I see. So the batch number on it doesn't match this delivery.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Exactly. One digit is different, and quality won't accept that.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Understood. But production needs this material. About forty percent of Friday's plan depends on it.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I know, and I'm not happy about it either. Without the right certificate, quality won't let us use it, not even for a trial run.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Could we at least unload it into the quarantine area so the truck can leave?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, I can arrange that. I'll also call the supplier right now and ask for the correct certificate today.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good. Tell them we need it before three o'clock, because quality needs a few hours to review it.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Will do. If they can't manage it, I'll tell you immediately, and we can talk about moving some production.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Thank you, Rachel. I'll ask the production manager to be ready to adjust Friday's plan.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I'll send you an update as soon as I hear from the supplier.

questions.q: What is the main problem in this conversation?
options: Delivered goods can't be used because of a wrong certificate
The truck arrived at the wrong site on the wrong day
The supplier sent too many pallets
Production lost the delivery schedule
questions.explanation: Rachel explains the certificate belongs to the previous lot, so the goods can't be released.

questions.q: By what time does Ibrahim want the correct certificate?
options: By the eighth of June
On Friday morning
Tomorrow at noon
Before three o'clock today
questions.explanation: Ibrahim says 'we need it before three o'clock'.

questions.q: What will Ibrahim probably do if the certificate is late?
options: Release the goods anyway
Send the truck back to the supplier
Change the production plan
Ask quality to skip the review
questions.explanation: He says he will ask the production manager to be ready to adjust Friday's plan.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Thanks for picking up, Arjun. I read your note about last week's stockout. How are you feeling about it?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Honestly, a bit embarrassed. We ran out of the product on Monday, and customers started calling on Tuesday morning.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Let's not look for blame. Let's look for causes. What do you think went wrong?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Two things, I think. First, sales changed the forecast late, only three days before the order deadline, so I had no time to adjust.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Right. And what is the second thing?

script.speaker: B
script.line: We haven't reviewed safety stock for that product in over a year. The old level was too low for the new demand.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good, that matches what I see. So two actions: ask sales to send forecast changes earlier, and review safety stock every quarter.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That makes sense. Should I draft a short proposal?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Yes please. Let's go through it together. How about Thursday at a quarter to four, in my office?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Thursday is tricky, I have a supplier call then. Could we do Wednesday at the same time?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Wednesday I'm in the other building, so let's do it by video call instead.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Perfect. Wednesday at a quarter to four, by video. I'll send you the draft the evening before.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Great. And Arjun, thanks for being so honest. It helps the whole team.

questions.q: What are Rachel and Arjun doing?
options: Looking for the causes of a stockout and agreeing actions
Deciding which person in sales should be blamed for the stockout
Planning a promotion for next month
Training new planners on safety stock
questions.explanation: They discuss what went wrong and agree on two actions.

questions.q: When and how will they meet?
options: Thursday at a quarter to four, in Rachel's office
Wednesday at a quarter to four, by video call
Wednesday at a quarter to four, in the other building
Thursday at a quarter to four, by video call
questions.explanation: Rachel moves it to 'Wednesday' and 'by video call', which Arjun repeats.

questions.q: How does Arjun feel at the start of the call?
options: Angry at his manager
A bit embarrassed
Proud of his work
Not worried at all
questions.explanation: He says 'Honestly, a bit embarrassed'.

questions.q: What does the conversation suggest about the forecast change?
options: It was made only after the stockout had already happened
Arjun never received it
Arjun himself sent it too late
It came too late for Arjun to react
questions.explanation: Arjun says it came 'only three days before the order deadline'.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good afternoon, this is Amara at the supplier's customer service. How can I help you?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Hello Amara, Mateo here from the planning team. The delivery note for today's shipment says twelve hundred units, but our purchase order is for one thousand. Which one is correct?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Let me check. Yes, your order from the third of March says one thousand. The extra two hundred units look like a loading mistake on our side.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I see. We didn't ask for them, and our warehouse is quite full, so I'd rather not keep them.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Understood, and I apologise for the confusion. We'll invoice only the thousand, and we'll arrange to collect the extra two hundred units.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Thank you. To confirm, you'll send a corrected delivery note and a new invoice by Monday, and I'll keep the extra units apart until your carrier comes.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Exactly. I'll own the paperwork, and our logistics team will confirm the pickup date with you by Monday as well.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Perfect. I'll also tell the warehouse today, so nobody puts the extra units on the shelf.

questions.q: Why does Mateo call the supplier?
options: To find out which quantity is correct
To ask for a faster delivery of the extra units
To cancel the purchase order
To complain about the invoice price
questions.explanation: He asks 'Which one is correct?' about the two different quantities.

questions.q: How many units did Mateo actually order?
options: Twelve hundred
Two hundred
One thousand
Ten thousand
questions.explanation: Amara checks and says the order 'says one thousand'.

options: Defensive and unwilling to change anything
Apologetic and ready to help
Bored and in a hurry
Angry at the planning team
questions.explanation: She says 'I apologise for the confusion' and offers to collect the extra units.

questions.q: What can we conclude about the mistake?
options: Mateo typed the wrong quantity into the purchase order
The carrier lost two hundred units
The warehouse counted incorrectly
The supplier loaded more units than ordered
questions.explanation: Amara says the extra units 'look like a loading mistake on our side'.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Ingrid, thanks for seeing me. Your driver didn't show up for the pickup yesterday, and the pallets are still on our dock.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I know, and I apologise. We had a breakdown on the morning route, and we couldn't send a replacement in time.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I understand, but this is the second time this month. The customer expects the goods on the twenty-second of May, so I'd like a priority slot tomorrow morning.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Tomorrow morning isn't possible. All my morning slots are full, and I'd have to bump other customers. What I can offer is tomorrow at four in the afternoon.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's later than I wanted, and the goods would reach the customer a day late. Would you at least guarantee that slot?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, I'll put my name on it. And for the second miss, I can offer a twenty percent discount on this shipment.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I appreciate that, but a discount doesn't solve my problem. If it happens again, we'll have to review the contract, which still runs for ten weeks.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Fair enough. I'll make sure the driver calls you an hour before arriving, and I'll check the route myself.

questions.q: What does Lukas want from Ingrid?
options: A lower price for the rest of the contract this year
A bigger truck for the pallets
A new pickup time after a missed one
A change of the delivery address
questions.explanation: Lukas complains about the missed pickup and asks for a priority slot.

questions.q: When is the replacement pickup?
options: Tomorrow at four in the afternoon
Tomorrow morning
On the twenty-second of May
In an hour
questions.explanation: Ingrid says 'What I can offer is tomorrow at four in the afternoon'.

questions.q: What does Lukas imply at the end?
options: He may change carrier if it happens again
He is happy with the discount
The contract is already cancelled
He wants a much bigger discount if it happens again
questions.explanation: He says they 'will have to review the contract' if it happens again.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Is it just me, or does this screen still say 'waiting for the host'? We've been looking at it for five minutes.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Same here. And the room speakers are useless today. I tested them on Monday and they worked perfectly, so something must have changed.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Probably the software update last week. Let's connect the headset instead, and I'll ask IT to look at the speakers.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good idea. Do you know who's late? I thought the regional lead would be here by now.

script.speaker: A
script.line: She often is on Wednesdays. Her train gets in late, and she's only about three weeks into the new commute, so she's still learning.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Ah, that explains it. Well, while we wait, are you free for lunch? There's a new place that does good noodles.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Lovely, but I have a call with a supplier at noon. Maybe one o'clock?

script.speaker: B
script.line: One works. I'll book a table for two.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Oh, the meeting just opened. Finally! But now there's no video, only a grey square.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Let's join with audio only, since the agenda is short. Afterwards I'll email IT to check the room tomorrow at ten.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Perfect. Please copy me, so IT knows it's urgent.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Will do. Then lunch at one, and I'll try not to complain about the sound.

questions.q: What are Victor and Fatima mostly doing?
options: Presenting a new office to visitors
Dealing with technical problems while they wait for a meeting
Interviewing a candidate for a job in the planning team
Rehearsing a talk for a conference that starts next week in Boston
questions.explanation: They talk about the host not arriving, bad sound, no video and lunch.

questions.q: When will they have lunch?
options: At noon
Tomorrow at ten
At one o'clock
After the train arrives
questions.explanation: Victor agrees 'Maybe one o'clock?' and Fatima says 'One works'.

options: Pleased with the update
Indifferent to the problem
Embarrassed about her own mistake
Annoyed that they stopped working
questions.explanation: She calls them 'useless today' and says they worked on Monday.

questions.q: Why do they join the meeting with audio only?
options: The video does not work and the agenda is short
The regional lead asked them to join without video
They want to save the battery on both of their laptops
The speakers are too loud
questions.explanation: Victor notes the grey square and says 'the agenda is short'.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hannah, I have to talk to you about demand in the northern market. I think your forecast is too low.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Okay. Tell me what you're seeing. What makes you think so?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Three big hospital groups told me they plan to double their orders over the next ten weeks.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Did they confirm that in writing, or is it a verbal comment?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Verbal, so far. And I'm honestly stressed, because if I'm wrong we end up with too much stock, and if I'm right we run out.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I know, it's a difficult spot. Let me check the timing. When would the extra orders start?

script.speaker: A
script.line: From the beginning of next month. The contracts are signed at the end of this one.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good. The risk is that the number is too high. What if only one of the three goes ahead?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Then the increase would be much smaller. I'd say about half of what I told you.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Alright. Don't worry, Ben, we'll handle it. I'll build two scenarios, a high and a low, and you just get written confirmation from the hospitals.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Thanks, that takes some pressure off. I'll ask for emails this week.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good. Let's meet on Wednesday at nine to compare the scenarios and the emails.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Perfect. I'll see you then, and thanks for the help.

questions.q: When will Ben and Hannah meet again?
options: At the end of the month
At the beginning of next month
In ten weeks
On Wednesday at nine
questions.explanation: Hannah says 'Let's meet on Wednesday at nine'.

questions.q: What will Hannah do next?
options: Phone the three hospital groups to confirm the numbers
Prepare a high and a low forecast scenario
Sign the new contracts
Cut the northern forecast in half
questions.explanation: She says 'I'll build two scenarios, a high and a low'.

questions.q: Why does Hannah ask 'What if only one of the three goes ahead?'
options: To doubt that Ben really visited the hospitals last week
To find out when the contracts end
To test how risky the high number is
To suggest cancelling the forecast
questions.explanation: She says earlier that 'the risk is that the number is too high', and this question checks it.

questions.q: What is the main idea of the conversation?
options: Ben asks Hannah for a day off
Hannah explains to Ben how the forecast tool works in detail this week
They decide to stop the northern sales
Ben shares market input and they plan how to handle the uncertainty
questions.explanation: Ben gives demand input, and Hannah questions the evidence and agrees a plan.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Ibrahim, I need a second pair of eyes on an email to the supplier about the late delivery. Do you have five minutes?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Sure, read me the tricky part.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I wrote: 'You must deliver by the fifth of March, or we will cancel the order.' It sounds too aggressive to me.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, a bit. How about: 'We need delivery by the fifth of March, otherwise we will have to review the order.' Firm, but not hostile.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I like that. Should I also add something about compensation?

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's not my decision. It depends on our contracts manager, and she's away until Friday. I'd leave it out for now.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Makes sense. I'll send the email without it. When can we talk again to decide on compensation?

script.speaker: B
script.line: She's back on Friday, so let's call at half past one that day.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Perfect. I'll send the email now and put the call in my calendar.

questions.q: What are they mainly doing?
options: Improving the tone of an email to a supplier
Planning a visit to the supplier's factory early next month
Cancelling an order with a supplier
Translating a contract into English
questions.explanation: Olivia asks for help to make her email 'firm, but not hostile'.

questions.q: When will they talk about compensation?
options: On the fifth of March at noon
On Friday at half past one
Today at five minutes past
On Friday, early in the morning
questions.explanation: Ibrahim says 'let's call at half past one' on the day the manager is back, Friday.

questions.q: Why can't they decide on compensation now?
options: The supplier has not replied
Ibrahim does not like the idea
The contracts manager is away
The email was already sent
questions.explanation: Ibrahim says it depends on the contracts manager, who is away until Friday.

questions.q: What will Olivia do with the email?
options: Wait until Friday to send it with the compensation line
Ask the supplier to rewrite it
Send the first, stronger version
Send it without a line about compensation
questions.explanation: She says 'I'll send the email without it' and sends it now.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Pavel, I need to tell you something before the budget meeting. Travel is cut by twenty percent for the rest of the year.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Ouch. I was about to ask for three trips. Which ones can we keep?

script.speaker: A
script.line: The supplier audit has to stay, because it's a regulatory requirement. Everything else we should look at carefully.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I'd also like to go to the planning conference in Prague. It's good for networking.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I can't approve that one, I'm afraid. But there's an alternative: the organisers offer a virtual pass for a fraction of the price.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's something. And the quarterly review with the site in Poland? I'd normally fly there.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Let's switch it to a video call this time. If we really need a face-to-face, we can revisit it in six weeks, once the next budget opens.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Understood. So I keep the audit, move the review online, and attend the conference virtually.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Exactly. Can you send me a short list of the audit dates by Wednesday? I need to show finance that the remaining trips are fixed.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Sure. I'll also check whether the airline tickets for the audit can be changed without a fee.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good idea. Thanks for taking it so well, Pavel.

questions.q: What are Leila and Pavel deciding?
options: Which trips to keep after a budget cut
Who will manage the audit team in Poland next year
How to increase the travel budget
When to hire a new planner
questions.explanation: Leila announces the cut and they decide what to keep, change or replace.

questions.q: By when must Pavel send the audit dates?
