Before the budget meeting
By Wednesday
At the end of the year
questions.explanation: Leila says 'Can you send me a short list of the audit dates by Wednesday?'

questions.q: What does Leila think about the conference trip?
options: It is mandatory for the team
It is less important than the audit
It is too cheap to refuse
It was Pavel's own idea to cancel it
questions.explanation: She keeps the audit as a requirement but refuses the conference, offering a virtual pass.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Omar, I have a few questions about the forecast for the new pack. Do you have a minute while we walk?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Only until the meeting room, but go ahead.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Your file says the launch is on the first of the month, but marketing told me it moved by two weeks. Which is right?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Marketing is right, I haven't updated my file. I assume sales peak after eight weeks, since the new pack looks almost identical to the old one.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's a big assumption. I'd like to go through it properly. Can we meet on Tuesday at two, in my office?

script.speaker: B
script.line: I'm travelling on Tuesday afternoon, I'm afraid. Could we do Tuesday morning instead?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Mornings are full for me. What about Wednesday at two? My office is being painted, so we'd use the small meeting room.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Wednesday at two in the small meeting room works. I'll update the file before then.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good, and please bring the sales history of the old pack.

questions.q: Where and when will they meet in the end?
options: Tuesday at two in Priya's office, as first planned
Tuesday morning in the small meeting room upstairs
Wednesday at two in Priya's office
Wednesday at two in the small meeting room
questions.explanation: Priya proposes 'Wednesday at two' in the small meeting room and Omar accepts.

questions.q: Why does Omar expect sales to peak after eight weeks?
options: The old pack will be sold out soon
The two packs are almost identical
Marketing plans a big discount for customers who switch
The launch date moved earlier by two weeks
questions.explanation: He says the new pack 'looks almost identical to the old one', so sales should rise fast.

questions.q: What can we infer about Omar's forecast file?
options: It is still missing the sales history of the old pack
It was written by marketing
It does not show the correct launch date
It already includes the eight-week peak
questions.explanation: He says 'I haven't updated my file yet' after Priya notes the launch date is wrong.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good afternoon, Marta. Welcome to the new building. How was the flight from Madrid? I heard it was raining there.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Thank you, Pedro. It was grey and cold when I left, but it's lovely and sunny here. Quite a difference.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Yes, spring arrived early. Do the time zones cause you trouble with the call? Our colleagues in Boston join at a quarter to four our time.

script.speaker: B
script.line: It's fine for me, but it's early for them, so we should be quick. Honestly, I'm a bit nervous about the presentation. I've changed the slides three times today.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Don't worry, you know the material better than anyone. If you like, I'll open the call and introduce everyone, so you only start with the first slide.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That would help a lot, thank you. What do you think of the new office layout, by the way? Do you like the open space?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Mixed feelings. It's bright and modern, but it's noisier than the old floor. I think the quiet rooms on the third floor are the best part.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I agree. I tried one this morning, and it was ideal for preparing.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good. By the way, we have a team dinner on Thursday to welcome you, if you're free.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Thursday is perfect. I leave on Friday, so it's my last evening here.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Wonderful. And the official opening is on the third of March, so you've seen the place before everyone else.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Lucky me. Shall I plug in the laptop now, so we're ready when the others join?

questions.q: What is the conversation mostly about?
options: Friendly small talk before a call, including some nerves
A dispute about the new office layout
A plan to change the time of the call
Feedback on Marta's performance
questions.explanation: They chat about weather, time zones, the office and Marta's nerves.

questions.q: When is the team dinner?
options: On Thursday
On Friday
On the third of March
At a quarter to four
questions.explanation: Pedro says 'we have a team dinner on Thursday'.

questions.q: What will Pedro do at the start of the call?
options: Present the first slide
Join from a quiet room
Open it and introduce everyone
Change the slides
questions.explanation: He offers 'I'll open the call and introduce everyone'.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Right, Ibrahim, let's go through your three tasks, shall we? Where do things stand?

script.speaker: B
script.line: The inventory report is done, the supplier scorecard is about thirty-five percent complete, and the demand review for the new region hasn't really started.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Okay. And you mentioned a risk?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes. The demand review is due on Wednesday, and the scorecard is due on the third of July. I can't finish both, so I need a priority call.

script.speaker: A
script.line: The demand review matters more this week, because the regional director is reading it. Can the scorecard slip?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Maybe, but the supplier asked for it before the third of July. If it's late, they won't be happy.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Let's meet halfway. You do the demand review first, and I'll ask the supplier for three extra days, if you can cut the scorecard down to the five key measures.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Deal. I'll finish the review by Wednesday, then send you the short scorecard on Monday so you can pass it on.

questions.q: What is the main topic of the call?
options: Choosing a new supplier
Deciding which task comes first
Planning a holiday for the team
Fixing a mistake in the inventory report
questions.explanation: Ibrahim needs a priority call between two tasks, and they find a compromise.

questions.q: How complete is the supplier scorecard now?
options: Not started yet
Almost finished
Fully complete
About thirty-five percent
questions.explanation: He says it is 'about thirty-five percent complete'.

questions.q: What will Ibrahim do on Monday?
options: Present the demand review to the director
Send the shorter scorecard to Olivia
Ask the supplier for more time
Finish the inventory report
questions.explanation: He says he will send the short scorecard on Monday.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Samuel, we have a gap today. Marco is off sick, so I need someone to cover three things. Can you help?

script.speaker: B
script.line: I can try. What do you need?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Two supplier calls this morning and the weekly report for the director.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Okay. Which supplier calls do you mean?

script.speaker: A
script.line: The first one is about the delay of four hundred and fifty batches. It's urgent, and it's before lunch.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Honestly, I'd rather not take that one. The last time I spoke to that team, we ended the call very quickly.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I see. And the second call is about the delivery plan for the next six weeks. It's easier.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That one I can do. Who will take the first call, then?

script.speaker: A
script.line: I can do it myself. But then who writes the report?

script.speaker: B
script.line: I'll write it after lunch. I have a clash this morning, so I can't start before.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's fine. The director needs it by four.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Then I'll send it by three, so you can check it.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Great, thank you. I'll tell Marco's customers that you're helping.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Fine. And please send me last week's report as an example.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of the conversation?
options: Sharing out a sick colleague's work
Planning a visit to a supplier
Reviewing the weekly report together
Complaining about a late delivery
questions.explanation: Camila asks Samuel to cover Marco's calls and report, and they divide the tasks.

questions.q: When does the director need the report?
options: By three
Before lunch
This morning
By four
questions.explanation: Camila says 'The director needs it by four', while three is when Samuel will send it.

questions.q: Who will make the first supplier call?
options: Samuel
Marco
Camila
The director
questions.explanation: Camila says 'I can do it myself' after Samuel declines.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Ben, I'm glad I caught you. I wanted to tell you that your desk is moving to the fourth floor.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Oh, that's news to me. When does it happen?

script.speaker: A
script.line: It's scheduled for the twenty-ninth of July. The movers will start packing at nine thirty in the morning.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That soon? Will my monitor and docking station come with me, or is there new equipment?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Your equipment moves with you, and IT will reconnect everything by lunchtime. You don't need to touch the cables.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good. And who will be sitting next to me? I ask because I'm on calls a lot.

script.speaker: A
script.line: The finance analysts will be around you. They're quiet, and there are phone booths nearby for calls.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That sounds reasonable. Can I see the new desk beforehand?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Of course. I can show it to you on Tuesday afternoon. Oh, but I just remembered a small problem: your badge isn't activated for the fourth floor yet.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That would be awkward on the day. Can you fix it?

script.speaker: A
script.line: I'll ask security to activate it today, though they need two days. Let's check again on Tuesday.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Fine. If it isn't done by then, may I call you?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Yes, call me anytime. Thanks for being so flexible, Ben.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of the conversation?
options: Asking Ben to choose between two new desks on the fourth floor
Planning a team party on the fourth floor
Explaining new rules for phone calls
Informing Ben about a desk move and answering his questions
questions.explanation: Ingrid announces the move and answers questions about timing, equipment and neighbours.

questions.q: At what time will the movers start?
options: Lunchtime
Nine thirty in the morning
Tuesday afternoon
Two days after the badge request
questions.explanation: Ingrid says 'The movers will start packing at nine thirty in the morning'.

questions.q: What will Ingrid do about the badge?
options: Move Ben's desk herself
Order a new badge from IT
Ask security to activate it
Cancel the move
questions.explanation: She says 'I'll ask security to activate it today'.

questions.q: Why does Ingrid mention the finance analysts?
options: To answer Ben's question about his neighbours
To warn him about noise
To explain who will move his equipment
To suggest he joins their team
questions.explanation: Ben asks who will sit next to him, and she says 'The finance analysts will be around you'.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Jon, I'm booking your hotel for the audit visit on the nineteenth of April. There's a small, quiet place a short walk from the supplier's site.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Sounds good. Does breakfast come with it?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Yes, it's included, from half past six. And it's a ten minute walk to the site, so no taxi needed.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Great. What about cancellation? The audit date might move, and last time the visit slipped by eight weeks.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Free cancellation up to forty-eight hours before. Check-in is from two in the afternoon, but you'll probably arrive earlier.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Actually, I'd prefer something closer to the airport. Could you check the big chain hotel?

script.speaker: A
script.line: I could, but I'd rather not. Remember your last trip there? You told me all about the shuttle, and not in a good way.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Ha, fair point. Let's keep the small hotel, then. Please send me the confirmation today.

questions.q: From what time can Jon check in?
options: From half past six
From the nineteenth of April
From two in the afternoon
From forty-eight hours before
questions.explanation: Elena says 'Check-in is from two in the afternoon'.

questions.q: How does Jon feel at the end?
options: Amused and persuaded
Annoyed with Elena
Worried about the cost
Disappointed about the audit
questions.explanation: He laughs, says 'fair point' and agrees to keep the small hotel.

questions.q: What does Jon ask Elena to do?
options: Check the chain hotel near the airport
Move the audit by eight weeks
Book a taxi for each day
Send him the confirmation today
questions.explanation: At the end he says 'Please send me the confirmation today'.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hi Ben, welcome to the team. Let's build your first thirty days together. Is this a good time to talk?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, it's perfect. Thanks, Ingrid. I'm excited to start on the twenty-ninth of September.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Great. In week one, I'd like you to meet the supply planners and the quality lead. Then you'll read the forecast process document.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Okay. Should I also prepare a ten-week forecast for all products in the first week? I wasn't sure what you expected.

script.speaker: A
script.line: No, no, that's far too much. The ten weeks is the horizon of our weekly report, not your deadline. I'd start with something much smaller.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Ah, I see. Thanks for clarifying.

script.speaker: A
script.line: For your first small project, I'd like you to own the review of one slow-moving product, which sells about three hundred units a month.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That sounds manageable. What should the outcome be?

script.speaker: A
script.line: A one-page proposal on whether our safety stock is right. You'd present it at the end of the first month.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Understood. Will I have someone to ask when I'm stuck?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Of course. I'll introduce you to a planner who has done this before.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of the call?
options: Interviewing Ben for the planning role he applied for
Planning Ben's first month in the job
Reviewing last year's forecast
Choosing a new safety stock policy
questions.explanation: Ingrid and Ben 'build your first thirty days together'.

questions.q: What does 'ten weeks' refer to?
options: The length of Ben's first project
The time until his first review
The horizon of the weekly report
The age of the product
questions.explanation: Ingrid says 'The ten weeks is the horizon of our weekly report, not your deadline'.

questions.q: What does Ingrid want for Ben's first week?
options: A light start with meetings and reading
A full forecast for every product
A presentation to the directors
A review of all the safety stock
questions.explanation: She plans meetings and reading, and says a ten-week forecast is 'far too much'.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Ana, can you hear me? The line's breaking up. I'm calling about the urgent order for the clinic, and frankly, I'm at my wits' end.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I can hear you, just about. Take a breath, Kenji, and let me pull it up. Which order is it?

script.speaker: A
script.line: The one that was meant to go out at nine this morning. Nobody's told me anything, and the customer has rung twice. They only started ordering eight weeks ago.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Right, I've found it. It was picked on time, but it's sitting at the dock because the carrier hasn't collected. I won't sugarcoat it: it won't leave before this afternoon.

script.speaker: A
script.line: This afternoon? That leaves us on the back foot with the customer. They were counting on tomorrow.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Realistically, the earliest they'd receive it is the day after tomorrow. About thirty-five percent of orders on this route arrive a day late, so I wouldn't promise tomorrow.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Fair enough. Better to be honest than to overpromise. I'll let them know. Can you chase the carrier?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Leave that with me. I'll call the dispatcher straight away and get back to you within the hour, and I'll ask for a priority slot.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Thank you, Ana. That takes a weight off my shoulders.

script.speaker: B
script.line: No problem. Try not to worry, we'll sort it out.

questions.q: What is the main situation in this call?
options: Ana complains to Kenji about a late payment from the clinic
Kenji is worried about a delayed urgent order and Ana reassures him
Kenji and Ana choose a new carrier for all of the clinic orders
Ana asks Kenji to place an order
questions.explanation: Kenji is 'at my wits' end' and Ana checks the order and calms him.

questions.q: At what time should the order have left?
options: This afternoon
Within the hour
The day after tomorrow
Nine this morning
questions.explanation: Kenji says it 'was meant to go out at nine this morning'.

questions.q: What will Ana do next?
options: Send the order by taxi
Phone the clinic herself
Ask Kenji to chase the carrier while she checks the stock
Call the carrier's dispatcher and report back soon
questions.explanation: She says 'I'll call the dispatcher straight away and get back to you within the hour'.

questions.q: Why does Ana say 'I won't sugarcoat it'?
options: To offer a better delivery date
To show she will give bad news honestly
To blame the carrier for the delay in front of the clinic
To end the call quickly
questions.explanation: She follows it with the unwelcome news that the order will not leave before the afternoon.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Tomas, welcome to the site. I understand you want to talk about the delivery date.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Thank you, Marta. Yes. Our warehouse is full, so we'd like to push our delivery from the original Wednesday slot to the seventeenth of October.

script.speaker: A
script.line: A week later. That isn't easy for us, but let's hear the reason.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Honestly, we're about forty percent above our normal stock level, because a big batch was released early. We simply have no free pallet places.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I see. And what would you do with the pallets in the meantime? Keep them at our depot?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, if you can hold them for a week, we'd be very grateful.

script.speaker: A
script.line: We can do that, but not for free. What would you offer in return?

script.speaker: B
script.line: We could commit to a larger order in November, and we'd pay the storage cost for the extra week.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Paying the storage is only fair. I can hold perhaps half of the pallets. You know what our depot looks like during inventory week.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I see. And the other half?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Let's deliver that on Wednesday as planned, and the rest on the seventeenth of October.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That works for us. Thank you for being flexible.

questions.q: What is the main topic of the conversation?
options: Marta asks Tomas to pay an old invoice before any new delivery
They plan a new warehouse for the northern region
Tomas asks for a later delivery and they find a compromise
Tomas cancels the order
questions.explanation: Tomas asks to push the delivery, and they agree to split it.

questions.q: What does Tomas offer in return?
options: A larger order in November and the storage cost
Early payment of the next two invoices and a small bonus
Collecting the pallets himself
A discount on the next delivery
questions.explanation: He says 'a larger order in November' and that they would pay the storage cost.

questions.q: How does Marta approach the request?
options: Cooperative, but with limits
Completely against it
Careless about the details
Eager to accept everything at once
questions.explanation: She agrees on storage costs but only holds half of the pallets.

questions.q: Why can't Marta hold all the pallets?
options: Her depot is being rebuilt
Her depot will be busy with inventory
The pallets are too heavy
Tomas refuses to pay for the extra week of storage
questions.explanation: She hints 'You know what our depot looks like during inventory week'.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hugo, thanks for meeting. The national holiday is on the Monday after, and I want to fix the delivery window before it.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Right. Our trucks are fully booked on Thursday, and traffic is heavy on Friday before a long weekend. What window do you need?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Ideally Thursday morning, between eight and eleven. The customer closes early on Friday, so a Friday delivery is risky.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Thursday morning works for us, then. As a backup, what about the Tuesday after the holiday?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Tuesday is fine. Only about eight percent of the volume, the urgent orders, would need the backup day.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Understood. I'll need the final pallet list by Wednesday at noon.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Done. And can you confirm the truck and driver by that evening?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, I'll confirm both by Wednesday evening. It's a tight week, but the contract has twelve weeks left, so I'd like to keep it smooth.

questions.q: Which delivery window do they agree for before the holiday?
options: Friday morning before the customer closes
Tuesday after the holiday
Wednesday at noon
Thursday between eight and eleven
questions.explanation: Mei asks for 'Thursday morning, between eight and eleven' and Hugo agrees.

questions.q: Why does Mei avoid Friday?
options: Trucks are broken down on Friday
The holiday is on Friday
The customer closes early that day
Hugo is on leave on Friday
questions.explanation: She says 'The customer closes early on Friday'.

questions.q: What will Hugo do by Wednesday evening?
options: Confirm the truck and driver
Send the pallet list
Deliver the urgent orders on the backup day
Review the holiday terms
questions.explanation: He says 'I'll confirm both by Wednesday evening'.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hi Olivia, thanks for asking for this call. You wrote that you want to talk about your career. What's on your mind?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Hi Mark. I'd like to move into a more strategic planning role one day. I enjoy the data, but I want to join the longer-term decisions.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's a good goal. For that role, you need two things: skills in scenario planning, and visibility with senior people.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Visibility is hard for me. I mostly work behind the scenes.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I know. What if I give you a stretch project? You would lead the review of our safety stock policy for eight weeks and present the result to the directors.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That sounds great, but I'm worried about the time. I already spend twenty percent of my week on the monthly report.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I understand. What could you give up?

script.speaker: B
script.line: I could hand the monthly report to a junior colleague, but only after I train him. That would take two weeks.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Okay. I can accept a later start, after the training, if you agree to present to the directors yourself and not only to me.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Okay, that's a bit scary, but I agree.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good. I'll write a short description of the project and send it to you.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Thanks! I'll also look for an online course on scenario planning.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Excellent idea. I'll approve the budget if it's cheap.

questions.q: How long would the stretch project last?
options: Two weeks
Eight weeks
Twenty weeks
One year
questions.explanation: Mark says 'for eight weeks'.

questions.q: Why is Olivia worried about taking the project?
options: She does not enjoy working with data and numbers every day
The project has no budget
The monthly report already takes a fifth of her week
She wants to stay in her current role
questions.explanation: She says 'I already spend twenty percent of my week on the monthly report'.

questions.q: What does Mark want for Olivia's career?
options: A move to a junior role
Less contact with the directors
A permanent end to the monthly report
More visibility with senior people
questions.explanation: He says she needs 'visibility with senior people' and sets up a project to present to the directors.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Chris, have you got a second? I need to move our review meeting. The director has called me into something tomorrow morning.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Of course. Tomorrow at ten is our current slot, right? What did you have in mind?

script.speaker: A
script.line: I was hoping to do it today, at half past four. Does that work for you?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Ah, I'd rather not, to be honest. I have to be at the school gate by five, and the traffic around there is terrible.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Understood, no problem. Then what about first thing tomorrow, at eight? Before the director's meeting.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Eight is early for the team, but I can do it if we keep it short. We'd have to cover the six-week outlook and the open risks.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Twenty minutes should be enough for that. If we run over, we can finish on a call later.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Fine. Should I send the slides tonight, so you can read them first?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Yes, please. Send them by eight this evening, and I'll look at them over dinner.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Done. And can you tell the others about the new time? I don't want anyone to miss it.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I'll send a message right now. Why don't I do it as we walk?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Perfect. Just say it's eight o'clock sharp, in the usual room.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Will do. Thanks for being flexible, Chris.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Anytime. Thanks for asking before just changing it.

questions.q: What time is the review meeting finally?
options: Tomorrow at ten, as in the original plan
Today at half past four, as Aisha first asked
Tomorrow at eight in the morning
Tonight at eight
questions.explanation: Aisha proposes 'first thing tomorrow, at eight' and Chris agrees.

questions.q: What will Chris do tonight?
options: Tell the others about the new time
Send his slides by eight
Meet the director
Pick up Aisha from dinner
questions.explanation: Aisha asks 'Send them by eight this evening' and Chris says 'Done'.

questions.q: Why does Chris say he has to be at the school gate by five?
options: To ask Aisha to come and meet him at the school gate
To complain about the traffic near the office at five
To suggest moving the meeting to five
To politely explain why he can't meet at half past four
questions.explanation: It is his polite reason for refusing the half past four slot.

questions.q: What is the conversation mainly about?
options: Finding a new time for a meeting
Preparing slides for the director and the whole team
Planning school pickup times
Cancelling the review meeting
questions.explanation: Aisha needs to move the meeting and they agree on a new time.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hi Katarina, it's Jon, your buddy for the first weeks. Welcome! Are you in the building yet?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Hi Jon! Yes, I'm at reception, but my badge isn't ready.

script.speaker: A
script.line: No problem, I'll come down. In the meantime, let me explain the week. Every Monday at eleven we have a short planning meeting, about thirty minutes.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good. What tools do I need to learn?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Mainly the planning system and a shared tracker. Don't worry, you'll get training. Last year, new colleagues took about six weeks to feel comfortable.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That sounds fine. Can I get access to everything today? I'd like to start reading.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Not everything. The finance reports need your manager's approval, which takes a day or two. But you can use the planning tool now, and read last month's report.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's a good alternative. And lunch? Is there a canteen?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Yes, on the second floor. It's cheap, and the company pays about eighteen percent of your lunch. Most of us go at half past twelve.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Great, I'll join you. Is there a quiet place to work afterwards?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Yes, small rooms on the third floor. I'll show you after lunch.

questions.q: What is the call about?
options: Planning a team lunch for the new colleague and her buddy
Orienting a new colleague on her first day
Solving a badge problem with security
Training Katarina on a new report
questions.explanation: Jon explains the meetings, tools, access and lunch to a new colleague.

questions.q: When is the weekly planning meeting?
options: Monday at eleven
Half past twelve
After six weeks
Monday after lunch
questions.explanation: Jon says 'Every Monday at eleven we have a short planning meeting'.

questions.q: Why can't Katarina get access to everything today?
options: The planning tool is broken and cannot be used today
Her badge is not ready
The finance reports need her manager's approval
Training has not started yet
questions.explanation: Jon says 'The finance reports need your manager's approval, which takes a day or two'.

questions.q: What will Jon do first?
options: Show her the third floor
Send her the monthly report
Book a table for lunch
Come down to reception
questions.explanation: He says 'I'll come down' right after she says she is at reception.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good morning, Mei, thanks for seeing me. I'm afraid I have bad news: our cartons will go up by six percent from the first of next quarter.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I see. That's quite a jump, Kenji. Before I take it to my director, could you explain what is driving it? Is it the board price?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Mainly the paperboard itself, plus higher energy costs at our mill. We've held the price for two years, but we simply can't absorb any more of it.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I understand, though it does put us in a difficult position. Would you consider a three-month transition, so we can finish our budget cycle before the new price applies?

script.speaker: A
script.line: I can't promise that without approval, but I think it's reasonable. Let me check with head office on Monday, and I'll email you the answer that afternoon.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That would help a lot. On another note, the forty units of the new tray that arrived yesterday have a printing fault on the lid. The logo is slightly off-centre.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Oh, I'm sorry to hear that. Could you send me photos and the delivery note? I'll ask our quality team to look at them before we speak again on Monday.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Of course, I'll send them this afternoon. Perhaps we can cover both points in a short call on Tuesday morning, once you've heard from head office.

questions.q: When will Kenji give Mei an answer about the transition period?
options: On Monday afternoon
On Tuesday morning
Later today
Yesterday evening
questions.explanation: Kenji says he will check with head office on Monday and email the answer that afternoon.

questions.q: Why is the price going up?
options: A new import tax on packaging film
A redesign of the tray lids this year
Higher board and energy costs
Mei's company ordering smaller volumes
questions.explanation: Kenji says it is mainly the paperboard plus higher energy costs at the mill.

questions.q: What will Kenji do about the printing fault?
options: Replace all forty units straight away
Have quality look at it once photos arrive
Cancel the price increase for the trays
Visit Mei's warehouse on Tuesday
questions.explanation: Kenji asks for photos and the delivery note and says the quality team will look at them.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hi Ethan, can you hear me? The sound is not great on my side. I wanted to talk about the reorganization that was announced this morning.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I can hear you, but you keep cutting out. Yes, I read the email. Our planning team will join the supply group, so we will get a new manager.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's what I understood too. But I think the change starts next Monday, and nobody has told us who will do our weekly reports.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Sorry, I think it starts in four weeks, not on Monday. I remember the email said Monday is only when the new manager meets everyone.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hmm, I'm not sure. Let me open the email again. I'm sharing my screen now. Can you see it?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, now it works. It says the new structure starts four weeks from today, and the first team meeting is on Monday. So we were both a little right.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Okay, thanks for checking. So we have some time. But what is still unclear is who will approve our holiday requests during the change.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good point. Maybe we should not guess. Let's write down our questions and send them to our manager before the meeting.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Agreed. I can write the list today if you add the question about the weekly reports.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Sure, I'll add it tonight. Then we can read the final list together on Friday morning.

questions.q: What are the two colleagues mainly doing in this conversation?
options: Preparing a presentation for the new manager
Testing the audio quality of the video call
Deciding who will write the weekly reports
Comparing notes and planning questions
questions.explanation: They compare what they understood from the email and agree to send their open questions to the manager.

questions.q: When does the new structure start?
options: Next Monday
Tomorrow morning
Four weeks after today
On Friday
questions.explanation: Ethan reads that the structure starts four weeks from today, and Monday is only the first team meeting.

questions.q: Why does Elena share her screen?
options: To show the email with the start date
To fix the sound problem on the call
To present the weekly report to Ethan
To show the new manager's profile to Elena
questions.explanation: Elena says she will open the email again and share her screen so Ethan can see it.

questions.q: What will Ethan do tonight?
options: Write the whole list of questions today
Send the finished list to the manager
Call the new manager about holidays
Add the reports question to the list
questions.explanation: Elena will write the list, and Ethan says he will add the weekly reports question tonight.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Thanks for staying behind, Chloe. You seemed a little quiet in the supplier meeting. Is something on your mind?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Honestly, yes. I get nervous when I have to speak English in big meetings. I know the content, but I freeze and lose my words.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's more common than you think, and your written updates are always sharp. It helps to send your notes round before the meeting, so people know your point.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I could try that, but I don't think it solves the problem. In the last meeting I barely said anything, so people probably think I have nothing to add.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Well, let's check. The meeting summary is open on my laptop. It shows you spoke six times, and one of your points led to the decision on safety stock.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Really? That's more than I remembered. It felt like I only said two things, and badly.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Exactly. So here's a small goal for the next two weeks: ask one question in every meeting, nothing more. Pick it from the agenda the day before.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That sounds manageable. Could we practise before Thursday's review? It starts at three forty-five, and I'd like to rehearse my question out loud.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Sure. Come to my office at three. We'll have plenty of time, and your item isn't until about four anyway.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Perfect, I'll bring my notes. I honestly feel a lot calmer than when I walked in.

questions.q: What time will Chloe and Mateo practise on Thursday?
options: At three forty-five
At three o'clock
At about four
In two weeks
questions.explanation: Mateo says, 'Come to my office at three,' while the review itself starts later at three forty-five.

questions.q: How does Chloe feel at the end of the conversation?
options: Annoyed that her data was checked
Sure that she said very little
Worried about the review itself
Calmer and more confident
questions.explanation: Chloe says she feels a lot calmer than when she walked in.

questions.q: What is Chloe's goal for the next two weeks?
options: To lead the Thursday review
To ask one question in every meeting
To speak for five minutes each time
To record every meeting for the team
questions.explanation: Mateo suggests a small goal: ask one question in every meeting for the next two weeks.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hi Raj, can you hear me? The connection keeps dropping. It's about my forecasting macro, which stopped working after Tuesday's update.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I saw your ticket. What exactly happens when you run it? Does it show an error or just freeze?

script.speaker: A
script.line: It freezes, then Excel closes. Before the update it refreshed ten weeks of demand data in about a minute.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Okay. Did anything else change, like the file location or the add-in version?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Not that I know of, except that our shared folder moved to a new server last week.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That could be it. The macro may still point to the old path. Can you read it out from the settings sheet?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Sorry, you cut out. I'll paste it into the chat instead. It starts with the old server name.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, that's the old server. I can't safely edit it without the macro's author, who knows which sheets depend on it.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Right, that's Tomas. He's on leave until the 14th of January, which is too late for month-end.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I'd rather not guess and break the file. As a workaround, paste the data into a new workbook and refresh your one hundred and twenty key units by hand.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's better than nothing. How long will the proper fix take, do you think?

script.speaker: B
script.line: I can't say yet. I'm escalating to the platform team, but nothing happens until Tomas explains how the path is used.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I understand. I just hope it doesn't take weeks.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Fingers crossed. I'll message you tomorrow morning, even if the news is just not yet.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of the call?
options: To get help with a broken macro
To ask IT to bring back the old server
To complain about the update schedule
To request Excel training for the team
questions.explanation: Marta reports the macro problem and Raj suggests a manual workaround while he escalates.

questions.q: When will Tomas be back from leave?
options: On Tuesday
Tomorrow morning
On the 14th of January
In ten weeks
questions.explanation: Marta says Tomas is on leave until the 14th of January.

questions.q: How does Raj feel about editing the macro himself?
options: Confident that it is a simple change
Cautious about breaking the file
Irritated that Marta asked
Relaxed about the month-end run
questions.explanation: Raj says he would rather not guess and break the file.

questions.q: Why can't the problem be fixed today?
options: The update deleted the macro completely
Marta has no access to the shared folder
The platform team already refused to help
The macro's author is away on leave
questions.explanation: Raj needs Tomas to confirm how the path is used, and Tomas is on leave.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good morning, Rachel. Thanks for joining. I have one blocker today: the master data update for the new tablet packs is missing, so I can't finish the weekly supply plan.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Morning, Omar. I see. Which part is stuck, exactly? Is it the lead times or the pack sizes?

script.speaker: A
script.line: The lead times. Without them, the system uses the old four-week value, and that makes the plan about eight percent too optimistic.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I can help with a workaround. I could send you the new lead times in a spreadsheet, and you could load them yourself. It's not the official route, though.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I'm not allowed to load data outside the normal process. Why don't we do this instead: I plan with your numbers in a separate file, outside the system?

script.speaker: B
script.line: I'd rather see it in the system, honestly. But I can live with that if you show the difference clearly and upload properly once the official update arrives on Thursday.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Fair. I'll skip the shortcut and keep it in a separate file. Could you send me the numbers before lunch? I know you wanted to finish the audit report first.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I did, but I'll put the report aside for an hour. You'll have the sheet by eleven, and I'll chase the data team about Thursday's update.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Thank you, that's kind of you. In that case, the plan should be ready by the end of the day.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Great. Let's talk again tomorrow if the data team says anything different.

questions.q: When is the official master data update expected?
options: On Thursday
Before lunch
At the end of today
Tomorrow
questions.explanation: Rachel says the official update arrives on Thursday.

questions.q: What will Rachel do first?
options: Upload the new lead times to the system
Finish the audit report before lunch
Email a sheet with the new lead times
Complete the weekly supply plan for Omar
questions.explanation: Rachel puts the audit report aside and says Omar will have the sheet by eleven.

questions.q: What is Omar doing when he says, 'Why don't we do this instead'?
options: Proposing a different solution
Refusing to continue with the plan
Asking Rachel for permission to load data
Complaining about the data team
questions.explanation: After refusing to load data outside the process, he proposes planning in a separate file.

questions.q: What is the conversation mainly about?
options: Choosing new pack sizes for the tablets
Correcting a mistake in the audit report
Finding a temporary way to keep planning
Moving the stand-up to another day
questions.explanation: Omar's plan is blocked by missing lead times and they agree on a workaround.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Mei, you said the Monday call with the Rotterdam team is a problem for you? Walk me through it, because I'd like to find something that works for everyone.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Well, it's four in the afternoon for them, but eleven at night for us. For six weeks I've been dialling in from my sofa, and I can't keep doing that.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Fair enough. What if we alternate? One week at their convenience, the next at ours, so neither side always pays the price.

script.speaker: B
script.line: A rotating schedule sounds fair. Every second call could be at eleven in the morning for them, which is six in the evening for us. That's bearable.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good. Also, their items only take about twenty-five percent of the agenda, so on the late calls they could present first and drop off. You'd stay for the Asia items.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's helpful. One small thing, though: the eighty containers arriving in March need a decision from both regions, so in those weeks they'd have to stay for the whole call.

script.speaker: A
script.line: True, I hadn't thought of that. Let me check the March shipping calendar to see which weeks are affected, and then I'll send a draft schedule to everybody.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Perfect. Why don't we meet on Wednesday to look at it together before it goes out?

questions.q: What do the two colleagues agree in the end?
options: To cancel the Monday call completely
To alternate who gets the late call
To move every call to the morning in Asia
To hire a planner in Europe
questions.explanation: Kenji proposes alternating and Mei says a rotating schedule sounds fair.

questions.q: How much of the agenda belongs to the European team?
options: About half
About eighty percent
About six percent
About a quarter
questions.explanation: Kenji says their items take up about twenty-five percent of the agenda.

questions.q: Why must the European team stay for the whole call in some weeks?
options: The Asia team asked them to present first this time
The call will be shorter in those weeks
March containers need decisions from both regions
They have no other meeting on that day

It is too early for the European planners
It was chosen by Mei
It is already fair to both sides

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hi Mateo, can you hear me? The audio is a bit rough today. I wanted to go through my open items before I leave on holiday.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I can hear you, just with a delay. Go ahead, I've got a notebook open.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Great. The most urgent one is the order for sixty batches of tablets for the Spanish market. The customer wants confirmation by Monday.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Okay. Is the supply already confirmed, or do I need to check with the plant?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Not yet, that's the problem. Sven, the plant manager, hasn't said if they can run all sixty batches. He promised an answer by Friday, but I doubt it will come.

script.speaker: B
script.line: So I can't promise anything to the customer until Sven replies?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Exactly. If he says yes, confirm the full order. If he says no, offer a first delivery of forty-five batches and the rest later. I can't decide without his answer.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Understood. What can wait until you're back?

script.speaker: A
script.line: The safety stock review. We talked about raising it by twenty-five percent, but that isn't urgent, and I'd like to be part of the discussion.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Fine. And where are the files?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Everything is in the shared folder called Handover. The customer emails are in a sub-folder with today's date.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Got it. Who should I call if something goes wrong?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Call Priya in customer service. She knows the account well. Only call me if the whole shipment is at risk.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Okay. Enjoy your holiday, Dana. I'll look after everything.

questions.q: What does the customer want by Monday?
options: A higher safety stock level
A delivery of forty-five batches
Access to the Handover folder
Confirmation of the full order
questions.explanation: Dana says the customer wants confirmation of the sixty batches by Monday.

questions.q: Why can't Mateo confirm the order yet?
options: The customer has not sent the order
The plant has not answered yet
Dana forgot to save the files
The safety stock is too low
questions.explanation: Dana says Sven still hasn't told them whether the plant can run all sixty batches.

questions.q: What will Mateo probably do if Sven says no?
options: Cancel the order
Raise the safety stock
Ask the customer to wait for Dana
Offer a smaller first delivery
questions.explanation: Dana says to offer forty-five batches first and the rest later if Sven says no.

questions.q: What is the conversation mainly about?
options: Planning Mateo's holiday
Dana handing over her work to Mateo
Fixing a problem with the video call
Reviewing the safety stock policy
questions.explanation: Dana goes through what is urgent, what can wait, where files are and who to call.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Lukas, I need to flag something before you see it in the numbers. Sales now expect demand to be fifteen percent lower next quarter, because a competitor entered the market.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Fifteen is significant. How firm is that figure? Last time, sales revised their estimate by five percent within a month.

script.speaker: A
script.line: It's still an estimate, to be honest. But the competitor has already won two of our biggest tenders, and I'd rather you plan with it than be caught out later.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Fair. What about the orders we've already placed with the plant? Can we reduce them?

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's actually what I wanted to ask. Could you cancel the ones for December? It would take some pressure off the warehouse.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I'd like to help, but I can't do that. Those orders were frozen on the seventeenth of November, and I've seen what the plant invoices for changes after a freeze.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Understood. So what do you suggest instead?

script.speaker: B
script.line: I'll build a lower scenario and show it to you on Friday. If the numbers hold up, we can slow down the January orders, which are still open.

questions.q: When will Lukas show Chloe the lower demand scenario?
options: On Friday
On the seventeenth of November
In December
In January
questions.explanation: Lukas says he will show the scenario on Friday.

questions.q: Why does Lukas refuse to cancel the December orders?
options: He thinks fifteen percent is too low
The warehouse has no space problem
Changing them would cost money
Sales did not approve the change
questions.explanation: He says the orders were frozen and the plant invoices for changes after a freeze.

questions.q: What will Lukas do next?
options: Cancel the January orders now
Prepare a scenario with lower demand
Ask the competitor about its tenders
Move the freeze date to Friday
questions.explanation: He says he will build a lower scenario and show it on Friday.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Victor, thanks for taking this while I head to the boardroom. I want to test the setup before the review on the fifth of November, and I need your ears.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Of course. Tell me when you're in the room and I'll say what comes through.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Okay, I'm in and the call is connected. Say something, and I'll check the levels.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Testing, one two. Honestly, you sound like you're at the bottom of a well. It's hard to follow.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Right, so it's too quiet? Let me push the room volume up. Is that better?

script.speaker: B
script.line: No, worse, sorry, I wasn't clear. It isn't the volume, it's the echo. Every word comes back a second later, as if the microphone were picking up the speakers.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Ah, I see. The speaker and the table microphone are close together. I'll turn the speaker down by about twenty-five percent and move the microphone to the middle.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Much better already. Now the picture: I can see the screen and the back of the room, but the front row is cut off.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That'll be the camera angle. The room booking number is one five two four, so I'll quote that when I ask facilities to tilt it before the review.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good idea. If they can't manage it in time, we could seat people along the sides instead.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Let's avoid that. I'll retest tomorrow at nine and send you a short recording, so you can confirm it sounds right.

questions.q: What are Olivia and Victor mainly doing?
options: Booking a room for the quarterly review
Comparing two video call platforms
Training new staff to use the camera
Testing a room for a hybrid meeting
questions.explanation: They test the call, then fix the echo and the camera angle.

questions.q: When will Olivia test the room again?
options: Tomorrow at nine
On the fifth of November
Right after this call
At the review itself
questions.explanation: Olivia says she will retest tomorrow at nine.

questions.q: What will Olivia do about the camera?
options: Move the table to the side
Replace it with a new one
Ask facilities to tilt it
Turn it off during the review
questions.explanation: She says she will quote the booking number when she asks facilities to tilt it.

questions.q: What is Victor doing when he says, 'No, worse, sorry, I wasn't clear'?
options: Correcting Olivia's misunderstanding
Apologising for a dropped connection
Asking to end the test
Complaining about the camera
questions.explanation: Olivia raised the volume because she misunderstood, and Victor explains the real problem is the echo.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hi Adam, you wanted to talk about the training for the new planning software? I have about ten minutes before my next meeting.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, thanks. Go-live is in four weeks, and I still don't know who should attend or how long the session should be.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Let's start with the audience. I'd say the six planners plus the two buyers. The buyers only need the ordering screens.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Makes sense. So maybe one session for everyone, and a short extra one for the planners?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Exactly. Two hours for the first, and ninety minutes for the planners. People get tired after that.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good. Could you also prepare the training materials? You know the system better than anyone.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I'd love to help, but next month I'm running supplier workshops from morning to night. I can give you my notes and review your slides, though.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's fair. I'll write a first version, then. Is there a template?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Yes, the one from the last project. It's in the shared drive, in the folder with the project number seven four seven four.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Perfect. And what time is best for the first session? Mornings are quiet, I think.

script.speaker: A
script.line: The ten fifteen slot works, after the daily stand-up has finished.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Sounds good. I'll book the big room and send the invitation today.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Please add a short quiz at the end. It helps people remember.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Great idea. I'll draft that too, and send you everything for review next week.

questions.q: How long will the extra session for the planners be?
options: Two hours
Ten minutes
Ninety minutes
Four weeks
questions.explanation: Nora says two hours for the first session and ninety minutes for the planners.

questions.q: Why won't Nora prepare the training materials?
options: She thinks Adam knows the system better
She is busy with other work next month
She cannot find the template
She does not think training is needed
questions.explanation: She says she is running supplier workshops from morning to night next month.

questions.q: What will Adam do today?
options: Give Nora his first draft of the slides
Send the finished materials to Nora
Run the first session with the planners
Book the big room and send the invite
questions.explanation: Adam says he will book the big room and send the invitation today.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Luis, thanks for making time. The cycle count for warehouse two came back with a difference. We're short by about five percent on the sterile vials.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Five percent is more than I'd expect. Is it a real shortage, or a booking problem?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Probably booking. A transfer of two pallets from warehouse one doesn't show in the system, so the stock is likely still physically there.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Which transfer, exactly? Do you have the document number?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Nine two four six. It was created eight weeks ago and never confirmed. That's what bothers me, because nobody noticed for two months.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's not great. Could someone have put the pallets in the wrong location instead?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Possible. They could be in the overflow area. I'd like to recount both places before I draw any conclusion.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Agreed. Let's recount tomorrow at nine in warehouse two, and I'll come along. Actually, I have a supplier call then. Make it two in the afternoon.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Two is fine for me, but the inspectors are in warehouse two all afternoon. Shall we meet at the loading dock of warehouse one instead, since the transfer started there?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good thinking. Fine, warehouse one at two. Let me know whatever you find, even if it's bad news.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Of course. I'll send you the count by the end of the day, and I'll fix the transfer in the system once it's confirmed.

questions.q: What is the main topic of the conversation?
options: A complaint about the warehouse inspectors
A plan to order more vials from the plant
A stock gap that may be a booking error
A supplier that delivered too little last month
questions.explanation: Aisha reports a five percent shortage and suspects a transfer that was never booked.

questions.q: Where will the recount finally take place?
options: At the loading dock of warehouse one
In warehouse two, near the inspectors
In the overflow area of warehouse two
In Luis's office on the first floor
questions.explanation: After two changes, Luis agrees to 'warehouse one at two'.

questions.q: How does Aisha feel about the unconfirmed transfer?
options: Relaxed because it is a small amount
Proud that she found it quickly
Angry with the inspectors
Bothered that nobody noticed sooner
questions.explanation: She says, 'That's what bothers me, because nobody noticed for two months.'

questions.q: What can we infer about the missing stock?
options: It was certainly stolen
It is probably just misrecorded
It was never delivered by the supplier
It was used up in production
questions.explanation: Aisha thinks the stock is likely still physically there and the transfer is missing in the system.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hi Hugo, you look like you're in a hurry. Is everything okay?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Hi Lucia. Sort of. The supplier meeting in Utrecht has moved, and I need to change my train ticket. Can you help?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Of course. What does your booking say at the moment?

script.speaker: B
script.line: It's for the fifth of February, the nine ten train. The meeting has been pushed back by two weeks, but the supplier hasn't given me the new time yet.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Ah, that's the problem, then. I can't rebook without a time. Do you know if it's a flexible ticket?

script.speaker: B
script.line: I'm not sure. I think so.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Let me check the confirmation. Yes, it's flexible, so the change fee is twenty euros, plus any difference in the fare.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Twenty is fine. Can you rebook it now for the new date, in the morning?

script.speaker: A
script.line: I could, but if the supplier changes the time again, we'd pay the fee twice. I'd wait until they confirm.

script.speaker: B
script.line: True. I've emailed Dirk, their planner, but he hasn't answered. He's out until tomorrow.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Then we can't decide today. When Dirk replies, send it to me and I'll rebook. There's a nine ten train, an eleven forty and a one fifteen.

script.speaker: B
script.line: The eleven forty would be nicer, honestly. Less stress in the morning.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good. Just forward me his email tomorrow, and I'll handle the rest. It only takes a few minutes.

questions.q: Which train would Hugo prefer for the new date?
options: The nine ten
The one fifteen
Whichever is cheapest
The eleven forty
questions.explanation: Hugo says the eleven forty would be nicer because there is less stress in the morning.

questions.q: How does Lucia feel about rebooking straight away?
options: Eager, because the fee is quite low
Cautious about paying the fee twice
Indifferent about the exact dates
Annoyed that Hugo changed plans again
questions.explanation: She says they might pay the fee twice if the supplier changes the time again, so she would wait.

questions.q: What will Hugo do tomorrow?
options: Forward Dirk's reply to Lucia
Pay the twenty euro fee
Call the train company himself
Cancel the supplier meeting
questions.explanation: Lucia asks Hugo to forward her Dirk's email tomorrow, and she will rebook.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Morning, Tomas. You look like you've been wrestling with something. How can I help?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Morning, Mei. It's about my ticket, the one ending seven four one four. It's been open a week and I still can't open the stock reports. Quarter close is looming.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Let me pull it up. Opened on the eighth of October, priority medium. It was classed as a convenience request, not a blocker.

script.speaker: B
script.line: A convenience? I can't do my job without those reports. Sorry, I'm a bit on edge. I have the finance review on Monday and I haven't slept much.

script.speaker: A
script.line: No need to apologise. Let's sort it out. I'll raise it to high priority right now, so the security team looks at it first.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That would be a relief. What's actually holding it up?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Your access needs approval from the data owner, and the request has been sitting in his inbox. Nobody chased him, which is on us.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Typical. So will it just sit there again?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Not this time. I'll walk over to his office myself this afternoon and get his approval face to face. That's my task, so cross it off your list.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Really? Thank you, Mei. I was about to escalate it to my director.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hold off on that. Once he signs, the security team needs about one working day. You should have access by Friday morning, well before your Monday review.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Friday works. And if it slips?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Then come and find me, and I'll export the reports for you by hand. You won't walk into that meeting empty-handed.

questions.q: When should Tomas get access to the reports?
options: On Monday
This afternoon
By Friday morning
On the eighth of October
questions.explanation: Mei says he should have access by Friday morning, before his Monday review.

questions.q: How does Tomas feel at the start of the conversation?
options: Calm and confident
Stressed about his deadline
Annoyed with Mei personally
Embarrassed about asking for help
questions.explanation: Tomas says he is on edge, has the finance review on Monday and has slept little.

questions.q: What will Mei do this afternoon?
options: Export the reports for Tomas by hand
Call Tomas's director about the delay
Close the ticket and open a new one
Visit the data owner for approval
questions.explanation: Mei says she will walk to the data owner's office this afternoon.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hello, Katarina, it's Henrik from supply planning. Thanks for taking my call. Is it a good moment?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Hi, Henrik. Yes, go ahead. I hope you have good news about my request for the Nordic market.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Partly. You asked for four thousand boxes this month, but I can only offer three thousand. Supply is limited, so we share it between all the markets.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's disappointing. My customers are already waiting. Why can't you give me more?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Every market gets a share based on last year's sales. Yours comes to about three quarters of what you asked for.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I understand, but I need the boxes early. Can the first delivery arrive on Tuesday?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Tuesday is difficult. The truck leaves on Monday, so it arrives on Wednesday. But I have some good news. This morning the plant told me an extra batch finished early.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's great! So can I get more boxes?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Yes, maybe five hundred more, and we can send them on the same truck. Let me confirm by nine on Friday.

questions.q: What is the main point of the call?
options: Limited supply means a partial order
The truck has broken down
The Nordic market has stopped ordering
The plant has closed for a week
questions.explanation: Henrik offers three thousand boxes instead of four thousand because supply is limited.

questions.q: When will Henrik confirm the extra boxes?
options: On Tuesday
On Monday
On Friday at nine
On Wednesday
questions.explanation: He says he will confirm by nine on Friday.

questions.q: What can we conclude about the first delivery?
options: It arrives a day later than wanted
It will arrive on Monday as planned
It will arrive on the day she asked
It has been cancelled by the plant
questions.explanation: She wants Tuesday, but the truck leaves Monday and arrives on Wednesday.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Lucia, I need to flag a temperature excursion. The pallet that left the airport depot on the 29th of June sat on the apron for nearly four hours.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Okay, that's serious. Do we know how high the temperature went?

script.speaker: A
script.line: The carrier says it peaked at twelve degrees, against an upper limit of eight. The cold-chain box wasn't pre-conditioned, apparently.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Then nothing from that pallet can be used until we've assessed it. Do you have the data logger report?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Not yet. The carrier promised the file, but it's been three days. I'll chase them this afternoon.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Please do, and ask for the raw file rather than just a PDF. We need the full curve, not a summary.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Understood. What happens once we have it?

script.speaker: B
script.line: I open a deviation, and the stability team assesses whether the product tolerates twelve degrees for that long. Until then, everything stays in quarantine. Extra tests could take ten weeks.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Ten weeks? That's a long time to block that much stock. The autumn order depends on it.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I know. If the logger data is clean, it might be a matter of days. But I won't release anything on a hunch.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Fair enough. Can we agree who does what, so nothing slips?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Sure. You get the raw logger file from the carrier by Friday. I'll open the deviation when I receive it, and update planning on Monday with a realistic timeline.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Done. I'll also tell the customer team today that the order may be delayed, so they're not surprised.

questions.q: What is the conversation mainly about?
options: Choosing a new carrier for the autumn
Training staff to read a data logger
Deciding how to handle a shipment that got too warm
Planning a new cold-chain box
questions.explanation: Luis reports the excursion and they agree on the steps before the goods can be used.

questions.q: What is the upper temperature limit for the product?
options: Twelve degrees
Eight degrees
Four degrees
Ten degrees
questions.explanation: Luis says the pallet peaked at twelve degrees against an upper limit of eight.

questions.q: What will Lucia do on Monday?
options: Chase the carrier for the logger file
Tell the customer team about the delay
Release the pallet to the customer
Update planning with a new timeline
questions.explanation: Lucia says she will update planning on Monday with a realistic timeline.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hi Olivia, it's Jon. Thanks for joining. I want to go through the OTIF numbers for this month. We're at ninety-one percent, against a target of ninety-five.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Hi Jon. Ninety-one against ninety-five. So we're ahead of target?

script.speaker: A
script.line: No, sorry, the other way round. Ninety-five is the target, and ninety-one is where we ended up. So we're four points short, and last month we were at ninety-four.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Got it, thanks. What's behind the drop?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Mainly two late shipments. One was held at the border for two days, and the other left the warehouse a day late because of a picking error.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I see. What do you propose?

script.speaker: A
script.line: First, a pre-alert for customs documents, so the border problem doesn't repeat. Second, a double check on pallet labels before release.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Sensible. Can you pilot both for four weeks and report back on the results?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Yes, starting next Monday. I'll send you a one-page plan before then.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good. Then let's put the review in the diary for two in the afternoon, four weeks from now.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Perfect, I'll send the invitation. Thanks, Olivia.

questions.q: What is the OTIF target?
options: Ninety-four percent
Ninety-one percent
Ninety-five percent
Ninety percent
questions.explanation: Jon says ninety-five is the target, while ninety-one is the result and ninety-four was last month.

questions.q: What will Jon send Olivia before the pilot starts?
options: A one-page plan
A report on customs delays
A list of pallet labels
An invitation for next Monday
questions.explanation: Jon says he will send a one-page plan before next Monday.

questions.q: What is Jon doing when he says, 'No, sorry, the other way round'?
options: Refusing her proposal for the pilot
Ending the call before the review
Apologising for a late shipment
Correcting Olivia's mistake
questions.explanation: Olivia thought the result was above target, and Jon corrects her.

questions.q: What is the call mainly about?
options: A plan to change to another carrier
A missed target and a trial of fixes
A new layout for the warehouse floor
A training day for the picking team
questions.explanation: They discuss the shortfall, its two causes and a pilot of two actions for four weeks.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hi Dana, I'm Raj from the IT service partner. I've been asked to walk you through the systems you'll need. Do you have fifteen minutes before your next meeting?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, a little. Let's walk while we talk, I need to get to the third floor.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Sure. There are three things: the planning tool, the shared drive, and the ticketing system. The planning tool is the big one, so request that first.

script.speaker: B
script.line: How do I get it? Is there a form?

script.speaker: A
script.line: You raise a request in the ticketing system. Use the template numbered five zero nine one, which is meant for new planners.

script.speaker: B
script.line: And how long does it take?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Normally about four weeks for the full licence, but read-only access comes faster, usually within two days. About eighteen percent of requests get stuck without manager approval, so remind yours.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good tip. I'll ping my manager today. What about the shared drive?

script.speaker: A
script.line: That one's automatic once your account is active. You should see it by tomorrow. If not, tell me.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Great. Could we meet again to check everything? Maybe Thursday at my desk?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Thursday is difficult, I'm at another site. How about Friday morning in the cafeteria on the second floor?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Friday morning I have the onboarding workshop. Let's do Monday at ten, then, in the small meeting room.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Monday at ten, small meeting room. Perfect. I'll put it in the calendar.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Thanks, Raj. This was much clearer than the intranet pages.

questions.q: What is the conversation mainly about?
options: How to book a meeting room
Why the intranet is out of date
A problem with Dana's laptop
Which systems Dana needs and what to request first
questions.explanation: Raj goes through the planning tool, shared drive and ticketing system, and says to request the planning tool first.

questions.q: How long does the full planning tool licence normally take?
options: About two days
About four weeks
About one day
About eighteen weeks
questions.explanation: Raj says about four weeks for the full licence; two days is for the read-only version.

questions.q: Where and when will they meet again?
options: On Monday at ten in the small meeting room
On Thursday at Dana's desk
On Friday morning in the cafeteria
On Monday at ten in the cafeteria
questions.explanation: After two changes, they settle on Monday at ten in the small meeting room.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hello Ibrahim, it's Rachel. Thanks for squeezing this in before the sales and operations pre-meeting. I'd like to show you the gap for the oral liquids family.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Sure, go ahead. I have your file open, but the line isn't great, so let's be quick.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Demand for November is around eleven hundred cartons above what supply can deliver. That's after I've already trimmed the forecast.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's more than I thought. Where does the gap start, exactly?

script.speaker: A
script.line: From the week of the 24th of October. Two weeks later it grows, because the new tender kicks in.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Option one is an extra shift at the plant, closing about half the gap. Option two is air freight from the sister site, closing all of it, but costing more.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I'd like the full gap closed, so option two. Could you also guarantee delivery within two weeks?

script.speaker: B
script.line: I can't promise that. The sister site can only send seven hundred cartons by air, because their own stock is tight. I'd propose option one plus a smaller air shipment.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hmm. That still leaves a shortfall. Why can't they send more?

script.speaker: B
script.line: They need to protect their own safety stock before their quarter ends, and I'd rather not push them below it.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's reasonable. But I'll need to tell the commercial team that coverage is only partial.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, and I'll give you the exact numbers by tomorrow, so you can show them what is covered and what isn't.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Thanks. Then I'll present it at the pre-meeting as a partial fix and ask for a decision on the rest.

questions.q: What is the main point of the call?
options: A forecast that has just been cancelled
A supplier that has raised its prices
A supply gap that is only partly covered
A tender that the company has lost
questions.explanation: Rachel shows the gap and Ibrahim offers option one plus a smaller air shipment.

questions.q: How many cartons can the sister site send by air?
options: About eleven hundred
About seven hundred
About half of the gap
About four hundred
questions.explanation: Ibrahim says the sister site can only send seven hundred cartons by air.

questions.q: Why can't the sister site send more?
options: Air freight is not available this month
Its quarter has only just started
The plant has stopped all production
It must protect its own safety stock
questions.explanation: Ibrahim says they need to protect their own safety stock before their quarter ends.

questions.q: What will Rachel probably tell the commercial team?
options: That the gap will only be partly covered
That the tender has been delayed
That demand has been cut by half
That all cartons will arrive in two weeks
questions.explanation: She says she will need to tell them coverage is only partial.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Marta, do you have a minute? The forecast for the injectable line jumps thirty percent in month three, and I can't see anything in the notes that explains it.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Of course. That's the tender. We submitted a bid last month, and if we win, volume steps up in month three.

script.speaker: A
script.line: And have we won it yet?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Not yet. The decision is due in about ten weeks. Honestly, I'd put our chances at around thirty-five percent.

script.speaker: A
script.line: If I plan production for a tender we might not win, we could end up with too much stock. Could you take it out of the forecast until it's confirmed?

script.speaker: B
script.line: I can't remove it, because if we win, the lead time would leave us short from day one. Instead I'll add the tender as a scenario, weighted at thirty-five percent.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That helps, although it means I'd still have to hold some material in reserve.

script.speaker: B
script.line: A little, yes. Let's sit down with finance at quarter to four today and agree how big that reserve should be.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good plan. I'll bring the material costs, and we can see what the weighted scenario costs us.

questions.q: What is the conversation mainly about?
options: How to close a production line safely
Why finance rejected the latest budget
Why a forecast jumps in month three
How to hire a new demand planner
questions.explanation: Tomas asks about the thirty percent jump and Marta explains the tender and proposes a scenario.

questions.q: When is the tender decision expected?
options: In about ten weeks
In month three
Today at quarter to four
Next month
questions.explanation: Marta says the decision is due in about ten weeks.

questions.q: Why can't Marta remove the tender volume completely?
options: Finance told her to keep it
The bid has already been accepted
They would be short if they win
The base forecast is locked
questions.explanation: She says the lead time would leave them short from day one if they win.
