questions.q: What does Marta think about the chances of winning?
options: She is certain they will win
She thinks they will probably lose
She has no idea at all
She thinks it is almost guaranteed
questions.explanation: She puts the chances at around thirty-five percent, which is below half.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hi Leila, Pavel here. Can you hear me okay? I know you're in a different time zone, so thanks for staying on. Shall we go through the weekly report?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, please. I have to be honest, I'm a bit overwhelmed. I took over this report with only a week's notice, and finance asks about it every Monday.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Understandable, but it's less scary than it looks. There are three inputs: the stock file from the warehouse, the open orders extract, and the forecast snapshot.

script.speaker: B
script.line: And when do I need them?

script.speaker: A
script.line: The stock file lands by nine on Monday, the others a bit later. The report itself must go out by eleven, because finance reviews it before their weekly call.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Eleven is tight. What typically goes wrong?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Mostly the stock file. About thirty percent of the weeks it arrives late or with duplicate lines, and then the totals don't match.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Right. And what do I do then?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Check the row count first. If it's off, ask Hamid in the warehouse for a resend. Don't try to clean it by hand, because that's how errors creep in.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Okay. I'm still worried I'll miss something once you've gone.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Tell you what, you shouldn't carry all of it. I'll write a checklist this afternoon, with screenshots, and save it under seven two two two. That's my job, not yours.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That would help enormously. Thank you, Pavel.

script.speaker: A
script.line: No problem. And for your first run next Monday, I'll be reachable until eleven, just in case.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's a relief. I already feel much better.

questions.q: By what time must the report go out on Monday?
options: By nine
By noon
After the finance call
By eleven
questions.explanation: Pavel says the report must go out by eleven, before finance's weekly call.

questions.q: Why does Pavel tell Leila not to clean the stock file by hand?
options: Hamid prefers to do it himself
The file is too large to open
Manual cleaning leads to mistakes
Finance forbids any changes
questions.explanation: He says that cleaning it by hand is how errors creep in.

questions.q: What will Pavel do this afternoon?
options: Write a checklist with screenshots
Ask Hamid to resend the stock file
Send the report to finance himself
Call Leila at eleven on Monday
questions.explanation: Pavel says he will write a checklist this afternoon, with screenshots.

title: Launch readiness for a new pack

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hi Olivia, I've pasted the status table in the chat. Shall I talk you through it, starting with the artwork?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, please. As far as I know, the artwork for the new sixty-count pack should be done.

script.speaker: A
script.line: It's green. The printer approved the final files this morning, so there's nothing more to do there.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good. And what about the first batch?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Amber. Filling is booked for next Monday, but the packaging material isn't all here yet. We're still missing twenty-five percent of the cartons.

script.speaker: B
script.line: And logistics? You said one item was red.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Yes, logistics. We don't have a carrier slot for the first shipment on the day we planned, so it's red.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's a problem. Can anything be done?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Actually, I just got a message. The carrier had a cancellation, so they can take our pallets on Monday at two in the afternoon, two days earlier than planned.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Excellent! Then logistics turns green. But we'll need the missing cartons earlier too, so please chase the supplier.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I'll call them first thing tomorrow and update the table in the chat tonight.

questions.q: What share of the cartons is still missing?
options: Three quarters
Half
All of them
A quarter
questions.explanation: Jon says they are still missing twenty-five percent of the cartons.

questions.q: What will Jon do tomorrow morning?
options: Approve the artwork
Call the carton supplier
Book a new carrier
Start filling the first batch
questions.explanation: He says he will call them first thing tomorrow.

questions.q: What is Jon doing when he says, 'Actually, I just got a message'?
options: Changing the subject of the meeting
Asking for permission to leave
Cancelling the rest of the meeting
Giving news that changes the situation
questions.explanation: He uses it to introduce the carrier's cancellation, which is good news.

questions.q: What is the conversation mainly about?
options: A complaint about the artwork printer
The progress of a new pack launch
A request for more project budget
A contract with a new carrier
questions.explanation: They go through artwork, first batch and logistics one by one.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Amara, thanks for coming by. The customer has asked for the whole order by the 15th, no exceptions, and I wanted to see what's realistic.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I appreciate you coming to me early. Honestly, the full quantity by the 15th is a stretch. We can ship sixty percent by then.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Sixty. That leaves forty percent hanging. The customer won't love that, since they're already stretched on their own production.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I get that. The rest depends on a raw material we ordered eight weeks ago that only lands next week.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Could you not borrow from another order to close the gap?

script.speaker: B
script.line: I thought about that, but we'd only move the problem to another customer. I'd rather not rob Peter to pay Paul.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Fair enough. So what's the alternative you have in mind?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Two shipments. Sixty percent on the 15th, as I said, and the rest by the end of the following week, airfreighted, with the extra cost on us.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That might work. I'll have to check with the customer before I agree to anything, though.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Of course. Could you let me know before a quarter to four? After that I'm in the plant review and offline.

script.speaker: A
script.line: A quarter to four, got it. And if they refuse the split?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Then we talk again tomorrow, but I doubt they'll turn down sixty percent on time and the rest within days.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I'd say you're right. I'll push for a yes.

questions.q: What are the two colleagues mainly doing?
options: Finding a way to split an urgent order
Cancelling an order for a customer
Choosing a different supplier for it
Checking a quality problem in a batch
questions.explanation: Amara cannot ship everything by the 15th, so she offers two shipments.

questions.q: By what time should Ben contact Amara?
options: On the 15th
By tomorrow
Before a quarter to four
Within eight weeks
questions.explanation: Amara asks to hear before a quarter to four because she will be offline afterwards.

questions.q: What does Ben probably think about the two-shipment plan?
options: That it is worse than waiting
That the customer will likely agree
That it is unfair to other customers
That air freight is impossible
questions.explanation: He says it might work, agrees with Amara's view and says he will push for a yes.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good morning, Leila, and welcome. Before we go onto the warehouse floor, I need to take you through a few safety rules. Is that alright?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Of course, Pavel. I've done site visits before, so I'm fairly familiar with the basics.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good, then this will be quick. First, your visitor badge must be visible at all times, and you need the high-visibility vest, safety shoes and glasses.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's fine. One question: do I really need the glasses? I'll only walk along the main aisle on Tuesday, not near any machines.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I'm afraid so, even in the aisle. We handle about two thousand five hundred order lines a day, and forklifts use that route all day long.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Is that so? From what I saw last time, the aisle was quiet.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Let me show you the log on my tablet. In the last ten weeks, there were fourteen near-misses in the main aisle, and only two near the machines.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Oh, I stand corrected. I'll wear the glasses, of course. That's clearly more serious than I thought.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Thank you. Second, always use the green walkways, and never cross the yellow forklift lanes without looking both ways.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Understood. And what should I do in an emergency?

script.speaker: A
script.line: If the alarm sounds, leave everything and go to the assembly point in the car park, next to the blue gate. Don't use the lift.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Assembly point, blue gate. Got it.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Then shall we put your vest on and start the tour? I'll walk you to the equipment room first.

questions.q: How many near-misses happened in the main aisle in the last ten weeks?
options: Two
Ten
Two thousand five hundred
Fourteen
questions.explanation: Pavel says there were fourteen near-misses in the main aisle and only two near the machines.

questions.q: How does Leila react to the figures?
options: She accepts the rule once she sees the data
She becomes angry about being corrected
She still doubts the log is accurate
She does not seem to care
questions.explanation: She says, 'Oh, I stand corrected. I'll wear the glasses, of course.'

questions.q: What will they do next?
options: Walk to the assembly point first
Watch a safety video together
Collect her safety equipment
Sign the near-miss log at the desk
questions.explanation: Pavel suggests putting her vest on and starting the tour, walking first to the equipment room.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Emma, would you mind if I run my update past you? I present to the leadership group at quarter to four, and I want the numbers to be right.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Not at all, go ahead. Give me the headline first, the way you'd say it to them.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Service level is back above target, we've cut overdue orders by forty percent since the spring, and the one risk is the packaging component due later this month.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good, though I'd lead with the risk. They'll remember that, and the good news will land better afterwards.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Understood. Would you be able to join me and take the questions on the supplier side? You know that contract far better than I do.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I'd be glad to help, but I'm in the budget review until half past four, and the leadership group likes to hear from the person who owns the numbers.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Fair enough. Then I'll prepare for the likely questions, such as why the component is late and what the fallback is.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good. Send me your answers by lunchtime, and I'll tell you if anything sounds weak.

questions.q: What are Mark and Emma mainly doing?
options: Rehearsing an update before a meeting
Planning a budget review with finance
Negotiating a contract with a supplier
Interviewing a new colleague for the team
questions.explanation: Mark runs his update past Emma and she advises him to lead with the risk.

questions.q: What has fallen by forty percent since the spring?
options: The service level
The delay of the component
The number of overdue orders
The supplier's prices
questions.explanation: Mark says they have cut overdue orders by forty percent.

questions.q: What will Mark do before lunchtime?
options: Present to the leadership group today
Send Emma answers to likely questions
Join Emma in the budget review
Rewrite the supplier contract terms
questions.explanation: Emma asks him to send his answers by lunchtime.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hi Aisha, your approval request is open, but the audio is awful on my side, so let me check the details. It's a purchase order for new pallet sensors, right?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, correct. Sorry about the sound. I need it approved today, because the supplier's offer expires at half past four.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Understood. First, which cost centre should it go on?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Logistics operations, four three two one.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Four three two one. And what's the justification? Finance won't approve an urgent order without a clear reason.

script.speaker: B
script.line: The sensors keep failing, so we lose temperature data on the trucks. They need replacing before the 20th of November. Sorry, I mean the 22nd, when the winter campaign starts.

script.speaker: A
script.line: The 22nd, noted. And the total is eight thousand six hundred euros?

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's right, and that includes delivery.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Okay. That sounds reasonable, but I can't approve anything over eight thousand on my own. I need my director's signature.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Oh no. Is she available this afternoon?

script.speaker: A
script.line: She's in meetings until three, but I'll send her the request now and flag it as urgent, with your justification.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Thank you, Chris. I'll stay by my phone in case she has questions.

questions.q: What is the call mainly about?
options: Changing the terms of a supplier contract
Fixing a problem with the cold-chain trucks
Setting up a new cost centre for logistics
Getting approval for an urgent purchase
questions.explanation: Aisha asks for approval of a purchase order for new sensors and gives the details.

questions.q: When does the winter campaign start?
options: On the 20th of November
At half past four today
On the 22nd of November
At three this afternoon
questions.explanation: Aisha first says the 20th, then corrects herself to the 22nd.

questions.q: Why can't Chris approve the order himself?
options: It is above his approval limit
The cost centre is wrong
The supplier has withdrawn the offer
The justification is missing
questions.explanation: He says he cannot approve anything over eight thousand without his director's signature.

questions.q: What will Chris do next?
options: Call the supplier to extend the offer
Change the cost centre on the form
Wait until three to call Aisha back
Send the request to his director marked urgent
questions.explanation: He says he will send the request to his director now and flag it as urgent.

title: Late updates and a new routine

script.speaker: A
script.line: Chris, got a minute while we walk? I have to be honest, I'm frustrated. For six weeks, I've heard about delays from the customer before I've heard them from you.

script.speaker: B
script.line: You're right, Amara, and I'm sorry. My updates have been late, and that's on me.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I don't want an apology so much as a fix. I need to know early, not when it's already a problem.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Agreed. What if I send you a short written update every morning, before eleven?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Every day is too much for me, to be fair. I get a hundred emails. I can't read another one daily.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Then how about twice a week, Monday and Thursday, and a phone call the same day if anything is red?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hmm, I'd prefer Tuesday instead of Monday, since I'm travelling on Mondays. But I'll accept two updates if they're really short, five lines at most.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Five lines is difficult with so many orders, but I'll make it work. I'll just list the exceptions.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Fine. And I'll give up my request for a daily report, as long as you phone me about anything urgent.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Deal. I'll start this week. The first one goes out on Tuesday, before eleven.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Perfect. Thank you, Chris. I appreciate you taking it seriously.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Of course. I'll put a reminder in my calendar so it doesn't slip again.

questions.q: On which days will Chris send updates?
options: Monday and Thursday
Tuesday and Thursday
Every morning
Monday and Tuesday
questions.explanation: Chris first suggests Monday and Thursday, but Amara asks for Tuesday instead of Monday.

questions.q: How does Amara feel at the start of the conversation?
options: Delighted with the service so far
Indifferent to the repeated delays
Ready to replace Chris with someone
Annoyed, but ready to find a solution
questions.explanation: She says she is frustrated but wants a fix, not just an apology.

questions.q: What will Chris do if something is urgent?
options: Send a longer email
Phone Amara
Wait until Thursday
Ask the customer to call
questions.explanation: Amara accepts fewer updates as long as Chris phones her about anything urgent.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hello Ana, thanks for joining the quarterly review. I'll start with one change: the standard lead time for the valve component moves from eight to ten weeks.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Ten weeks? That's two weeks longer. Why the change?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Our own supplier is slower now, and we need more time for testing.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Hmm, that worries me. With ten weeks I'd have to raise the safety stock. Could you keep eight weeks for my orders, at least until next summer?

script.speaker: A
script.line: I can't do eight for everything. But I can offer a compromise: eight weeks for orders placed in the next four weeks, and ten weeks after that.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That helps a bit. Still, it means I need to order earlier than planned.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Yes, I understand. And on the stock side, I suggest you work out how much extra safety stock you need.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I did a quick check. Roughly two more weeks of cover, which is a lot of cash. I'll have to ask finance.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Understood. Shall we look at the numbers together? I'm free at half past one tomorrow.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Tomorrow at half past one works. I'll send you my stock figures this evening.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Great. I'll update the lead time in the portal after we've spoken.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Thanks, Marco. I'm not happy about it, but at least there's some flexibility.

questions.q: For how long can Ana still order with the old lead time?
options: For the next four weeks
For the next eight weeks
For the next ten weeks
Until next summer
questions.explanation: Marco offers eight weeks for orders placed in the next four weeks.

questions.q: How does Ana feel about the change at the end?
options: Delighted with the new lead time
Angry and ready to stop ordering
Unhappy, but sees some flexibility
Relaxed because the cost is small
questions.explanation: She says, 'I'm not happy about it, but at least there's some flexibility.'

questions.q: What will Ana do this evening?
options: Update the lead time in the portal
Send her stock figures to Marco
Ask finance for extra cash today
Place a large order with Marco
questions.explanation: She says she will send Marco her stock figures this evening.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Morning, Sofia. How was the commute? I heard the trains were a mess again.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Don't ask. Forty minutes stuck outside the station. But this new coffee machine makes up for it, doesn't it?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Honestly, yes. It's the first time I've enjoyed office coffee, though it takes ages to grind the beans.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Patience, Victor. So, what are you really after? You've got your deadline face on.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Ha, fair. It's about the capacity plan submission. Is it still due on the 27th of January?

script.speaker: B
script.line: It is, but I'd aim to send it a week earlier. The twelve-week outlook needs sign-off from finance first, and they're slow.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Understood. So I should have the draft ready by Monday, so finance has time?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Exactly, Monday at the latest. Then I'll review it on Tuesday morning.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good. I'll send it to finance myself and copy you in.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Perfect. And please remind me to book the review room today.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I will. I'll put it on my list right now.

questions.q: What is the conversation mainly about?
options: Complaints about the train service
A decision to buy a coffee machine
A change to the finance process
Small talk, then agreeing when a plan must be ready
questions.explanation: They chat about commuting and coffee, then settle who does what for the capacity plan.

questions.q: When does Victor need the draft ready?
options: By Monday at the latest
By Tuesday morning
On the 27th of January
In twelve weeks
questions.explanation: Sofia says, 'Monday at the latest,' and she reviews it on Tuesday morning.

questions.q: What does Sofia mean by 'You've got your deadline face on'?
options: Victor looks tired from the commute
Victor looks happy about the coffee
Victor looks worried about timing
Victor looks angry with her
questions.explanation: She guesses he wants to ask something about a deadline, so he must look concerned about it.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hello Hannah, it's Pedro from the carrier. You asked me to confirm a firm delivery date for the order of twelve hundred cartons.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, thanks for coming back. The customer wants all of it by next Wednesday. Is that possible?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Let me go through the pieces. Transport is fine, we have a truck free. Customs is the question mark, since clearance usually takes two days.

script.speaker: B
script.line: And production? I checked this morning, and the plant finished packing everything last night, so the cartons are ready to leave.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Great, that helps. We can collect from the plant tomorrow, Friday, from nine.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Okay. So can you make Wednesday?

script.speaker: A
script.line: For all twelve hundred, no, because one truck only takes eight hundred cartons. So it would be eight hundred on Wednesday and the other four hundred on Thursday.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's not exactly what I hoped for, but it's better than nothing. Can you confirm it's firm?

script.speaker: A
script.line: I can, if customs clear it. I'll know by noon today, and I'll ring you straight away.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Fine. I'll tell the customer it's firm for eight hundred on Wednesday and Thursday for the rest. That's still far quicker than the four weeks we normally quote.

questions.q: What is the call mainly about?
options: Agreeing a delivery date for an urgent order
Cancelling a transport contract
Reporting damaged cartons
Changing the packing material
questions.explanation: Pedro and Hannah check transport, customs and production to agree when the order can arrive.

questions.q: When will Pedro call Hannah about customs?
options: On Friday at nine
On Wednesday
By noon today
On Thursday
questions.explanation: Pedro says he will know by noon today and will ring straight away.

questions.q: Why can't all the cartons arrive on Wednesday?
options: The plant has not finished packing
One truck holds only eight hundred
The customer asked for Thursday
The warehouse is closed on Fridays
questions.explanation: Pedro says one truck takes only eight hundred, so the other four hundred go on Thursday.

questions.q: What will Hannah do after the call?
options: Collect the cartons from the plant herself
Ask the plant to repack the whole order
Cancel the Thursday shipment of the rest
Tell the customer about the two-part delivery
questions.explanation: She says she will tell the customer it is firm for eight hundred on Wednesday and the rest on Thursday.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Ingrid, thanks for coming. I have to tell you that batch four seven two is on hold while we investigate an out-of-spec result.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Oh no. Which test failed, and how bad is it?

script.speaker: A
script.line: The dissolution test came back slightly low. It's not dramatic, but we can't release until we understand why.

script.speaker: B
script.line: How long will the hold last? I have an order due on the 5th of July.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Realistically, about two weeks. We have to repeat the test and review the equipment.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Two weeks seems long to me. Last time a similar hold took five days.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hmm, I remember it differently. But let's check. I have the tracker on my laptop. Last time, the hold ran eleven days from opening to closing.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Eleven. You're right, I was thinking of the first review, which only took five days. Okay, so two weeks isn't unreasonable.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Exactly. And I'd rather be honest now than promise something short and miss it.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Fair. How much inventory is affected? Just this batch?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Just this one. Two other batches from the same line were tested yesterday, and they're fine.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's good news, at least. Can I use those two for the 5th of July order?

script.speaker: A
script.line: I think so, but the line supervisor has to confirm. I'll have the repeat result by eleven on Wednesday and let you know straight after.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Perfect. I'll hold off telling the customer anything until I hear from you on Wednesday.

questions.q: According to the tracker, how long did the last hold last?
options: Five days
Two weeks
Eleven days
Three days
questions.explanation: Hugo reads from the tracker that the hold ran eleven days, while Ingrid had remembered five.

questions.q: How does Ingrid feel about a two-week hold by the end?
options: She accepts it as reasonable
She refuses to accept it
She is happy it is short
She wants the batch released now
questions.explanation: After seeing the data she says, 'two weeks isn't unreasonable.'

questions.q: What will Ingrid do until Wednesday?
options: Ask the customer to cancel the order
Repeat the test herself
Release the two other batches
Wait before telling the customer anything
questions.explanation: Ingrid says she will hold off telling the customer until she hears from Hugo.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Nora, a quick update on the dashboard. Yesterday it showed stock levels about double the real ones, and I know you used it for an ordering decision. I'm sorry.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, I noticed it when the warehouse called me. What happened?

script.speaker: A
script.line: A nightly job failed halfway and retried, so the file of the 5th of July was loaded twice. I've added a deduplication step, and today's numbers are correct.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good. But what about the history? The twelve-week trend looked odd too.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Two days were wrong, and I've corrected them in the live view. But the monthly archive was touched too, and only the finance data owner can approve rewriting it.

script.speaker: B
script.line: And has she responded to your request yet?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Not yet. Priya is out until Friday, and nobody else has the rights. So I can't say whether the archive will be corrected.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's awkward. I made an ordering decision based on the wrong numbers.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I understand. If you send me the order, I'll check it against the corrected stock today.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I will, thanks. Then we'll decide what to do about the archive on Friday, once Priya is back.

questions.q: What is the main point of the conversation?
options: Planning a new dashboard
Explaining a dashboard error and what is still unresolved
Complaining about the warehouse
Training Nora to load data
questions.explanation: Ethan explains the cause and the fix, and that the archive still needs approval.

questions.q: When will they decide what to do about the archive?
options: Today
Yesterday
In twelve weeks
On Friday
questions.explanation: Nora says they will decide on Friday, when Priya is back.

questions.q: What probably happened to Nora's order?
options: It was too large for the warehouse space
It was probably too small
It was not affected by the error at all
It was cancelled by the warehouse team
questions.explanation: The dashboard showed double the real stock, so Nora probably ordered less than she needed.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Samuel, do you have a moment? I need to tell you that the shipment for the Czech market is stuck at customs.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Stuck? That's bad. What exactly are they missing?

script.speaker: A
script.line: A copy of the importer licence wasn't attached. It was renewed ten weeks ago, but the copy never reached us. It's twelve hundred orders' worth of stock, so it's urgent.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Right. About thirty-five percent of those orders are promised for this week. What can we send from stock in the meantime?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Vienna has enough for the first week's priority orders. You could truck them from there tomorrow.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good, I'll arrange that. Who should I call about the licence?

script.speaker: A
script.line: The broker, Jakub. I'll call him now. Let's meet in your office at three to see what he said.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Three doesn't work, I'm at the plant until four. Could we do four thirty in the canteen?

script.speaker: A
script.line: The canteen is closed by then. Let's say four thirty in the small meeting room on the second floor.

questions.q: Why is the shipment stuck at customs?
options: A copy of the importer licence is missing
The trucks reached the border too late
The orders were bigger than allowed
The broker made a mistake on the form
questions.explanation: Claire says the copy of the importer licence wasn't attached.

questions.q: Where does the shipment for the first week's priority orders come from?
options: From the plant near the border
From the broker's own storage
From the Vienna warehouse
From the customs office depot
questions.explanation: Claire says Vienna has enough stock for the first week's priority orders.

questions.q: Where and when will Claire and Samuel meet?
options: At three in Samuel's office
Four thirty, small meeting room
At four thirty in the canteen
At four, at the plant entrance
questions.explanation: After two changes, they agree on four thirty in the small meeting room on the second floor.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Pedro, I think I've found why our numbers never match. Your forecast says four thousand, but the supplier's plan shows forty thousand for the same month.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Forty thousand? That can't be right. Hold on, ours is in packs, isn't it? One pack holds ten units.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Exactly. Your forecast is in packs, and the supplier's plan is in units. So four thousand packs equals forty thousand units. We were comparing apples with oranges.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Ah, that explains it. I should have caught that. How long has it been like this?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Since at least the 3rd of January, when the plan was uploaded. Nobody noticed because both numbers looked plausible.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Well, that's embarrassing. So what do we do?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Add a conversion check to the weekly template, so every file has to state its unit. Could you do that?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes. I'll add a column and a warning cell, and have it ready by Friday.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Great. Oh, and there's good news, by the way. Now that I've converted properly, the supplier's stock covers the next two weeks of extra demand.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Really? That changes things. Then we don't need the expedited order I was about to place.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Right, it saves us a fair bit of money. I'd drop it for now and review on Monday.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Agreed. I'll cancel the draft today. Thanks for spotting this, Yuki.

questions.q: By when will Pedro add the conversion check to the template?
options: On Monday
Today
On the 3rd of January
By Friday
questions.explanation: Pedro says he will have the column and warning cell ready by Friday.

questions.q: How does Pedro feel about missing the mismatch?
options: Embarrassed
Proud
Indifferent
Angry with Yuki
questions.explanation: He says, 'Well, that's embarrassing.'

questions.q: What will Pedro do today?
options: Convert the supplier's plan into packs
Order two weeks of extra stock
Cancel the draft expedited order
Review the new template with Yuki
questions.explanation: After the good news, he says he will cancel the draft order today.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hello Katarina, can you hear me clearly? It's my first time chairing this cross-functional call, so I'd like to check the agenda order with you before the others join.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I can hear you fine, Henrik. Welcome to the chair. What's the plan?

script.speaker: A
script.line: First the order backlog, where six hundred order lines are waiting for release. Then the supplier update, and last the forecast review.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I'd swap the last two. The forecast review needs more time, and the supplier update is mostly informational.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good point. Forecast second, then supplier. The last meeting, on the 27th of April, ran twenty minutes over, and I have a hard stop at half past eleven.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Understood. I'll keep my comments short. You may want to be firm with the finance people, they love to talk.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Noted. I'll also say upfront that we'll park anything that needs a longer discussion.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Sensible. Oh, before I forget, I have good news: the backlog is smaller than you think. The warehouse cleared about two hundred of those order lines this morning.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's great. Then the first item should take five minutes, and we can give the extra time to the forecast.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Exactly. Just announce it at the start, and people will be pleased.

questions.q: Which item will come second on the agenda?
options: The forecast review
The supplier update
The order backlog
A report from the warehouse
questions.explanation: Katarina suggests swapping the last two items, and Henrik agrees: 'Forecast second, then supplier.'

questions.q: Why does Henrik want each item kept short?
options: Katarina asked him to finish early
The finance team has to leave early
He must leave at half past eleven
The agenda is very short today
questions.explanation: He says he has a hard stop at half past eleven, and the last meeting ran over.

questions.q: How will the good news change the meeting?
options: The meeting will end much earlier
The first item will be shorter
The supplier update will be dropped
The backlog item will be longer
questions.explanation: Henrik says the first item should take five minutes, giving extra time to the forecast.

title: Too much work at quarter close

script.speaker: A
script.line: Emma, do you have a few minutes? I need to be honest about my workload during quarter close. I'm roughly forty percent over what I can handle.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Thanks for telling me, Mark. Walk me through what's on your plate.

script.speaker: A
script.line: There's the stock reconciliation, the accruals reports, three supplier audits, and a training session I agreed to run. They all peak this week.

script.speaker: B
script.line: The training can't be a priority right now, so let's postpone it. What else can we drop?

script.speaker: A
script.line: The audit prep for the packaging supplier could be delegated. Someone else could pull the data, and I'd just review it.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Fine, I'll ask Hamid to take that. And the reconciliation?

script.speaker: A
script.line: That one I should keep, since I know it best. But the deadline is Thursday at two, and I won't make it unless I stop doing the rest.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Well, there's some good news, actually. Finance just told me they're moving the reconciliation deadline to next Monday.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Oh, that's a relief. That gives me some breathing space.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good. Let's still meet on Thursday at two to check where you are, and then decide what else can wait.

questions.q: What was the original deadline for the reconciliation?
options: Next Monday
Thursday at four
This weekend
Thursday at two
questions.explanation: Mark says the deadline is Thursday at two, before Emma tells him it moves to next Monday.

questions.q: Why does Mark want to keep the reconciliation?
options: It is the easiest task on his list
Hamid is on leave this week
He knows it better than anyone
The deadline has just been moved
questions.explanation: He says, 'That one I should keep, since I know it best.'

questions.q: What will happen to the training session?
options: It will be postponed
Mark will run it next week
Hamid will run it
It will be cancelled for good
questions.explanation: Emma says the training can't be a priority and suggests they postpone it.

questions.q: What is the conversation mainly about?
options: Hiring extra staff for the audits
Changing the quarter close process
Planning Mark's holiday
Reducing Mark's workload
questions.explanation: Mark says he is overloaded and they decide what to postpone or delegate.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hi Yuki, thanks for making time. I just got back from the packaging conference in Rotterdam, and it was better than I expected.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Welcome back, Hugo. Which talks were worth your time?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Two stood out. One was about lighter cold boxes that cut transport emissions by about eight percent. The other was about carriers sharing live tracking data.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Eight percent is not small. Was there anything you didn't like?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Well, the lunch was terrible, but more seriously, the speaker I really wanted to hear cancelled, so the closing session was quite weak.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's a shame. Did you meet anyone useful?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Yes, a woman from a box manufacturer. I'd like to bring her into a call with you. I suggested a two-hour workshop, but I know you're busy.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Two hours is too long for me. I could do forty-five minutes, but only on Thursday, the fifth of January.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That works if she agrees to a shorter slot. I'll skip my slides and send you the numbers by email first.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Deal. I give up my long workshop, you keep it short. Send me the invitation today.

questions.q: What did the lighter cold boxes achieve, according to the talk?
options: They lowered the shipping costs
They shortened the transit times
They reduced transport emissions
They increased the pallet capacity
questions.explanation: Hugo says the boxes cut transport emissions by about eight percent.

questions.q: Why was the closing session weak?
options: Hugo arrived very late
The lunch ran much too long
The topic was not relevant to him
A planned speaker cancelled
questions.explanation: Hugo says the speaker he wanted to hear cancelled.

questions.q: What does Hugo mean by 'the lunch was terrible, but more seriously'?
options: The food was the main problem for him
The cancellation mattered more to him
He wants to complain to the organizers
He did not eat at all at the conference
questions.explanation: He moves from a small complaint about lunch to the cancellation, which he calls more serious.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good morning, Sofia. Thanks for joining. I've posted the accuracy chart in our chat, and I'm afraid the news isn't great.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I can see it. The northern market is over-forecast almost every month. How big is the gap?

script.speaker: A
script.line: On average, twenty-five percent above actual sales. I'm worried the directors will think my model is broken. I haven't slept well this week.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Samuel, please don't panic. This is rarely a model problem. In my experience, the regional sales team adds a safety margin to their numbers, just in case.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Yes, that fits. They told me they would rather have too much stock than lose a tender.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Then we correct the bias instead of rebuilding anything. Apply an adjustment based on the last twelve months and show both versions side by side.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Understood. I can prepare that, although the review is on the seventeenth of January, so time is tight.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I'll take the conversation with the sales director myself, so you can focus on the numbers. Send me the draft by Monday.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Thank you, that's a big relief. I'll send it as soon as the adjusted version is ready.

questions.q: By how much does the northern forecast exceed actual sales on average?
options: About twenty-five percent more
About fifteen percent more
About twelve percent more
About seventeen percent more
questions.explanation: Samuel says it is twenty-five percent above actual sales.

questions.q: What will Sofia do next?
options: Cancel the January review
Prepare the adjusted forecast
Rebuild the forecast model
Speak to the sales director
questions.explanation: Sofia says she will take the conversation with the sales director herself.

questions.q: Why does Sofia say 'please don't panic'?
options: To end the call quickly
To ask for an explanation
To calm Samuel down
To criticize his model
questions.explanation: She reassures him and explains it is rarely a model problem.

questions.q: What do they decide in the end?
options: To adjust for the sales team's bias
To ignore the northern market for now
To replace the whole forecast model
To ask sales to send lower numbers
questions.explanation: Sofia says they correct the bias instead of rebuilding anything.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hi Jon, do you have a few minutes? I wanted to share some thoughts on yesterday's presentation to the steering group.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Sure, Nora. To be honest, I felt it was a bit rushed, so I'm curious what you saw.

script.speaker: A
script.line: The strongest part was the service story. When you showed that on-time delivery improved by eighteen percent, you had everyone's attention.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good, I worked hard on that chart. What didn't work?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Too much detail in the middle. The slides on lane-by-lane costs lost the directors. They wanted the decision, not the spreadsheet.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Hm, I see your point, although a couple of them asked for those numbers last time.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Fair, but put them in an appendix. Next time, open with your recommendation and keep it to three slides.

script.speaker: B
script.line: All right, I'll try that. Would you look at my next draft before I send it?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Of course. Actually, there's one more thing. The deck you circulated afterwards still has last quarter's cost table.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Oh no, that's embarrassing. I must have attached the wrong version. I'll send the corrected file this afternoon.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good. And let's go through the new draft together on Friday morning, before anything goes out.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Friday works for me. Thanks for being so direct, Nora.

questions.q: What improved by eighteen percent?
options: Attendance at the meeting
On-time delivery
Lane-by-lane costs
The number of slides
questions.explanation: Nora praises the chart showing on-time delivery up by eighteen percent.

questions.q: What will Jon do this afternoon?
options: Meet the directors again
Ask finance for the cost table
Rewrite the whole deck from scratch
Send out a corrected file
questions.explanation: Jon says he will send the corrected file this afternoon.

questions.q: Why does Nora say 'Fair, but put them in an appendix'?
options: She accepts his point but offers another solution
She wants him to delete the numbers completely
She disagrees and ends the whole discussion
She asks him to add many more slides
questions.explanation: She agrees some directors wanted the numbers, then suggests an appendix.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of Nora's call?
options: To ask Jon for a new cost analysis
To give Jon feedback on his presentation
To complain about the circulated deck only
To cancel the next steering meeting
questions.explanation: She starts by saying she wants to share thoughts on yesterday's presentation.

script.speaker: A
script.line: IT help desk, Fatima speaking. I've got your chat message, Omar. You can't open the supplier planning folder, correct?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, it says access denied. I started on Monday, and I really need it for the forecast review.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Let me check your account. Hm, you're not in the planning group yet. Normally you need approval from the folder owner, and that takes about three days.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Three days? The review is on Thursday. Is there any way to speed it up?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Give me a second. Oh, that's lucky. The owner, Priya, is online right now, so I'll message her directly and ask for a quick approval.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That would be fantastic. Honestly, I was expecting to wait until next week.

script.speaker: A
script.line: She just replied, and she approved it. Your access should work within ten minutes. It's valid for twelve weeks, because you're a temporary hire, and then we renew it.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Twelve weeks, got it. So I don't need to fill in the long request form on Tuesday anymore?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Exactly, you can skip it. Just log out and back in, and tell me if it still fails.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Will do. Thanks, Fatima, you saved my week.

questions.q: How long will Omar's access last before it needs renewing?
options: Ten minutes
Until Thursday
Twelve weeks
Three days
questions.explanation: Fatima says the access is valid for twelve weeks.

questions.q: How does Omar feel about the quick approval?
options: Worried about the long form
Relieved and grateful
Indifferent to the result
Annoyed with Priya
questions.explanation: He says it would be fantastic, he expected to wait, and thanks her for saving his week.

questions.q: What should Omar do now?
options: Wait three more days
Call Priya himself
Log out and log in again
Fill in the form on Tuesday
questions.explanation: Fatima tells him to log out and back in and report if it still fails.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hello Victor, it's Rachel from production planning. Thanks for taking my call. We both asked for the validation specialist in the same week next month.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, I noticed that. She's booked for my audit preparation, and my deadline is fixed.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Mine is flexible, to be honest. I only need her for fifteen percent of her time, about two days. Could she split her week between us?

script.speaker: B
script.line: That could work. The audit is in three weeks, so I need her every morning from Monday.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Fine, then I'll take her afternoons on Tuesday and Wednesday. If we can't agree with her, we escalate to our director.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Agreed, but only if we fail. I'll confirm the mornings with her today.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good. I'll send you a short email with the plan by tomorrow noon.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Perfect. And I'll update the shared calendar by Friday.

questions.q: How much of the specialist's time does Rachel need?
options: About fifteen percent
Every single morning
About three weeks of it
A full week of it
questions.explanation: Rachel says she only needs her for fifteen percent of her time.

questions.q: Who will update the shared calendar?
options: The specialist
Rachel
The director
Victor
questions.explanation: Victor says he will update the shared calendar by Friday.

questions.q: Why does Rachel mention the director?
options: To say that the director booked the specialist
To ask the director for a decision right now
To describe what they do if they fail to agree
To complain about the audit schedule
questions.explanation: She says they escalate to the director only if they can't agree.

questions.q: What do Rachel and Victor agree in the end?
options: To share the specialist between them
To let the director decide for them
To postpone the audit by a month
To hire a second specialist soon
questions.explanation: Victor takes the mornings and Rachel the afternoons.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Claire, thanks for picking up. I'll be direct: the last consignment arrived nine days late, and the contract's penalty clause is fifteen percent of the order value.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I understand your position, Victor, but I'd push back a little. Your team changed the quantity in the second week, after we had already scheduled the line.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That change was small, though. Surely it doesn't explain nine days.

script.speaker: B
script.line: It cost us four days, because the new quantity needed a different tooling setup. Take a look at the production log, which I can share now.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Please do. Right, I see the changeover entry. So four days are on our side, and the remaining five are yours?

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's how I read it. So the penalty should cover five days at most, not nine.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Fair enough. I'd rather apply the clause to five days only. I'll recalculate and send you the figure by Friday.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's reasonable, and I'd rather settle this now than let it drag on. I'll send the signed log extract so your finance team can file it.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Thank you, Claire. I'll copy my finance colleague so it's all on record.

questions.q: What is the call mainly about?
options: A plan to renegotiate the whole contract
A request to change the next order
A complaint about the supplier's invoice
A late-delivery penalty both sides share
questions.explanation: They agree the penalty applies only to the days that were the supplier's fault.

questions.q: For how many days of the delay does Claire's side accept responsibility?
options: Fifteen days
Five days
Four days
Nine days
questions.explanation: After the log, Victor says four days are on his side and the remaining five are Claire's.

questions.q: Why does Claire disagree with applying the full penalty?
options: Her factory was closed for a long holiday
The contract has no penalty clause at all
The change meant a new tooling setup
The carrier lost several pallets on the road
questions.explanation: Claire says the changed quantity needed a different tooling setup and cost four days.

questions.q: What will Victor do next?
options: Order a new consignment from Claire
Cancel the contract with the supplier
Share the production log with finance
Recalculate and send the figure
questions.explanation: He says he will recalculate and send the figure by Friday.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Jon, got a minute? I'm afraid the rollout is going to slip by two weeks, and I'd like to settle what we tell the steering committee before the meeting.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Two weeks, ouch. Is it the data migration again?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Partly. The test cycle found that about twenty percent of the supplier records failed validation, and cleaning them by hand will take time.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Then let's be upfront. I'd give them a firm date, the twenty-fourth of June, rather than a vague late June.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Honestly, I'd prefer a range. If we promise the twenty-fourth and miss it again, we lose all credibility.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Fair point. How about this: we present the twenty-fourth as a target, and I drop my demand for a hard commitment if you agree to a checkpoint in two weeks.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I can live with that. I give up the range, you stop pushing for a guarantee. The committee meets today at four thirty, so I'll update the slides now.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good. Send them to me before the call and I'll double-check the numbers.

questions.q: What do the two colleagues agree on?
options: A cancellation of the whole rollout
A target date with a checkpoint
A vague range and no checkpoint
A firm and guaranteed date
questions.explanation: Jon suggests a target date plus a checkpoint, and Nora accepts.

questions.q: When does the steering committee meet?
options: Today at four thirty
Early in June
On the twenty-fourth of June
In two weeks
questions.explanation: Nora says the committee meets today at four thirty.

questions.q: Why does Nora prefer a range at first?
options: She wants to avoid meeting the committee
She thinks the rollout will be cancelled soon
A missed date would hurt their credibility
She does not trust the supplier data at all
questions.explanation: She says promising the twenty-fourth and missing it would cost them credibility.

questions.q: What will Nora do next?
options: Clean the supplier records
Write a new test plan
Call the steering committee
Update the slides
questions.explanation: She says she will update the slides now.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Ethan, I'm glad I caught you. About the urgent order for the hospital distributor, do you want air or sea?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Honestly, I can't decide. What are the numbers?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Air freight costs about four times more, but it arrives in four days. Sea takes five weeks.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Five weeks is too long. The customer has already waited twelve weeks for this order, and they're getting nervous.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I understand. But air has a risk too, because cargo space is tight before the summer holidays.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Hmm. What if we split it? Air for the first pallets and sea for the rest?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good idea. I can put the first six pallets on a flight that leaves on the twenty-second of July, and the rest goes by ship.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That works for me. The customer will be happy, and the extra cost isn't so bad.

script.speaker: A
script.line: One small thing, though. The export declaration needs a signature from your quality team, and I don't see it in the documents.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Oh, I think it's still on someone's desk. I'm a bit worried now.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Don't worry. If you send it by tomorrow, I can still confirm the booking.

script.line: Yes. On the third of March, one pallet was packed with the old leaflet version. That's about one hundred and twenty cartons.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Did the product reach the customer?

script.speaker: A
script.line: No, we caught it at the warehouse check. The pallet is on hold, and the product itself isn't affected, only the leaflet.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good. So the corrective action is to reopen the cartons and insert the right leaflet?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Yes, and we'll add a second check at the end of the line. One more thing: the warehouse says another pallet from the same batch may have the same problem.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Then let's not assume. I'll ask them to inspect it tomorrow and call you with the result.

questions.q: How many pallets are confirmed to have the wrong leaflet?

One
Two
One hundred and twenty
questions.explanation: Amara says one pallet was packed with the old leaflet.

questions.q: What is the main point of the call?
options: A pallet was lost in transport
A customer complained about a leaflet
A packaging error was caught in time
The product itself was damaged badly
questions.explanation: Amara says they caught it at the warehouse check and the product is not affected.

questions.q: What does the warehouse check show?
options: The corrective action has failed
The control step worked as a safety net
The whole line must close now
Every pallet was packed correctly
questions.explanation: The pallet was stopped at the warehouse check, before it left.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Sorry I'm late, Sara. My train was delayed for forty minutes. What did I miss?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Not much, don't worry. We mostly talked about the plan for the new product launch in the north.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Did we already decide the launch date? I need it for my calendar.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes. We agreed on the twenty-ninth of May for the first delivery.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good. And how big is the first order?

script.speaker: B
script.line: One thousand cartons. No, wait, sorry. I looked at the wrong line. It's twelve hundred cartons.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Twelve hundred. Okay. Who will make them?

script.speaker: B
script.line: The factory in the north. They need the artwork by Thursday.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Thursday is soon. Who sends the artwork?

script.speaker: B
script.line: I do. Marketing already approved it this morning.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Great. Is there anything I need to do?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, please check the transport plan and give us your answer before the next meeting.

questions.q: What is the size of the first order?

Twelve thousand cartons
One thousand cartons
Two hundred cartons
questions.explanation: Sara first says one thousand, then corrects it to twelve hundred cartons.

questions.q: What is the conversation mostly about?
options: A change of factory in the north
A problem with the marketing team
A delayed train on the way in
Decisions about a product launch
questions.explanation: Sara tells Daniel the launch date, order size, factory and tasks.

questions.q: What can we infer from 'Marketing already approved it this morning'?
options: The artwork is still missing today
The launch date will change soon
The artwork can be sent on time
The factory is in the south
questions.explanation: Because the artwork is approved, Sara can send it before Thursday.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hi Tomas, it's Lucia. I just posted in the chat. We're organizing a goodbye lunch for Marta, since she's moving to Lisbon, and we'd love you to come.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Of course, she's been great to work with. When is it?

script.speaker: A
script.line: I was thinking Tuesday, the fourteenth of October, around half past twelve.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Hmm, Tuesday is difficult. I have our monthly review that morning, and it often runs late. Could we do Wednesday?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Wednesday doesn't work, because Marta is on the road. What if you join us for dessert and coffee? We'd stay until two.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That I can do. I'll leave the review as soon as it ends.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Perfect. For the place, I thought of the Italian restaurant by the port, but it's very noisy. Do you know somewhere quieter?

script.speaker: B
script.line: There's a small Basque restaurant behind the station, with a back room. Shall I book it?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Yes, please, for eight people. Now, the gift. I thought of a nice notebook.

script.speaker: B
script.line: She's always taking notes, so that's perfect. I'll pay my share by transfer if you send me the details.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Will do. Thanks, Tomas, I'm sure she'll be touched.

questions.q: What is the main result of the call?
options: They move the whole lunch to Wednesday
They cancel the lunch for Marta
They decide that Tomas will skip it
Tomas will join the lunch late
questions.explanation: Tomas cannot make the start, so he will join for dessert and coffee.

questions.q: Where will the lunch take place?
options: In Marta's office
At the canteen by the port
At a small Basque restaurant
At the Italian restaurant
questions.explanation: Tomas suggests the Basque restaurant behind the station, and Lucia says yes.

questions.q: Why can't Tomas be there at the start?
options: He dislikes noisy restaurants
His monthly review may run late
He has a dentist appointment
He is travelling to Lisbon
questions.explanation: He says the monthly review that morning often runs late.

questions.q: What can we infer about the Italian restaurant?
options: It was rejected because of the noise
It is too far away from work
Marta dislikes Italian food
It is always closed on Tuesdays
questions.explanation: Lucia calls it very noisy and asks for somewhere quieter.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good morning, Ms. Dana. I appreciate that you came in, and I'm glad we can discuss the damaged cartons face to face.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good morning. Frankly, I'm disappointed. Sixty cartons arrived crushed, and I have customers waiting.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I apologize sincerely. Could you tell me exactly what you found when the pallets arrived?

script.speaker: B
script.line: The bottom layer collapsed on two pallets. The straps were loose, as if they had been loaded in a hurry.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Understood. We'll need photographs and the delivery note to open a claim.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I have both here. What I want, though, is a full replacement shipped this week.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I can't promise a full replacement this week. A new print run takes about eight weeks. But I do have thirty cartons in stock that could leave tomorrow.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Thirty is only half. I'd accept that if the rest follows within four weeks, not eight.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I'll push for four weeks. In return, could you keep the damaged cartons for our inspector rather than sending them back? That saves us time.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Fine, I'll give up on returning them, as long as the credit note arrives quickly.

script.speaker: A
script.line: You'll have it by Friday, and I'll send you a written summary of everything we agreed.

questions.q: What do Pavel and Dana agree in the end?
options: Part of the order now, the rest later
A full refund and no replacement
A complete replacement this week
A new contract with another supplier
questions.explanation: Pavel offers thirty cartons tomorrow and Dana accepts if the rest follows in four weeks.

questions.q: How many cartons can be sent tomorrow?
options: Sixty
Thirty
Eight
Four
questions.explanation: Pavel says he has thirty cartons in stock that could leave tomorrow.

questions.q: What will Pavel do next?
options: Collect the damaged cartons
Visit Dana's warehouse
Send a credit note by Friday
Print sixty new cartons today
questions.explanation: He promises the credit note by Friday, plus a written summary.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Tomas, do you have five minutes? I'm new, and in meetings everyone keeps saying lead time, safety stock, OTIF. I nod, but I don't really follow.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Of course. Lead time is simply the time between placing an order and receiving it. For our main supplier it's six weeks.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Okay, that helps. And what about safety stock?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Extra inventory we keep as a cushion, in case demand jumps or a delivery is late.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That makes sense. And what about OTIF?

script.speaker: B
script.line: On time, in full. It shows whether an order arrived by the promised date, complete. Last month we shipped six hundred order lines, and only a few failed.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Nice. And what about the term batch release?

script.speaker: B
script.line: That one is more technical. It's the final quality sign-off before a batch can be sold. Honestly, I'd rather not explain it badly on the phone.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Could you write it down for me? A short note would be great.

script.speaker: B
script.line: A full note is too much work this week, but I can do something better. I'll introduce you to Hana from quality, and she'll explain it on Monday.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Oh, that would be even better. What time on Monday?

script.speaker: B
script.line: I'll ask her and message you this afternoon. In the meantime, have a look at the glossary on the intranet.

questions.q: What does OTIF measure?
options: When a batch gets its quality sign-off
How much extra stock the team keeps
How long a supplier takes to deliver
Whether orders are on time and complete
questions.explanation: Tomas explains OTIF as on time, in full: the promised date and the complete quantity.

questions.q: Why does Tomas not explain batch release himself?
options: He does not know the term himself
It is not used in the company
He is late for another meeting
He might explain it badly
questions.explanation: He says it is more technical and he would rather not explain it badly.

questions.q: What will Tomas do this afternoon?
options: Update the glossary on the intranet
Message Lucia about Hana's time
Call the main supplier today
Write a full note for Lucia
questions.explanation: He says he will ask Hana and message Lucia this afternoon.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Ingrid, I understand you have two files and a message from the regional team, and you're not sure which forecast is current.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Exactly. One file is dated Friday, the other is called final, version two, and the regional team insists their numbers from this morning are the latest.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Let's look at both. The Friday file shows demand for the second half up by forty percent. The other file is almost flat.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Forty percent seems wildly optimistic. But the regional message says the tender volumes were added after the review.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Which would explain the jump. Whoever added them should have changed the file name.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I'd prefer to use the flat one, because it passed our review. I assume you'd prefer the Friday file.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I would, but we can't ignore the review. What if we use the reviewed file as our base and add the tender volumes only as a separate line?

script.speaker: B
script.line: I can accept that compromise. I give up the clean single number, and you give up the full forty percent.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Agreed. We'll flag clearly which volumes are unconfirmed, in case someone reads it out of context.

script.speaker: B
script.line: And the board pack closes on the twenty-seventh of June, so we should lock the version by then.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Yes. I'll send the combined file tomorrow and name it properly this time, with the date in it.

questions.q: How do they resolve the problem?
options: They use the Friday file as it is
They wait for a new regional file
A reviewed base plus a separate tender line
They delete both files and restart
questions.explanation: Luis proposes the reviewed file as the base plus a separate tender line, and Ingrid agrees.

questions.q: How much higher does the Friday file show demand?
options: Forty percent
Almost nothing
Fifty percent
Twenty-seven percent
questions.explanation: Luis says the Friday file shows the second half up by forty percent.

questions.q: How does Ingrid feel about the Friday file at first?
options: Indifferent to the whole file
Enthusiastic about the numbers
Doubtful about its optimism
Angry at the regional team
questions.explanation: She says forty percent seems wildly optimistic.

questions.q: What can we infer about the file names?
options: The board chose the names
They were not managed carefully
They are all dated correctly
They follow a strict policy
questions.explanation: Luis says whoever added volumes should have changed the name and promises a proper name this time.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Nora, I need to flag a problem. Our pallet storage is almost full, and forty percent of the space is taken by one product family.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Which one is it? Is it the winter packs?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Yes, the winter packs. Three more trucks arrive on Tuesday, and I simply don't have room for them.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Can any of those deliveries be delayed?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Possibly two of them. The third carries the urgent items.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Then let's postpone those two. I'll ask the supplier to hold them for one week.

script.speaker: A
script.line: One week won't be enough. I'd need two weeks before there's space.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Hold on, I've just seen an email. The distributor is collecting twelve pallets of winter packs tomorrow, much earlier than planned.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's good news! That frees up enough space, so one week might be fine after all.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Then we postpone the two trucks by a week only, and keep the third one as planned.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Agreed. I'll update the dock schedule this afternoon and confirm with the transport office.

questions.q: For how long will the two deliveries be postponed in the end?
options: One week
Two weeks
Three weeks
Until Tuesday
questions.explanation: After the good news, Nora says they postpone the two trucks by a week only.

questions.q: What is the main problem at the start of the call?

A carrier lost all three trucks
The distributor cancelled its big order
Not enough room for incoming trucks
questions.explanation: Ibrahim says storage is almost full and he has no room for the trucks.

questions.q: What can we infer about the third truck?
options: It will be sent back to the plant
It carries the winter packs
It will be postponed for two weeks
It arrives as planned, being urgent

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hello Hannah, it's Tomas from the planning team. I need a flight to the supply-chain conference in Lisbon.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Hi Tomas. Sure, what dates are you thinking of?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Out on the Monday before, and back on Thursday evening.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I see two options. The first lands at eleven in the morning and costs more. The second is cheaper, but arrives at nine at night, with a stop.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hmm. I'd like to arrive in the morning so I can prepare my talk. But our policy says cheaper fares must be booked twelve weeks ahead, doesn't it?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, and you're booking late, so the expensive flight needs a manager's approval.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Right. My manager is travelling, which is a problem.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Wait, let me check something. Oh, good news. The airline has just released a promotional fare on the morning flight, and it's cheaper than the night flight.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Really? Then there's no problem with the policy.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Correct. The promotional fare is within policy, so no approval is needed.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Fantastic. Please book it. Can you add a vegetarian meal?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Done. I'll email the confirmation in a few minutes.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Thanks, Hannah. You made my day.

questions.q: What do they decide in the end?
options: To book the night flight with a stop
To cancel the trip to Lisbon
The morning flight at the special fare
To wait for the manager's approval
questions.explanation: Hannah finds a promotional fare on the morning flight, and Tomas asks her to book it.

questions.q: When does the morning flight land?
options: At eleven in the morning
At nine at night
On Thursday evening
At noon, after Frankfurt
questions.explanation: Hannah says the first option lands at eleven in the morning.
