options: He dislikes stopping in Frankfurt
He wants time to prepare his talk
It is the cheapest option
His manager asked for it
questions.explanation: He says he wants to arrive in the morning to prepare his talk.

questions.q: Why will Tomas not need his manager's approval?
options: Hannah will pay for it herself
He is booking early enough
His manager is already abroad
The new fare is inside the policy
questions.explanation: Hannah says the promotional fare is within policy, so no approval is needed.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good afternoon, how can I help you?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Hi. My flight from Frankfurt was over an hour late, so I'll miss my connection to Madrid. I have a supplier meeting there on the seventeenth of November, tomorrow morning.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I'm sorry about that. Let me check your booking. Yes, your connection leaves in twenty-five minutes, so you won't make it.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's what I feared. I booked this trip eight weeks ago, and it's the first time anything has gone wrong. What are my options?

script.speaker: A
script.line: The next flight to Madrid leaves at seven this evening and lands at nine fifteen. I have seats on it.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That works. Will my suitcase follow me automatically?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Yes, I'll re-tag it now. It should be on the same flight, but please check the belt anyway.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Great. I also have to tell my host in Madrid that I'll arrive late. She was going to pick me up at the airport.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Then use the lounge while you wait. I'll give you a pass, and it has free Wi-Fi.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's very kind. I'll message her right now, and call again once I land.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Perfect. I'll also email you a confirmation within ten minutes, so you have proof of the delay for your expense report.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Brilliant. Thanks so much, you've been very calm about all this.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Happy to help. Have a safe flight.

questions.q: What is the main result of the conversation?
options: The traveller cancels the whole trip
The traveller is rebooked on a later flight
The traveller takes a train instead
The traveller gets a hotel voucher
questions.explanation: The agent books him on the seven o'clock flight to Madrid.

questions.q: When will the new flight land?
options: At nine fifteen
In the morning
At seven
In twenty-five minutes
questions.explanation: The agent says the evening flight lands at nine fifteen.

questions.q: How does the traveller feel at the end?
options: Still very angry
Completely uninterested
Grateful and more relaxed
Embarrassed about the delay
questions.explanation: He thanks the agent and says she has been very calm.

questions.q: Why will the agent send an email confirmation?
options: So the lounge will accept him
So he can prove the delay for expenses
So he can skip the meeting
So the host can pick up his suitcase
questions.explanation: She says it gives proof of the delay for his expense report.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Elena, thanks for dialing in. I thought we could agree on how to compare the two vendors and then split the next steps.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good idea. I've been reading both proposals. The first vendor says it improves forecast accuracy by twenty percent.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Yes, but that figure comes from their demo data. We should ask for a pilot on our own history.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Okay, so you want them to pilot it on twenty percent of our products?

script.speaker: A
script.line: No, no, sorry, I wasn't clear. The twenty percent is the improvement they claim. I meant a pilot on a small sample of our past data, any size.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Ah, got it, I mixed the two up. So the criteria are accuracy on our data, integration effort and price.

script.speaker: A
script.line: And implementation time. The second vendor says ten weeks, which is much faster.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Though faster isn't always better. I'd weigh integration effort higher than speed.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Fair. I'll propose weights tomorrow. Meanwhile, could you ask both vendors for references from other pharma companies?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Sure. And you'll talk to our data team about what integration would involve?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Yes. Shall we compare notes next Thursday at half past one?

script.speaker: B
script.line: One thirty works. I'll block the time.

questions.q: What does the twenty percent refer to?
options: The improvement the vendor claims
The part of the system already built
The share of products in a pilot
A discount on the vendor's price
questions.explanation: Arjun clarifies that the twenty percent is the improvement the vendor claims.

questions.q: What will Elena do next?
options: Propose weights for the criteria
Talk to the data team
Run the pilot herself
Ask both vendors for references
questions.explanation: Arjun asks her to request references, and she says sure.

questions.q: Why does Arjun say 'No, no, sorry, I wasn't clear'?
options: To end the call early
To refuse the first vendor
To correct a misunderstanding
To change the meeting time
questions.explanation: Elena misread the twenty percent, and he explains what he meant.

questions.q: What is the main outcome of the call?
options: They choose the second vendor today
They agree criteria and next steps
They give the data team the decision
They cancel the whole project
questions.explanation: They list criteria and split tasks before meeting again.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hi Olivia, thanks for the call. I'd like to ask for an extra production slot next month. Our demand is higher than planned.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Hi Henrik. How much extra are we talking about?

script.speaker: A
script.line: About eighty orders more, so one additional batch.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Let me check the schedule. Hmm, next month is completely full. The earliest free slot is the fifth of October.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's later than I hoped. Honestly, I thought you had spare capacity, because your line looked idle in August.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I see why you'd think so, but look at the planning sheet. In August we had maintenance, so the line looked idle, but the machine wasn't available.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Ah, I see it now. Maintenance explains the gap. So the fifth of October is the first option?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, and I can hold it for you, on one condition. You confirm by Friday, and the film must be here two weeks before. Last time it took ten weeks.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Understood. Ten weeks is a worry, but I'll ask our buyer to expedite and tell you by Friday.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Perfect. I'll keep the slot on hold until then.

questions.q: When is the first free production slot?
options: On the fifth of October
Early next month
At the end of August
On Friday this week
questions.explanation: Olivia says the earliest free slot is the fifth of October.

questions.q: Why did the line look idle in August?
options: Orders were very low
The film had not arrived yet
Staff were on holiday
It was in maintenance
questions.explanation: Olivia says August was maintenance, so the machine wasn't available.

questions.q: What can we infer about Henrik's chance to keep the slot?
options: It is already fully guaranteed
It depends on the maintenance team
It depends on the film arriving in time
It depends on Olivia's holiday plans
questions.explanation: Olivia holds the slot only if the order is confirmed and the film arrives early.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hi Pedro, I'm writing about the clinic order. Could you pull the delivery forward by one week? Our own schedule changed.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Hi Chloe. I'd like to help, but the production slot is fixed, and the order was planned for eight weeks from now.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Honestly, I thought the batch was already finished. Isn't it in the warehouse?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Let me share the status sheet on the call. Look, the batch is still in quality testing, and release is expected on Monday.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hmm, I see. So release is Monday, and the earliest shipping is Tuesday?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes. But here's an option. The order for the northern hospital is also scheduled to ship on Tuesday. If they agree to wait a week, I can send yours then.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I'd rather not delay a hospital. But if they accept, fine. Can you ask them?

script.speaker: B

questions.q: When is the batch release expected?

In eight weeks
On Monday
In one week

questions.q: Why can't Pedro ship the order right now?
options: The carrier is not available
The warehouse is already full
The clinic cancelled the order
The batch is in quality testing

questions.q: What is the main result of the conversation?
options: Pedro refuses to help at all
Pedro offers to swap two orders
Pedro ships the whole batch today
Chloe cancels the whole order
questions.explanation: He offers to send Chloe's order on Tuesday if the northern hospital accepts to wait a week.

questions.q: What will Pedro do next?
options: Ask the hospital's planner
Change the production slot today
Release the batch himself
Contact the clinic directly
questions.explanation: He says he will message the planner of the northern hospital.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Adam, do you have a minute while we walk? I wanted to share an observation about our Monday meeting. Nothing serious.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Sure, go ahead. Is something wrong?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Not wrong, but I've noticed the updates run long. Last week we spent over thirty-five percent of the hour on the first two people, and we never reached the decisions.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Ah. I suppose I do tend to explain everything in detail. And honestly, there's never an agenda.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's fair, and partly my fault for not asking for one. Could we try a simple structure? Two minutes per update, then decisions, then risks.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I like that. Should I send the agenda the day before?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Yes, by noon on Friday. And I'd like to start at eleven instead of ten, to give people time to prepare.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That would help me too. But I'm not sure the other team leads can make eleven.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good point. I need to ask Samira, who manages the shared room, whether it's free at eleven. Until she answers, we keep the old time.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Fine. I'll draft the new format and test it next Monday anyway.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Great. Thanks for taking the feedback so well, Adam.

questions.q: What proportion of last week's meeting went on the first two updates?

About eleven percent
Over thirty-five percent
Under ten percent
questions.explanation: Elena says over thirty-five percent of the hour went on the first two people.

questions.q: What is the main outcome of the conversation?
options: They move the meeting to eleven for sure
They drop the agenda for good
They cancel the Monday meeting
A simple structure, but the time is open
questions.explanation: They agree on updates, decisions and risks, but the time depends on the room.

questions.q: Who will check whether the room is free at eleven?
options: Elena, by asking Samira
Adam, by asking the team leads
The team leads, by email
Samira, by asking Elena

script.speaker: A
script.line: HR service desk, Mark speaking. How can I help?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Hello Mark, it's Katarina from logistics. I have nine unused vacation days, and I'd like to know whether I can carry them over.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good question. The rule is that you can carry over up to five days. The rest expire at year end.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Five only? That's a shame. Is there any exception? The project was very heavy this year.

script.speaker: A
script.line: There is, if your manager confirms in writing that you couldn't take them for business reasons. Then you keep all nine, but you must use them within twelve weeks.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I'll ask my manager. Could you walk me through the form in person? Tomorrow in your office, maybe?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Tomorrow I'm out. How about Thursday at ten in my office?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Thursday I'm in a workshop all day. Could we do a video call on Friday instead?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Friday works, but my office is being repaired, so let's make it a video call at nine.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Perfect, thanks. I'll bring my manager's note.

questions.q: When and how will they go through the form?
options: Tomorrow in Mark's office
On Friday at nine by video call
On Thursday by video call
On Thursday at ten in his office
questions.explanation: After two changes, Mark and Katarina agree on a video call on Friday at nine.

questions.q: Why can't Katarina automatically keep all nine days?
options: Vacation days never carry over
Her manager has already refused
She has no unused days left
The standard limit is five days
questions.explanation: Mark says the rule is up to five days unless the manager confirms in writing.

questions.q: What can we infer about Katarina's next step?
options: She must visit the HR office tomorrow
She needs a note from her manager
She must cancel her vacation days
She must work on Friday morning
questions.explanation: Mark says the exception requires written confirmation, so she says she will ask her manager.

title: Peaks in months four and five

script.speaker: A
script.line: Pavel, thanks for coming in. I've brought the new twelve-month rolling forecast, and I'd like to walk you through it.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Thanks, Hannah. Let me see. Months four and five jump quite a bit. Honestly, those peaks worry me.

script.speaker: A
script.line: They reflect two tenders. Combined, they push demand about a third above the average.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's more than our line can cover without extra shifts. We'd want a firm commitment before we invest in capacity.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I can't give a firm commitment on months four and five yet. The tenders aren't decided, and forecasts are not orders.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Understood, but then I'd say the peaks are unrealistic for us. Last year you forecast a peak in month five, and it came in much lower.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Let me check that. Right, the actual peak was about two thirds of what we forecast, so you're right that it was overstated. This year the tenders are documented, though.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Then give me the tender dates, and I'll decide whether to book extra capacity.

script.speaker: A
script.line: The decision on the tenders is due on Wednesday, the twenty-fourth of May. Until then, I'll update you every two weeks.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That works. And if the tenders go through, can we agree a minimum volume?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Yes, I'll ask my director and answer you in our next update.

questions.q: When is the tender decision due?
options: At the end of month five
On Wednesday next week
Wednesday the twenty-fourth of May
Two weeks from today
questions.explanation: Hannah says the decision is due on Wednesday, the twenty-fourth of May.

questions.q: How does Pavel feel about the forecast peaks?
options: Worried and doubtful
Delighted and eager
Relaxed and uninterested
Angry and hostile
questions.explanation: He says the peaks worry him and calls them unrealistic.

questions.q: What will Hannah do next?
options: Cancel the twelve-month forecast
Sign a firm commitment today
Ask her director about a minimum
Book extra shifts for Pavel
questions.explanation: She says she will ask her director and answer in the next update.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Morning, Mei. Got a minute? I need to know when batch R V four oh three oh can be released, because the customer keeps asking me.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Hi, Chris. Honestly, I'm not sure yet. I'm on my own this week, and my desk looks like a paper storm.

script.speaker: A
script.line: No problem. Just tell me what's still open and we'll see what's realistic.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Well, the final potency test finishes on Thursday, and then I need a second review of the results. That takes a day, if nothing goes wrong.

script.speaker: A
script.line: So Friday at the earliest. Is that your only worry?

script.speaker: B
script.line: No, there's a gap in the paperwork. The packaging record for the last eighty units has no signature, and I can't release anything without it.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Eighty units only? That's a small part of the batch.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, about five percent, but the rule is the same. One missing signature and the whole batch stays on hold.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Okay, take a breath. You've got enough on your plate, so let me chase the signature. I'll talk to the packaging supervisor this afternoon.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Would you? That would help a lot. I was going to spend my whole morning on it.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Of course. You focus on the tests and the review. If we get the signature today, Friday still works.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good. If it comes through, I'll tell you by lunchtime tomorrow, and you can confirm the date to the customer.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Perfect. And Mei, go and get yourself a coffee. We'll get there.

questions.q: Why does Chris talk to Mei?
options: To ask her to repeat a failed potency test on the batch
To tell her that the customer has cancelled the order
To find out when a batch can be released and what is holding it up
To offer to take over all of her quality reviews
questions.explanation: Chris asks when the batch can be released and Mei lists the remaining checks and the paperwork gap.

questions.q: When is the earliest possible release date?
options: On Friday
On Thursday
Tomorrow at lunchtime
This afternoon
questions.explanation: Chris says 'So Friday at the earliest' after Mei explains the test and the review day.

questions.q: How does Mei feel at the start of the conversation?
options: Annoyed with the packaging team
Confident about the release date
Bored with the routine checks
Overwhelmed by her workload
questions.explanation: She says she is on her own and her desk looks like a paper storm.

questions.q: What can we infer about the release rules in this company?
options: Units are released one by one as they pass
A small paperwork gap can block a whole batch
Only managers are allowed to sign packaging records
Customers may accept batches without full documents
questions.explanation: Mei says one missing signature and the whole batch stays on hold.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good morning, Victor. Packaging found a labelling mistake on a pallet from batch S T nineteen twenty, and I wanted you to hear it from me.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good morning, Sofia. I appreciate that. What exactly is wrong with the label?

script.speaker: A
script.line: The expiry date is printed three weeks later than it should be. One of the packers noticed it while he was scanning the cases.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Then the pallet cannot move. Please put it into quarantine straight away and mark it clearly, so nobody picks it by mistake.

script.speaker: A
script.line: It's already in the blocked area, and the warehouse knows. Now, rework: the earliest slot on the relabelling line is the twenty-fourth of October.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That is acceptable, provided two people check the new labels. Let's meet tomorrow at nine in the packaging hall to look at the pallet together.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That works for me, though I would like to bring the supervisor.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Of course. Actually, I've just remembered a supplier audit at nine. Could we make it ten instead?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Ten is fine. But I should warn you that the hall will be used for a line trial at that time, and it will be very noisy.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Then we shouldn't talk there. Is meeting room two, on the second floor, free?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Let me check. Yes, it's free at ten. So, ten o'clock, meeting room two, and I will bring photographs of the pallet.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Excellent. Please send me the invitation with the batch details, so that everything is documented.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Certainly. I'll send it this afternoon. Thank you for your quick decision, Victor.

questions.q: Where and when will Sofia and Victor meet?
options: At nine in the packaging hall
At ten in the packaging hall
At ten in meeting room two
At nine in meeting room two
questions.explanation: The time moves from nine to ten and the place moves from the hall to meeting room two.

questions.q: Why does the pallet have to stay in quarantine?
options: The label shows an expiry date that is three weeks too late
The pallet was damaged while it was being moved
The cases on it belong to a different product
It was stored at the wrong temperature overnight
questions.explanation: Sofia says the expiry date is printed three weeks later than it should be.

questions.q: What can we infer about the pallet?
options: It will be destroyed after the meeting
It has already been delivered to a customer
It will be relabelled by the supplier
It will not be shipped until the labels have been replaced
questions.explanation: Victor says the pallet cannot move and agrees to a rework slot on the relabelling line.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hi Jon, thanks for picking up. I know the timing isn't great, but I wanted to go through the stockout properly before the review.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Sure, Elena. Honestly, I'm still annoyed. Two weeks without stock for a key product is hard to explain. What happened?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Two things. Sales changed the forecast late, after we'd frozen the plan, and nobody told us in time.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Okay, and what was the second thing?

script.speaker: A
script.line: We hadn't reviewed safety stock for that item since last spring. The buffer was based on old demand, so it was far too low.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Right. So one problem was communication and the other was our own process. I don't love the second one.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Fair. I'd suggest a monthly safety stock review, and a rule that any forecast change after the freeze needs my approval.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That sounds sensible. Who checks it, and when do we start?

script.speaker: A
script.line: I'll own it and start next month. But there's something else. Just before this call, the supplier wrote to me with good news.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Go on, I could use some.

script.speaker: A
script.line: They finished an extra batch early. A partial shipment will arrive on the twenty-second of January, so the gap will be shorter than we feared.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That changes things. We don't need the emergency air freight now. Please cancel it, and let's keep that money for a higher safety stock.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Will do. Should I send you the new review schedule before we speak again?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, and let's talk tomorrow at ten fifteen my time, so I can give the directors a clean story.

questions.q: When will the partial shipment arrive?
options: Next month
On the twenty-second of January
Tomorrow at ten fifteen
In two weeks
questions.explanation: Elena says a partial shipment will arrive on the twenty-second of January.

questions.q: What will Elena do about the emergency air freight?
options: Pay for it from the safety stock budget
Move it to next month
Cancel it
Ask the supplier to organise it
questions.explanation: Jon asks her to cancel it and Elena answers 'Will do'.

questions.q: Why does Elena say 'there's something else'?
options: To introduce news that changes the plan
To blame the sales team once more
To ask for a bigger budget
To close the conversation politely
questions.explanation: She then explains the supplier's good news about an early batch.

questions.q: What is the call mainly about?
options: Planning an audit of a supplier
Introducing a new forecasting tool
Negotiating a lower freight price
Why a stockout happened and how to avoid another one
questions.explanation: They discuss the late forecast change and the missing safety stock review, and agree on new rules.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Dana, hi, thanks for squeezing me in. I wanted to run something by you before the budget window closes.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Of course. Is this the conference in Lisbon you mentioned? I'm afraid travel is frozen until the summer.

script.speaker: A
script.line: No, no, it isn't a conference. It's an online course on probabilistic forecasting, reference T C fourteen fifty-five, run by a university.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Ah, I see, I'd got the wrong end of the stick. So what would it cost, and how much time would you be away from your desk?

script.speaker: A
script.line: About nine hundred euros, and the time is lighter than you'd think. It's one live session a week, on Wednesday at half past four, for six weeks.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Half past four on a Wednesday is right in the middle of our demand review prep. How would we cover that?

script.speaker: A
script.line: I've thought about it. Priya could run the prep on those afternoons, and I'd catch up with the recording. Nothing would slip.

script.speaker: B
script.line: And the relevance? I want to be able to tell finance that this isn't just a nice-to-have.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Our error on slow movers is still the weak spot. The course covers exactly the methods that would help, and I'd present the results to the team afterwards.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's a convincing case. I'll sign off on it, subject to finance agreeing the budget line.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Brilliant. I'll send you the course outline today, so you've got something concrete to forward.

questions.q: What does Mateo want from Dana?
options: Permission to attend a conference in Lisbon
Approval to join an online forecasting course
A larger travel budget for the team
A change to the schedule of the demand review
questions.explanation: Mateo explains it is not a conference but an online course and Dana agrees to approve it.

questions.q: When are the weekly live sessions?
options: On Wednesday at six o'clock
On Wednesday at half past nine
On Wednesday at half past four
On Thursday at half past four
questions.explanation: Mateo says one live session a week, on Wednesday at half past four.

questions.q: Why is Dana worried about the Wednesday sessions?
options: They overlap with preparation for the demand review
They fall on the day finance closes the budget
They are at the time of her own team meeting
They are held while Mateo is usually travelling
questions.explanation: She says half past four on a Wednesday is right in the middle of demand review prep.

questions.q: What will Mateo do after the call?
options: Book a flight to Lisbon
Ask Priya to approve the course
Contact finance about the budget line
Send Dana the course outline
questions.explanation: He says he will send the course outline today so Dana has something to forward.

script.speaker: A
script.line: IT service desk, Fatima speaking. How can I help you today?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Hello, Fatima, Daniel from planning here. My VPN keeps dropping during video calls, and I present on Monday with a huge file on six hundred batches. I'm starting to panic.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Please don't worry, we'll sort this out together. First, are you on Wi-Fi or on a cable, and does it drop at regular intervals?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Wi-Fi, from my home office. It drops about every fifteen minutes, and then I have to log in again, which is very embarrassing in front of the directors.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Understood. Let's try something quick. I'm sending you a setting that forces the VPN to use a more stable protocol. Could you restart the client and join a test call?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Done. Okay, it has held for five minutes already. But last time it also looked fine at first.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's a fair point, so I won't trust it yet. I'll open ticket C K thirty-five twenty-four for the network team and mark it urgent because of your Monday presentation.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Thank you. Will somebody get back to me before then?

script.speaker: A
script.line: The network team checks its queue on Friday morning. I'll chase them myself and call you back before noon, and meanwhile please keep a phone dial-in ready as a backup.

questions.q: Why is Daniel calling the service desk?
options: He cannot open a file with batch data
His VPN disconnects during video calls
He forgot the password for his laptop
His Wi-Fi at home is not working at all
questions.explanation: Daniel says the VPN keeps dropping whenever he joins a video call.

questions.q: When will Fatima call Daniel back?
options: Within fifteen minutes
On Monday before the presentation
On Friday before noon
In five minutes, after the test call
questions.explanation: Fatima says she will chase the team and call him back before noon, after the Friday morning queue check.

questions.q: Why doesn't Fatima trust the quick fix yet?
options: Daniel says it also looked fine at first last time
The protocol she sent is not approved yet
The test call lasted only a minute
The directors asked her to wait
questions.explanation: Daniel says 'last time it also looked fine at first', and Fatima agrees it's a fair point.

questions.q: What will Fatima do next?
options: Visit Daniel's home office to check the cable
Send Daniel a new laptop on Friday
Move his presentation to another day
Open a ticket and follow it up with the network team
questions.explanation: She says she will open a ticket for the network team and chase them herself.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Jon, can you hear me? You were cutting out a moment ago. I just need the headline on line two before we get to the rest of the agenda.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Better now. So, line two goes down for planned maintenance for three days, and the technicians start at ten tomorrow morning.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Three days. What does that cost us in output? I'd rather have a number than a feeling.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Roughly five percent of the week's volume, once you include the restart losses. Oh, and sorry, a correction on the start: eleven, not ten. The contractor has just moved it.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Eleven, got it. Five percent is tolerable, but not if it lands on the orders with tight delivery dates. Which ones are exposed?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Mainly the order under reference K K forty-seven fifty-six. It's the only one that really can't wait, so I'd run it on line one.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Could line one absorb it without pushing out the others?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Only just. We'd lose the buffer we've kept for the export tender, and that's a trade-off I'd rather you made than me.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Fair enough. Let me test it against the plan this afternoon, and I'll tell you which of the lower-priority orders slide to next week.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Perfect. Send me the list by the end of the day and I'll warn the shift leaders.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of the call?
options: To report an unexpected breakdown on a production line
To assess how planned maintenance on one line affects output and orders
To negotiate the price of a maintenance contractor
To announce a new line starting next week
questions.explanation: Elena asks what output is lost and which orders are exposed; Jon explains the maintenance.

questions.q: When will the maintenance start?
options: Tomorrow at ten
Today at eleven
Tomorrow at eleven
In three days at ten
questions.explanation: Jon first says ten, then corrects it: 'eleven, not ten'.

questions.q: What will Elena do this afternoon?
options: Check the effect on the plan and decide which orders move
Call the contractor to change the start time
Brief the shift leaders about the new schedule
Run the urgent order on line two
questions.explanation: She says she will test it against the plan and say which lower-priority orders slide.

questions.q: Why does Jon say 'a correction on the start'?
options: To complain about the quality of the audio
To ask for the maintenance to be postponed
To confirm the figure he gave before
To replace the time he gave earlier with the right one
questions.explanation: He then says 'eleven, not ten', changing the time he had just said.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good afternoon, Mark, this is Emma from Facilities. I'm calling about your desk. We're reorganising the fourth floor, so you will be moving to the fifth.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good afternoon, Emma. That's news to me. When would this happen?

script.speaker: A
script.line: In about three weeks. Your request is registered under K H twenty-seven sixty-one, so please quote that if you need anything.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Thank you. And what about my equipment? I have two monitors and a docking station.

script.speaker: A
script.line: We will move everything the evening before, and it will be connected when you arrive. The new area is also about eight percent bigger, so you'll have more room.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's good to hear. Who will be sitting next to me?

script.speaker: A
script.line: The marketing team, I'm afraid. It can get lively, but there is a quiet room two steps away, which is useful for calls.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I'm on calls most of the day, so that matters. Could we walk around the new area together before the move?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Certainly. Shall we say Monday afternoon, at the reception on the fourth floor?

script.speaker: B
script.line: I have a workshop on Monday. Would Tuesday afternoon be possible?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Tuesday is fine. But the reception will be closed for cleaning, so let's meet at the lifts on the fifth floor instead.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Perfect, Tuesday afternoon at the lifts on the fifth floor. I'll note it down.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Excellent. I'll send a confirmation by email today. Thank you for your patience, Mark.

questions.q: Why is Emma calling Mark?
options: To ask him to give up his monitors
To tell him about a desk move and arrange the details
To invite him to a workshop on Monday
To report a problem with the cleaning schedule
questions.explanation: Emma says he will move to the fifth floor and then discusses equipment, neighbours and a walk-through.

questions.q: When will Emma and Mark walk through the new area?
options: On Monday afternoon
On Monday morning
On Tuesday afternoon
On Tuesday morning
questions.explanation: Monday is rejected because of Mark's workshop, and they agree on Tuesday afternoon.

questions.q: What can we infer about Mark?
options: He needs a quiet place for his calls
He would prefer to stay on the fourth floor
He does not get on with the marketing team
He plans to work from home after the move
questions.explanation: He says he's on calls most of the day, so the quiet room matters to him.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hugo, can you hear me okay? The line's crackling on my side.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Just about. Go ahead, Mei. You said you wanted to talk about your next step.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Yes. I'd like to move into a more strategic planning role eventually, and you've seen people make that jump. What does it take?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Honestly, two things: a view broader than your own product family, and people outside planning knowing your name. Visibility counts as much as skill.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I'd say my results speak for themselves. Our forecast accuracy has improved a lot over the last year.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I'm not sure that's the whole picture. From what I've seen, the headline number hasn't moved much.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Let me pull up the dashboard. Okay, you're partly right. Overall error is only five percent better, but on the fast movers it's much better.

script.speaker: B
script.line: There we go. That's useful, because it tells us which story to tell. Fast movers are a good start, but leadership will ask about the rest.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Fair. So what would you suggest, concretely?

script.speaker: B
script.line: A stretch project. Take the slow movers, find out why the bias is there, and propose a fix. Give it four weeks.

script.speaker: A
script.line: And who would see the result?

script.speaker: B
script.line: You'd present it at the S and O P meeting on the twenty-fourth of February, in front of the commercial and finance leads.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's exactly the visibility I need. Count me in. I'll draft a plan and send it to you before the end of the week.

questions.q: What is the conversation mainly about?
options: How to fix a problem with the video connection
Why the forecast dashboard shows wrong data
Whether Hugo should change departments
How Mei can progress towards a more strategic role
questions.explanation: Mei asks what it takes to move to a strategic role and Hugo suggests a project.

questions.q: How long should the stretch project last?
options: Five weeks
Four weeks
Twenty-four weeks
Four months
questions.explanation: Hugo says 'Give it four weeks'.

questions.q: What does Hugo's suggestion imply about the slow movers?
options: They are the most profitable products
They are forecast by another department
They are where the forecast is weakest
They will soon be removed from sale
questions.explanation: He proposes finding out why the bias exists there, after the dashboard shows overall error barely improved.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hi Elena, Andrew from customer service. Sorry about the connection. You wrote about order C B nineteen oh three, marked urgent, so I've just checked it in the system.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Thanks for getting back to me, Andrew. We placed that order eight weeks ago and my team is running out of patience. Where is it now?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Fair question. Production finished it last week, but about twelve percent of the lot didn't pass inspection and had to be redone. The rest is waiting for release.

script.speaker: B
script.line: So the good part could ship now? Please send it as a partial and give us the redone part later.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I understand why you're asking. To be honest, I'd rather not promise that on this call. Partial shipments on this product have to go through quality first.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Right. So you can't commit to anything before they have looked at it?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Not honestly, no. What I can do is flag the order as top priority, so it's the first one they review, and call you straight after.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Okay. That's better than nothing. Please do that, and send me an email with the status as well.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Of course. You'll have it in your inbox within the hour.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of the call?
options: To give an update on a late urgent order
To cancel an order that was placed earlier
To ask for a discount on a large order
To train Elena on the new ordering system
questions.explanation: Andrew checks the order in the system and tells Elena where it is.

questions.q: How long ago was the order placed?
options: Twelve weeks ago
Last week
One hour ago
Eight weeks ago
questions.explanation: Elena says 'We placed that order eight weeks ago'.

questions.q: What does Andrew mean by 'I'd rather not promise that on this call'?
options: He does not want to talk to Elena any more
He cannot be sure that quality will approve a partial shipment
The whole order has already been shipped
He thinks a partial shipment is a bad idea for her team
questions.explanation: He explains partial shipments have to go through quality first, so he cannot commit.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Thanks for making time, Priya. I'll be quick. Three things to report, and one risk where I need a decision from you.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Go ahead. I'm listening, and I have about twenty minutes before my next meeting.

script.speaker: A
script.line: The supplier scorecard is finished and shared. The demand review deck is about eighty percent ready, and the data cleanup is on track for the end of the month.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good. And what is the risk you mentioned?

script.speaker: A
script.line: The packaging film. Our lead time is eight weeks, and if we don't place the order soon, we could have a gap in March.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I thought we had until the end of the month. And isn't the scorecard presentation on Thursday the bigger priority?

script.speaker: A
script.line: I see it differently. The scorecard can slip, but the film order can't. Eight weeks back from the start of March lands on the eleventh of January.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Let me check that. You're right. Counting backwards, the eleventh really is the deadline. I was using last year's lead time.

script.speaker: A
script.line: It was six weeks last year. The supplier changed it in the autumn.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Then the film goes first. Can you place the order this week, and I'll ask the team to push the presentation to next week?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Yes, I can place it tomorrow if finance approves the amount.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I'll message finance right after this, so approval shouldn't hold us up. I'm glad you raised it early, Daniel.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Thanks. I'd rather have an awkward conversation now than a stockout in March.

questions.q: By what date must the film order be placed?
options: Thursday of this week
The end of the month
The eleventh of January
Eight weeks from today
questions.explanation: Daniel counts eight weeks back from the start of March and gets the eleventh of January.

questions.q: How does Priya feel about Daniel's report at the end?
options: Grateful that he raised the risk early
Irritated that he questioned her priority
Worried that the scorecard is wrong
Indifferent to the packaging film
questions.explanation: She says she is glad he raised it early.

questions.q: What will Priya do next?
options: Place the film order herself
Cancel the scorecard presentation
Call the supplier to shorten the lead time
Ask finance to approve the order
questions.explanation: She says she will message finance right after the meeting so approval won't hold them up.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Okay, everyone is leaving, so let me do a quick summary before we stop. Raj, can you still hear me?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, but the sound is not very good. Please go slowly.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Sure. First, sales will go down by eight percent next month, so we will lower the plan for the two main products.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Right. Who will change the plan?

script.speaker: A
script.line: I will, and I'll finish it by Friday. Second, order K V thirty seventy needs a new supplier date. Raj, you will call the supplier by Wednesday.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Wednesday is a problem. I am travelling, so I can call on Thursday. Is that okay?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Thursday is fine. Third, the new storage area. It will be ready in four weeks, and Sana will check the shelves.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes. And there is one more action you forgot. Someone must tell the warehouse team about the change.

script.speaker: A
script.line: You're right, thank you. Can you do that?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, I will send them an email on Monday morning, after the plan is updated.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Perfect. So the plan by Friday is mine, the supplier call on Thursday and the warehouse email on Monday are yours, and Sana checks the storage in four weeks.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's all correct. I will write it down and send the list to everyone.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Great. Thanks for your patience with the bad connection, Raj.

questions.q: Why is Lucia speaking at the end of the meeting?
options: To summarise decisions, owners and deadlines
To introduce a new member of the team
To ask for more time on the project
To complain about the sound quality
questions.explanation: She goes through each decision and says who will do it and by when.

questions.q: When will Raj call the supplier?
options: On Wednesday
On Friday
On Monday
On Thursday
questions.explanation: Raj cannot call on Wednesday because he is travelling, so Lucia accepts Thursday.

questions.q: Why can't Raj call the supplier on Wednesday?
options: He has to prepare the warehouse email
He will be travelling
He is checking the shelves
He is on holiday until Thursday
questions.explanation: He says 'I am travelling, so I can call on Thursday'.

questions.q: What will Raj do on Monday morning?
options: Update the plan for the two main products
Call the supplier about order K V thirty seventy
Email the warehouse team about the change
Check the new storage area
questions.explanation: Raj says he will send the warehouse team an email on Monday morning after the plan is updated.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Still nothing on the screen. Do you think the host forgot to open the room, or is it just the sound that's broken again?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Both, probably. Last week we spent ten minutes talking to a speaker that was muted. And Karim hasn't joined either.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Typical. I'd like to get through the agenda quickly today, because twelve hundred cartons for the trial are stuck in customs, and I need a decision.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Three weeks they've been stuck now, haven't they? I'd be surprised if anyone can unblock them without a proper escalation.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Exactly my point. And the carrier now wants eighteen percent more to reroute them, which I can't approve on my own.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Then let's put that first, before the sound gets worse. If Karim appears, he can catch up.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Fair enough. By the way, shall we grab lunch afterwards? The canteen at noon?

script.speaker: B
script.line: I'd love to, but I have a call at noon. Could we do half past twelve instead?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Half past twelve is fine. Though the canteen will be heaving by then. How about the café across the road?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Even better, I'm tired of the canteen's soup. Half past twelve at the café, then.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Done. Oh, the host has finally joined, I can see the little icon. Can you hear anything?

script.speaker: B
script.line: A bit of crackle, but yes, that's workable. Let's start, and if it breaks again we'll dial in by phone.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Agreed. Fingers crossed, because I have no patience left for technology today.

questions.q: Where and when will Amara and Mateo have lunch?
options: At half past twelve in the café across the road
At noon in the canteen
At half past twelve in the canteen
At noon in the café across the road
questions.explanation: They change from noon to half past twelve, and from the canteen to the café.

questions.q: What will they do if the sound breaks again?
options: Postpone the meeting to next week
Ask Karim to host instead
Move to another meeting room
Dial in by phone
questions.explanation: Mateo says that if it breaks again they will dial in by phone.

questions.q: Why does Amara say 'Typical'?
options: She is pleased that Karim is late
She is frustrated that the technology is failing again
She expects the carrier to cancel
She thinks the agenda is too long
questions.explanation: She says it right after Mateo mentions the muted speaker and the missing participant.

questions.q: What is the conversation mainly about?
options: Planning a trip to the customs office
Training a new colleague on the video system
Filling the wait for a meeting and choosing what to discuss first
Reorganising the canteen menu
questions.explanation: They complain about the delay, agree to start with the stuck cartons, and arrange lunch.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Amara, thanks for calling. The line isn't great, so I may ask you to repeat things. Is this about the travel plan I sent?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes. I'll be direct: the travel budget has been cut by twenty percent for the year, and I need to know what you would keep.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Twenty percent? That's a lot. To be honest, I'm a bit worried. I've already promised three suppliers a visit.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I know, and I'm sorry. Let's go through it calmly. Which trip matters most?

script.speaker: A
script.line: The audit at the packaging supplier. It's planned for the eleventh of April, and we really can't do that on a screen.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Agreed, an audit needs someone on site. That one stays. It's only about eight percent of what we have left, so it's affordable.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good. The other two visits are relationship meetings. I suppose video calls could replace those, although it won't be the same.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I'd rather lose the coffee than the audit. Let's try video first and see whether the suppliers mind.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Fair. But I'm uneasy about telling them. Some of them have been expecting us for months.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Then I'll take that one. I'll write to the two suppliers myself this week and explain that it's a company decision, not a reflection on them.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That would really help. Thank you. What do you need from me?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Send me the audit details by Friday, so I can get the approval signed before the end of the month.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Will do. I'll have everything with you by Friday morning.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of the call?
options: To decide which trips to keep after a budget cut
To plan a new supplier audit from scratch
To cancel all visits for the year
To review the results of an audit
questions.explanation: Amara announces the cut and asks Tomas what he would keep.

questions.q: By when must Tomas send the audit details?
options: On the eleventh of April
By the end of the month
In eight days
By Friday
questions.explanation: Amara asks for the audit details by Friday so she can get approval signed.

questions.q: Why does the audit trip stay in the plan?
options: The supplier asked for it personally
It cannot be done properly by video
It is cheaper than the other two visits
The director insisted on it
questions.explanation: Tomas says they really can't do an audit on a screen, and Amara agrees it needs someone on site.

questions.q: Why does Amara offer to write to the suppliers?
options: She wants to cancel the audit herself
She does not trust Tomas with the suppliers
She senses Tomas is uncomfortable giving them bad news
She needs to ask them for a discount
questions.explanation: After Tomas says he is uneasy about telling them, Amara says 'Then I'll take that one'.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Sara, have you seen the error list from the test load? Twelve percent of the item records failed, and I'd like us to agree on a cleanup plan.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I looked this morning. Most of the errors are units of measure, and a few have impossible weights. One item says two hundred forty kilograms for a single carton.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That one is a typo. It should be two hundred forty grams. But if we load it like that, our transport planning would break.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Exactly. So I suggest we split the work. I'll fix the units, you take the weights, and we finish before the nineteenth of November, which is the go-live date.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Agreed. Should we review the corrected file together on Monday at ten, in your office?

script.speaker: B
script.line: On Monday I'm at the plant. Tuesday at ten, then, but my office is tiny. Could we use the meeting room by the warehouse?

script.speaker: A
script.line: The warehouse room is booked on Tuesday. What about the canteen annex? It's quiet that early.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Fine by me. Tuesday at ten, canteen annex. I'll bring the units file on my laptop.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Great. And I'll send you the weights list tonight, so you can see what's coming.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of the conversation?
options: To agree how to fix errors found in a data test
To decide which warehouse should receive the data
To train Sara on the new tool
To choose a date for the plant visit
questions.explanation: Arjun proposes a cleanup plan after the failed records and they split the work.

questions.q: When and where will they review the corrected file?
options: On Monday at ten in Sara's office
On Tuesday at ten in the warehouse room
On Monday at ten in the canteen annex
On Tuesday at ten in the canteen annex
questions.explanation: Monday fails because Sara is at the plant, and the warehouse room is booked, so they choose the canteen annex.

questions.q: Why would the wrong weight be a problem?
options: It would delay the go-live by a month
It would break transport planning
It would make the carton too heavy to ship
It would block the units file from loading
questions.explanation: Arjun says that loading the typo would break transport planning.

questions.q: What will Arjun do tonight?
options: Fix the units of measure
Book the warehouse meeting room
Send Sara the list of weight errors
Visit the plant
questions.explanation: He says he will send Sara the weights list tonight.

script.speaker: A
script.line: It's much warmer here than I expected for this time of year. Back home it's raining every day.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Enjoy it while it lasts. The forecast says it will turn cold on Thursday. How was your flight?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Long. I left at five in the morning, and there's a seven-hour time difference, so my body thinks it's the middle of the night.

script.speaker: B
script.line: You'll be fine after a coffee. Come this way, this is our new office. We moved in three weeks ago, and everything is open plan now.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Very bright. But where do you keep the meeting rooms? I can't see any doors.

script.speaker: B
script.line: They're on the far side, behind the green wall. Before we go in, a quick word on volumes. We'll need about four hundred fifty containers over the next ten weeks.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's fifteen percent more than last quarter, if I remember correctly. We can handle it, but I'd need a firm plan by next week.

script.speaker: B
script.line: You'll have it. By the way, a few of us are going for dinner tonight. Would you like to join us?

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's kind of you, but I'm afraid my hotel is a long way from here, and tomorrow I fly out at six.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Of course, I understand. Another time, then.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Definitely. Maybe when I come back in the spring. Now, shall we go in? I'd like to see that green wall.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Follow me. I'll send the plan to your email this evening, so you can read it on the plane.

questions.q: How many containers does Rachel's company need over the next ten weeks?
options: About four hundred fifty
About fifteen
About ten
About seven
questions.explanation: Rachel says they'll need about four hundred fifty containers over the next ten weeks.

questions.q: How does Ibrahim react to the dinner invitation?
options: He is annoyed to be asked
He accepts with enthusiasm
He is unsure about meeting her colleagues
He is grateful but cannot accept
questions.explanation: He says 'That's kind of you, but I'm afraid...' and gives practical reasons.

questions.q: What will Rachel do this evening?
options: Take Ibrahim to the hotel
Send the plan by email
Go to dinner with Ibrahim
Book his flight home
questions.explanation: She says she will send the plan to his email this evening.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hello Adam, it's Katarina from the supplier. I got your message about the delivery that arrived this morning. What's the problem?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Hello, Katarina. The goods are here, all the pallets, but there's no certificate of analysis in the paperwork. Without it, quality won't release anything.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's odd. I'm sure it was attached. Perhaps it got stuck on our side. Is it urgent?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Very. Production starts on Monday, and what we have in stock covers only twenty percent of the run. If these goods stay on hold, we have a real problem.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I see. I'll ask our laboratory to reissue it. You should have it by two o'clock. No, sorry, wrong time: half past one, because the lab closes early today.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Half past one, understood. Please send it to me and to the quality inbox, otherwise it'll sit in somebody's queue.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Will do. And please apologise to your colleagues on my behalf. This shouldn't happen with a shipment of this size.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Thanks. I'd prefer not to need an apology next time, though. Could you add a document check to your shipping list?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Fair point. I'll raise it with our logistics lead this week.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of the call?
options: To reschedule a delivery to next week
To complain about damaged pallets
To sort out a missing document needed to release a delivery
To negotiate a lower price
questions.explanation: Adam explains the goods cannot be released without the certificate and they agree how to get it.

questions.q: When will Adam receive the certificate?
options: At half past one
At two o'clock
On Monday morning
At the end of the day
questions.explanation: Katarina corrects herself: 'Half past one, because the lab closes early today'.

questions.q: Why can't the goods be released?
options: Some pallets arrived damaged
The delivery was sent to the wrong site
Production has not started yet
Quality needs the certificate of analysis first
questions.explanation: Adam says that without the certificate quality won't release anything.

questions.q: What does Adam suggest with his last comment?
options: He wants a refund for this delivery
He expects the supplier to improve its process
He will cancel the next order
He thinks Katarina is to blame personally
questions.explanation: He asks her to add a document check so no apology is needed next time.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Chloe, hello, it's Pavel. I'm sorry to call at short notice, but I'd like to move our review from the nineteenth of May to this Thursday.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Hello, Pavel. That's quite a jump. What's changed?

script.speaker: A
script.line: The director wants to see the new forecast before the end of the week, and our numbers show a twelve percent gap against last year. I'd like your view first.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I understand the urgency. The trouble is that on Thursday morning I'm running a customer workshop, and I can't move that.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Would Thursday afternoon be possible, then?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Only partly. I can give you thirty minutes at three, not the full session. Does that work as a first step?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Thirty minutes is tight, but it's better than nothing. We could skip the background and go straight to the gap.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Exactly. And to save time, I'll send you my cost comments tonight, so you can read them beforehand.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That would help enormously. Then we keep the original date, the nineteenth of May, for the detailed discussion.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Agreed. Shall I send an invitation for Thursday at three?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Please do. And thank you, Chloe, for being flexible.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of Pavel's call?
options: To cancel the review completely
To invite Chloe to a customer workshop
To ask for an earlier, shorter review of the forecast
To report the results of the review
questions.explanation: He wants to move the review to Thursday and Chloe offers thirty minutes.

questions.q: When will the Thursday meeting take place?
options: At three in the afternoon
In the morning, before the workshop
On the nineteenth of May
Tonight after work
questions.explanation: Chloe says she can give him thirty minutes at three.

questions.q: Why does Pavel want to meet earlier?
options: Chloe will be on holiday on the nineteenth
The customer workshop was cancelled
The gap of twelve percent has disappeared
The director wants to see the forecast before the end of the week
questions.explanation: He says the director asked to see the new forecast before the end of the week.

questions.q: What will Chloe do tonight?
options: Move the customer workshop
Send Pavel her cost comments
Prepare the full session for the nineteenth
Send the forecast to the director
questions.explanation: She says she will send her cost comments tonight so Pavel can read them beforehand.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Dana, have a look at this delivery note. It says twelve hundred units, but our purchase order was for one thousand.

script.speaker: B
script.line: So the order was wrong? I thought we had increased it last month.

script.speaker: A
script.line: No, the order is correct. One thousand. It's the supplier's note that shows two hundred more, so either they shipped extra or they made a typing mistake.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Ah, I misunderstood. Then we should count the pallets before we sign anything. Only about eighteen percent of our racking is free, so two hundred extra units would be tight.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good point. I've counted, and the pallets add up to twelve hundred, so they did ship extra. I'll call the supplier now and ask what they want us to do.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Shall I mark the extra pallets as not received, so nobody books them in?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Yes, please, and keep them to one side. If the supplier confirms it's an error, we'll return them. If not, I'll check with finance whether we keep them.

script.speaker: B
script.line: And when do you need an answer? The carrier is here again on Thursday.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Ideally before Thursday, so the driver can take the extra pallets back. If it drags on, we'll agree a pickup for the eleventh of April.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of the conversation?
options: To increase next month's purchase order
To find a new place to store pallets
To check a delivery with more units than ordered and decide what to do
To complain to the carrier about a late truck
questions.explanation: Mateo notices the delivery note shows more units than ordered and they plan next steps.

questions.q: How many units were ordered?
options: One thousand
Twelve hundred
Two hundred
Eighteen hundred
questions.explanation: Mateo says the purchase order was for one thousand and the note shows twelve hundred.

questions.q: What will Dana do first?
options: Call the supplier to ask about the error
Book the extra units into the system
Return the pallets with the Thursday carrier
Mark the extra pallets as not received and keep them aside
questions.explanation: Dana offers to mark the extra pallets as not received, and Mateo says 'Yes, please'.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Welcome, Amara. I'm Tomas, your buddy for the first weeks. Let me walk you through how the week works, and please stop me whenever something doesn't make sense.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Thanks, Tomas. Honestly, I'm a little overwhelmed already. There seem to be so many tools, and my access isn't working on half of them.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's completely normal on day one. I'll take care of access. I've raised a request, reference H F two oh three three, and I'll chase it this afternoon.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's a huge relief. And what does the week look like in practice?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Mondays we clean the data, Tuesdays are for supplier calls, and the big moment is Wednesday: the demand review, where everyone challenges the numbers. You'll just listen at first.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good, I'd rather listen than get asked questions I can't answer yet. How long until I'm expected to run things on my own?

script.speaker: A
script.line: There's a twelve-week plan, so nobody expects miracles. Oh, and lunch is at the canteen on the ground floor. I usually go around half past twelve, so join me.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I'd love to. Thank you, you've made this much less scary than I'd feared.

questions.q: What is Tomas doing in this conversation?
options: Interviewing a candidate for a planning role
Helping a new colleague understand the team's routine
Explaining a problem with a supplier
Training Amara to run the demand review
questions.explanation: He introduces himself as her buddy and walks her through the week.

questions.q: On which day is the demand review?
options: On Monday
On Tuesday
On Wednesday
On Thursday
questions.explanation: Tomas calls Wednesday the big moment: the demand review.

questions.q: How does Amara feel at the start?
options: Overwhelmed by the number of tools
Bored by the introduction
Angry about the late start
Confident about the new role
questions.explanation: She says she's a little overwhelmed because of the many tools and access problems.

questions.q: What does Tomas imply about the first weeks?
options: She will present at the demand review at once
She will work only with suppliers
She will have no access to any tools
Amara will mainly observe rather than lead
questions.explanation: He says she'll just listen at first and that nobody expects miracles in the twelve-week plan.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Marco, do you have five minutes? I need your help with a supplier. They have not answered us about order A G seventy-nine fifty-one for two weeks.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Two weeks is long. Tell me the facts first. What did you ask them, and what did they say?

script.speaker: A
script.line: I asked for a new delivery date three times by email. They only said, we are checking. Nothing more.

script.speaker: B
script.line: And what is the impact on us?

script.speaker: A
script.line: We are missing forty cartons. Without them, the line stops in ten days.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That is serious. So you want me to call their director?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Yes, today, please. I think it is the only way to get an answer.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I understand, but today is too early. I don't want to jump over their sales manager without warning. Let's send a clear email today and give them until tomorrow.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Okay, I accept that. But if there is no answer by eleven tomorrow, I want you to call the director.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Agreed. Eleven tomorrow is the limit. I will keep my calendar free, and you send me the email text before you send it.

questions.q: Why does Hannah talk to Marco?
options: She wants to cancel an order with the supplier
She wants his help with a supplier who does not answer
She needs to report a problem with her computer
She would like to change to a new supplier
questions.explanation: She says the supplier has not answered for two weeks and asks Marco to help.

questions.q: How many cartons are missing?
options: Ten
Fifty-one
Forty
Four hundred
questions.explanation: Hannah says 'We are missing forty cartons'.

questions.q: What will happen if the supplier does not answer by eleven tomorrow?
options: Marco will call the supplier's director
Hannah will visit the supplier
The line will stop at once
They will send a third email
questions.explanation: Hannah asks Marco to call the director then, and Marco agrees.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Thanks for coming, Lucia. As you know, the national holiday is coming up, and I'd like us to agree a delivery window before it, and a backup after.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Of course, Hugo. So you want everything delivered on the twenty-ninth of November, if I understand correctly?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Not quite. The twenty-ninth is the backup date, after the holiday. What I need first is a window before it.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Ah, I see, I mixed those up. So the main delivery is before the break. When does the holiday start for you?

script.speaker: A
script.line: On Thursday. Our dock closes at noon on Wednesday, so we can only receive goods until then.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Then Wednesday morning is the latest. I should warn you that our capacity drops by thirty percent that week, and drivers are scarce.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's why I'd like to fix it today. Could you commit to Wednesday between eight and eleven?

script.speaker: B
script.line: I can promise that for the priority pallets. Anything left over would go on the twenty-ninth as a backup.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That works. I'll identify the priority pallets by tomorrow, so you can plan the loads.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Perfect. Once you send the list, I'll confirm the trucks in writing.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good. I'd rather have it all on paper than rely on goodwill in a busy week.

questions.q: What is the backup delivery date?
options: The twenty-ninth of November
Wednesday between eight and eleven
Thursday, the first day of the holiday
Wednesday at noon
questions.explanation: Hugo says the twenty-ninth is the backup date after the holiday.

questions.q: What will Hugo do by tomorrow?
options: Confirm the trucks in writing
Close the dock early
Hire extra drivers
Identify the priority pallets
questions.explanation: He says he'll identify the priority pallets by tomorrow so Lucia can plan the loads.

questions.q: Why does Hugo say 'Not quite'?
options: To refuse the idea of a backup date
To correct Lucia's misunderstanding about the dates
To complain about the carrier's capacity
To ask her to repeat the question
questions.explanation: Lucia thought everything would be delivered on the twenty-ninth, and he explains it is the backup.

questions.q: What is the conversation mainly about?
options: Planning a new holiday schedule for the dock
Complaining about drivers who are not available
Agreeing delivery dates before and after a holiday
Moving the carrier's office to a new site
questions.explanation: They agree a main window on Wednesday and a backup on the twenty-ninth.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Thanks for sitting down with me, Yuki. I'd like to check our assumptions for the new pack before I lock the forecast.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Sure. Where do you want to start? The launch date, I guess.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Yes. My current assumption is that we launch in the first week of next quarter. Is that still right?

script.speaker: B
script.line: As far as I know, yes. Production will deliver the first order of twenty-five hundred units a few days before.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good. Then the uptake curve. I assumed a slow start and about eight weeks to reach normal volume.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That sounds reasonable for a normal launch. And what share of the old pack will the new one replace?

script.speaker: A
script.line: About forty percent in the first year. The rest of the customers will probably keep buying the old one.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Fine. Oh, and one thing I forgot to tell you. A big retailer has just confirmed it will list the new pack from day one.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's great news! The ramp-up will be faster, maybe five or six weeks. I'll need to raise the early numbers.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I'd do that, yes. But keep a cautious view on the tail, because we don't know yet if they will keep it on the shelves.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Agreed. Can we check these new assumptions with the commercial team at two this afternoon?

script.speaker: B
script.line: I'll book a room. Two o'clock works for them as well.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of the conversation?
options: To check the assumptions behind a forecast for a new pack
To plan the production of the old pack
To prepare a visit to a retailer
To train Yuki in forecasting methods
questions.explanation: Luis wants to check the assumptions before he locks the forecast.

questions.q: How long did Luis first assume the uptake would take?
options: Five to six weeks
About four weeks
About twelve weeks
About eight weeks
questions.explanation: He says he assumed a slow start and about eight weeks, and later revises to five or six.

questions.q: What does Yuki's advice about the tail suggest?
options: The old pack will disappear completely
Later demand is uncertain because the retailer may drop the pack
The retailer wants a lower price
The first order will be delayed
questions.explanation: She says to be cautious because they don't know if the retailer will keep it on the shelves.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Kenji, do you have a minute while we walk? I just came back from the port inspection, and I have no idea how to file my expenses.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Of course. The simplest way is to upload every receipt in the system, with a short note on why you were there.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Any receipt at all? I checked about three hundred containers, and honestly I lost track of the small purchases.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Anything above twenty-five euros needs a proper receipt. Below that, a note is enough. The per diem covers meals, so don't submit restaurant bills as well.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good to know. And what's the deadline? I'd hate to miss it.

script.speaker: B
script.line: You have six weeks from the day you return. After that, finance can reject the whole claim without discussion.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Six weeks is generous, but I'll do it this week. There's one item I'm not sure about, though. A taxi I took when the shuttle was cancelled.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's fine with a note. The one finance will probably bounce is the hotel minibar. We never reimburse that.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Fair enough, I'll pay for that myself. I assumed it might be included.

script.speaker: B
script.line: It's a common mistake. Now, one more thing: your train ticket is only a card slip, and that isn't enough. You need the invoice from the rail company.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Oh no, I don't have it. Can I download it somewhere?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Probably, but let's check together. Come by my desk at quarter to four and we'll go through the portal.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of the conversation?
options: To report a problem found at the port
To ask for a bigger travel budget
To learn how to file expenses after a business trip
To book a trip to another port
questions.explanation: Chloe asks how to file her expenses and Kenji explains receipts, deadlines and rules.

questions.q: What is the deadline for filing the claim?
options: Six weeks after the trip
By the end of this week
Twenty-five days after the trip
Three weeks after the trip
questions.explanation: Kenji says she has six weeks from the day she returns.

questions.q: What will Chloe do at quarter to four?
options: Submit her taxi receipt
Pay for the minibar
Return to the port
Go to Kenji's desk to look for the train invoice
questions.explanation: Kenji invites her to his desk at quarter to four to go through the portal.

questions.q: Why does Kenji mention the hotel minibar?
options: To warn her about a hotel price rise
As an example of an item finance will reject
To explain how the per diem works
To suggest where she should stay next time
questions.explanation: He says it's the one finance will probably bounce, because they never reimburse it.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Pavel, do you have a few minutes? I wanted to give you an early warning rather than a nasty surprise later.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That sounds ominous. Please go on, I'm listening.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Based on current orders, we run out of stock on the main product in about six weeks. Not tomorrow, but the window to act is closing.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Why now? Last month the plan looked fine.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Two reasons. The tender you won pulled demand forward, and our last production run came out smaller than planned.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I see. What do you need from me?

script.speaker: A
script.line: A decision this week. The next free production slot is the twenty-seventh of July, and the factory needs a confirmed quantity by Friday.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Friday is very soon. How big a quantity are we talking about?

script.speaker: A
script.line: A full extra run. Anything less and we'll still be short in the autumn.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I can't sign off a full run. Finance will want to see the tender contract first. But I could approve half now.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Half would cover the next two months, but not the peak. Is there a way to keep the rest open?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes. Approve half today, and I'll bring the contract to the finance meeting on Friday at ten fifteen. If they agree, we release the second half straight afterwards.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's an acceptable compromise. I'll tell the factory to prepare for both options.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good. And thanks for the early warning, it gives us room to manoeuvre.

questions.q: When does Leila expect the stockout?
options: On the twenty-seventh of July
On Friday at ten fifteen
In about six weeks
Tomorrow
questions.explanation: She says they run out of stock in about six weeks.

questions.q: Why is the stock running low?
options: Demand came earlier than planned and a production run was small
A supplier delivered the wrong material
The forecast was cut by finance
Customers returned a large order
questions.explanation: Leila says the tender pulled demand forward and the last production run was smaller than planned.

questions.q: What will happen on Friday at ten fifteen?
options: The factory will start the extra run
Leila will visit the factory
Pavel will sign a full run alone
Finance will look at the tender contract
questions.explanation: Pavel says he'll bring the contract to the finance meeting on Friday at ten fifteen.

script.speaker: A
