script.line: Hi Claire, can you hear me? The connection's poor here. I've found a hotel for your audit trip on the fourteenth of January, two nights, close to the supplier's site.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Just about, Samuel. How far is it from the site? The audit starts at nine, and I don't want to be late.

script.speaker: A
script.line: About ten minutes by car. It's the best option within your budget, and I've held the room under reference N M twenty-eight seventy-seven.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good. What about breakfast? I'd need to eat by six thirty to be on site early.

script.speaker: A
script.line: The hotel only serves breakfast from seven, I'm afraid. What they can do is prepare a packed breakfast the night before, if you ask at reception.

script.speaker: B
script.line: A packed breakfast is acceptable, though not ideal. And the cancellation terms?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Free cancellation until forty-eight hours before arrival. After that you pay the first night.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Fine. Please confirm the booking, and send me the details by email in case the call drops again.

questions.q: What is the conversation mainly about?
options: Changing the date of an audit
Booking a hotel for a two-night audit trip
Booking a flight to the supplier
Cancelling a hotel reservation
questions.explanation: Samuel presents a hotel for the audit trip and Claire asks about breakfast, distance and cancellation.

questions.q: What time does the hotel serve breakfast?
options: From six thirty
From nine
From seven
From ten
questions.explanation: Samuel says the hotel only serves breakfast from seven.

questions.q: What will Samuel do after the call?
options: Confirm the booking and email the details
Ask the hotel for earlier breakfast
Cancel the reservation
Drive Claire to the supplier
questions.explanation: Claire asks him to confirm the booking and send details by email.

questions.q: Why does Samuel mention a packed breakfast?
options: To explain a cancellation fee
To say the hotel is too far
To suggest eating at the supplier's site
To offer an alternative to the early breakfast Claire wants
questions.explanation: The hotel cannot serve breakfast early, so a packed breakfast is the alternative.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Right, let's start the stand-up. Mateo is sick today, so I need to share his work. He had two supplier calls and the weekly report.

script.speaker: B
script.line: How sick is he? Will he be back tomorrow?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Probably not before Thursday. So today we need someone for the call about the forty missing units and the call about the late invoices.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's a lot for one afternoon. What time are the calls?

script.speaker: A
script.line: The first is at two o'clock, and the second at quarter to four.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Then I have a problem. I'm hosting a customer visit at quarter to four, and I can't move it.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I see. Could you at least take the two o'clock one, then? It's about the forty units, and you know the supplier.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, that I can do. I've spoken to them before, so I won't need a briefing.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good. I'll take the invoice call myself, even though it's not my favourite topic. What about the report?

script.speaker: B
script.line: I'm happy to do the report as well, but I'll need it simplified. Can we skip the detailed charts this week?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Only the charts. The headline numbers must stay, especially the twelve percent drop in on-time deliveries, because the director will ask.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Understood. Headline numbers, no charts. I'll send it by the end of tomorrow.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That works. Thank you, Pavel. I know it's an awkward day.

script.speaker: B
script.line: No problem. Just let me know if Mateo calls with anything useful.

questions.q: When is Pavel's customer visit?
options: At two o'clock
At quarter to four
On Thursday
At the end of tomorrow
questions.explanation: Pavel says he is hosting a customer visit at quarter to four.

questions.q: How does Leila feel about asking Pavel for help?
options: She is irritated by his objections
She doubts that Mateo is really sick
She knows she is asking a lot of him
She is indifferent to his schedule
questions.explanation: She thanks him and says 'I know it's an awkward day'.

questions.q: What will Leila do herself?
options: Take the call about the late invoices
Write the weekly report
Call the supplier about the missing units
Host the customer visit
questions.explanation: She says 'I'll take the invoice call myself'.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hi Tomas. You wrote that you need help with an email to a supplier. Can you share your screen? The sound is bad, so I'll read it myself.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Sure. It's about order V P eighty-two sixty-five. It was two weeks late again, and I'm angry, but I don't want to sound rude.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I understand. Your first sentence says, You must fix this immediately. That sounds a bit aggressive.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, I know. But I want them to understand it is serious. What would you say instead?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Maybe, We would appreciate a clear plan to avoid further delays. It is polite, but it is still firm.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's better. Can we also add a date? I want an answer this week.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good idea. Add, Please reply by Friday. A date makes it a real request, not just a wish.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Perfect. I will change both sentences now. I want to send it before half past one, because the supplier's office closes early today.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Okay. Then update the email now and send it. I will check it quickly before you press send.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Great, thank you. I will send you the new version in ten minutes.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of the call?
options: To report a late order to the manager
To learn how to use a screen-sharing tool
To translate an email into another language
To make an email to a supplier sound firm but polite
questions.explanation: Tomas asks Marta to help reword his email so it is not rude.

questions.q: By what time should Tomas send the email?
options: By Friday
Before half past one
In ten minutes
Before two o'clock
questions.explanation: He says he wants to send it before half past one because the supplier's office closes early.

questions.q: How does Tomas feel about the delay?
options: Relaxed, because delays are normal
Embarrassed about his own mistake
Angry, but he wants to stay polite
Confused about the order number
questions.explanation: He says 'I'm angry, but I don't want to sound rude'.

questions.q: What can we infer about the supplier?
options: It has been late with deliveries before
It never answers emails
It is a new supplier
It wants to close its office
questions.explanation: Tomas says the order was two weeks late 'again'.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Luis, thanks for taking this by voice. I'm seeing demand in my region grow by around forty percent, and I want it in the next forecast.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Forty is a big number, Dana. Before I touch anything, what is it based on?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Mostly the new distributor. They've signed a letter of intent and shortlisted us in three major cities.

script.speaker: B
script.line: A letter of intent isn't an order, though. When would the volume actually start?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Their first purchase order should arrive on the seventeenth of September, and volume ramps up from there. I can send you a draft on Monday.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Understood. And what if the number's too high? I'm the one who explains the excess stock.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Moderate, I'd say. They've never missed a start date with us, though this is their biggest launch.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's what worries me. Here's my proposal: twenty percent in the base forecast, and the other twenty as upside until the purchase order is in hand.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hmm. I was hoping for all forty, honestly. We could lose sales if the stock isn't there.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I hear you, and I trust your read of the market. But last year I booked a similar jump on a promise, and I'm still working off that stock.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's fair. I won't push. Can we agree a trigger, so the upside moves into the base quickly?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Of course. The day the purchase order arrives, I'll update the base, and the factory gets a fresh plan within forty-eight hours.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good. I'll send the draft on Monday and flag the purchase order the moment it lands.

questions.q: What is the conversation mainly about?
options: Whether to sign a contract with a new distributor
How to reduce excess stock from last year
Which cities should receive the first shipment
How much of an expected demand increase to put into the forecast
questions.explanation: Dana wants a forty percent rise in the forecast and Luis proposes a split between base and upside.

questions.q: How much of the increase will go into the base forecast?
options: Forty percent
Twenty percent
Forty-eight percent
Ten percent
questions.explanation: Luis proposes twenty percent in the base and the other twenty as an upside scenario.

questions.q: Why does Luis not accept the full forty percent?
options: He does not believe the distributor exists
The factory cannot produce that quantity
He was left with extra stock after a similar promise last year
Finance has forbidden any increase
questions.explanation: He says he booked a similar jump on a promise last year and is still working off the inventory.

questions.q: What will Dana do on Monday?
options: Send Luis a draft of the expected volumes
Place the first purchase order
Update the base forecast
Sign the letter of intent
questions.explanation: She says 'I'll send the draft on Monday'.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Morning, Ethan. Thanks for making time before I disappear. I'm off for two weeks from tomorrow, so I wanted to walk you through what's still open on our side.

script.speaker: B
script.line: No problem, Elena, I've cleared the morning. Where shall we start, with whatever could bite us first?

script.speaker: A
script.line: The urgent one is the pickup on the 11th of October. Twenty-five hundred cartons leave your dock at nine thirty, so someone must be at the gate.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Nine thirty, got it. I'll be there myself, or at least I'll make sure the shift lead is. Anything that could go wrong with the paperwork?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Only the customs invoice. It still shows the old consignee address, and the broker won't release anything until that's corrected.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Right, I'll ask finance to reissue it. Who do I call if the broker pushes back while you're away?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Call Tomasz, my colleague at the depot. He knows the account inside out, but he's often on the road, so message first rather than ringing.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Fair enough. And what can wait until you're back?

script.speaker: A
script.line: The quarterly rate review. Honestly, it's been dragging for months, so another fortnight won't hurt. The draft is in the shared folder marked pending.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Okay, let me read it back. I'll chase the corrected invoice today, and I'll cover the gate on the day.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Exactly. I'll send Tomasz a note this afternoon so he expects you. And if the invoice isn't fixed by Friday, tell me anyway, even on holiday.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Understood. Enjoy the break, and I'll keep my phone close.

questions.q: What time is the truck due at the dock on the day of the pickup?
options: This afternoon
On Friday morning
Early tomorrow
At nine thirty
questions.explanation: Elena says the truck is booked for nine thirty, so someone has to be at the gate.

questions.q: Why can't the customs broker release the goods yet?
options: The truck has not been confirmed
The invoice shows an out-of-date address for the receiver
Tomasz is away from the depot
The rate review is unfinished
questions.explanation: Elena says the invoice still shows the old consignee address and the broker won't release anything until it's corrected.

questions.q: What does Elena imply about the quarterly rate review?
options: It can safely be left until she returns
It must be finished before Friday
Tomasz will complete it for her
Ethan has already approved it
questions.explanation: She says it has been dragging for months, so another fortnight won't hurt.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Mateo, thanks for jumping on. For item N G nine nine four zero, the supplier plan is twelve times bigger than our forecast. Something's off.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Twelve times, that's a strange ratio. Hang on, what unit is your forecast in?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Packs, as always. And the supplier's file just says quantity. Oh. Their plan could be in single units.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That would fit. A pack holds twelve units, so both numbers are the same demand, just counted differently.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good, so nobody is double-ordering. Still, I'm annoyed nobody labelled that column. Can we agree a conversion check before the plan is locked on the 14th of November?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Sure. I'll build a small check that multiplies packs by twelve and flags any line that doesn't match. I'll have it ready for a quarter to four tomorrow.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Perfect. Although, one more thing I just spotted: the supplier file lists two lines for the same item, and one has a different pack size. That could break your check.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Then let's not guess. I'll ask the supplier which pack size is right, and we'll go through it together tomorrow, once they've confirmed.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of the call?
options: To cancel an order with the supplier
To choose a new pack size for the product
To find out why two plans for the same item looked so different
To report a late delivery
questions.explanation: Dana opens by saying the supplier plan is twelve times bigger and they work out it is a units-versus-packs mismatch.

questions.q: When will Mateo have the conversion check ready?
options: Today at a quarter to four
Tomorrow at a quarter to four
On the 14th of November
Tomorrow morning
questions.explanation: Mateo says he'll have it ready for a quarter to four tomorrow.

questions.q: How does Dana feel about the unlabelled column?
options: Amused by the mistake
Grateful to the supplier
Annoyed that nobody marked it
Worried the forecast is wrong
questions.explanation: Dana says 'I'm annoyed nobody labelled that column'.

questions.q: What does the second line for the same item suggest?
options: The forecast needs to be multiplied again
Mateo's check is not necessary
The supplier is double-ordering
The supplier data may still contain an error
questions.explanation: Dana says one line has a different pack size and that could break the check, so Mateo will ask the supplier.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Fatima, have you read the reorganization email? I've read it twice and I'm still not sure what it means for us.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, I just finished it. As far as I can tell, the order desk moves under Customer Operations, and your planning group stays where it is.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's my reading too. What worries me is the three hundred open tickets in our queue. Apparently they all move to the new team's system, over two weeks.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Hm, I thought the email said three weeks.

script.speaker: A
script.line: You're right, sorry, three weeks. Two was in the draft that circulated last month. And the first transfer day is Monday.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Hold on, I have it as Tuesday. Monday is the town hall.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Let me check. Yes, Tuesday. So much for careful reading. What I really don't know is who sets priorities while the tickets are moving.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That isn't in the email at all. Honestly, I'd ask our manager directly rather than guess, and ask for the answer in writing.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Agreed. I'll draft the question and send it to you first, so we ask with one voice.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good idea. Send it this afternoon and I'll add the point about customer escalations.

questions.q: What are the two colleagues mainly doing?
options: Trying to understand what a reorganization means for them
Planning the town hall meeting
Complaining about their manager
Training new staff on a ticket system
questions.explanation: They go through the email together and end up listing a question for their manager.

questions.q: How long will the ticket transfer take?
options: Two weeks
Three weeks
Until Monday
Until Tuesday
questions.explanation: Fatima says three weeks, and Samuel agrees that two was only in the old draft.

questions.q: How does Samuel feel about the email?
options: Unsure and a little worried
Excited about the changes
Angry at Fatima
Not interested at all
questions.explanation: He says he has read it twice and is still not sure, and the tickets 'worry' him.

questions.q: What can we infer about the email?
options: It was sent to the wrong people
It contains no dates at all
It cancels the planning group
It leaves an important question unanswered
questions.explanation: Fatima says who sets priorities 'isn't in the email at all'.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Omar, thanks for seeing me. My market asked for the full quantity on order F B three one zero five, and I've heard we won't get it.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's right, Emma, and I'm sorry to tell you in person. Supply is short this month, so I can only release forty percent of what you requested.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Forty? That's a big cut. Our pharmacies have been waiting since last quarter, and I promised them a full delivery.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I understand. Every market is in the same position. We allocate by last year's sales, not by who asks loudest, otherwise it wouldn't be fair.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Fair enough, but last year doesn't reflect our growth. We added two hospital contracts in the spring.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Those are real and I'm not dismissing them. Send me the contract volumes and I'll ask my manager to review your share, though I can't promise a change.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's already something. When would I know?

script.speaker: B
script.line: The allocation locks on Monday, so I'd need the volumes before then. The rest of your order follows when the next batch is released.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Okay. So the forty percent ships now, and the balance comes once the new batch is out.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Correct, as long as quality release goes to plan. I'd rather not promise a date until then.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Understood. I need to tell my hospitals something honest. Can I give them a window?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Say end of the month, subject to release. One other thing though: your delivery address has no postcode in our system, and that will block the first shipment.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Oh no, how embarrassing. I'll send the corrected address today.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Perfect. Let's speak again on Monday morning, once the allocation is locked, and I'll confirm the exact quantities.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of the meeting?
options: To negotiate a lower price for the pharmacies
To explain why Emma's market will get only part of its order
To announce a new production site
To cancel Emma's hospital contracts
questions.explanation: Omar explains the forty percent cut and how the allocation works.

questions.q: What problem could block the first shipment?
options: The contract volumes have not arrived
Quality release has been refused
Her delivery address is missing a postcode
The allocation was locked too early
questions.explanation: Omar says the address has no postcode in the system and that will block the first shipment.

questions.q: How does Omar feel about giving Emma the news?
options: Sorry, but firm about the rules
Pleased to be rid of the problem
Annoyed with her for asking
Indifferent to the cuts
questions.explanation: He says he is sorry to tell her in person but keeps to the fair allocation rule.

questions.q: What can we infer about the rest of Emma's order?
options: It has been cancelled for good
It may arrive later, but only if the new batch is approved
It will ship together with the first part
It will go to other markets instead
questions.explanation: Omar says the balance follows after the next batch is released, as long as quality release goes to plan.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hi Marco. I need to tell you about the shipment that arrived yesterday. The temperature went too high for a short time.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Thanks for telling me early, Leila. Can you send me the data logger report?

script.speaker: A
script.line: The data what? Sorry, do you mean the driver's paper form?

script.speaker: B
script.line: No, no. It's the small electronic device inside the box. It records the temperature all the way. We need its file.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Ah, now I understand. I'll download it today. It showed about five percent above the limit for two hours.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's useful. The goods stay in quarantine until I check it. They have twelve weeks of shelf life left, but I want a decision by the 19th of October.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Okay. Should I move the pallets to the quarantine area now?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes please, and put a red label on each one. Thanks, you did the right thing.

questions.q: When does Marco want a decision?
options: Today
In twelve weeks
After two hours
By the 19th of October
questions.explanation: Marco says he wants a decision by the 19th of October.

questions.q: How does Marco react when Leila does not know the term?
options: He gets angry with her
He asks someone else to do it
He explains it patiently
He ignores her question
questions.explanation: He says 'No, no. It's the small electronic device inside the box' and explains.

questions.q: What will Leila do with the pallets?
options: Send them back to the supplier
Open them to check the product
Throw them away today
Move them to quarantine and label them red
questions.explanation: Marco says to move the pallets to quarantine and put a red label on each one.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hi Andrew, thanks for picking this up on voice. The chat was going in circles. My supplier meeting has been pushed back a day, so my train must move too.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Happy to sort that, Camila. I've got your booking in front of me. You're on the early service to Lyon on Tuesday, correct?

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's the one. Is there much of a penalty for changing it?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Because you booked ten weeks ahead, it's a flexible fare, so the fee is twelve percent of the ticket rather than the full difference.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Twelve percent I can live with. I only care because the supplier wants to walk through a hundred and twenty late orders, and I can't be late for that.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Understood. There's a mid-morning train on Wednesday that gets you in with a good two hours' buffer. Or the early one again, if you'd rather keep your afternoon free.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Mid-morning sounds sensible. I'd rather not rush for a sandwich on the platform.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Then I'll rebook it now. You'll get the confirmation by email, and the new ticket will be in the app.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Lovely. Should I tell my manager about the fee, or does it go through automatically?

script.speaker: B
script.line: It goes to your cost centre, but it's good manners to give her a heads-up. Could you forward her the confirmation by the end of today?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Will do. And I'll ask the supplier to confirm the new time in writing by tomorrow noon.

questions.q: Why is Camila calling Andrew?
options: She wants to cancel her whole trip
She is complaining about a wrong charge
She needs to change a train because a meeting moved
She is asking for a hotel recommendation
questions.explanation: Camila says her supplier meeting was pushed back a day, so her train needs to move.

questions.q: What percentage is the change fee?
options: Twelve percent
Ten percent
Twenty percent
One hundred percent
questions.explanation: Andrew says the fee is twelve percent because it is a flexible fare.

questions.q: What is Camila asked to do by the end of today?
options: Pay the fee at the station
Ask the supplier for a written confirmation
Collect a paper ticket
Send the booking confirmation to her manager
questions.explanation: Andrew asks her to forward her manager the confirmation by the end of today.

questions.q: Why does Camila mention a sandwich on the platform?
options: To explain why she prefers the later train
To ask about food on the train
To say she is hungry right now
To complain about the early service
questions.explanation: She says mid-morning sounds sensible because she doesn't want to rush for a sandwich.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hello Leila, thanks for making time. I'm calling about a price change. From next quarter, our corrugated boxes will cost more.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Hi Pavel. How much more, and why? We haven't had an increase in two years.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Around six percent. Cardboard and energy costs both went up, and we can't absorb it any longer.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Six percent on a hundred and twenty pallets is a lot. Could we keep the old price for three months? The reference is E V three two nine five.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I can't promise three months, but I'll ask my director. Can we talk again on Thursday morning?

script.speaker: B
script.line: I'm at the plant on Thursday morning. Thursday afternoon works, in my office.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Fine, though I'll be driving, so can we do it by phone instead?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Okay. A call at three on Thursday, then. Please try to bring a better offer.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I will. Thanks for taking it so calmly, Leila.

questions.q: What is the main reason for the call?
options: To change the size of the boxes
To complain about a late delivery
To announce a higher price and discuss a delay
To ask for a bigger order
questions.explanation: Pavel announces the increase and Leila asks for a three-month transition.

questions.q: How will Pavel and Leila speak again?
options: In her office on Thursday morning
By phone on Thursday at three
In her office on Thursday afternoon
At the plant on Thursday at three
questions.explanation: They move from the morning, then from the office to a phone call at three on Thursday.

questions.q: How does Leila react to the news?
options: She accepts it without question
She is concerned but stays constructive
She ends the call angrily
She asks to change supplier at once
questions.explanation: She asks why, then proposes a transition period.

questions.q: What does Pavel imply with 'I can't promise three months'?
options: He refuses any discount
He has already agreed to it
He needs approval from someone more senior
He does not know the price
questions.explanation: He adds 'I'll ask my director', which shows the decision is not only his.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Ben, can you hear me? The line's terrible on my side. I'm calling about the stock count at our warehouse. We're showing twenty-five hundred units fewer than your system.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Twenty-five hundred? That's more than a rounding error. Let me think. Are there any transfers pending?

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's what I wondered. Maybe a transfer between buildings that nobody booked in.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Possible. Or a pallet could be sitting in the wrong location. Last month we found a whole pallet in a staging bay.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Right. I'll check the transfer log and the staging bays now, while you look for open movements on your side.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Fine. Give me a minute. Hannah, I found something. There's an open transfer order for exactly that quantity, never confirmed.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Sorry, say that again? You're cutting out.

script.speaker: B
script.line: An open transfer for twenty-five hundred units, still pending. If you confirm it, the difference may disappear.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Oh, that's good news. I can confirm it right now, so no full recount, just a quick spot check on Thursday at nine.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Great, that saves a lot of effort. Send me the confirmation afterwards.

questions.q: When will the spot check take place?
options: Right now
Last month
After a full recount
On Thursday at nine
questions.explanation: Hannah says there will be a quick spot check on Thursday at nine.

questions.q: What does Hannah do next?
options: She confirms the open transfer order
She starts a full recount
She moves a pallet from a staging bay
She cancels the transfer
questions.explanation: Hannah says she can confirm the transfer right now.

questions.q: Why does Ben mention the pallet in the staging bay?
options: To blame the warehouse team
To suggest another possible cause
To say the problem is solved
To ask for a recount
questions.explanation: He offers it as an example of a wrong location after saying a transfer was possible.

questions.q: What is the call mainly about?
options: Planning a new warehouse
Complaining about the phone line
Finding the reason for a stock difference
Ordering more units
questions.explanation: Hannah reports a gap of twenty-five hundred units and they look for causes.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Priya, good to hear you. I'll be honest, I'm under pressure with the gap on product family Delta. Demand is forty percent above what supply can cover next month.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I saw it in the pre-read. How many customers are exposed?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Forty order lines are still unconfirmed. If nothing changes, the Asian markets lose out first.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Let's not panic yet. I see two options. One, we bring a production run forward and accept overtime. Two, we ship part by air, which is quicker but costly.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Overtime sounds cheaper, but can the plant really absorb it? I'm worried we promise something we can't deliver.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Fair concern. I'll ask the plant manager for a realistic yes or no before the meeting. That's my task, so you don't need to chase it.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Thank you, that takes a weight off. And the decision itself?

script.speaker: B
script.line: We need it from the S and OP lead by Friday, otherwise the air option disappears because the booking window closes.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Understood. So you bring the plant's answer, and I'll prepare the demand side, with the order lines ranked by priority.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Exactly. We'll get through this. Let's talk again before Friday.

questions.q: By when is the decision needed?
options: By Friday
Next month
Before the plant visit
After the pre-read
questions.explanation: Priya says they need the decision by Friday.

questions.q: How does Arjun feel at the start of the call?
options: Calm and confident
Pleased with the numbers
Uninterested
Under pressure and worried
questions.explanation: He says he is under pressure and later worries about promising something undeliverable.

questions.q: What is likely to happen if no decision is made by Friday?
options: Overtime will start automatically
The forty order lines will be cancelled
The air shipping option will no longer be available
The plant manager will decide alone
questions.explanation: Priya says the air option disappears because the booking window closes.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Morning, Ethan. About yesterday's dashboard. The stock numbers were wrong, and I'm sorry about that.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Thanks for explaining. By how much were we off?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Stock was eighteen percent too high for some products. The cause was a duplicate load. One file was imported twice.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I see. Is it fixed now?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Yes, I removed the duplicate and added a check, so a repeated file gets rejected. The ticket is L N six four five four.

script.speaker: B
script.line: And what about the history? Last week's reports used the wrong data too, no?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Not corrected yet. I'll rebuild the history by Wednesday and tell you when it's done.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good. I'll warn the planners not to use last week's numbers until then, and I'll ask them to tell me about any decision they based on them.

questions.q: Why is Elena talking to Ethan?
options: To explain a dashboard error and how it was fixed
To ask for a new dashboard
To report a late delivery
To train the planners
questions.explanation: She opens by apologising for the wrong stock numbers and explains the cause and fix.

questions.q: By how much was stock too high for some products?
options: Six percent
Eighteen percent
Fourteen percent
Forty-five percent
questions.explanation: Elena says stock was eighteen percent too high.

questions.q: How does Elena feel about the error?
options: Proud
Apologetic
Annoyed with Ethan
Indifferent
questions.explanation: She says 'I'm sorry about that'.

questions.q: What can we infer about last week's reports?
options: They were already corrected
They are not used by planners
They were deleted yesterday
They may still be wrong until the history is rebuilt
questions.explanation: Elena says the history is not corrected yet, and Ethan warns planners not to use the numbers.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Priya, sorry about the line, I'm in a lift lobby. I need an urgent purchase order approved today. The request is D P five zero five three.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I can hear you fine, Arjun. What is it for, and which cost centre?

script.speaker: A
script.line: It's a block of two hundred forty support tickets from our planning software vendor. The cost centre is supply chain planning, but I don't have the number memorised.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I'll need the number and a justification. Urgent isn't enough for finance, I'm afraid.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Fair. The team has used almost all its current tickets, and open issues are stacking up before month end.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Understood. But two hundred forty is a lot at once. Could you buy half now and review in a month?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Half won't last. The contract runs twelve weeks, and we'd run dry in the middle of the busiest period.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Hmm. What if we approve all of it today, but you send me a usage report after six weeks?

script.speaker: A
script.line: I can accept that, as long as you don't ask for it every week.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Deal. Once, at six weeks. And I need the cost centre number in writing before I release the order.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I'll send it right after this call, with the justification in the email so you have it for the audit.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Perfect. Then I'll approve it this afternoon.

questions.q: What is the main point of the call?
options: Getting an urgent purchase approved and agreeing conditions
Cancelling a software contract
Training finance on the vendor system
Explaining a late invoice
questions.explanation: Arjun asks for approval and they agree the full purchase with a usage report.

questions.q: How long does the contract run?
options: Six weeks
One month
Twelve weeks
Until this afternoon
questions.explanation: Arjun says the contract runs twelve weeks.

questions.q: How does Priya feel about 'urgent' as a justification?
options: She finds it fully convincing
She thinks it is not enough on its own
She is angry about the request
She has no opinion
questions.explanation: She says urgent isn't enough for finance.

questions.q: Why does Arjun reject buying only half?
options: He wants to save money
He thinks the vendor will refuse
He has not decided the cost centre
He expects the tickets to run out during a busy period
questions.explanation: He says half won't last and they'd run dry in the busiest period.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hello Ibrahim, it's Rachel from QA. I'm calling because batch S C seven zero six four has been put on hold.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Oh, that's not what I wanted to hear on a Tuesday. What happened?

script.speaker: A
script.line: A deviation during filling. There's an investigation open, so nothing from that batch can ship until it closes.

script.speaker: B
script.line: How long are we talking about? I have customers waiting.

script.speaker: A
script.line: The team meets next week, and I expect a decision by the 5th of March.

script.speaker: B
script.line: The 5th. Okay, that gives me a little room. How much stock is affected?

script.speaker: A
script.line: The whole batch, around eight thousand packs. Oh wait, sorry, I read the wrong line. The decision date is the 3rd of March, not the 5th.

script.speaker: B
script.line: The 3rd is even better. But I should be careful. Is there any chance the decision is a rejection?

script.speaker: A
script.line: I can't say yet. It's possible, but nothing points that way at the moment. Don't plan around a rejection, but don't promise the stock either.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Understood. Can I use stock from the neighbouring batch meanwhile?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Yes, that batch isn't affected. Just check with me before you reserve it, so I can confirm its status.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Will do. I'll tell the customers there may be a short delay, without giving a date.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That sounds sensible. I'll call you as soon as the team has the result.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Thanks, Rachel. I appreciate you telling me so early.

questions.q: Why is Rachel calling?
options: To ask him to reject a batch
To report a late truck
To tell Ibrahim a batch cannot ship during an investigation
To offer extra stock
questions.explanation: She says the batch is on hold and nothing can ship until the investigation closes.

questions.q: When is the decision expected in the end?
options: On the 5th of March
On Tuesday
At the end of next week
On the 3rd of March
questions.explanation: Rachel corrects herself: the decision date is the 3rd of March, not the 5th.

questions.q: How does Ibrahim react to the news?
options: Concerned but practical
Delighted
Furious with Rachel
Completely calm and uninterested
questions.explanation: He asks about timing and stock, then plans to use another batch and warn customers.

questions.q: What does Rachel imply about the outcome?
options: The batch will certainly be released
The batch will certainly be rejected
The neighbouring batch will also be held
It is not certain yet and rejection is possible
questions.explanation: She says rejection is possible but nothing points that way, so don't promise the stock.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Marta, thanks for joining. You said in your message you wanted to talk about meetings. What's on your mind?

script.speaker: B
script.line: It's a bit embarrassing. When the big review meetings are in English, I get nervous and go quiet, even when I know my numbers.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's more common than you think. Last month you traced the six hundred late orders on case V A four nine eight one to a master data error, remember?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Thanks, but it was five hundred sixty in the end. Forty were duplicates. Still, nobody heard about it, because I stayed silent in the review.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Sorry, five hundred sixty, of course. That's exactly why I want your voice in the room. What would make it easier?

script.speaker: B
script.line: I probably speak in maybe twelve percent of the meetings, and only when someone asks me directly. I freeze when I have to answer on the spot.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Then let's remove the surprise. Send me two or three bullet points before each meeting, and I'll make sure you get the floor on that topic.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That sounds doable. If I've written it down, I feel much calmer.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Second idea: ask one question per meeting, nothing more. A short one, like 'could you clarify the deadline?'. It builds the habit without pressure.

script.speaker: B
script.line: One question, I can manage that. What if my English fails me halfway through a sentence?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Then say 'let me rephrase that' and carry on. Honestly, nobody minds. I do it constantly.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Okay, I like that. Could we practise before next week's review?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Absolutely. Send me your bullets on Monday and we'll run through them for ten minutes. I'm glad you told me.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of the conversation?
options: The manager criticises Marta's analysis
The manager helps Marta feel more confident in English meetings
They plan a new order process
They discuss moving Marta to another team
questions.explanation: Marta says she gets nervous in English meetings and Tomas gives practical tips.

questions.q: How many orders were really late?
options: Six hundred
Forty
Five hundred sixty
Five hundred forty
questions.explanation: Marta corrects the number: 'it was five hundred sixty in the end. Forty were duplicates.'

questions.q: How does Marta feel about speaking in big meetings?
options: Proud and eager
Annoyed at her colleagues
Bored by the topics
Embarrassed and nervous
questions.explanation: She says it's a bit embarrassing and that she gets nervous and goes quiet.

questions.q: Why does Tomas mention Marta's earlier analysis?
options: To show she has valuable knowledge that others should hear
To complain about a mistake she made
To ask her to repeat the work
To compare her with another planner
questions.explanation: He says that is exactly why he wants her voice in the room.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Marta, about the training for the new planning software. I'd like a two-hour session for the whole team on the 19th of January, starting at half past one.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Two hours for everyone is difficult. Half the team will be closing orders that afternoon, and we still have forty open.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I understand, but I want everyone trained before the system goes live. Is a shorter session possible?

script.speaker: B
script.line: What if we run one hour on the 19th, and I record it for people who can't attend? They can watch it the next morning.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hmm. I'd prefer live. But a recording plus a short question session on Friday could work. Who prepares the materials?

script.speaker: B
script.line: I can prepare the slides, but I'd need the demo environment from IT. Could you ask them?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Fine, I'll ask this afternoon. Please keep it practical, with real examples from our own orders.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Understood. I'll send you the draft agenda by Wednesday so you can check it before we invite people.

questions.q: What are Tomas and Marta mainly doing?
options: Agreeing how to organise training despite a busy period
Choosing new planning software
Closing the open orders
Complaining about IT
questions.explanation: Tomas asks for a long session and they settle on a shorter one plus a recording.

questions.q: How long will the live session be?
options: Two hours
Half a day
One hour
Until Friday
questions.explanation: Marta proposes one hour on the 19th instead of Tomas's two-hour plan, and Tomas accepts.

questions.q: How does Marta react to the two-hour plan?
options: She is delighted with it
She is concerned about the team's workload
She thinks it is too short
She refuses to hold any training
questions.explanation: She says two hours is difficult because half the team is closing orders.

questions.q: What can we infer about Tomas and the recording?
options: He thinks recordings are better
He refuses the idea completely
He wants IT to make the recording
He accepts it, though he would prefer a live session
questions.explanation: He says 'I'd prefer live' but then agrees a recording plus a Friday session could work.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hello Lukas, I'm Chloe, the safety officer. Before your visit on Tuesday, I'll explain the rules for the site.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Thanks, Chloe. I'm happy to listen.

script.speaker: A
script.line: First, please arrive at the main gate at one o'clock. Sorry, correction: your visit starts at half past one, not one. Please come then.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Half past one on Tuesday, noted. What do I need to bring?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Just your ID. Around fifteen percent of visitors forget it, so please check your bag. At the gate you get a visitor badge. Wear it all the time.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Okay. And what about protective equipment on the site?

script.speaker: A
script.line: We give you a helmet and safety glasses, and you need shoes with steel toes in the warehouse. Please don't wear sandals.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I'll wear boots. Are there special walking routes?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Yes, always use the green path on the floor. The yellow path is for forklifts, so please don't walk there.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Understood. What happens if there's an alarm?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Stop what you're doing and follow your guide to the assembly point in the car park. Don't use the lifts.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Got it. Is there anything else I should know?

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's all. I'll email you the rules, so you can read them again before Tuesday.

questions.q: What is the call mainly about?
options: A change to a delivery route
Safety rules for a site visit
A job interview
A forklift training course
questions.explanation: Chloe explains badge, equipment, routes and the alarm procedure for Lukas's visit.

questions.q: What time does the visit start?
options: One o'clock
Fifteen minutes later
Half past one
Half past two
questions.explanation: Chloe corrects herself: the visit starts at half past one, not one.

questions.q: What should Lukas do if the alarm sounds?
options: Follow his guide to the assembly point
Take the lift to the exit
Return to the main gate alone
Wait where he is
questions.explanation: Chloe says to follow the guide to the assembly point in the car park and not use the lifts.

questions.q: Why does Chloe mention the yellow path?
options: To warn him that forklifts use it
To show the shortest route
To say it is for visitors
To explain where the badge is
questions.explanation: She says the yellow path is for forklifts, so he should not walk there.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hi Chris, it's Amara. Have you got a moment? I'm looking at the forecast for the blue range, and month three jumps by thirty percent. What's behind it?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Hi Amara. Yes, I was expecting that question. It's a tender with a big hospital group. If we win, volumes go up from month three.

script.speaker: A
script.line: And have we won that tender already?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Not officially. The result should be out in two weeks. Sales told me to include it, and honestly I'm not comfortable with that.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I hear you. What's the problem exactly?

script.speaker: B
script.line: If I include it and we lose, we've ordered material for nothing. If I leave it out and we win, we can't deliver. Either way it lands on me.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Okay, take a breath. Nobody expects you to guess. Can you split it, with the base forecast and the tender as a separate line with a probability?

script.speaker: B
script.line: I could, but I don't know what probability to use. Sales keeps saying very likely.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Then I'll ask the commercial lead for a number. That's my job, not yours. I'll message her today.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That would help a lot, thank you. I just worry about being blamed if it goes wrong.

script.speaker: A
script.line: You won't be. You're showing the risk openly, which is the right thing to do. I can also run two supply scenarios, with and without the tender.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Brilliant. When could you have those?

script.speaker: A
script.line: I'll try to have a first view by half past four tomorrow. Nothing fancy, just the material needs.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Perfect. I'll send you the tender line as soon as I've separated it, before lunch.

questions.q: When is the tender result expected?
options: From month three
Tomorrow afternoon
In about two weeks
Before lunch today
questions.explanation: Chris says the result should be out in two weeks.

questions.q: How does Chris feel about the forecast?
options: Proud of the large increase
Anxious about being blamed either way
Sure that the tender is won
Uninterested in the outcome
questions.explanation: He says either way it lands on him and he worries about being blamed.

questions.q: What can we infer about the sales team's view?
options: They have lost the tender
They want the forecast reduced
They already signed the contract
They are optimistic but give no firm figure
questions.explanation: Sales told Chris to include it and keeps saying 'very likely' without giving a probability.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Raj, welcome. Let's start the quarterly review with your update. You said there was a change on component H V eight zero seven two?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, and it's not good news. The standard lead time moves from eight weeks to ten. I'm sorry, I know this hits your plans. My manager only told me yesterday.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Thanks for being straight with me. Ten weeks, from when exactly?

script.speaker: B
script.line: From orders placed after next month. Orders already confirmed keep the eight weeks.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That helps. The question is how much extra safety stock we need to cover two more weeks.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I'm not sure how you calculate that. I'm worried I'll give you a wrong answer.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Don't worry, that's our side. As a rough rule, two more weeks means about five percent more safety stock. I'll run the numbers properly.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That would be a relief. Honestly, I've been dreading this meeting.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Understandable, but problems like this are better caught early. What I need from you is written confirmation of the new lead time.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I can do that. I'll ask my manager to send it by Friday.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Great. And is there any chance ten weeks becomes twelve later?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Not that I know of. It comes from a one-off capacity change at our plant.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Okay. I'll recalculate the safety stock this week and share the result with you.

questions.q: What is the main topic of the meeting?
options: A price reduction
A longer lead time and its effect on safety stock
A change of supplier
A quality complaint
questions.explanation: Raj announces the lead time change and Marta asks about safety stock.

questions.q: What was the lead time before the change?
options: Eight weeks
Ten weeks
Two weeks
Twelve weeks
questions.explanation: Raj says it moves from eight weeks to ten.

questions.q: What will Marta do this week?
options: Write to Raj's manager
Order more components
Visit the plant
Recalculate the safety stock
questions.explanation: She says she'll recalculate the safety stock this week.

questions.q: Why does Marta say 'Don't worry, that's our side'?
options: To tell him the work is not needed
To blame Raj's company
To reassure Raj and take the calculation on herself

script.line: Hi Adam, good to hear you. Go ahead. The customer is waiting, so I need to choose between air and sea quite fast.

script.speaker: A
script.line: So, by air, the one hundred and fifty kilograms would arrive in three days. By sea, they would arrive on the twenty-fourth of July.

script.speaker: B
script.line: The twenty-fourth is too late. The customer needs the goods by the twentieth. How much more is the air option?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Roughly four times the sea price, but nothing is final until you confirm. I can hold the space for you for a day.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Hmm, if we run out of stock, it will cost us more than the freight. Let me check with my manager. Can we speak again tomorrow at eleven?

script.speaker: A
script.line: I have a customer call at eleven. Would ten work for you instead?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Ten is too early, I have a team meeting. How about two in the afternoon?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Two is fine. I'll keep the air space until then and send you the final quote by email before our call.

questions.q: What is the main topic of the call?
options: Changing the customer's delivery address
Reducing the size of the order
Choosing the transport for a rushed order
Asking for a refund from the agency
questions.explanation: Adam gives air and sea options and Fatima has to choose one.

questions.q: When will Fatima and Adam talk again?
options: At eleven tomorrow morning
At two tomorrow afternoon
At ten tomorrow morning
On the twentieth of July
questions.explanation: After eleven and ten are both rejected, they agree on two in the afternoon.

questions.q: What will Adam do before the next call?
options: Ask the customer for a later date
Book the sea shipment now
Speak with Fatima's manager
Hold the air space and send a quote
questions.explanation: Adam says he will keep the air space and send the final quote by email.

questions.q: Why does Fatima say "if we run out of stock, it will cost us more than the freight"?
options: To say the sea option is cheaper
To refuse the quote completely
To say why air looks better to her
To ask Adam for a discount
questions.explanation: She compares the cost of no stock with the freight price, which supports choosing air.

title: Why is safety stock so high

script.speaker: A
script.line: Marta, you wanted to see me about the inventory report?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes. Item G R fifteen twelve is sitting at almost double its safety stock target. Can you tell me what happened?

script.speaker: A
script.line: It goes back to the fourteenth of February. Sales gave us a big forecast spike, so we raised our orders. But the tender they expected never came through.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I remember that. So the extra stock is the result of a sale that did not happen.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Exactly. I'd like to burn it down by stopping new orders until the stock is back at target. Another option is to return part of it to the supplier.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Let's not return anything. I'd rather not reopen that conversation with them right now. We'll need their flexibility later in the year.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Understood. Then I'll block new orders and update the plan by Thursday, so you can see how long it takes to reach the target.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good. Send it to me on Thursday morning, and add a short note about the tender so we remember why this happened.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Will do. I'll also ask sales to tell us earlier if a big deal looks uncertain.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Please do. That alone would save us a lot of trouble.

questions.q: What caused the extra stock?
options: A forecast spike for a tender that failed
A supplier delivered the wrong quantity
A customer returned a large number of units
A mistake in the safety stock target
questions.explanation: A says sales gave a big forecast spike, but the tender never came through.

questions.q: What will Ben do by Thursday?
options: Return part of the stock to the supplier
Ask sales for a new forecast
Lower the safety stock target
Update the plan after blocking new orders
questions.explanation: Ben says he will block new orders and update the plan by Thursday.

questions.q: Why does Marta say "I'd rather not reopen that conversation with them"?
options: She wants to change supplier next month
She is politely refusing the return idea
She does not understand the stock report
She is asking Ben to call them today
questions.explanation: She turns down the return idea and says they will need the supplier's flexibility later.

questions.q: What is the main point of the conversation?
options: Planning a new tender with sales
Reducing the extra stock of one item
Changing the supplier contract terms
Training the sales team on forecasts
questions.explanation: They talk about why the stock is too high and agree to burn it down.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hi Ingrid, it's Luis. Do you have a minute? I wanted to organise a lunch for Daniel, since it's his last week with us.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Oh, yes, of course. Sorry if I sound frazzled. We have six hundred tickets in the queue, which is thirty-five percent more than normal.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That sounds rough. Look, don't worry about the lunch, I'll take care of the organising. I only need your opinion on the day.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Thanks, that's a relief. Friday is out, since half the team works from home. What about Monday?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Monday it is. I'll book the Italian place near the station. And I was thinking of a small gift, maybe a framed photo of the whole team.

script.speaker: B
script.line: What a lovely idea. Could you also collect the money? With this queue, I'd probably forget.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Sure, I'll ask everyone for ten euros. I'll write the card too, so all you have to do is sign it.

script.speaker: B
script.line: You're a lifesaver, Luis. I'll sign it on Monday morning and come straight to the restaurant.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Perfect. And try to step outside for some air today. Those tickets will still be there, but you'll think more clearly.

questions.q: What gift does Luis suggest?
options: A card signed by Daniel
A voucher for the restaurant
A book about teamwork
A framed photo of the team
questions.explanation: Luis suggests a small gift, maybe a framed photo of the whole team.

questions.q: Why do they choose Monday instead of Friday?
options: Many people work from home on Fridays
The restaurant is closed on Friday
Daniel leaves before Friday
The queue is longer on Fridays
questions.explanation: Ingrid says Friday is out because half the team works from home.

questions.q: How is Ingrid probably feeling at the start of the call?
options: Annoyed that Daniel is leaving
Excited about the restaurant
Overwhelmed by her workload
Bored with her job
questions.explanation: She says she sounds frazzled and mentions six hundred tickets in the queue.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hello Amara, thanks for the call. The connection is not great, so tell me if I cut out. I have a question about my unused vacation days.

script.speaker: B
script.line: No problem, Pedro, I can hear you well enough. What would you like to know?

script.speaker: A
script.line: I still have eight days left this year, and I'd like to carry some into next year. Is that allowed?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, but there is a limit. Normally you can carry over thirty percent of your yearly allowance, and the rest is lost at the end of the year.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I see. With twenty-five days, thirty percent is about seven. So I would lose one day. In that case I will take a Friday off next week to use it.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That is one option. But wait, I actually have some good news. Yesterday management approved a full carry-over for everyone this year, because of the busy season.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Really? That changes things. Then I do not need to rush and book that Friday off.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Exactly. All eight days can go into next year. You just need to fill in a form.

script.speaker: A
script.line: When is the deadline for the form?

script.speaker: B
script.line: It has to reach us by the nineteenth of November. After that date, the system closes the requests.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Okay, I will fill it in today. Can you send me the link? The email did not arrive last time.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Of course, I'll send it right after this call. Thank you for asking early.

questions.q: How many days can Pedro carry over after the good news?
options: All eight days
About seven days
Only one day
Twenty-five days
questions.explanation: Amara says all eight days can go into next year.

questions.q: Why does Pedro decide not to take a Friday off?
options: He has lost the days already
His manager refused his earlier request
Management approved a full carry-over
The form deadline has already passed
questions.explanation: Amara says management approved a full carry-over, so Pedro says he doesn't need to rush.

questions.q: What will Amara do after the call?
options: Fill in the form for Pedro
Send Pedro the link to the form
Call management about the rule
Move the deadline to Friday
questions.explanation: Amara says she will send the link right after the call.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Andrew, thanks for squeezing me in. I've been locked out since I changed my password this morning, and I'm up against the clock.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Happy to help, Claire. First I need to confirm it's really you. Do you have your badge with you?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Right here, and my employee number.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Perfect, that matches. Now, the usual process asks for a code from your authenticator app, which is where the snag is, isn't it?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Exactly. I got a new phone last week and the app didn't carry over, so I can't generate the code at all.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I suspected as much. Normally I'd wait for your manager's written approval before setting up a new device, which can take a day.

script.speaker: A
script.line: A day is a problem. I have to approve the shipment of eighty cartons before eleven, otherwise the truck leaves without it.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Understood. I can't bypass the check altogether, but I can give you temporary access, limited to the shipping screen, until noon.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That would solve my morning. What's the catch?

script.speaker: B
script.line: The catch is that you register the new phone properly on Tuesday, in person, with me. No more shortcuts after that.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Fair enough. I'd rather have sorted it today, but I'll give up that bit, as long as the shipment goes out.

script.speaker: B
script.line: And I'm giving up my usual wait for your manager's approval, so we're both bending a little. Let me set it up now.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Brilliant. How long will it take?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Two minutes. You'll get a temporary password by message, and you'll change it when you log in.

questions.q: How long will the temporary access last?
options: Until eleven
Until Tuesday
For one whole day
Until noon
questions.explanation: Andrew offers temporary access limited to the shipping screen until noon.

questions.q: Why can Claire not produce the login code?
options: She forgot her employee number again
Her manager blocked her account access
Her login app is not on her new phone
Her badge does not work at the door
questions.explanation: Claire says she got a new phone and the app didn't carry over.

questions.q: What will Claire do on Tuesday?
options: Set up her new phone with Andrew
Approve the shipment of eighty cartons
Ask her manager for written approval
Change her password a second time
questions.explanation: Andrew says she must register the new phone properly on Tuesday, in person, with him.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Emma, I read your message about deviation K G two six nine nine, but I'd like to hear it from you. What exactly happened?

script.speaker: B
script.line: During packaging last night, the label printer jammed, and about one hundred and twenty units went out with a smudged batch number. We caught them at the final check.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Okay, so the product itself isn't affected, only the labelling. Are the units still in the building?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, they're all on hold in the cage. To be honest, I'm quite worried, because this is the second printer problem this year and the audit is coming up.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Let's keep it in proportion. Relabel the units under supervision, then send me a corrective plan within two weeks. Shall we review it in my office on Wednesday?

script.speaker: B
script.line: I'm at the other site on Wednesday. Could we do Thursday instead?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Thursday my office is booked all day, I'm afraid. Let's do it by video on Friday morning, then.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Friday morning works. I'll have the plan ready, and I'll ask maintenance to check the printer before then.

questions.q: When will Jon and Emma review the plan?
options: On Wednesday, in Jon's office
On Thursday, in Jon's office
Within two weeks, at the other site
On Friday morning, by video
questions.explanation: After Wednesday and Thursday fail, Jon suggests video on Friday morning and Emma agrees.

questions.q: How does Emma feel about the problem?
options: Calm because the product is safe
Worried because it happened before
Angry at the maintenance team
Pleased that the check caught it
questions.explanation: Emma says she is quite worried, because it is the second printer problem this year.

questions.q: What will Emma do before the review?
options: Send the units to the customer today
Ask maintenance to check the printer
Relabel all the units without any help
Move the audit to a later date
questions.explanation: Emma says she will ask maintenance to check the printer before then.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Mark, thanks for joining. I'd like to float an idea: automating the weekly service report, which eats half a day of mine every Monday.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I can see the appeal. Before I commit to anything, though, what are we talking about in terms of effort?

script.speaker: A
script.line: I'd estimate three weeks of development, mostly on pulling data from the planning system. The layout stays the same.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Three weeks sounds optimistic, Priya. We said the same about the dashboard last year, and it took six.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Fair point. Let's say five, to be safe. The data feed is already documented under ticket T K sixty-four sixty-four, which should save us some time.

script.speaker: B
script.line: And the risks? If the numbers are wrong and go straight to leadership, I'm the one who has to explain it.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's why I want a parallel run. For a month we send both versions, and switch only when they match.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Reasonable. Then who maintains it afterwards? I don't want to inherit a tool that only one person understands.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good question. Your team could own it, and I'd write a short guide before handover.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I can live with that, as long as the guide exists before we take over.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Agreed. To wrap up: I'll send you the written plan with the effort estimate by the third of July.

script.speaker: B
script.line: And I'll ask IT about data access and reply the same day. Let's review everything the following Monday at half past one.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Perfect. I'll put it all in the minutes tonight.

questions.q: When will Priya send the written plan?
options: On the following Monday
After the month of parallel running
Before the handover guide is ready
By the third of July
questions.explanation: Priya says she will send the plan with the effort estimate by the third of July.

questions.q: Why does Priya want a parallel run?
options: To check the figures before leadership sees them
To save half a day of work every Monday
To train Mark's team on the planning system
To compare two possible reporting vendors
questions.explanation: Mark fears wrong numbers reaching leadership, and Priya answers that both versions will run for a month until they match.

questions.q: What can we infer about Mark's view of the first estimate?
options: He thinks it is too long
He wants the work done by IT
He does not trust it fully
He is happy to skip the guide
questions.explanation: He calls three weeks optimistic and reminds Priya that the dashboard took six.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Mark, thanks for coming over. We see the upside for next quarter differently, so let's sort it out today.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Agreed. Priya, my problem is the size. You want twelve percent on top of the baseline, and I can't take that to the committee without support.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I understand, but the pipeline is strong. The hospital group contract, filed under M H five two one four, would add most of that.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Would. That's the point. It isn't signed yet. If I plan cash for volume that never comes, we carry inventory we can't afford. My ceiling is three percent.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Three feels too cautious. If the contract lands and we're not ready, we'll be short, and that costs more than inventory.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Fair. What if we split the difference?

script.speaker: A
script.line: That would be about seven and a half percent, which is still more than I'm comfortable with.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Then let's tie the number to a clear assumption. We plan five percent, and it only grows if the contract is signed by the end of the month.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I can work with that. Five percent, with the signature as the trigger for anything above it.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good. I'll write it up as the finance assumption so nobody forgets the condition.

script.speaker: A
script.line: And I'll update the demand plan with a note explaining the trigger.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Let's put dates on this. I'll send you the revised cash projection by Thursday morning.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Thursday works. I'll send the updated demand plan to the whole S and O P group on Wednesday evening.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Perfect. If the contract news changes, call me straight away.

questions.q: What is the main result of the meeting?
options: They agree on a lower upside with a condition
They cancel the upside scenario completely
They wait for the contract before planning
They accept the twelve percent plan in full
questions.explanation: They settle on five percent, and more only if the contract is signed by the end of the month.

questions.q: What upside number do they agree to plan with?
options: Twelve percent
Three percent
Five percent
Seven and a half percent
questions.explanation: Mark says they plan five percent, and Priya accepts it as the consensus.

questions.q: Why does Mark resist a bigger upside?
options: The demand plan is out of date
The contract is not signed yet
The committee has refused the number
Inventory is already too low
questions.explanation: Mark says the contract isn't signed and cash for volume that never comes would be a problem.

questions.q: What will Mark do by Thursday morning?
options: Update the demand plan for the group
Sign the hospital contract
Call the committee to explain
Send a revised cash projection to Priya
questions.explanation: Mark says he will send the revised cash projection by Thursday morning.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Jon, I'd like to go through the cold-chain shipment for next week. It's the order under reference R D two eight five four.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Sure. Start with the packaging. Are we using the standard insulated box?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Yes, the same one that passed qualification six weeks ago. It keeps the temperature in range for up to seventy-two hours.

script.speaker: B
script.line: And what's the transit time with the main carrier?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Around forty hours door to door, so we have a comfortable cushion. If a flight is cancelled, though, we could lose a whole day.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's what worries me. Do we have a backup?

script.speaker: A
script.line: I've lined up a second carrier. They fly out at ten fifteen from the same airport, so we can switch on the same morning if we need to.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good. And who's tracking the shipment on the day?

script.speaker: A
script.line: I will, with the logger alerts going to my phone, and I'll keep you in copy.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Great. Anything else I should know?

script.speaker: A
script.line: One small thing, actually. The data logger for this order is out of stock until tomorrow.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Okay, no drama. Check with the supplier in the morning and tell me by noon. If they can't deliver, we'll borrow one from the other site.

questions.q: How long does the box keep the right temperature?
options: About forty hours in total
For about six weeks
Up to seventy-two hours
For one whole day
questions.explanation: Nora says the box keeps the temperature in range for up to seventy-two hours.

questions.q: Why does Jon ask about a backup carrier?
options: A cancelled flight could cost a day
The main carrier is too expensive
The box is not approved yet
The logger needs to be replaced
questions.explanation: Nora warns that a cancelled flight could lose a whole day, and Jon says that's what worries him.

questions.q: What will Nora do about the logger?
options: Borrow one from the other site today
Cancel the shipment until it arrives
Switch to the second carrier tomorrow
Check with the supplier and report by noon
questions.explanation: Jon tells her to check with the supplier in the morning and tell him by noon.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hello Lukas, it's Ana. Do you have a few minutes to talk about yesterday's presentation?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Of course, Ana. I was hoping you would call. How did it look from your side of the room?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Overall, very good. Your story was clear, and the chart showing twelve percent fewer stockouts really caught their attention.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's good to hear. I spent a lot of time on that slide.

script.speaker: A
script.line: It showed. If I may, there's one thing I'd change. You spent a long time on the method, and I noticed the directors checking their phones around the tenth minute.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Hmm. I wanted to show the numbers were reliable. Project H K seventy-eight seventy-seven was questioned last year.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I understand, and it's a fair worry. But senior people usually trust the work and want the decision first.

script.speaker: B
script.line: So what would you suggest I do instead?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Start with the recommendation, give two or three key numbers, and move the method into an appendix. If anyone asks, you can go straight there.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That makes sense. I'm presenting again in four weeks, so I could try it then. Would you listen to a rehearsal?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Gladly. How about Tuesday at three?

script.speaker: B
script.line: I'm at the plant on Tuesday. Could we do Wednesday morning instead?

script.speaker: A
script.line: I'm travelling on Wednesday. Let's make it Thursday at nine, and I'll send you an invitation today.

questions.q: What is the main message of Ana's feedback?
options: The chart should be removed from the talk
The talk was good but too detailed in the method
The talk was far too short for the directors
The recommendation was not clear enough
questions.explanation: Ana praises the story and chart, then says he spent too long on the method.

questions.q: When will Ana listen to the rehearsal?
options: On Tuesday at three
On Thursday at nine
On Wednesday morning
In four weeks
questions.explanation: After Tuesday and Wednesday fail, Ana proposes Thursday at nine.

questions.q: Why did Lukas include so much on the method?
options: The directors asked him to include it
He had run out of other things to say
Ana had told him to explain it all
He wanted the numbers to look trustworthy
questions.explanation: Lukas says he wanted to show the numbers were reliable, because a project was questioned last year.

questions.q: What will Ana do today?
options: Send Lukas a calendar invitation
Present to the directors herself
Write the appendix for him
Travel to the plant on Tuesday
questions.explanation: Ana says she will send an invitation today.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Arjun, thanks for making time. I'll get straight to it: the last delivery arrived on Thursday, nine days late, and the penalty clause kicks in after the first week.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I appreciate you being direct, Olivia. First, a small correction: our carrier's record shows delivery on Wednesday at eleven in the morning, so we're talking about eight days, not nine.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Fine, eight then. It doesn't change the principle, though. The contract gives us a clear remedy, and I'm under pressure to apply it in full.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Please look at the timeline. The lead time is ten weeks, and your change request came in at week seven. Redoing the artwork alone cost us a fortnight.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I won't pretend that played no part. But a change request doesn't excuse missing a date we both signed.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Not entirely, no. Which is why I'm not asking you to waive the penalty, only to share it. Half would be fair, in my view.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Half is more than I can sign without my director. What I could do is recommend sixty percent of the penalty, if you commit to a written recovery plan.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Sixty is hard for me, honestly, but a recovery plan I'm happy to give you. Let me see what my finance people say.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's all I ask. I'll write it up this afternoon as a proposal, not as a decision.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good. I'd rather settle this between us than let it sour the relationship.

questions.q: What is the conversation mainly about?
