options: Cancelling the contract completely
Changing the lead time for packaging
How to share the cost of a late delivery
Finding a new carrier
questions.explanation: Olivia raises the penalty and Arjun asks to share it.

questions.q: When did the delivery really arrive, according to the carrier?
options: On Wednesday at eleven in the morning
On Thursday, as Olivia first said
On Wednesday, a week before the penalty
On Thursday at eleven in the morning
questions.explanation: Arjun corrects Olivia: the carrier's record shows Wednesday at eleven, eight days late.

questions.q: How does Arjun feel about the sixty percent offer?
options: Pleased and ready to sign now
Angry and ready to walk away
Reluctant, but willing to talk
Indifferent to the amount of money
questions.explanation: He says sixty is hard for him but offers a recovery plan and will check with finance.

questions.q: What can we infer about Olivia's position?
options: She wants the penalty to be waived
She needs her director to approve half
She works for the carrier company
She approved the change request alone
questions.explanation: She says half is more than she can sign without her director.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hello Elena, thanks for calling. I understand we both need Dev the week of the twenty-fourth of January.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, and that's a problem. My project lasts six weeks, and he's the only one who knows the model. I thought you needed him full time that week.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Oh, no, that's a misunderstanding. I only need about thirty percent of his time, mainly for a few checks.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Ah, that's much better than I feared. So there may be room for both of us.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I think so. What if I take him on Monday and Tuesday mornings, and he's all yours for the rest of the week?

script.speaker: B
script.line: That works for me, as long as he agrees. I don't want to put him in the middle of this.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Agreed. I'll ask him today. If it doesn't work, we call our managers on Friday, but not before.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good. Let's try ourselves first. I'll send a short summary of what we agreed.

questions.q: What is the main point of the call?
options: Elena asks for a new specialist
Arjun cancels his project for now
Both leads call their managers today
Two leads try to share one specialist
questions.explanation: They look for a way for both projects to use Dev without escalating.

questions.q: How much of Dev's time does Arjun need?
options: All of his time that week
About half of his time
About thirty percent
Six full weeks
questions.explanation: Arjun clarifies he only needs about thirty percent of his time.

questions.q: Why does Elena need Dev for her project?
options: He alone knows the model
He is her direct manager
He owns the project budget
He asked to join her team
questions.explanation: Elena says he's the only one who knows the model.

questions.q: What will Arjun do next?
options: Call both managers right now
Move his project to February
Send the summary to Dev
Ask Dev about the plan today
questions.explanation: Arjun says he will ask him today, and managers only come in on Friday if it fails.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hello Sara, I can see you, but your audio keeps cutting out. Can you hear me?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, I hear you, but only just. Let's keep it short, and I'll confirm everything in writing afterwards.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good idea. I wanted to ask about the order under reference K C fourteen twenty-six. What is the status?

script.speaker: B
script.line: There are two key points. First, the delivery has moved to the eighth of September.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Sorry, the line broke up. Did you say the eighteenth of September?

script.speaker: B
script.line: No, the eighth. Eight. The eighth of September. The second point is that the supplier offers a twenty-five percent discount if we take the full quantity.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Fifteen percent, you said? That would still be useful.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Not fifteen, twenty-five. Two five. It's a good discount, so I'd like us to accept before Friday.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Twenty-five, understood. That's better than I thought. Let me check with my team, but I think we will accept.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Excellent. Let me repeat the main points so we're clear: delivery on the eighth, a discount of twenty-five percent, and your answer by Friday.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Yes, that's right. I'll answer by Thursday evening to be safe.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I'll send you an email in a few minutes with everything in writing. Please reply to confirm.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Will do. Thanks for your patience with this connection.

questions.q: What is the new delivery date?
options: The eighteenth of September
The eighth of September
The fifteenth of September
The last Friday of the month
questions.explanation: Sara corrects Daniel: no, the eighth, the eighth of September.

questions.q: What will Sara do after the call?
options: Call the supplier again
Email Daniel a written summary
Reply to Daniel's team
Accept the discount by phone
questions.explanation: Sara says she will send an email in a few minutes with everything in writing.

questions.q: Why does Sara repeat the main points?
options: To sound more polite on the call
To end the meeting a bit sooner
To ask for a much bigger discount
To make sure both people understood
questions.explanation: After the confusing line, she repeats the date, discount and deadline so they are clear.

questions.q: What is the call mainly about?
options: A delivery date and a discount
A problem with the video software
A late payment from a customer
A change of supplier next year
questions.explanation: Sara gives a new date and a twenty-five percent discount for the order.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hi Samuel, take a seat. You said you can't open the shared folder. What do you see when you click on it?

script.speaker: B
script.line: A message saying I don't have permission. It's the folder with the warehouse counts, the one covering the twelve hundred pallets at the north site.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Let me check your account. Hmm, I can see you're not in the group for that folder any more.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's odd. I opened it without any problem until recently.

script.speaker: A
script.line: It looks like your membership was temporary. It ended six weeks ago, but the folder only started refusing you this week, probably after a system update.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I see. Can you just add me again?

script.speaker: A
script.line: I can't do that myself, I'm afraid. The folder owner has to approve it. I'll send her the request now.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Honestly, that's a bit frustrating. I need those counts for a report, and the owner is often travelling.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I understand. I'll mark the request as urgent, and I'd expect an answer by Tuesday at the latest.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Tuesday is cutting it fine, but okay. I'll use last month's counts in the meantime.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That sounds sensible. Oh, wait, there's one more thing. Your profile still shows an old manager, so the approval email might go to the wrong person.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Ah, that could be why my last request got stuck. Can you fix it?

script.speaker: A
script.line: I'll correct it tomorrow morning, and I'll call you on Monday to check whether the approval has arrived.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Thanks, that's reassuring. I'll wait for your call.

questions.q: Why can Samuel not open the folder?
options: The folder was deleted last week
His password has expired again
His temporary group membership ended
The north site has been closed down
questions.explanation: Sara says his membership was temporary and ended six weeks ago.

questions.q: When does Sara expect an answer from the folder owner?
options: By Tuesday at the latest
By Monday, when Sara calls
Tomorrow, after the profile fix
In six weeks, when it renews
questions.explanation: Sara says she'd expect an answer by Tuesday at the latest.

questions.q: How does Samuel feel about the approval step?
options: Pleased with the fast process
Confused about the folder name
Frustrated about the wait
Relaxed because he has the counts
questions.explanation: He says it's a bit frustrating, because he needs the counts and the owner is often away.

questions.q: What probably happened to Samuel's earlier request?
options: It was approved and then lost
It was sent to the wrong manager
It was never written or sent
It was refused by the owner
questions.explanation: Sara notes the profile shows an old manager, and Samuel says that could be why the last request got stuck.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hi Henrik, you said you wanted to go over some terms before Wednesday. Where shall we start?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Honestly, everywhere. I'm a bit stressed. Everyone says lead time and O T I F in meetings, and I just nod.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's normal in your first month. Lead time is the days between ordering and receiving. Safety stock is extra inventory we keep in case demand or deliveries surprise us.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Okay, that's clear. And O T I F?

script.speaker: A
script.line: On time, in full: the share of order lines delivered when promised, in the right quantity. Last week we missed five percent of our hundred and twenty lines.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Got it. And what about batch release?

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's when quality approves a batch so it can be sold. Don't worry, Henrik. I'll write you a one-page glossary today, for Wednesday's meeting.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That would be a huge relief. Thank you, Camila. I'll read it tonight.

questions.q: What does batch release mean, according to Camila?
options: A supplier sends a batch to the site
Planning orders a new batch today
The warehouse counts a batch of stock
Quality approves a batch for sale
questions.explanation: Camila says batch release is when quality formally approves a batch so it can be sold.

questions.q: What will Camila do today?
options: Present at Wednesday's meeting
Send Henrik the list of order lines
Write a one-page glossary for Henrik
Call the quality team about the batch
questions.explanation: Camila promises a one-page glossary today.

questions.q: Why does Camila say "That's completely normal in your first month"?
options: To calm Henrik down
To correct a mistake he made
To change the topic
To end the call quickly
questions.explanation: Henrik says he is stressed, and she tells him it is normal to reassure him.

questions.q: What is the call mostly about?
options: Fixing a late delivery problem
Planning the next quarter together
Reviewing the quality complaints
Explaining work terms to a new joiner
questions.explanation: Henrik asks for terms and Camila explains lead time, safety stock, O T I F and batch release.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Camila, come in. You wanted to book a flight to the supply chain conference?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, it starts on Friday morning, so I need to land the day before. Two options came up in my search, and I can't decide.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Let me pull them up. The first is direct, landing at half past one on Thursday, but eight percent dearer. The second has a stopover and lands in the evening.

script.speaker: B
script.line: The evening one worries me. If anything slips, I'd be walking into a Friday keynote exhausted.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Fair enough. Here's the catch, though. Our policy says any fare more than five percent above the cheapest needs your director's sign-off, and the direct one is eight percent above.

script.speaker: B
script.line: So I need approval. She's usually quick when there's a good reason, and I'd argue the earlier arrival protects my first day.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I'd say the same, and I can attach a note explaining the comparison. The price should hold until the end of the day.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Then let's go with the direct flight, pending her approval.

script.speaker: A
script.line: One more snag, I'm afraid. The name on your profile is spelled differently from your passport. I'll need to see the passport to correct it.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good catch. I'll bring it tomorrow before nine, so we can fix it and finish the booking.

questions.q: How much more expensive is the direct flight?
options: Five percent
Eight percent
Ten percent
Thirteen percent
questions.explanation: Omar says the direct flight is eight percent above the cheapest.

questions.q: Why does Camila hesitate about the second flight?
options: It leaves very early on Friday morning
She would arrive tired on conference day
It is against the company travel policy
It costs more than the direct flight
questions.explanation: She says if anything slips she'd walk into the keynote exhausted.

questions.q: What can we infer about Camila's choice?
options: She will pay the extra amount herself
She will skip the first day of the conference
She will take the cheapest fare to save money
She will take the direct flight if approved
questions.explanation: She says the earlier arrival protects her first day, and they go with the direct flight pending approval.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Mateo, thanks for coming in. I understand you'd like us to pull the delivery forward by a week, from the twenty-seventh of April.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Small correction, Aisha: the confirmed date is the twenty-ninth of April, I have the email. And our launch moved up, so we need the stock by Thursday of next week.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Thank you, the twenty-ninth it is. I do see the urgency, but there are constraints. The line is fully booked, and the lab needs five working days for release testing.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Could the testing run in parallel? We've done it before for urgent orders.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Only partly, though that helps. I can put your order ahead of another one, but that delays another customer by a few days. It's a genuine trade-off.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Which order would you move back?

script.speaker: A
script.line: The one for the northern region, since their stock level is healthy. I'd need to ask them first, though. I'm not comfortable deciding that for them.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's reasonable. How soon can you let me know?

script.speaker: A
script.line: I'll call them this afternoon, and I'll confirm with you tomorrow at nine, before the production meeting.

questions.q: What is the original delivery date?
options: The twenty-seventh of April
The twenty-ninth of April
The Thursday of next week
A week before the launch
questions.explanation: Mateo corrects Aisha: the confirmed date is the twenty-ninth of April.

questions.q: Why can Aisha not simply move the delivery forward?
options: The customer has not paid the deposit yet
The northern region has already refused
The launch was cancelled last week
The line is full and testing takes time
questions.explanation: She says the line is fully booked and the lab needs five working days for release testing.

questions.q: What will Aisha do next?
options: Cancel the northern order and apologise
Skip the release testing to save time
Call the northern customer, then tell Mateo
Move the production meeting to today
questions.explanation: She says she will call them this afternoon and confirm with Mateo tomorrow at nine.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Marta, thanks for jumping on a call. I dropped you a note in the chat, but it's easier to say this out loud.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Of course, Ben. Is something the matter?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Nothing serious. It's about the weekly supplier meeting. The updates have been running long, and some of us arrive without knowing what we need to decide.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I see. I suppose I do tend to go through everything in detail, and we haven't had an agenda since project K P sixty-four twelve started eight weeks ago.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I don't blame you, it just grew that way. What if we try a short agenda the day before, two minutes per update, and decisions at the end?

script.speaker: B
script.line: I like that. Two minutes will be hard for me, though. Could I put the detail in a shared note instead?

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's exactly the idea. Say what changed, what you need, and link to the note for the rest.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Okay. I'll draft an agenda template and send it to you by half past four tomorrow.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Great. On Friday I'll introduce the new format to the group, and people will send their items by noon the day before.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Perfect. Thanks for putting it so kindly, Ben.

questions.q: What is Ben's main message?
options: The meetings need a simpler format
The supplier meeting should be cancelled
Marta's updates are often inaccurate
The project is already eight weeks late
questions.explanation: Ben says updates run long and suggests an agenda and short updates.

questions.q: By when will Marta send the agenda template?
options: By noon the day before each meeting
On Friday
In eight weeks
By half past four tomorrow
questions.explanation: Marta says she will send the template by half past four tomorrow.

questions.q: Why does Ben call Marta?
options: The chat message did not arrive at all
Updates run long and people lack a clear goal
Marta missed the last supplier meeting entirely
The agenda template has not been written yet
questions.explanation: Ben says the updates have been running long and people arrive not knowing what to decide.

questions.q: What will Ben do on Friday?
options: Write the agenda template himself
Introduce the new format to the group
Send his items to Marta by noon
Start a new project with Marta
questions.explanation: Ben says on Friday he will introduce the new format to the group.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Tomas, good morning. As you know, I'm moving to the strategy team next month, and I'd like to walk you through our suppliers before I go.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Thanks, Lucia. I appreciate it. Where would you like to start?

script.speaker: A
script.line: With Kestrel Materials, which supplies about thirty-five percent of our volume. They're excellent on quality, but they confirm late. Chase them on Wednesdays, because their planning team reviews orders then.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Sorry, so they confirm late because Wednesday is the first time they see the order?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Not quite. They see it early, but they only commit after the Wednesday review. So if you send an order on Thursday, it can sit there for almost a week.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Ah, understood. So orders should go out before Wednesday morning.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Exactly. Second, the contract manufacturer. Their lead time is long, and they quote optimistic dates. The file under N L sixty-five eighteen is a good example.

script.speaker: B
script.line: So I should build in a buffer, and never take their first date at face value.

script.speaker: A
script.line: You've got it. I'll send you my notes today, and I'm happy to join your first call with them if you like.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of the call?
options: To complain about a late order
To plan an audit of a supplier
To negotiate a new supply contract
To hand over supplier know-how
questions.explanation: Lucia says she is moving teams and walks Tomas through the suppliers.

questions.q: When does the first supplier commit to orders?
options: After its Wednesday review
As soon as it receives them
On Thursday morning
Before Wednesday morning
questions.explanation: Lucia clarifies that they only commit after the Wednesday review.

questions.q: Why might an order sent on Thursday wait almost a week?
options: The supplier is closed every Thursday and Friday
Orders need a quality check before they leave
The supplier only commits after its Wednesday review
The planner is away until the following Monday
questions.explanation: Lucia says they see orders early but only commit after the Wednesday review.

questions.q: What can we infer about the contract manufacturer?
options: Its promised dates are often too early
Its lead time is very short
It confirms orders faster than Kestrel
It supplies most of the volume
questions.explanation: Lucia says they quote optimistic dates, and Tomas concludes he should build in a buffer.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hi Kenji, thank you for agreeing to be my mentor. I'm happy to finally meet you in person.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Me too, Yuki. Please, sit down. Before we start, how are you doing? You look a bit tense.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Is it that obvious? I'm leading my first project, the one called N C nine zero eight eight, and I feel a little lost.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's normal, and it's exactly the kind of thing we can work on. Let's begin with goals. What do you want from these meetings?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Mainly two things. I want to learn how to manage stakeholders, and I want to feel more confident when I speak in meetings.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good, both are realistic. How often shall we meet? I'd suggest every two weeks, for an hour.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Every two weeks sounds perfect. Should we try it for a fixed period?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, let's say ten weeks. After that we look at what has worked and decide whether to continue.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Great. And the project? I'm afraid I'll fail at the kick-off.

script.speaker: B
script.line: You won't. Don't worry, I've done this many times. Tell you what, I'll send you my kick-off checklist today, so you don't start from zero.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That would really help. Thank you.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Let's also pick a regular slot. Are mornings good for you? I'm free at nine o'clock on Mondays.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Nine o'clock on Monday suits me. I'll put the first one in the calendar.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Perfect. Come with one question about the project, and we'll start there.

questions.q: How long will the mentoring period last before they review it?
options: Two weeks
One hour
Ten weeks
Nine weeks
questions.explanation: Kenji says they will try ten weeks and then decide whether to continue.

questions.q: What will Kenji send Yuki today?
options: A list of the stakeholders to meet
His checklist for starting a project
The budget for the project plan
A calendar invitation for Monday
questions.explanation: Kenji says he will send his kick-off checklist today.

questions.q: Why does Kenji say "You won't. Don't worry"?
options: To disagree with her goals for mentoring
To change the meeting time to Monday
To ask her for the project name
To reassure Yuki about her kick-off
questions.explanation: Yuki says she's afraid she'll fail, and he reassures her.

questions.q: What is the main idea of the meeting?
options: Reviewing a finished project with a mentor
Choosing a new project leader for the team
Setting goals and a mentoring schedule
Learning a new software tool together
questions.explanation: They agree on goals, frequency, a fixed period and a regular slot.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Victor, thanks for making time. I want to show you something about the forecast for the southern market.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Sure, go ahead. I hope it isn't another report about how bad we are.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Not at all. Look at this chart. For the last six months we have forecast more than we sold, every single month, by about twelve percent on average.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I see it. To be fair, the sales team likes to be optimistic. When they're not sure, they round up, because nobody gets blamed for having too much stock.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I understand the habit, but it costs us in inventory. What if we apply a bias correction of five percent to all the numbers from that market?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Five percent sounds fair as a start. Could you also come to the sales call on Tuesday and explain the chart to the team yourself?

script.speaker: A
script.line: I'd like to help, but Tuesday afternoons are when I send the month-end numbers, and that deadline is not flexible.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Ah, I see. Then I'll present it myself, if you send me the slides.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Of course. I'll prepare a one-page version, with the chart from the eighth of April report, where the gap was widest.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good. Is the correction applied automatically from now on?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Yes, from the next cycle, and we'll review it after three months to see if the bias shrinks.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Great. I'll tell the team the correction isn't a punishment, just a way to keep the numbers honest.

questions.q: What is the main result of the conversation?
options: They agree to correct over-forecasting in one market
They stop using the forecast for that market
They replace the sales team in the southern region
They cancel the plan for the southern market
questions.explanation: Rachel proposes a five percent bias correction and Victor accepts it.

questions.q: When will they review the correction?
options: After six months
On Tuesday
On the eighth of April
After three months
questions.explanation: Rachel says they will review it after three months.

questions.q: Why can Rachel not join the sales call?
options: She is travelling to the south
She has a fixed month-end deadline
She disagrees with the correction
She is away on holiday on Tuesday
questions.explanation: She says Tuesday afternoons are when she sends the month-end numbers and the deadline is not flexible.

questions.q: What will Rachel give Victor?
options: A new sales forecast for the quarter
A one-page version of the chart
A full list of the customers
The month-end numbers for the year
questions.explanation: Rachel says she will prepare a one-page version for him to present.

title: Catching up after a late arrival

script.speaker: A
script.line: Sorry, Lucia, I'm very late. My train was delayed. Can you hear me properly? My connection is a bit shaky.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I can, but only just. No problem, Lukas. We've covered two points so far, and I can summarise them quickly.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Please do. Mainly I want to know whether we've settled the planning horizon.

script.speaker: B
script.line: We have. The plan is frozen for four weeks, then we look at twelve months rolling. The scenario file is N A six three five nine, by the way.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good. And what about the weekly review? Last time we couldn't agree on a day.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That was the tricky part. Operations wanted Monday, and sales wanted Friday morning. In the end each side gave something up, so it's Friday afternoon, at half past four.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's a fair compromise, though Friday at half past four isn't exactly my favourite! I'll live with it. What's left?

script.speaker: B
script.line: We still have to decide who owns the data cleaning. We'll pick that up right after the break, so you haven't missed it.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Perfect. I'll stay on mute and catch up on the rest. Please send me the slides afterwards.

questions.q: What has the group decided so far?
options: Who will own the data cleaning work
A new scenario file for the planning team
The date and place of the next workshop
The planning horizon and the review slot
questions.explanation: Lucia explains the plan freeze and horizon, and then the review slot.

questions.q: When will the weekly review take place?
options: Friday afternoon at half past four
Monday morning, as operations wanted
Friday morning, as sales wanted
Monday afternoon, after the break
questions.explanation: Lucia says it's Friday afternoon, at half past four.

questions.q: Why was the review set for Friday afternoon?
options: The data cleaning ended on Friday
Lukas asked for that exact time
Each side gave something up
The break starts at that time
questions.explanation: Lucia says operations wanted Monday and sales wanted Friday morning, so each side gave something up.

questions.q: How does Lukas feel about the review time?
options: He accepts it, though not gladly
He is delighted and wants it every week
He refuses and asks to reopen the debate
He thinks it is too early in the week
questions.explanation: He says it isn't his favourite but he'll live with it.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Lukas, thanks for picking up. I'm preparing for the steering committee, and I need to settle what we tell them about the rollout.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Okay. What's the current thinking on the delay?

script.speaker: A
script.line: That we slip by two weeks. Go-live moves to the nineteenth of April, and the committee will see ticket T S three zero three nine as the main cause.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Honestly, I'm not sure two weeks is enough. I'd say we should tell them three, to be on the safe side.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I hear you, but I don't want to ask for more time than we need. They'll lose confidence if we come back a second time.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's true. I just worry that we'll be back anyway if the testing goes wrong.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Let's check the data. Can you open the defect chart for the last two weeks?

script.speaker: B
script.line: One moment. Right, the open defects have dropped every day, and at this speed they reach zero around the tenth of April.

script.speaker: A
script.line: So the trend gives us a margin of nine days before the nineteenth. That's a decent cushion.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Okay, that convinces me. Two weeks, with a clear note that it depends on testing staying on track.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Exactly. The committee meets at half past four tomorrow, so please send me the chart by lunchtime.

questions.q: What do Ana and Lukas decide to tell the committee?
options: The rollout slips three weeks, as Lukas said
The rollout is cancelled and restarted
The rollout slips two weeks, if testing holds
The rollout stays on time, with no delay
questions.explanation: They agree on two weeks, depending on testing staying on track.

questions.q: What is the new go-live date?
options: The tenth of April
The nineteenth of April
Tomorrow at half past four
Three weeks after the old date
questions.explanation: Ana says go-live moves to the nineteenth of April.

questions.q: How does Lukas feel at the start about the two-week delay?
options: Sure that it is far too long
Annoyed at the steering committee
Happy with the plan from the start
Worried that it may not be enough
questions.explanation: He says he isn't sure two weeks is enough and would tell them three.

questions.q: Why does Ana not want to ask for three weeks?
options: The defects are rising every single day
The chart is still missing from the file
Asking again would hurt the committee's trust
The committee already refused more time
questions.explanation: She says they'll lose confidence if they come back a second time.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hi Katarina, I'm back from the conference in Lisbon, and I wanted to share the highlights while they're fresh.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Great, go ahead. I've been curious what you thought.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Two talks stood out. The first was about digital twins for distribution networks. The second was about demand sensing, and the speaker claimed a twenty percent drop in forecast error.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Twenty percent? That sounds high to me. In my experience, vendors tend to exaggerate.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I thought so too, at first. But she was a customer, not a vendor, and she showed the numbers.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Politely, I'd like to see the slides before I believe it. Can you send them?

script.speaker: A
script.line: I have them right here. Look at slide twelve: twenty percent, yes, but measured over six months at a single site, with a control group.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Okay, that's more convincing than a bare claim. Still, one site isn't the whole network.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Agreed. I'd call it promising, not proven. The third highlight is a contact, a planner who runs a similar pilot. She's happy to talk to you on Thursday.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Excellent. And the disappointment you mentioned?

script.speaker: A
script.line: The closing session on the nineteenth of March was cancelled, the one about sustainability. I had travelled a day early just for it.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's a shame. Send me her details, and I'll set up the call for Thursday.

questions.q: What did the slides show about the twenty percent result?
options: It came from one site over six months
It came from the whole network
It came from a vendor demonstration
It came from a one-week test
questions.explanation: Mark says the twenty percent was measured over six months at a single site, with a control group.

questions.q: Why was Katarina doubtful at first?
options: She did not attend the talk herself
She disliked the digital twins idea
She had already seen those slides
She believes vendors often exaggerate
questions.explanation: Katarina says that in her experience vendors exaggerate.

questions.q: What will Katarina do next?
options: Travel to the next conference in June
Arrange a Thursday call with the contact
Ask Mark to rebook the cancelled session
Test demand sensing at her own site
questions.explanation: She says she will set up the call for Thursday once Mark sends the details.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Chloe, hi, it's Raj. Is it a good moment? It's early over there, isn't it?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Hi Raj. Yes, it's just past seven, but go ahead. I'm listening.

script.speaker: A
script.line: It's about the internal audit on Tuesday. I'd like you to check that the training records and the equipment logs are up to date before then.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Okay. Honestly, I'm a bit nervous about it. Last time the auditor found gaps, and I took it personally.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Understandable, but that was a while ago and the process has improved. Let me help. I'll take the equipment logs myself, so you only deal with the training records.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That would take a weight off my shoulders. Thank you.

script.speaker: A
script.line: We should also agree who answers what. I suggest you take training and documentation, and I take equipment and deviations.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Fine. What about the batch file under B V twenty-four seventy-four? That one is more complicated.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Let me keep that one, and you can sit in. The auditor's session on it starts at a quarter past ten.

script.speaker: B
script.line: A quarter past ten, got it. I'll check the training records by Monday noon and tell you if anything is missing.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Perfect. Call me if you find something odd. Better to know now than on Tuesday.

questions.q: What are Raj and Chloe preparing for?
options: An internal audit
A supplier visit
A staff training session
A product launch
questions.explanation: Raj says the call is about the internal audit on Tuesday.

questions.q: When does the auditor's session on the batch file start?
options: At just past seven
On Monday at noon
At a quarter past ten
On Tuesday evening
questions.explanation: Raj says the auditor's session on it starts at a quarter past ten.

questions.q: What will Chloe do next?
options: Take over the equipment logs
Check the training records by Monday
Run the batch file session alone
Call the auditor to confirm the date
questions.explanation: Chloe says she will check the training records by Monday noon.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hugo, good to see you. I'll be upfront: we need an extra production slot next month, and I'm hoping you have some give in the schedule.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Always happy to help where I can, Marta. Let me pull up the plan. When would you need to start?

script.speaker: A
script.line: By the fifteenth of March at the latest, ideally.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Hmm, difficult. The line is booked until the twenty-fourth. No, sorry, I misread my sheet: the campaign finishes on the twenty-second, and the line is free then.

script.speaker: A
script.line: So the earliest start is the twenty-second. That's a week later than I wanted. Can it work?

script.speaker: B
script.line: It can, with conditions. We're running about thirty-five percent over our normal workload, so we'd want a firm order now, and a premium on the price.

script.speaker: A
script.line: A premium? How big are we talking?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Not huge, but you'd need approval on your side. And I should warn you: if you don't take this slot, the next free one is in eight weeks.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Understood. That makes the decision easier. I'll take it to my director this afternoon and confirm tomorrow.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Wonderful. I'll hold it until then, but not a day longer.

questions.q: What is the main topic of the meeting?
options: Cancelling an order for the next campaign
Moving production to another plant abroad
Reducing the price of the next batch
Booking a later slot, with conditions
questions.explanation: Hugo can offer a later slot if Marta gives a firm order and accepts a premium.

questions.q: When is the earliest start date for Marta's batch?
options: The fifteenth of March
The twenty-fourth of March
The twenty-second of March
In eight weeks
questions.explanation: Hugo corrects himself: the campaign finishes on the twenty-second and the line is free from then.

questions.q: What can we infer about the contract manufacturer's workload?
options: It is very busy at the moment
It has a lot of free capacity
It plans to close the line
It never changes its schedule
questions.explanation: Hugo says they're running thirty-five percent over normal and the next slot is in eight weeks.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Pedro, thanks for coming. I have to be direct: eighteen cartons from the last delivery arrived damaged, and my customers are already complaining.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I'm sorry to hear that, Chloe. Let me take down the details. Which delivery was it?

script.speaker: A
script.line: The one that arrived on Tuesday, order M K fifty-seven sixty-nine. The outer boxes were crushed on one side.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Thank you. May I ask whether the damage could have happened during unloading at your dock? Sometimes it does.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I don't think so. Our team checked the pallets as they came off the truck.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I'm not doubting your team, but I'd like to see the facts. Do you have the receiving photos?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Yes, time-stamped. Here, you can see the pallets still wrapped, with the damage visible on the truck bed.

script.speaker: B
script.line: You're right. The photos show it clearly, and the time stamp is before unloading. So the damage happened in transit, and it's on us.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Thank you for accepting that. What happens now?

script.speaker: B
script.line: We'll send replacement cartons. Normally it takes two weeks, but I'll ask for priority handling and promise you ten days. I'll email you the confirmation before I leave the site.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Ten days is acceptable. Thank you.

questions.q: How long will the replacement take?
options: Two weeks
One week
Until Tuesday
Ten days
questions.explanation: Pedro says normally it takes two weeks, but he promises ten days.

questions.q: How does Chloe sound at the start of the conversation?
options: Confused and quiet
Firm but polite
Cheerful and relaxed
Rude and angry
questions.explanation: She says she has to be direct, as her customers are already complaining.

questions.q: What will Pedro do before leaving?
options: Collect all the damaged cartons
Email Chloe a written confirmation
Call the carrier about the truck
Photograph the pallets once more
questions.explanation: He says he will email the confirmation before he leaves the site.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Morning, Marco. You look rested. Did you do anything over the weekend?

script.speaker: B
script.line: I did, actually. We drove up to the coast, to a small village I'd never been to. The weather was kind to us, which was a lucky break.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Lovely. I stayed home and caught up on sleep, which was exactly what I needed.

script.speaker: B
script.line: No shame in that. Anyway, we still have a few minutes before the others arrive. Did you see the numbers for the annual batch plan?

script.speaker: A
script.line: I did. Six hundred batches for the year, which is about twenty-five percent more than last year. It's a big jump.

script.speaker: B
script.line: It is. And the new line, G E seven three eight six, is supposed to absorb most of it. I'd like your honest view on that.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Honestly, I think it's ambitious. The new line hasn't been through a full year yet, and I'd prepare a plan B.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good, that's what I wanted to hear. Let's discuss it properly after this meeting. Shall we say my office, at three?

script.speaker: A
script.line: I'm afraid I'm at the supplier site until four. Could we do half past four?

script.speaker: B
script.line: I have a call then. What about the small meeting room on the second floor, at five?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Five in the small meeting room works for me.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Right, here come the others. Let's get started.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Fine. I'll bring the numbers for the new line, printed out.

questions.q: What happens in the conversation overall?
options: Two colleagues plan a holiday together
A manager criticises a colleague's plan
They cancel the batch plan for the year
A chat turns into work talk and a plan
questions.explanation: They talk about the weekend, then the batch plan, and arrange a later meeting.

questions.q: What does Ingrid think of the plan for the new line?
options: It is ambitious and needs a backup
It is too cautious for such a line
It is perfect and needs no changes
It is already finished and running
questions.explanation: She says it's ambitious and she would prepare a plan B.

questions.q: Where and when will they continue the discussion?
options: In Marco's office at three
In Marco's office at half past four
In the small meeting room at five
At the supplier site at four
questions.explanation: After two changes, they agree on the small meeting room on the second floor at five.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Morning, Raj. Let's go through what's still open for the close. I count two late goods receipts and some unconfirmed purchase orders.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Same on my side. Which receipts are late?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Both are from the same carrier. The first is under B H twenty-one seventy-four. The truck was unloaded on the twenty-ninth of April, but nobody posted it.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's the one the warehouse flagged to me. I'll chase the warehouse team to post it today.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Thanks. For the second receipt, we still can't find the paperwork.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Hmm. Maybe the driver took it back. I'll ask the carrier for a copy, and I should have it by lunchtime tomorrow.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good. Now the purchase orders. There are seven without confirmation from the supplier, and the system closes for the month at half past four today.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Half past four today? I thought it closed tomorrow.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Today, for purchase orders. Receipts have until tomorrow noon.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Okay, that changes my priorities. I'll call the suppliers on the five largest orders first.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Sensible. I'll send you the list sorted by value, so you can start straight away.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Thanks. One more thing, actually. The list I received yesterday seems to be missing a column, the supplier contact name.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Ah, I see. That's an export issue. I'll fix it and resend within the hour.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Perfect. Then let's speak again at noon to see where we stand.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of the call?
options: To agree who chases open items
To close the supplier contract early
To train a new planner on closing
To review the carrier's prices
questions.explanation: They list late receipts and unconfirmed orders and decide who chases each.

questions.q: When does the system close for purchase orders?
options: At noon tomorrow
At lunchtime tomorrow
At half past four today
Within the hour
questions.explanation: Mei says the system closes for the month at half past four today for purchase orders.

questions.q: What does Raj's reaction "I thought it closed tomorrow" suggest?
options: He wants to change the deadline
The earlier deadline is news to him
He already ordered everything
He does not trust Mei
questions.explanation: He expected tomorrow, and says that changes his priorities.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Victor here, thanks for calling back, Fatima. I've got about ten minutes before my next meeting, so let's make them count.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Thanks, Victor. It's about the advanced demand sensing course. It starts on the seventeenth of May, and I need to confirm my place by the end of this week.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Right, and my first question is the obvious one. Why this course, and why now? We're stretched thin as it is.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Fair challenge. Last month I spent two days fixing eighty order lines by hand because our model misread a promotion. This course covers exactly that failure.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hm, that's an anecdote, not a business case. What does it cost, and how many days would you be out?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Twelve hundred euros, plus three days out of the office spread over two weeks.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Three days during quarter close is a hard sell, to be blunt. And finance hinted that training money might be frozen, though I've seen nothing in writing.

script.speaker: B
script.line: So who can confirm that? I'd rather not wait until the place is gone.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Lena in finance has the final say, and she's travelling until Thursday. Until I hear from her, I can't say yes or no.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I understand, though it's a bit frustrating. I did the groundwork weeks ago. Could you get an answer by Friday at the latest?

script.speaker: A
script.line: I'll chase her first thing on Thursday and call you on Friday morning, whatever she says. Meanwhile, send me a one-page note on the benefits.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Will do, I'll have it with you tonight. Thanks for being straight with me, Victor.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of the call?
options: Victor gives Fatima feedback on her forecast work
Fatima announces that she wants to leave the team
Fatima asks for approval of a course, but Victor cannot decide yet
Victor tells Fatima that the course has been cancelled
questions.explanation: Fatima asks Victor to approve the course, and he says he cannot say yes or no until he hears from Lena.

questions.q: When has Victor promised to give Fatima his answer?
options: On Thursday, when Lena returns
On the seventeenth of May
On Friday morning
Tonight, with the benefits note
questions.explanation: Victor says, 'I'll chase her first thing on Thursday and call you on Friday morning, whatever she says.'

questions.q: How does Fatima feel about the delay?
options: Relieved that she has more time to think
Completely indifferent to the outcome
Angry enough to stop cooperating
Somewhat frustrated, but willing to accept it
questions.explanation: She says 'it's a bit frustrating' but then agrees to send the benefits note and thanks Victor.

questions.q: What does Victor's attitude suggest about the course?
options: He thinks the course is a complete waste of time
He is not against it, but he needs stronger arguments and approval
He has already promised the money to someone else
He wants a different employee to take the course
questions.explanation: He asks for a business case and a benefits note and says the decision depends on Lena, so he is open but cautious.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good morning, Omar. I'm sorry to start with a problem, but Daniel is sick today and we need to cover his work.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Oh no, I hope he feels better soon. What do you need me to do?

script.speaker: A
script.line: He has two supplier calls, one at ten and one at two, and a report to finish. It covers one hundred and twenty open tickets from the last twelve weeks.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's a lot. I'm sorry, but I have a clash. I have the planning review at two, so I can't take the second call.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I see. I'm a bit stressed too, because the report is due at half past four and I have meetings all afternoon.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Please don't worry, Priya. We can solve this. I can't do the two o'clock call, but I can write the report.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Really? That would help a lot. Can you finish it before half past four?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, I'll send it by four. I only need the ticket list from Daniel's folder.

script.speaker: A
script.line: It is on the shared drive, in the folder called Weekly. I will take the ten o'clock call myself.

script.speaker: B
script.line: And the call at two? Should I ask the supplier to move it?

script.speaker: A
script.line: No, I'll write to them. I'll ask for tomorrow morning instead. Thank you, Omar. I really appreciate this.

script.speaker: B
script.line: No problem. If you need more help, just tell me.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I will. One more thing: please check the tickets that have no owner. There are some from last week.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Sure. I'll start now and message you when the report is ready.

questions.q: What are Priya and Omar mostly talking about?
options: Who will do Daniel's work while he is sick
How to fix a problem with a supplier
When to hold the planning review
How to find a new person for the team
questions.explanation: Priya says Daniel is sick and they need to cover his work, and then they share the tasks.

questions.q: When is the report due?
options: At four o'clock
At half past four
At ten o'clock
At two o'clock
questions.explanation: Priya says the report is due at half past four; Omar only says he will send it by four.

questions.q: What will Priya do about the call at two?
options: Take the two o'clock call herself after her meetings
Ask Omar to join the call a bit late
Ask the supplier to move it to tomorrow morning
Cancel the supplier meeting for good this week
questions.explanation: Priya says, 'I'll write to them. I'll ask for tomorrow morning instead.'

questions.q: Why does Omar say, 'Please don't worry, Priya. We can solve this.'?
options: To refuse to do any of the work
To give Priya an order
To ask for more time
To calm Priya and offer to help
questions.explanation: Priya sounds stressed, and Omar answers by calming her and then offering to write the report.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Thanks for coming, Lucia. I have the error list from the new tool, and honestly it's longer than I expected. About twenty percent of the item records have problems.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Twenty percent is a lot. What kind of errors are they? I'm worried that my team will have to fix everything by hand.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Mostly missing units and old supplier codes. The cleanup plan I have in mind takes ten weeks, and we would start on Monday at nine.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Ten weeks is too long for us. Go-live is in the spring, and we also have the year-end close. Can we make it shorter?

script.speaker: A
script.line: I know, I'm not happy with it either. But wait, I just got a message from the vendor. They say their tool can fix the missing units automatically.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's great news! How many of the errors is that?

script.speaker: A
script.line: About half of them, I think. So the plan could go down to six weeks, but I need to check this before I promise anything.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good idea. Let's keep nine o'clock on Monday, and I'll ask my team to start with the supplier codes.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Perfect. I'll send you the vendor's answer by tomorrow, and then we decide.

questions.q: What are Hugo and Lucia mainly discussing?
options: How to fix errors in the item data
How to choose a new software vendor
Who will lead the year-end close
Why the go-live moved to spring
questions.explanation: They review the error list from the new tool and talk about a cleanup plan.

questions.q: How long was the first cleanup plan?
options: Six weeks
Nine weeks
Twenty weeks
Ten weeks
questions.explanation: Hugo says the cleanup plan he has in mind takes ten weeks; six weeks is only the possible new plan.

questions.q: How does Lucia feel when she first hears about the errors?
options: Worried about the work for her team
Excited about the new tool
Angry with Hugo
Bored by the details
questions.explanation: She says 'I'm worried that my team will have to fix everything by hand.'

questions.q: What can we infer about the six-week plan?
options: Lucia has already approved it for the team
It depends on what the vendor confirms about the tool
The go-live will move to the summer instead
It leaves out the supplier codes completely
questions.explanation: Hugo says he needs to check before he promises anything, so the shorter plan is still uncertain.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hi Mark, it's Emma. Welcome back, or almost! I wanted to give you a quick update, because six weeks away is long enough for things to change.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Hi Emma, thanks. Please do. I heard there was a reorganisation, and I'm a bit lost about who reports to whom.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Yes, planning now sits under Daniela. We also moved to a new forecasting tool, so request a login. The priority for November is the safety stock review.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good to know. Could we go through the tool together? My first day is Thursday, the twenty-second of November, so maybe at ten that morning?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Ten is difficult for me, I have a supplier review. How about eleven? We can do it by video, since you're abroad.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Eleven could be a problem too, because my laptop access probably won't be ready until after lunch. Shall we say two in the afternoon?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Two works. Then I'll book a room with a big screen and send you the invitation, and I'll ask Daniela to join for the first ten minutes.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Great, thanks Emma. See you on Thursday then.

questions.q: What time do they finally agree to meet on Thursday?
options: At ten in the morning
At eleven in the morning
At two in the afternoon
At lunchtime
questions.explanation: Mark suggests two in the afternoon and Emma says, 'Two works.'

questions.q: Why does Mark say eleven could be a problem?
options: He will still be on leave until the afternoon
His laptop access will probably not be ready until after lunch
He has a supplier review at that time
Daniela cannot join at that time
questions.explanation: Mark says his laptop access probably won't be ready until after lunch; the supplier review is Emma's reason for ten.

questions.q: What will Emma do after the call?
options: Book a room and send an invitation
Request a new login on Mark's behalf
Move her supplier review to Thursday
Fly to Mark's office before Thursday
questions.explanation: Emma says she will book a room with a big screen and send Mark the invitation.

script.speaker: A
script.line: We have ten minutes before the next meeting, so let's sketch your first thirty days on the walk. What worries you most?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Honestly, learning who's who. I know the planning team, but I haven't met anyone in quality or the warehouse.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Then that's step one. I'll set up introductions with the QA lead and the warehouse supervisor, and send the invitations on Tuesday.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Great. And reading? I've got a stack of process documents, but I don't know where to begin.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Skip most of them. Start with the last two S and OP packs and the service level report. On-time delivery dipped twelve percent in the south last quarter.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Understood. Is that the problem you want me to look at, then?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Partly. For your first project, I'd like you to own something small: why about six hundred orders shipped late last month.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Six hundred is bigger than small, though. Could I focus on one customer group first?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Fair. Pick the group with the most delays, and we'll agree the scope together. I don't want you buried in week two.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Thanks. In that case I'll read the two packs first and then draft the scope.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good. To recap: I send introductions on Tuesday, you read the two packs by Friday, and you send me the draft scope the Wednesday after.

script.speaker: B
script.line: And I'll bring my first questions to our check-in, so you can tell me if I'm heading the wrong way.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Please do. Don't be afraid to ask the obvious questions. They're often the ones nobody has asked in years.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Noted. That's actually a relief to hear.

questions.q: When will Ethan send the introduction invitations?
options: On Tuesday
On Friday
On the Wednesday after next
At the end of the first month
questions.explanation: Ethan says, 'I'll send the invitations on Tuesday'; Friday is Camila's reading deadline.

questions.q: Why does Camila ask to focus on one customer group?
options: She wants to avoid meeting the quality team yet
Six hundred late orders seem too many for a first project
The service level report was missing from the packs
Ethan asked her to shorten the reading list
questions.explanation: She says six hundred is bigger than small, so she wants a narrower scope.

questions.q: What does Ethan imply when he talks about obvious questions?
options: Camila already asks too many questions at work
The team does not really welcome newcomers
Some old assumptions may never have been checked
The process documents are all badly out of date
questions.explanation: He says obvious questions are 'often the ones nobody has asked in years', so old assumptions go unchecked.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hi Samuel, it's Camila from the Madrid team. I'm your buddy for the first few weeks, so I thought I'd call and see how day one is going.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Hi Camila, that's kind of you. It's going fine, though I'm still waiting for access to the planning system, and nobody has told me what the week looks like.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Classic. Access usually lands around two in the afternoon. The week is simple: Monday is demand review, Wednesday is supply, and Friday is clean-up and our team lunch.

script.speaker: B
script.line: What's the Monday review like? Is it a big, formal affair?

script.speaker: A
script.line: About ten people, very informal. We mostly look at where actuals missed the forecast by more than twelve percent. You won't be asked to speak this week.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's a relief. What about tools? Do I need to install anything before I get in?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Just the planning platform and the chat app. I'll send the links and a one-page cheat sheet, so you won't have to hunt through the wiki.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Brilliant. By the way, who's organising the Friday lunch?

script.speaker: A
script.line: I am, this week. We're going to the Thai place near the office. Everybody comes on a Friday, so you're very welcome.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Thanks, that's thoughtful. I'll pass this time, though. Peanuts and I don't get on, and I'd rather not spend my first week at the pharmacy. Coffee afterwards?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Oh, of course, no problem at all. We'll pick somewhere safer next time. Coffee it is.

questions.q: When does access to the planning system usually arrive?
options: Around two in the afternoon
On Monday morning
After the Friday lunch
At the end of the week
questions.explanation: Camila says access requests 'usually land around two in the afternoon'.

questions.q: What will Camila send to Samuel?
options: A copy of the Monday forecast
Links to the tools and a one-page cheat sheet
The menu for the Friday lunch
His login for the planning platform
questions.explanation: She says, 'I'll send you the links and a one-page cheat sheet.'

questions.q: Why does Samuel say, 'Peanuts and I don't get on at all'?
options: To criticise Camila's choice of restaurant
To say he is too busy to eat
To ask for a different day
To politely decline the lunch by hinting at a food problem
questions.explanation: He says it right before he says he will pass on the lunch and join for coffee, so he is hinting at an allergy.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of the call?
options: Samuel asks Camila to change his team
Camila helps Samuel settle in on his first day
Camila reports a problem with the planning system
They plan the Monday demand review
questions.explanation: Camila calls as his buddy to see how day one is going and explains the week, tools and lunch.

title: A pallet with the wrong label

script.speaker: A
script.line: Elena, thanks for coming down so quickly. I wanted you to see this before anything gets loaded. The batch number on the outer cartons doesn't match the pallet sheet.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Show me. Right, the cartons end in forty-seven and the sheet says forty-nine. How many cartons are affected?

script.speaker: A
script.line: We counted one hundred and twenty cartons, all from the same run. My team spotted it at the end of the shift, so nothing has left.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good. First step is to quarantine it. I'll put a hold on the pallet in the system and ask QA to tag it physically.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Understood. I'll move it to the cage next to the dock, so nobody picks it by mistake.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Now, the rework. The customer order is due out in four weeks, so we have time, but not forever. How soon can you relabel it?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Our relabelling line is booked solid until the end of next week, I'm afraid. I could squeeze you in after that.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That still meets the deadline, but I'd like it sooner, because QA has to re-inspect afterwards.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Actually, hang on. The other job on that line was cancelled this morning. The customer pulled it. So the line is free from Monday.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Well, that's good news. Monday, then. Can your team start at seven and finish by lunchtime?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Should be doable. Four people, a couple of hours. We'll need the correct batch data to print fresh labels, though.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I'll send it this afternoon, and I'll ask QA to witness the relabelling and release the pallet once it's checked.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Perfect. I'll tell my supervisor and we'll keep you updated.

questions.q: When will the relabelling start?
options: At the end of next week
This afternoon
On Monday
In four weeks
questions.explanation: Andrew says the line is free from Monday; the end of next week was the original slot.

questions.q: Why can the relabelling happen earlier than first expected?
options: Another job on the line was cancelled by its customer
QA agreed to skip the re-inspection
The pallet turned out to have fewer cartons
Extra staff arrived at the site
questions.explanation: Andrew says the other job on the line was cancelled because the customer pulled it.

questions.q: What will Elena do this afternoon?
options: Relabel the pallet herself
Move the pallet to the cage
Tag the pallet for QA
Send Andrew the correct batch data
questions.explanation: She says, 'I'll send it to you this afternoon'; moving the pallet is Andrew's task.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Ben, do you have a minute? I've just come back from the Nordic accounts, and I think we're underforecasting winter demand by quite a lot.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Sure, take a seat. What are you seeing, and more importantly, what's the evidence? I can't move numbers on a feeling.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Two things. The biggest wholesaler wants four weeks of extra cover before a winter promotion, and a health group is about to tender. I'd add a quarter.

script.speaker: B
script.line: When would the extra volume start? And what's the risk if the tender doesn't come through? I'd be building stock for nothing.

script.speaker: A
script.line: The wholesaler's cover starts from week forty-eight. The tender result is due on the twenty-fourth of November, so that part is uncertain. I'd say the odds are about sixty percent.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Then here's what I can do. I'll add the wholesaler's volume now, because it's confirmed in writing, but keep the tender volume as a scenario until we know.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's less than I hoped, to be honest. Is there any way to protect some stock for the tender case?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Possibly. I can ask production to hold a two-week slot open without committing materials. Let's meet at quarter past ten on the twenty-fourth to decide.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That works. I'll send you the wholesaler's email today, so you have it for the file.

questions.q: What does the wholesaler want before its winter promotion?
options: Four weeks of extra stock cover
A two-week production slot kept open
A written guarantee on the tender result
A lower price on the baseline volume
questions.explanation: Ingrid says the biggest wholesaler wants 'four weeks of extra cover before their winter promotion'.

questions.q: Why does Ben refuse to add the tender volume now?
options: The wholesaler asked him to wait until winter
Production has no free slots in the next month
He thinks the Nordic market is getting smaller
It is unconfirmed, and he could build unused stock
questions.explanation: Ben says the wholesaler's volume is confirmed in writing, while the tender is uncertain and he'd be building stock for nothing.

questions.q: What will Ben and Ingrid do on the twenty-fourth of November?
options: Send the wholesaler's email to Ben for the file
Visit the Nordic accounts together in person
Meet at quarter past ten to decide on the tender
Start the two-week production run for the tender
questions.explanation: Ben proposes to 'meet at quarter past ten on the twenty-fourth to decide'.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Amara, got two minutes while we walk? I'd rather you hear this from me now than see it in a report on Friday.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Of course. That sounds ominous. What is it?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Our projection shows we'll run out of the main pack in about six weeks. We're short by roughly twenty-five hundred cartons for the end of the quarter.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Six weeks? That's right in the middle of the tender deliveries. Why wasn't this flagged earlier?

script.speaker: A
script.line: The forecast moved after the big order from the north came in last week. Fair question, but we still have time if we decide this week.

script.speaker: B
script.line: This week... I have the board pack due, two customers shouting about delays, and now this. I honestly don't know how I'm going to fit it in.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Understood, and it's manageable. You don't have to solve it alone. Either the plant adds a production run, or we pause smaller accounts. I'll lay out both options with costs.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That would really help. If I have something concrete, I can take it to the director.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I'll write it up myself. I'll send you a one-page comparison on Tuesday at quarter to four, so we can decide before you see him on Wednesday.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Thank you, Tomas. That takes a weight off. I'll keep Tuesday afternoon clear so we can go through it.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good. And Amara, try not to worry. Six weeks is plenty of time as long as we start now.

questions.q: When will Tomas send the comparison of the options?
options: On Friday, in the report
On Tuesday at quarter to four
On Wednesday, before the director meeting
In six weeks
questions.explanation: Tomas says, 'I'll send you a one-page comparison on Tuesday at quarter to four.'

questions.q: What will Amara do on Tuesday afternoon?
options: Ask the plant for a production run
Keep time free to go through the options with Tomas
Pause the smaller accounts
Write the board pack with the director
questions.explanation: She says she will keep Tuesday afternoon clear to go through the comparison.

questions.q: Why does Tomas say, 'it's manageable'?
options: To ask for more time
To complain about his workload
To reassure Amara
To change the subject
questions.explanation: Amara sounds overwhelmed, and Tomas answers that it's manageable and she doesn't have to solve it alone.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of Tomas's conversation with Amara?
options: To report a mistake in the board pack figures
To ask her for a bigger budget this quarter
To tell her that the tender had been lost
To warn her about a shortage and offer a plan
questions.explanation: He warns of a stockout in about six weeks and offers to prepare options for a decision this week.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Morning, Mateo. Here's your new laptop, all set up. Before you take it, let me walk you through what happens to your data, because some of it won't carry over.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Please do. I've got a lot on the old one, mostly spreadsheets and a few local databases, and I'd hate to lose any of it.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Everything in documents and on the desktop migrates automatically. We don't copy local databases or the downloads folder. That's policy, I'm afraid, because we can't verify what's in them.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Those databases are the problem. They're planning models I haven't uploaded to the shared drive. Can't you make an exception?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Not me, no, but you can move them to the shared drive today, and then they're safe. Once the old laptop is wiped, there's no way back.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Understood. When does the wipe happen?

script.speaker: A
script.line: When you return the old one. It has to be back with us by the third of September, otherwise your account gets flagged. We scan and wipe it that week.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Fine. I'll bring it back in time. And is there anything I need to do tomorrow to start using the new one?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Yes, a short session to set up your authentication app. It's at quarter past ten in the IT room, so please bring your phone.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Quarter past ten, phone, got it. So I move the databases today, return the old laptop by the third, and you confirm once it's wiped.

questions.q: What will NOT be copied to the new laptop automatically?
options: Local databases and the downloads folder
Files in the documents folder
Spreadsheets on the desktop
Files on the shared drive
questions.explanation: Amara says documents and desktop are migrated, but local databases and downloads are not copied.

questions.q: Why can't Amara make an exception for the databases?
options: The new laptop has too little space
It is company policy
The shared drive is full
Mateo's account is flagged
questions.explanation: She says, 'That's policy, I'm afraid,' because they can't verify what's in them.

questions.q: What can we infer about the databases?
options: IT will copy them over to the laptop overnight
Mateo could lose them if he does not move them
They are already safe on the shared drive
They are too large for the new laptop to hold
questions.explanation: They aren't on the shared drive, they won't be copied, and 'once the old laptop is wiped, there's no way back'.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good morning, Marta. Thank you for seeing me. I understand the pallets we delivered on Monday are still on hold, and I'd like to understand why.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good morning, Pedro. Yes, the certificate of analysis wasn't in the paperwork. Without it, we can't release the goods into stock, whatever the delivery note says.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I do appreciate that, but the batch passed our tests last week. Could you release it provisionally? Your production team is waiting, as I understand it.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I'm afraid that's not possible. It's a regulatory requirement. I can keep the goods in a separate area so nothing gets mixed up.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Fair enough. Then what would you need from me, and by when?

script.speaker: B
script.line: The signed certificate for this batch, by email, before noon. QA normally reviews documents on Wednesday, but if it arrives in time, they will look at it this afternoon.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Noon is tight, since the lab is in another city. Could we say two o'clock? I'll call them as soon as I leave this room.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Two o'clock, then. I'll ask QA to keep the afternoon open. In return, I must record the delivery as incomplete in your supplier score, twelve percent of your rating.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's acceptable, though I'm not happy about the score. I'll get the certificate to you by two and call to confirm.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Thank you. Please send it to my direct address, and I'll let QA know to expect it.

questions.q: What is the main outcome of the conversation?
options: Marta agrees to release the goods without the certificate
Pedro agrees to take the pallets back
They decide to cancel the contract
They agree how to get the missing certificate so the goods can be released
questions.explanation: Marta explains why the goods are on hold and they agree a deadline for the certificate and a same-day review.

questions.q: By what time will Pedro send the certificate?
options: By two o'clock
By noon
By Monday
By Wednesday
questions.explanation: Marta first asks for noon, and Pedro negotiates it to two o'clock.

questions.q: What will Marta do next?
options: Release the pallets provisionally
Call the lab in the other city
Tell QA to expect the certificate
Send the supplier score to Pedro
questions.explanation: She says, 'I'll let QA know to expect it.'

questions.q: Why does Marta say, 'I'm afraid that's not possible'?
options: To say she cannot hear Pedro on the line
To complain about the delivery date change
To ask Pedro to wait outside the office
To politely refuse Pedro's request for a provisional release
questions.explanation: She says it right after Pedro asks to release the batch provisionally.

title: When will the batch be released

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good morning, Jon. I know you want a date for the batch, so let me tell you where we are before you ask.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Thanks, Elena. That would help a lot. Sales keep asking me, and I'd like to give them a realistic answer.

script.speaker: A
script.line: The lab results are in and they look fine. Two checks remain: the stability data review and the final document check. Realistically, the document check is where we could slip.

script.speaker: B
script.line: What's the gap? Is something missing from the batch record?

script.speaker: A
script.line: One signature page from the filling line is missing, and the operator who signed is on leave until Monday. Until it's replaced, I can't close the record.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Understood. So if the page turns up on Monday, when could you release?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Tuesday at nine in the morning, if the page is fine. I wouldn't promise Monday, because the review takes a full day.

script.speaker: B
script.line: In that case, could you release forty percent of the batch now, the part from the first pallets, so sales can ship something this week?

script.speaker: A
script.line: I'm sorry, but I can't. Release is per batch, not per pallet, and splitting it would break our procedure. I'll message you the moment the page arrives.

questions.q: What is missing from the batch record?
options: A signature page from the filling line
The stability data review for the batch
The lab results from the quality team
The pallet numbers for the first pallets
questions.explanation: Elena says one signature page from the filling line is missing.

questions.q: What will Elena do when the missing page arrives?
options: Release forty percent of the batch
Call the operator on leave
Message Jon straight away
Repeat the lab tests
questions.explanation: She ends by saying, 'I'll message you the moment the page arrives.'

questions.q: Why does Elena say, 'I'm sorry, but I can't'?
options: To say that the lab results are not correct
To politely refuse to release part of the batch
To cancel the meeting with Jon today
To ask Jon for the missing signature page
questions.explanation: She says it after Jon asks to release forty percent of the batch, and explains that release is per batch.

questions.q: What is the main point of the conversation?
options: Jon reports a problem with the lab equipment
Elena asks Jon to cancel a customer order
Elena explains the remaining checks and a possible delay
They plan a meeting with the sales team
questions.explanation: She lists two remaining checks and warns about the missing signature page.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good afternoon, Olivia, it's Mark from planning. Thank you for taking my call. I'd like to sort out our deliveries around the holiday next week.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good afternoon, Mark. Yes, I was about to ring you. The holiday throws everything off. What are you looking at?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Ideally, the temperature-controlled order, about one hundred and twenty kilograms, would reach the customer before the holiday. That means Thursday at the latest.

script.speaker: B
