script.line: Thursday is going to be tough. Our volumes ahead of a holiday run about eighteen percent higher than normal, and the drivers are already stretched.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I understand. What about Friday morning, then, before the customer closes at noon? I know it's the last working day, but it's a small load.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Friday morning could work, but I'd need to check with Gareth at the depot, who plans the routes. He's out until tomorrow, so I can't confirm.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Right. Can we at least agree a fallback? If Friday doesn't work, what's the first date after the holiday?

script.speaker: B
script.line: The Tuesday after is realistic, but Gareth has the final word, because it depends on how many drivers are back.

script.speaker: A
script.line: So for now we have a provisional Friday morning window and a backup on the Tuesday. I'd like to confirm one or the other by tomorrow.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's fair. I'll speak to Gareth first thing in the morning and ring you by lunchtime.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Lunchtime is fine. I'll warn the customer in the meantime, so they can plan to receive it.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, please do, and tell them we'll confirm the exact slot as soon as we can.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Will do. Thanks, Olivia. Speak tomorrow.

questions.q: What are Mark and Olivia trying to do?
options: Plan a delivery before the holiday, with a backup date
Cancel the order because of the holiday
Raise the order by eighteen percent for a promotion
Choose a new carrier for the depot's routes
questions.explanation: They agree a provisional Friday window and a Tuesday backup, but Gareth must confirm.

questions.q: Which delivery slot is provisionally agreed?
options: Thursday
Friday morning
The Tuesday after the holiday
Friday afternoon
questions.explanation: Mark says they have 'a provisional Friday morning window and a backup on the Tuesday'.

questions.q: Why can't Olivia confirm the Friday delivery now?
options: The customer closes before noon on Friday
The order is too heavy for her trucks
She has not yet spoken to her drivers
Gareth, who plans the routes, is away until tomorrow
questions.explanation: She says Gareth plans the routes, is away until tomorrow, and she can't confirm without him.

questions.q: What will Olivia do first thing tomorrow morning?
options: Warn the customer about the delay
Add more drivers to the Thursday route
Send Mark a list of backup dates
Speak to Gareth and call Mark by lunchtime
questions.explanation: She says, 'I'll speak to Gareth first thing in the morning and ring you by lunchtime.'

title: Jet lag and a new layout

script.speaker: A
script.line: Adam, good to see you in person at last. How was the flight in? You must be exhausted with the time difference.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Not bad, thanks. I live six hours behind, so my body thinks it's the middle of the night, but coffee helps. And this weather! It was boiling when I left.

script.speaker: A
script.line: It's grey and drizzly here most of autumn, I'm afraid. At least the new office is warm. Have you seen the layout? It's open plan, on the third floor.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Only on paper. I'm a bit nervous, honestly. Could I have a desk near a window, away from the printers? I take early calls with the other time zone.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I like the thinking, but the window desks are all taken. Only about twenty percent of the floor has windows. I can offer a desk by the phone booths.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's a reasonable alternative. How far are the booths from the planning team?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Just across the corridor. And the whole team will be in on Friday for the move, so you can pick your exact spot then.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Fine. Before Friday I also want to finish checking the eighty batches in the tracker, so I'll probably work from a meeting room until then.

script.speaker: A
script.line: No problem. I'll book the small meeting room for you for the whole week. Would you like a second screen?

script.speaker: B
script.line: That would be very kind, thank you. Shall we head to the call? It's almost time.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Yes, let's go. We can look at the layout again afterwards.

questions.q: What are Katarina and Adam mainly talking about?
options: Travel, weather and the new desk arrangements
A problem with a delayed flight
How to plan the eighty batches
A complaint about the noisy printers
questions.explanation: They chat about the flight, the weather and the time zones, and then agree a desk and a room.

questions.q: How many batches does Adam still need to check before Friday?
options: Twenty
Eighty
Six
Three
questions.explanation: Adam says he wants to finish checking the eighty batches in the tracker.

questions.q: What will Katarina do for Adam?
options: Move him to a desk by the window
Order a new laptop for him this week
Book a meeting room for him for the week
Change the date of the office move
questions.explanation: She says, 'I'll book the small meeting room for you for the whole week.'

questions.q: Why does Katarina say, 'I like the thinking, but the window desks are all taken'?
options: To thank Adam for advice on the layout
To say that the desks by the printers are free
To politely refuse the request and offer an alternative
To ask Adam to move to another floor
questions.explanation: She sounds positive but refuses the window desk and then offers a desk by the phone booths.

title: Waiting for the meeting to open

script.speaker: A
script.line: Still nothing. It's already ten fifteen and the host hasn't let us in. Is it just me, or has the speaker in this room stopped working again?

script.speaker: B
script.line: It's not just you. I tested it yesterday and the sound cut out after a minute. Facilities say thirty-five percent of the rooms on this floor have the same fault.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Wonderful. And Priyanka? She said she'd join from the hotel, but with her connection I can't see her getting in before half past.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Hang on, I've just had a message. The host says the meeting is pushed to twelve, because the regional team overran. So we have nearly two hours to ourselves.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's actually good news. Then I can finish the report I've been avoiding. Could we fix the sound first, though, with a portable speaker?

script.speaker: B
script.line: I'll borrow one from the third floor. And what about lunch? If we go now, we'd be back before twelve.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I'd rather eat after, to be honest. I'm in the middle of something. Why don't we have lunch together once the call is over?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Fine by me. I'll get the speaker, you open the report, and we'll meet back here at quarter to twelve.

questions.q: What time will the meeting now start?
options: At twelve
At ten fifteen
At half past ten
At quarter to twelve
questions.explanation: Ethan says the host pushed the meeting to twelve; ten fifteen was the original time.

questions.q: Why has the meeting been delayed?
options: The host has a sound problem
Priyanka's connection failed
Facilities are replacing the room's speaker
The regional team's meeting ran over
questions.explanation: The host says the meeting is pushed 'because the regional team overran'.

questions.q: What will Ethan do next?
options: Phone Priyanka at her hotel to check
Get a portable speaker from the third floor
Go out to lunch with Nora right away
Write the report that Nora has avoided
questions.explanation: He says, 'I'll borrow one from the third floor.'

questions.q: What is the main topic of the conversation?
options: A complaint about the host's behaviour
A plan to move to a different building
A discussion about a new report format
A broken speaker and a meeting that starts late
questions.explanation: They talk about the broken speaker, a late participant and lunch, then learn the meeting is delayed.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hi Hugo, it's Mei. Do you have five minutes? I'd like you to take a supplier issue to their director.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Sure. Tell me the facts first. What is the problem, and how long has it lasted?

script.speaker: A
script.line: The packaging supplier hasn't delivered the film we ordered. It was due three weeks ago, and they keep saying next week. I've emailed them four times.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Hmm. Three weeks is long, but I think it's too early to go over their heads. Let's give the account manager one more week.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I see it differently. I checked the data this morning. Last month they were late on every order, and the delay is getting longer each time.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Can you send me those numbers? If it's every order, that changes things. What is the impact on us?

script.speaker: A
script.line: If the film doesn't arrive by next Monday, line three will stop, and we will miss orders for two customers.

script.speaker: B
script.line: OK, you've convinced me. I'll call their director tomorrow morning. Please send me the data and a short summary today.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Great, I'll do it right away. Thanks, Hugo.

questions.q: What does Mei ask Hugo to do?
options: Take a late delivery to the supplier's director
Find a new packaging supplier quickly
Stop line three until the film arrives
Email the account manager for a fifth time
questions.explanation: She says, 'I'd like you to take a supplier issue to their director.'

questions.q: How late is the film delivery?
options: Four weeks
Three weeks
One week
Two weeks
questions.explanation: Mei says it was due three weeks ago; four is the number of emails and one week is Hugo's first suggestion.

questions.q: Why does Hugo change his mind?
options: Mei has emailed the account manager four times
Two customers have already complained
The data shows the supplier was late on every order last month
The director called him first
questions.explanation: After Mei explains the data, he says, 'If it's every order, that changes things.'

questions.q: What will Hugo do tomorrow morning?
options: Send the data to the account manager
Stop line three
Write a summary for Mei
Call the supplier's director
questions.explanation: He says, 'I'll call their director tomorrow morning.'

script.speaker: A
script.line: Thanks for staying on, Kenji. Let me quickly recap before we hang up. First, we raise the safety stock for the two main products by twenty-five percent.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Sorry, I'm not sure I follow. Do you mean we set safety stock at twenty-five percent of demand, or twenty-five percent higher than now?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Twenty-five percent higher than now. So if we hold four hundred units today, we move to five hundred. Sorry, I should have been clearer.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Thanks, that makes sense now. Please go on.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Second, the supplier pilot runs for ten weeks, and Peter owns it. Third, the plant review call is on Wednesday at ten fifteen. I'll send the invitation.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Small correction: the plant review is on Thursday, not Wednesday. The plant manager is travelling on Wednesday, so Thursday at ten fifteen is the only slot.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good catch, thank you. I'll fix it in the notes. Anything else?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, one thing is missing. Somebody needs to tell the warehouse about the extra stock, because they'll need space for it.

script.speaker: A
script.line: You're right, I forgot that. Can you do it, since you know the warehouse team?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, I'll email them tomorrow. Then I think we're done. Thanks, Chloe.

questions.q: What did Kenji correct in Chloe's recap?
options: The length of the supplier pilot
The day of the plant review call
The size of the safety stock increase
The person who owns the pilot
questions.explanation: Kenji says the plant review is on Thursday, not Wednesday.

questions.q: Why is the plant review on Thursday?
options: The plant manager is travelling on Wednesday
Chloe has a meeting on Wednesday
The warehouse needs more time
Peter is on leave on Wednesday
questions.explanation: Kenji says the plant manager is travelling on Wednesday, so Thursday is the only slot.

questions.q: What will Kenji do tomorrow?
options: Send the invitation for the plant review
Start the supplier pilot
Email the warehouse about the extra stock
Change the notes of the meeting
questions.explanation: He says, 'I'll email them tomorrow,' about telling the warehouse team.

title: Weekly check-in and a priority call

script.speaker: A
script.line: Come in, Henrik. Let's start with the good news. How are the three tasks going?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Mostly well. The forecast cleanup is done, and accuracy on the top products is up three percent. Actually, let me check my notes. It's five percent, three was last month.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Five percent is a real improvement, nice work. And the others?

script.speaker: B
script.line: The supplier scorecard is about two thirds finished. I'm waiting for data from procurement, so it's slightly behind. The third task, the inventory report, hasn't started.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's fine. Is something worrying you? You look like you want to say something.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, one risk. The data from procurement could slip another week, and if it does, the scorecard won't be ready for the supplier meeting on Thursday.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hmm. Could you work around it with last month's data?

script.speaker: B
script.line: I could, but they'd be old, and I won't present what I can't stand behind. Which comes first, the scorecard or the inventory report? I need a priority call.

script.speaker: A
script.line: The scorecard, definitely. The inventory report can wait until after the meeting. Use last month's data and mark it clearly as provisional.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Understood. Should I tell procurement it's urgent?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Yes, and I'll mention it to their lead at my catch-up with him at half past one today, so they know it comes from me.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Great, thanks. That takes a weight off.

Seven percent

Raise the data delay with procurement's lead
Present the scorecard to suppliers
Move the supplier meeting

To change the subject
To invite Henrik to raise a concern
To end the meeting

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hi Victor, can you hear me? Your video keeps freezing on my side. You wanted to ask about filing expenses after your trip?

script.speaker: B
script.line: I can hear you fine, Sofia, just a little delayed. Yes, I've got a pile of receipts from Berlin and I'm not sure what you need.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Every receipt over twenty-five euros needs the original or a clear photo. Meals are covered by the daily allowance, so you don't need those receipts. Just hotel, trains and taxis.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good. And the deadline? I know it's strict.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Claims are rejected six weeks after the trip ends. For you that's the fourteenth of September. Don't leave it to the last day.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Fine. One thing: last time a taxi receipt was rejected. Why was that?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Because it had no date or company name. Check those, and send me the report first. Shall we go through it tomorrow at eleven, in my office?

script.speaker: B
script.line: I'm in Lisbon tomorrow, I'm afraid. What about Friday at eleven, on video?

script.speaker: A
script.line: This connection is terrible, so let's meet in person instead: Friday at eleven, in the canteen.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of the call?
options: Victor reports a receipt he has lost
Sofia asks Victor to change his trip
They discuss the cost of a hotel room
Sofia explains how Victor should file his expenses
questions.explanation: Victor asks what receipts he needs and when the deadline is, and Sofia explains.

questions.q: When and where will Sofia and Victor finally meet?
options: Tomorrow at eleven, in Sofia's office
On Friday at eleven, in the canteen
On Friday at eleven, on video
Tomorrow at eleven, in Lisbon
questions.explanation: After the first two ideas fail, Sofia says, 'let's meet in person instead: Friday at eleven, in the canteen.'

questions.q: What does Sofia imply when she says, 'Don't leave it to the last day'?
options: A late claim could be rejected, so he should file early
She will be away on the last day
The system is very slow on the last day
Victor has already missed the deadline
questions.explanation: She has just said the system rejects claims after the cutoff, so she is urging him to file early.

title: Booking a hotel for an audit

script.speaker: A
script.line: Mei, thanks for fitting me in. I need a hotel for a two-night supplier audit, arriving Thursday the fourteenth of November. I'm a bit worried about it.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Of course, Chris. I'd suggest the hotel in the business park on the east side. It's ten minutes by car from the site, and several of our auditors stay there.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Ten minutes is good. Does it include breakfast? My first session starts at seven thirty, so I'll need something early.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Breakfast starts at six, so that's fine, and it's included in the rate.

script.speaker: A
script.line: And if the audit gets postponed, which has happened before, can I cancel without a penalty?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Free cancellation until forty-eight hours before arrival. After that, you'd pay the first night.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's acceptable. I have to say, I'm nervous about this audit. The supplier has already had two warnings, and I'll be on my own on the first day.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's understandable, but you're well prepared. Leave the logistics to me: I'll book the hotel and a taxi from the station, and send you the confirmation tomorrow.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Thank you, that's a weight off my mind.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of the conversation?
options: Mei asks Chris to cancel his trip
Chris complains about a hotel he used
Chris books a hotel for an audit with Mei's help
They plan a meeting with the supplier
questions.explanation: Chris needs a hotel for a two-night audit and Mei suggests one and offers to book it.

questions.q: When does breakfast start at the hotel?
options: At half past seven
At seven
At eight
At six
questions.explanation: Mei says breakfast starts at six; half past seven is when Chris's first session starts.

questions.q: What can we infer about the audit?
options: The audit is routine and low risk
Mei will go with Chris on the first day
The supplier's quality record is a concern
The hotel is too far from the site
questions.explanation: Chris says the supplier has already had two warnings, which is why he is nervous.

title: A missed pickup at the depot

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good morning, Tomas. Thank you for seeing me. I'm here about yesterday's pickup, which your truck never made.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good morning, Marta. Yes, I saw the report, and I'm sorry. Our driver was delayed at the previous stop, and the truck didn't reach you before the warehouse closed.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I understand, but the pallets were for the nineteenth of September, and now the customer will be late. We need a priority slot tomorrow morning.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I wish I could promise that. But tomorrow morning every truck is committed to the airport run, and I can't take one off it.

script.speaker: A
script.line: I see. Then what can you offer? About twelve percent of this week's shipments are now late because of the missed pickup.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I can give you the first slot in the afternoon, at two o'clock, and I'll send our most experienced driver. I can also waive the fee for the missed pickup.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Two o'clock works if the pallets are loaded by one. Can you confirm in writing?

script.speaker: B
script.line: Yes, I'll send an email in ten minutes with the pickup time and the booking number.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Thank you. And please tell the driver to call me when he arrives, so we can open the gate straight away.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I'll pass that on. Again, sorry for the trouble, Marta.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of Marta's visit?
options: To complain about the price of transport
To cancel the contract
To change the customer's order
To get a new pickup after a missed one
questions.explanation: She says she is there about the pickup the truck never made and asks for a priority slot.

questions.q: What time is the new pickup?
options: One o'clock
Two o'clock
Tomorrow morning
Ten minutes from now
questions.explanation: Tomas offers the first afternoon slot at two o'clock; one o'clock is when the pallets must be loaded.

questions.q: What will Tomas do in ten minutes?
options: Send an email confirming the pickup
Send a driver to the warehouse
Call the customer
Waive the fee in the system
questions.explanation: He says, 'I'll send an email in ten minutes with the pickup time and the booking number.'

questions.q: Why does Tomas say, 'I wish I could promise that'?
options: To blame Marta for the delay
To say the driver is unavailable
To ask Marta for more time
To politely refuse a priority slot
questions.explanation: He says it after Marta asks for a priority slot, and then explains the trucks are committed.

title: Delivery note and order don't match

script.speaker: A
script.line: Good morning, Pedro, it's Ana from planning. I'm calling about the delivery that arrived on the seventeenth of June.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Good morning, Ana. Of course. Is there a problem with it?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Possibly. The delivery note says twelve hundred units, but our purchase order was for one thousand. We counted the pallets, and there really are twelve hundred.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Hm, that's odd. Let me look. Yes, the order says one thousand, so you're right. I'm not sure how the extra two hundred got on.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Which figure is correct? If you meant to send twelve hundred, our order may have been changed, and I have no record of that.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I understand. Perhaps Raquel in dispatch added a second order from your site to this shipment. She's the only one who can confirm, and she's off until Thursday.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Thursday is a bit late. We'd have to store the extra pallets meanwhile, and space is expensive for us.

script.speaker: B
script.line: I appreciate that. Could you keep them separate until we know?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Yes, but I'd like to avoid booking the extra two hundred into stock before we've agreed. Otherwise our system will show an invoice mismatch.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Agreed. Please don't book them. As soon as Raquel is back on Thursday, I'll ask her and call you the same day.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That's fine. And if they were sent by mistake, who arranges the return, and who pays?

script.speaker: B
script.line: If it was our mistake, we'll collect them at our cost. I can't decide that until we've heard from Raquel, but we'll be fair.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Thank you, I appreciate that. I'll wait for your call on Thursday.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Of course. Sorry again for the confusion, Ana.

questions.q: How many units does the delivery note show?
options: One thousand two hundred
One thousand
Two hundred
One thousand four hundred
questions.explanation: Ana says the delivery note says twelve hundred units; the order was for one thousand.

questions.q: How does Ana come across in the conversation?
options: Angry and openly accusing Pedro
Polite but firm, and worried about the extra pallets
Casual and uninterested in the answer
Confused about what she should do
questions.explanation: She stays courteous but insists on clarity, and worries about storage costs and an invoice mismatch.

questions.q: What will Pedro do on Thursday?
options: Collect the extra pallets
Send a corrected delivery note
Ask Raquel what happened and call Ana
Cancel the purchase order
questions.explanation: He says, 'As soon as Raquel is back on Thursday, I'll ask her and call you the same day.'

script.speaker: A
script.line: Camila, thanks for coming. I wanted to tell you in person: your team is moving from the second floor to the fifth on the twenty-ninth of July.

script.speaker: B
script.line: The fifth? That's quite a change. What's the reason? I thought we had just settled in here.

script.speaker: A
script.line: The second floor is being redone for the customer service team, and the work will take about six weeks. It's nothing to do with planning, it's just a space issue.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Understood. And what about equipment? I have two monitors and a dock, and the team keeps a lot of paperwork in the cabinets.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Originally you would have packed everything yourselves, but IT has just said they'll pack and move all the equipment overnight. You only need to label your cabinets.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's good news, honestly. And who are the neighbours up there? We work closely with the logistics team.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Logistics are on the same floor, about ten desks away. The finance group sits at the other end, but there's a glass partition, so noise shouldn't be a problem.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Perfect. Then I'll tell my team today and ask them to label their cabinets this week.

Camila asks for a bigger desk
Ethan reports a problem with the finance team
They plan a renovation budget

The customer service team
IT staff, overnight
The logistics team
questions.explanation: Ethan says IT will pack and move all the equipment overnight.

questions.q: Why is Camila's team moving?
options: The planning team has become too large
The second floor is being redone for another team
The finance group wants a quieter floor
Logistics asked for more space nearby
questions.explanation: Ethan says the second floor is being redone for customer service and it's just a space issue.

options: It is permanent
It is only for Camila
It is a punishment for the planning team
It is temporary, lasting while the work is done

title: Asking to push a delivery out

script.speaker: A
script.line: Hi Ibrahim, it's Olivia. Is this a good moment? I have to ask you a favour, and I'm afraid it's not a small one.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Of course, go ahead. You sound a bit stressed. What's happened?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Our loading dock is jammed with returned pallets, and we can't pick your order in time for the eleventh of May. Could you accept the delivery a week later?

script.speaker: B
script.line: A week isn't ideal, we have customers waiting. But I can probably cope. In return, I'd want a firm date and first call on your next production slot.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That seems fair. I'll talk to the warehouse manager and call you back at half past one with a firm date. The first slot on the next run is yours.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Don't panic, Olivia, these things happen. I'll tell my sales team to hold off on customer promises, and I'll check whether part can ship sooner from your other site.

script.speaker: A
script.line: That would be a huge help, thank you. And your ten-week supply plan stays exactly as it is. This won't affect your priority.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Appreciated. Speak at half past one, then.

questions.q: When will Olivia call Ibrahim back with a firm date?
options: On the eleventh of May
A week later
At half past one
In ten weeks
questions.explanation: Olivia says, 'I'll ... call you back at half past one with a firm date.'

questions.q: Why can't Olivia's team prepare the order in time?
options: The production run was cancelled this week
The warehouse manager is away on leave
Ibrahim changed the size of the order
The loading dock is blocked with returned pallets
questions.explanation: She says the dock is jammed with returned pallets and they can't pick his order in time.

questions.q: What will Ibrahim do to help?
options: Move the order to another distributor
Tell his sales team to pause promises to customers
Collect the pallets from the dock himself
Cancel the next production run
questions.explanation: He says, 'I'll tell my sales team to hold off on promises to customers.'

questions.q: What is the main purpose of the call?
options: Olivia asks Ibrahim to accept a later delivery
Ibrahim asks Olivia for a full refund
They plan a new ten-week contract
Olivia reports a problem at the other site
questions.explanation: Olivia asks for a one-week delay and Ibrahim agrees in return for a firm date and priority.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Claire, thanks for having me on site. I wanted to go through the stockout properly, not just by email. From where I sit, the cause was on both sides.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Agreed. Let's be honest about our part. The forecast jumped by twenty percent late in the month, and our system didn't flag it to purchasing until it was too late.

script.speaker: A
script.line: And on our side we were running a lean schedule, so we had nothing to cover that jump. That's something we can fix.

script.speaker: B
script.line: The other thing is that nobody had reviewed safety stock for over twelve weeks. Nobody owned it. Honestly, that was the bigger failing.

script.speaker: A
script.line: So what do we change? I'd suggest an alert whenever the forecast moves by more than ten percent in a week.

script.speaker: B
script.line: Fine. And a named owner for safety stock, reviewed monthly. I'll take that one myself. Could you commit to a one-week buffer on the top products?

script.speaker: A
script.line: Yes, that's reasonable. One more thing, while I think of it. Our new pallet labels won't scan on your dock readers, so the next shipment may be held up.

script.speaker: B
script.line: That's the last thing we need. Can you send me a sample label today? I'll ask our IT team to test it on the reader.

script.speaker: A
script.line: Of course. Let's talk again on Friday, once you have an answer, and I'll hold the shipment until then.

questions.q: What are Samuel and Claire mainly doing?
options: Planning a new product launch together
Arguing about an overdue invoice
Finding what caused a stockout and agreeing changes
Training a new planner on the system
questions.explanation: They discuss the forecast jump, missing safety stock review and changes to prevent a repeat.

questions.q: What size of forecast change will trigger the new alert?
options: More than twenty percent
More than ten percent in a week
More than twelve percent
More than five percent

questions.q: Why couldn't Samuel's company cover the forecast jump?

It never received the forecast
It was running a lean schedule

Hold the shipment until Friday
Set up a weekly forecast check by herself
Review safety stock with Samuel
questions.explanation: She says, 'I'll ask our IT team to test it on the reader' after receiving a sample.
